WhatsApp Help Compendium

Official WhatsApp help for iPhone, WhatsApp Web, and the Windows desktop app

2026-07-27

WhatsApp Help Compendium

This compendium contains the main content of 696 articles from WhatsApp’s official Help Center. Each article was collected in three platform editions – iPhone, WhatsApp Web, and the Windows desktop app; where the editions are identical they appear once, and where the instructions differ the article presents labeled platform sections. WhatsApp’s served pages do not expose the Help Center’s own topic organization, so articles are grouped under editorial categories assigned by title keywords, sorted alphabetically, with article titles alphabetized within each category (ignoring leading words such as About and How to). Site navigation, feedback prompts, and tracking parameters have been removed.

Turning on high contrast and color accessibility features can improve your experience:

  • If you have visual or cognitive impairments: These features can make it easier to read text and navigate content.
  • In challenging lighting conditions: High contrast settings can help you see your screen more clearly in bright sunlight or low-light environments.
  • Whenever you need increased clarity and legibility: Enabling these features can make on-screen information stand out, making it easier to use your device.

Apply color filters

  1. Go to device Settings.
  2. Tap Accessibility > Display & Text Size.
  3. Tap Color Filters to view controls.

Enable color inversion

  1. Go to device Settings.
  2. Tap Accessibility > Display & Text Size.
  3. Toggle Classic Invert to reverse the colors of the display or toggle Smart Invert to reverse the colors of the display except for images, media, and some apps that use the dark color styles.

Enable a high contrast display

  1. Go to device Settings.
  2. Tap Accessibility > Display & Text Size.
  3. Toggle to turn on Increase Contrast.

Magnification and zoom

  1. Go to device Settings.
  2. Tap Accessibility > Zoom.
  3. Toggle to turn on Zoom.
  4. Double-tap with three fingers to zoom in or out.

For more info, visit the Apple Support.

Switch Control is an accessibility feature designed to help people with limited mobility interact with their devices using external switches. These switches can include physical buttons, adaptive devices, or even facial gestures, allowing users to operate their devices without touchscreens.

Account and Registration

5 Tips to keep your WhatsApp account safe and secure

Copy link

WhatsApp privacy and security is more than just end-to-end encryption. Optional features like chat lock, profile photo privacy, app lock, view once messages, and status privacy add extra layers of protection to your account. Here’s how you can explore each one:

1. Lock your private chats

You can lock and password protect your most personal chats. Locked chats will be hidden from your chats list in the Locked Chats folder.

Android & iOS:

  1. Swipe left or tap and hold the chat you want to lock or unlock.

  2. Tap more options > Lock Chat or Unlock chat. Web & Windows

  3. Right click the chat.

  4. Click Lock Chat or Unlock Chat.

When you turn chat lock on, no one else in the chat is notified—and the chat will automatically close when you lock your device. You can also create a secret code, view your locked chats folder and hide locked chats.

If you liked this tip, try turning on disappearing messages. Learn more about how to use disappearing messages.

2. Control who sees your profile photo

When your contacts receive a message from you and they have notifications enabled, your profile photo is displayed in their notification, unless you decide to adjust your privacy settings.

To edit who can see your profile photo:

Android

  1. Tap more options > Settings > Privacy > Profile photo.

  2. Choose Everyone, My contacts, My contacts except…, or Nobody. iOS

  3. Tap Settings or your profile picture, then tap Privacy > Profile Photo.

  4. Choose Everyone, My contacts, My contacts except…, or Nobody.

Learn more about why someone’s profile photo, last seen and online, about information, stories, or read receipts might not be visible to you.

3. Secure your account with Face ID, Touch ID, or Fingerprint

As an additional, optional security measure, you can use app lock on WhatsApp so only you can access it. When turned on, you must use Fingerprint or face recognition (Android), Touch ID or Face ID (iOS) or password (Web), to unlock WhatsApp. You can still reply to messages from notifications and answer calls if WhatsApp is locked.

Learn how to turn app lock on and off on Android, iOS or Web.

4. Send media and voice messages more privately

You can send personal photos, videos and voice messages that disappear from a chat after the recipient has opened them once. This is known as ‘view once’.

View once photos and videos won’t be saved to the recipient’s Photos or Gallery. Recipients also won’t be able to take a screenshot or screen recording of your view once media.

Learn how to send and open view once media and voice messages on iOS and Android.

5. Choose who can see your status

You can choose who can see your status by adding them to your status audience or mentioning people or groups in your status. By default, your status updates are shared with all your contacts.

Note:

  • People or groups you mention in your status can reshare it to their audience.
  • You can mention people who aren’t in your contacts.

Learn how to change your status privacy and share status updates to Facebook Stories and other apps.

About account bans

Copy link

[Embedded video omitted]

0:00 / 1:50

If your account is banned, you’ll see the following message when you open WhatsApp: “This phone number can’t use WhatsApp: [phone number]. You can request a review of this number. Most reviews are completed within 24 hours.”

How to request a review

  1. Tap Request review in the app.
  2. You’ll receive a WhatsApp notification once we review your account and make a decision.

We only review one phone number per appeal. If you don’t see an option to request a review, it means the ban is final and can’t be appealed.

You can check the status of your request by opening WhatsApp. Please keep in mind that contacting WhatsApp outside of the review process or through another user’s account, won’t expedite the review process or impact the decision. Learn what to do after your account is unbanned here.

Please note, third party services can’t ban your WhatsApp account or remove your account ban. Only WhatsApp can ban or unban a WhatsApp account.

We ban accounts if we believe the account activity violates our Terms of Service, for example if it involves spam, scams or if it puts WhatsApp users’ safety at risk. We recommend carefully reviewing the “Acceptable Use of Our Services” section of our Terms of Service to learn more about the appropriate uses of WhatsApp and the activities that violate our Terms of Service. Learn how to use WhatsApp responsibly in this article.

You can’t access your chat history or backups while your account is banned. You can only access a WhatsApp account backup after the phone number tied to the backup is unbanned.

About account bans for previously owned phone numbers

Copy link

If you’re using a new phone number, it’s possible that the previous owner of your new phone number violated our Terms of Service and this caused the account to be banned. Read our Terms of Services here.

To request a review of the account ban, you can tap Request review in the app and then tap Request review to submit the request. Once submitted, we’ll look into your case and get back to you as soon as we complete our review. Once your account is reviewed, you’ll receive a notification from WhatsApp.

To access your WhatsApp account after your account is unbanned, you’ll need to verify your account by entering your phone number. You can visit our website to download WhatsApp or the WhatsApp Business app.

Note: We don’t provide support for unsupported apps, devices, or versions of WhatsApp, or jailbroken or rooted devices. Learn more about our supported operating systems in this article. For more information about unofficial apps and why we don’t support these apps, you can refer to this article.

About account bans for unofficial apps

Copy link

Using an unauthorized application and/or unsupported device violates our Terms of Service and can result in your account being banned. Unofficial apps are fake WhatsApp apps, developed by third parties, which violate our Terms of Service. We don’t support these apps because we can’t validate their security practices. Learn more about unofficial apps and why we don’t support them in this article.

To continue using WhatsApp, uninstall the unofficial app and download the official WhatsApp app. You can download WhatsApp or the WhatsApp Business app on our website or from official app stores.

If you’re using an unofficial app because you’re interested in new features, check our Help Center or blog to learn about our new and upcoming features.

Note: We can reinstate an account ban if the account activity continues to violate our Terms of Service. We recommend carefully reviewing the “Acceptable Use of Our Services” section of our Terms of Service to learn more about the appropriate uses of WhatsApp and the activities that violate our Terms of Service.

About account deactivation

Copy link

When a WhatsApp account is deactivated, this means the account is temporarily disabled. The WhatsApp account will be deleted 30 days after deactivation if the account isn’t re-registered.

If your phone is lost or stolen, call your mobile provider as soon as possible and ask them to block your SIM card.

When an account is deactivated

  • Your contacts can still see your profile.
  • Your contacts can send you messages, which will remain in a pending state for up to 30 days.
  • If you don’t activate your account within 30 days, it’ll be completely deleted.

Re-registering a deactivated account

If you re-register your account before it’s deleted, you’ll:

  • Receive any pending messages on your new phone.
  • Remain in all of your group chats.
  • Have an option to restore your data. Learn how to restore your chat history in this article.

Account security tips

On iPhone

Copy link

Android

iOS

More

Android

iOS

To better secure your WhatsApp account, follow these tips:

  • Never share your registration code or two-step verification PIN with others.
  • Enable two-step verification and provide an email address in case you forget your PIN.
  • Set a voicemail password on your phone that’s difficult to guess to prevent anyone from accessing your voicemail.
  • Check your linked devices regularly. Tap your profile picture, then tap Linked Devices to review all devices linked to your account. To remove a linked device, tap the device > Log Out > Log Out.
  • It’s possible to add WhatsApp to your Accounts Center. If you believe that someone else has access to the Facebook, Instagram, or Meta account in your Accounts Center, and has used one of those accounts to access your WhatsApp account, reach out to the Support team of the impacted account to help recover your account. You can also temporarily remove your WhatsApp account from Accounts Center until all of your accounts are secured. Learn more about Accounts Center here.
  • It’s also recommended to review your accounts by navigating to WhatsApp Settings and tapping Accounts Center. If you notice a suspicious account in your Accounts Center, you can remove it by following the steps in this Meta Help Center article.

For those who believe they may be targeted by sophisticated attacks, WhatsApp offers Strict account settings. This is an advanced, optional security feature that, when enabled, applies WhatsApp’s strictest privacy and security controls to help reduce your vulnerability to cyber attacks. This feature is built for users who may face elevated risk and should only be turned on if you believe you may be targeted.

Note:

  • If you receive unrequested emails to reset your two-step verification PIN or registration code, don’t click on any links. Someone could be attempting to access your phone number on WhatsApp.
  • If you see the message “Your phone number was registered with WhatsApp on a new device” when you open WhatsApp, follow the onscreen steps to recover your account. Learn more about account recovery.

How to add an international phone number

Copy link

  1. Open your phone’s address book.
  2. When adding the contact’s phone number, start by entering a plus sign (+).
  3. Enter the country code, followed by the full phone number.
    • Note: A country code is a numerical prefix that must be entered before the full national phone number to make a call to another country. You can search online to find the country code you need.

For example, if a contact in the United States (country code “1”) has the area code “408” and phone number “XXX-XXXX”, you’d enter +1 408 XXX XXXX.

Note:

  • Make sure to remove any leading 0s or special calling codes.
  • If you meant to add a local (in country) phone number to your phone’s address book, enter the number as if you were calling your contact on the phone.
  • All phone numbers in Argentina (country code “54”) should have a “9” between the country code and area code. The prefix “15” must be removed so the final number will have 13 digits total: +54 9 XXX XXX XXXX
  • Phone numbers in Mexico (country code “52”) need to have “1” after “+52”, even if they’re Nextel numbers.

About automatic phone number verification

Copy link

This feature is only available in limited countries and may not be available to you yet.

WhatsApp can automatically verify your login when you register your phone number. You can also use manual verification methods such as SMS or voice call.

There are several ways WhatsApp can do this:

  • By storing a unique code on your phone. This happens when you sign up to WhatsApp and confirm your phone number through a missed call (available only on Android) or SMS. The unique code is then used to automatically verify your phone number in future.
  • You can opt in to save your phone number and verification information for future logins through Facebook or Instagram. When you opt in, a unique code stored on your mobile phone is used to create verification information for your account. When this happens, Facebook and Instagram won’t save your WhatsApp phone number or use it for any other purpose. If you’re using the same phone number and device to log into WhatsApp, Facebook or Instagram will share your verification information with WhatsApp to automatically log you in. Find out how to opt out on Facebook or Instagram.
  • You can enable end-to-end encrypted backups in your Google Account. If enabled, WhatsApp saves a unique back-up code to Google Cloud. This means when you delete and reinstall WhatsApp, you can skip SMS verification and we can automatically verify you. Learn more about backups in this help article.
  • WhatsApp can automatically verify your phone number without an SMS or missed call (available only on Android) by working with your phone carrier to validate that your device information matches the phone number that you’re registering.

After verification, you will see a Verified confirmation to let you know that your phone number has been securely verified on your device without sending a code.

Note:

  • As always, your personal messages and calls are end-to-end encrypted. No one, not even WhatsApp, can read or listen to them.
  • By entering your phone number, you authorize your wireless carrier to share data from your account and wireless device to WhatsApp or its service providers for phone number verification and fraud prevention purposes. To learn more about the data we collect and how we use it, view our Privacy Policy.

Can’t change phone number

Copy link

If you can’t change your phone number, there are a few things to check:

Check if your old number is registered

Check whether the old phone number you entered is currently registered on your WhatsApp account.

You can see what phone number is registered by going to WhatsApp Settings. Then, tap your profile photo.

If your old phone number isn’t registered, register it first before you try to change your phone number again.

Check if your account is banned

If you can’t change your phone number because your account is banned, you’ll see the following message when you open WhatsApp: “This phone number can’t use WhatsApp: [phone number]. You can request a review of this number. Most reviews are completed within 24 hours.”

Your account may be banned if we believe the account activity violates our Terms of Service, for example if it involves spam, scams or if it puts WhatsApp users’ safety at risk. We recommend carefully reviewing the “Acceptable Use of Our Services” section of our Terms of Service to learn more about the appropriate uses of WhatsApp and the activities that violate our Terms of Service. Learn more about banned accounts in this article.

If you think your account was banned by mistake, tap Request review in the app to submit the request. Once submitted, we’ll look into your case and get back to you as soon as we complete our review. We only review one phone number per appeal. If you don’t see an option to request a review, it means the ban is final and can’t be appealed.

Check your SIM

You have an active and working SIM card for the new phone number you want to use with WhatsApp.

If you changed the SIM card or phone number on your device but are still using the WhatsApp account associated with your old phone number, you must use the change number feature to transfer your WhatsApp account to your new phone number to maintain access to your account. If you don’t use the change number feature and you lose access to your old SIM card or number, you will permanently lose access to your WhatsApp account and will need to create a new WhatsApp account with your new SIM card. Learn how to change your phone number in this article.

Check your connection

Check that you have a strong and stable cellular connection.

Check your storage

Make sure your device has sufficient internal storage.

Check that you’re using a supported phone number

Make sure you’re using a supported phone number. Unsupported phone numbers can’t be registered on WhatsApp and include:

  • VoIP

  • Landlines.

  • Note: Landlines are only accepted on the WhatsApp Business app.

  • Toll-free numbers.

  • Paid premium numbers.

  • Universal access numbers (UAN).

  • Personal numbers.

Note:

  • You can only change your phone number on your primary device. The “Change number” option will be greyed out if you are on a linked/companion device instead of your primary phone. You can’t change your phone number on a linked device like WhatsApp Web or WhatsApp for desktops.
  • If you see that your new number is already registered on WhatsApp while changing your number, it is possible that the previous owner of your new phone number used WhatsApp. Learn more about recycled numbers here.
  • If you lost access to your SIM card and want to keep using the same number, you will need to contact your mobile provider to get a new SIM card with the same number to recover your account. Learn more about recovering your account here.
  • If you’ve previously registered your new number on a different device, you can transfer your account to the device you intend to use. Learn more about changing phones here.
  • If you’re trying to register a new phone number after you’ve changed it, read about registering your phone number.
  • We don’t support unofficial clients or for jailbroken, rooted, or unsupported devices.

Can’t complete registration

Copy link

WhatsApp registration may fail to complete due to phone number or SIM card issues, unstable Internet connection, or problems receiving the verification code. If you’re having trouble completing the registration process to activate your account, try the following troubleshooting steps:

Phone number or SIM card issues

WhatsApp registration may fail if the number is not supported or entered correctly, or if the SIM card is not active and can’t receive SMS or phone calls. If you are having issues related to your phone number or SIM card, make sure:

  • You have an active SIM card in your phone for the phone number you want to register and can receive SMS or phone calls.
  • You entered your phone number correctly in full international format.
  • You are registering a supported number. Unsupported phone numbers, such as VoIP, landlines, toll-free, paid premium numbers, universal access numbers (UAN), shared cost, and personal numbers can’t be registered on WhatsApp. Landines can only be used when registering on on the WhatsApp Business App, where you will receive the code via your landline number. Learn more about registering for the WhatsApp Business app.
  • If you have a prepaid line, confirm you have enough balance to receive SMS or phone calls on the number you are trying to register.
  • If you’re abroad, you must enable roaming to receive international SMS and/or phone calls. Keep in mind that enabling roaming might incur extra charges.
  • Turn off all task killers and blockers, such as Advanced Task Killer or Handcent Next SMS.

Make sure you meet the minimum age eligibility requirements to use WhatsApp, per our Terms of Service. Also, update WhatsApp to the latest version available.

Unstable cellular network and Internet connection

WhatsApp account registration requires a stable Internet connection. If you are having connection issues:

  • Try to connect to a different network or move to a different location to get a cellular connection.
  • Check your phone manufacturer’s settings to enable Wi-Fi Calling options. Wi-Fi Calling lets you make calls and send texts over a Wi-Fi network, which is useful when you experience network issues during registration.

Unable to receive a verification code

WhatsApp verification codes can take up to 24 hours to arrive after requesting one. If your code hasn’t arrived, try these steps:

  • Request a new registration code via SMS or phone call. Tap Need help getting a code? to choose a registration code option. If you still haven’t received your code through SMS, try tapping Call me to request a code through a phone call. For most regions, if you choose the phone call option and have voicemail enabled, our automated system will leave you a voicemail with your code.
  • If you still haven’t received your code after 24 hours and are unable to verify your account, contact your mobile provider for additional information.

You may see the message “You have guessed the code too many times.” if you enter the wrong code more than once. Please wait the designated amount of time before you request another code. There’s no way to make this faster.

If you’re logging in to your existing WhatsApp account and you added your email address in your WhatsApp settings during your initial registration or during two-step verification setup, you can receive a verification code through email. Select Email under Choose how to verify > Continue.

For security reasons, we can only send your registration code via SMS message or phone call. However, we can send a verification code through email only if you’re logging in to your existing account using your registered phone number and you’ve already added your email address to your account in your WhatsApp settings, during your initial registration, or when setting up your account PIN.

If you didn’t receive the 6-digit code by SMS

  • Make sure you’ve entered your full international phone number, including the country code. Remove any leading zeros (0s) or exit codes from your number. An example of a US phone number is: + 1 408 XXX-XXXX.
  • Wait for the five-minute timer to finish counting down.
  • Don’t edit your number during this time.
  • If the timer runs out before you receive the code, tap Call Me.
  • When you answer the call, an automated voice will announce the 6-digit code. Insert this code to verify WhatsApp.

If you have issues registering, try:

  • Making sure you’re using the latest version of WhatsApp installed on your phone.
  • Making sure you meet all of the requirements when you register your phone number.
  • Turning off your phone, wait 30 seconds, and turning it back on.
  • Deleting and reinstalling the latest version of WhatsApp. We recommend using the chat backup feature to back up your messages before you delete WhatsApp from your device.
  • Checking your reception by sending an SMS message from any phone to your phone number. Make sure you’re sending it to the same phone number you entered in WhatsApp, including the country code.
  • Checking your phone manufacturer’s settings to enable Wi-Fi Calling options. Wi-Fi Calling lets you make calls and send texts over a Wi-Fi network, which is useful when you experience network issues during registration.

If you’re still having issues with registration, try some of the tips listed in this article.

Note: You may see the message “You have guessed the code too many times.” if you enter the wrong code more than once. Please wait the designated amount of time before you request another code. There’s no way to make this faster.

You can change the phone number associated with your WhatsApp account. Learn more about changing your phone number in this article.

Before changing your phone number:

  • Make sure your new phone number can receive SMS texts or phone calls.

  • Make sure your new phone number has an active cellular connection.

  • Make sure your old phone number is currently registered on WhatsApp on your phone. You can find your registered phone number by opening WhatsApp Settings or your profile.

  • Make sure you’re using a supported phone number. Unsupported phone numbers can’t be registered on WhatsApp and include:

  • VoIP

  • Toll-free numbers

  • Paid premium numbers

  • Universal access numbers (UAN)

  • Personal numbers

  • Landlines (Note: Landlines are only accepted on the WhatsApp Business app)

Note:

  • You can’t change your phone number on WhatsApp Desktop or WhatsApp Web. You must change your phone number on your primary device.
  • If you change your phone number and use the same WhatsApp account, your blocked contacts will stay blocked and wouldn’t be notified of your updated phone number.
  • Cloud backups of your chat history are linked to the phone number used when the backup is created. This means that when you change your number, all backups made using the old number can no longer be used to restore your data. It is highly recommended to create a new backup after you’ve changed your number to have a valid and accessible backup and avoid any loss of data. Learn how to back up your chat history here.

Change phone number on the same phone

If you want to change your phone number or use a new SIM card in your device, you must use the change number feature to transfer your WhatsApp account to your new phone number in order to maintain access to your account. To change your phone number using the same phone, first insert the SIM card with the new phone number and follow these steps:

  1. Tap WhatsApp Settings or your profile picture.
  2. Tap Account > Change Number > Next.
  3. Enter your old phone number in the first field and your new phone number in the second field, both in full international format.
  4. Tap Next.
    • If you turn on Notify Contacts, you can choose if you want to notify All contacts, Contacts I have chats with or Custom… If you select Custom…, you’ll need to search for or select the contacts you want to notify, then tap Done.
    • Your group chats are automatically notified when you change phone numbers, regardless of whether you choose to notify your contacts.
  5. Tap Done.
  6. You’ll then be prompted to register your new phone number. Learn more in this article.

Change phone number on a new phone

If you want to change your phone number and transfer your chat history to a new phone, you’ll need to change your number on your old phone and then create an iCloud or computer backup on your new number. Learn how to back up to iCloud in this article. For information on restoring your chat history without an iCloud or computer backup, visit the Apple Support website. Backups can only be restored using the phone number used when the backup was created. It is important to have a backup that is associated with your new number to be able to restore the backup to your new phone.

After changing your phone number and creating a backup on your old phone, follow the steps below using your new phone:

  1. Install WhatsApp.
  2. Register your new phone number again.
  3. Restore your backup.

About changing phone numbers

Copy link

You can change the phone number associated with your account to transfer your account information to a new phone number. Learn how to change your phone number.

When you change your phone number, WhatsApp will:

  • Transfer your account information and settings to your new phone number. This includes your profile photo, username, display name, privacy settings, WhatsApp contacts, individual chats, and group chats.
  • Delete the WhatsApp account associated with your old phone number, so your contacts will no longer see your old phone number in their WhatsApp contacts lists.

We recommend that you take the following steps before changing your phone number:

  • Tell your contacts about your new phone number before changing phone numbers. Ask them to add your new number to their phone’s contacts to avoid any confusion.
  • If you manage a broadcast list, tell the recipients to save your new number to their contacts. Only those who’ve added your new number to their phone’s contacts will receive your broadcast message.

Cloud backups of your chat history are linked to the phone number used when the backup is created. This means that when you change your number, all backups made using the old number can no longer be used to restore your data. It is highly recommended to create a new backup after you’ve changed your number to have a valid and accessible backup and avoid any loss of data. Learn how to back up your chat history here.

Note

  • If you change your phone number and use the same WhatsApp account, your blocked contacts will stay blocked and wouldn’t be notified of your updated phone number.
  • If you change your phone number by mistake, there’s no way to revert this change. If you resume use of your original phone number and want to regain access to your groups, you’ll need to ask the group admin to re-invite you. Learn more about how to rejoin a group chat.

To enhance the security of WhatsApp accounts, you may be required to wait for a few hours before setting up two-factor authentication. When you begin the setup process, you may see an error message that says “2FA can’t be set at this time. Please try again later.” The exact duration of this waiting period may vary.

This waiting period helps ensure you can keep control over your account. During the waiting period, it is important to monitor your account for any unusual activity. Keep your account information secure and do not share your login details with anyone.

If you’re still having problems setting up two-factor authentication after the waiting period, you can try changing between a VPN, cellular, or WiFi connection, then setting up your two step verification code after switching back and forth.

As a parent or guardian, you can either delete your child’s parent-managed account yourself, or walk them through the steps so they can do it on their own.

  1. Open WhatsApp on your child’s device.
  2. Tap Account > Delete account.
  3. Tap Continue and select a reason for why you’re deleting the account in the dropdown.
  4. Tap Continue.
  5. Enter your child’s phone number in full international format and tap Delete account.
  6. Tap Delete account.

Note: These instructions are for how to delete a parent-managed account on WhatsApp. For help on deleting a WhatsApp account that isn’t parent-managed, learn more in this article.

When does WhatsApp delete accounts?

To maintain security, limit data retention, and protect the privacy of our users, WhatsApp accounts are generally deleted after 365 days of inactivity. Inactivity means the account hasn’t connected to WhatsApp. Learn more about inactive deletion in this article.

How to delete your account

On iPhone

Copy link

Android

iOS

More

Android

iOS

Note: Deleting your account is irreversible, this action can’t be reversed even if you delete WhatsApp by accident.

You can delete your account from within WhatsApp. You’ll need to be logged into the account you wish to delete, and account deletion can only be performed from your primary device, not from any linked devices.

As a reminder, WhatsApp can’t restore or transfer chats, documents, media files, backups, or call history from deleted accounts.

To delete your account

  1. Tap Settings or your profile picture.
  2. Tap Account > Delete My Account.
  3. Enter your phone number in full international format and tap Delete My Account.

Deleting your account will:

  • Delete your account info and profile photo.
  • Delete you from all WhatsApp groups.
  • Delete your WhatsApp message history backup.
  • Remove you as a channel admin or follower, but not delete any updates you made or channel interactions like reactions or poll votes.
  • Delete any channels you created if there aren’t additional channel admins.

If you delete your account:

  • You can’t regain access to your account.
  • It may take up to 90 days from the beginning of the deletion process to delete your WhatsApp information. Copies of your information may also remain after the 90 days in the backup storage that we use to recover in the event of a disaster, software error, or other data loss event. Your information isn’t available to you on WhatsApp during this time.
  • It doesn’t affect your information related to the groups you created or the information other users have relating to you. For example, their copy of the messages you sent them.
  • We may retain certain log data in our databases even after you delete your account, but such data will be disassociated from any identifying information such that it can no longer be linked to your account. To do this we regularly wipe certain identifying information from this log data. We also replace any instance of your account ID with a replacement identifier which can’t be linked back to your account once it is deleted.
  • We may also keep your information for things like legal issues, terms violations, or harm prevention efforts.
  • Please refer to our Privacy Policy for more information.
  • Your information shared with other Meta Companies will also be deleted.

If contacts are still seeing you as a WhatsApp user after you’ve deleted your account, ask them to restart WhatsApp.

This will refresh their WhatsApp contacts and you should be removed from their contacts list. This won’t delete their chats with you, though.

WhatsApp Channels

To keep your channel active, be sure to add additional admins before deleting your account. If you delete your account without additional admins on your channel, your channel will be permanently deleted.

Channel deletion doesn’t delete your previous channel activity from your followers’ devices.

If you own a WhatsApp channel:

  • If you want to delete your channel and your WhatsApp account, delete your channel first.

  • Your channel and channel updates may not be deleted automatically.

  • If you have other channel admins, channel ownership will transfer to the admin who has followed the channel longest.

  • If you’re the only channel admin, your channel will be deleted. Deleting your channel is permanent and means:

  • You won’t be able to share updates from it again.

  • You won’t be able to recover the channel or follower list.

  • Existing updates are still visible to followers but non-followers won’t be able to find your channel or view updates. If you want to delete updates you shared in a channel, learn how to delete updates.

If you’re a channel admin:

  • Updates you’ve shared in channels aren’t deleted. If you want to delete updates you made in a channel, learn how to delete updates.

About email verification codes and resetting two-step verification

On iPhone

Copy link

Two-step verification is an optional feature that adds more security to your WhatsApp account.

You’ll see the two-step verification screen after you successfully register your phone number on WhatsApp. Learn how to enable two-step verification.

When you enable two-step verification, you have the option to enter your email address. Entering your email address will add an extra safeguard to your account and help you reset your two-step verification PIN.

You can add your email to your account at any time by going to your WhatsApp Settings > Account > Email Address. You will be asked to verify this email to confirm that it is accessible to you.

How to log in using an email verification code

You can log in to your account through email if you added and verified your email address in your WhatsApp settings during your initial registration or during two-step verification setup, and you have an active SIM card with the number associated with your account in your device. This applies when you log into your existing WhatsApp account on a new phone.

  1. Ensure your phone has a strong internet connection.
  2. Open WhatsApp.
  3. Follow the steps to register your phone number.
  4. You’ll receive a 6-digit registration code via email once you enter your phone number.
  5. Enter your 6-digit code to complete registration.

Note:

  • An active SIM card with the phone number associated with your WhatsApp account must be in your device to receive verification codes through any method, including email, SMS, or phone call.
  • If you are registering your account for the first time, you can only receive the verification code through SMS or phone call. Learn how to register your phone number.
  • If you have lost access to your number or SIM card, you can not use your email to receive the verification code and log in to your account. You must call your mobile provider and request a new SIM card with the same phone number, or learn how to change your phone number.

Email verification code not working

If you received a 6-digit verification code via email but the code isn’t accepted, try the following:

  • If you requested multiple codes, only the most recent code is valid. Check your inbox for the latest email from WhatsApp and use that code.
  • Email verification codes expire after a short time. If your code has expired, request a new code and enter it promptly.
  • Make sure you’re entering all six digits correctly without extra spaces.
  • Check that you’re entering the code on the same device where you initiated the verification request.

Note: If you continue to receive codes that don’t work, try restarting WhatsApp and requesting a new code.

If you can’t access your email

If you no longer have access to the email address where WhatsApp sends your verification code, you may have the following options:

  • If you’re still logged in to WhatsApp on another device, update your email address by going to Settings > Account > Email Address before trying to log in on the new device.
  • If you have an active SIM card for the phone number associated with your account, check if there’s an option to receive the verification code via SMS or phone call instead of email.

Note: You can only update your email address from within WhatsApp while logged in on an active device.

Reset your two-step verification PIN

If you provided an email address when you set up two-step verification or added it in your WhatsApp Settings, you can reset the PIN immediately by requesting a reset link. You’ll need to have two-step verification enabled to complete these steps. Learn how to reset your two-step verification PIN.

Reset your two-step verification PIN for a previously owned number

If you have a new SIM card and see a request to enter a two-step verification PIN, it’s possible that the number was used before. If that’s the case, the previous owner of that phone number may have created a WhatsApp account and set up two-step verification with an email address.

In this case, you’ll need to wait seven days after you’ve registered before you can reset your two-step verification PIN.

How are data and privacy protected on parent-managed accounts

On iPhone

Copy link

Android

iOS

More

Android

iOS

Parent-managed accounts are rolling out gradually and may not be available in your region.

At WhatsApp, we understand that privacy and security are top priorities for parents and guardians, and that’s why we built parent-managed accounts with that in mind.

As always, personal chats are end-to-end encrypted, which means no one outside of these chats, not even WhatsApp, can read or share them. This is the foundation of your child’s privacy on WhatsApp.

For WhatsApp to keep everyone safe, we collect some limited account information, as noted in our Privacy Policy. We don’t use your child’s information, nor the fact that you are using parental controls to manage their account, for ads.

Your child’s information is handled with care. We only keep information for as long as we need it to allow your child to use a managed account and to comply with our legal requirements. You have the ability to delete your child’s account at any time.

For more information about your child’s privacy, see our Privacy Policy.

Additional tips on how to stay safe

  • Review privacy settings: You determine your child’s privacy settings, but we encourage you to also help your child understand what information others can see about them.
  • Talk about sharing: Remind your child of the importance of thinking about what they share with others, and not to share personal details about themselves with people they don’t know.
  • Stay involved: Encourage your child to come to you with any questions or concerns they have.

About inactive account deletion

Copy link

To maintain security, limit data retention, and protect the privacy of our users, WhatsApp accounts are generally deleted after 365 days of inactivity. Inactivity means the user hasn’t connected to WhatsApp.

You may see the notification “WhatsApp profile removed automatically” or a user’s profile picture removed if their account is inactive.

An internet connection is required for an account to be active. If a user has WhatsApp open on their device, but they don’t have an internet connection, then the account will be inactive.

If you have turned on WhatsApp contacts, contacts saved to your WhatsApp account will be deleted along with your account.

Content stored locally on a user’s device prior to account deletion will remain until WhatsApp is deleted from the device. When a user reregisters for WhatsApp on the same device, their locally stored content will reappear.

About international phone number format

Copy link

A phone number in full international format includes a plus sign (+), then country code, city code, and local phone number. When contacting WhatsApp, always send your phone number in full international format.

For example, if a contact in the United States (country code “1”) has the area code “408” and phone number “XXX-XXXX”, you’d enter +1 408 XXX XXXX. If a contact in Portugal (country code “351”) has the area code “21” and phone number “XXX-XXXX”, you’d enter +351 21 XXX XXXX.

Remember to remove any leading 0s or special calling codes from the phone number, as these can cause errors during registration.

Note:

  • Make sure to remove any leading 0s or special calling codes.
  • All phone numbers in Argentina (country code “54”) should have a “9” between the country code and area code. The prefix “15” must be removed so the final number will have 13 digits total: +54 9 XXX XXX XXXX
  • Phone numbers in Mexico (country code “52”) need to have “1” after “+52”, even if they’re Nextel numbers.
  • WhatsApp is designed for mobile phones. You can only register a landline on the WhatsApp Business App, where you will receive the verification code through a call to your landline number. Learn more about registering for the WhatsApp Business app here.
  • If you’re not receiving a verification code, try checking your phone’s spam filter or restarting your phone. If you’re still having trouble, try re-registering your phone number after a few hours.

You can link a device using your primary account phone number and a one-time code. Up to four linked devices can be linked without the need to keep your primary phone connected to WhatsApp. You’ll need to log in to WhatsApp on your primary phone every 14 days to keep linked devices connected to your WhatsApp account. For the best experience, update to the latest version of WhatsApp on all devices.

Note: This feature is currently only available on WhatsApp for Windows and WhatsApp Web.

On WhatsApp for Windows or WhatsApp Web

To begin linking a companion device using your phone number, open Whatsapp for Windows or WhatsApp Web on the device you want to link.

  1. Click Link with phone number or Log in with phone number.
  2. Select your country and enter your primary account phone number, then click Next. (Learn how to use international phone number format.)
  3. You’ll see an eight-character code on the screen.

On your primary phone

  1. Tap the Enter code to link new device notification from WhatsApp.
  2. Your primary phone will show the location and name of the device you’re trying to link. If this is correct, tap Confirm.
  3. If prompted, verify your identity.
  • If your device has biometric authentication, follow the on-screen instructions.
  • If you don’t have biometric authentication enabled, you’ll be prompted to enter the PIN you use to unlock your phone.
  1. Enter the eight-character code from your companion device on your primary phone.

Note: If we detect an unrecognized device, we’ll ask you to confirm that you want to link this device. Tap Don’t link if you don’t want to link the device, and tap Link device to link the device.

Alternatively, you can directly link companion devices to your primary phone using the following steps:

  1. Open WhatsApp on your primary iPhone.
  2. Go to the Settings tab, then tap Linked devices > Link device > Link with phone number instead.
  3. If prompted, verify your identity.
  • If your device has biometric authentication, follow the on-screen instructions.
  • If you don’t have biometric authentication enabled, you’ll be prompted to enter the PIN you use to unlock your phone.
  1. Enter the eight-character code from your companion device on your primary phone.

Note: If we detect an unrecognized device, we’ll ask you to confirm that you want to link this device. Tap Don’t link if you don’t want to link the device, and tap Link device to link the device.

How to manage two-step verification settings

Copy link

You can manage two-step verification settings in your WhatsApp account. You have the option to enable or disable this feature or change the PIN. You can also update the email address associated with two-step verification.

[Embedded video omitted]

How to use two-step verification to protect your WhatsApp account

0:00 / 0:57

Turn on two-step verification

  1. Tap WhatsApp Settings or your profile picture.
  2. Tap Account > Two-step verification > Turn on or Set up PIN.
  3. Enter a six-digit PIN of your choice and confirm it.
  4. Provide an email address you can access or tap Skip if you don’t want to add an email address. We recommend adding an email address as this allows you to reset two-step verification, and helps safeguard your account.
  5. Tap Next.
  6. Confirm the email address and tap Save or Done.
  7. Enter the six-digit verification code sent to your email.
  8. Tap Verify.

If you forgot your PIN, you’ll need to wait 7 days before you can reset it. Alternatively, if you’ve previously added your email address, we’ll send reset instructions to your email. We don’t verify this email address, so make sure it’s accurate and accessible to you.

Note:

  • For security purposes, there isn’t an option for us to speed up the 7-day timeframe or disable your account after two-step verification is enabled.
  • You will need an active SIM card in your device to complete the email verification process.

Turn off two-step verification:

  1. Tap WhatsApp Settings or your profile picture.
  2. Tap Account > Two-step verification >Turn off >Turn off.

Change your two-step verification PIN

  1. Tap WhatsApp Settings or your profile picture.
  2. Tap Account > Two-step verification > Change PIN.

Add an email address

  1. Tap WhatsApp Settings or your profile picture.
  2. Tap Account > Email address > Add Email.
  3. Enter email address and tap Next or Verify.
  4. Enter the six-digit verification code sent to your email.
  5. Tap Verify.

Change an email address

  1. Tap WhatsApp Settings or your profile picture.

  2. Tap Account > Email address >

    [Image: Draw (pencil)]

    Change Email > Next.

  3. Enter the six-digit verification code sent to your email.

  4. Tap Verify.

PIN-protected access

A parent PIN prevents others from making account changes without the parent’s permission.

Parents will create a PIN when they first set up a managed account and can change it at any time. Learn more about how to set up a parent-managed account.

How to change a parent PIN

As a parent, you can change your PIN from your device.

  1. Open WhatsApp on your phone.
  2. Tap Settings > Parental controls.
  3. Select your child’s account.
  4. Tap More options > Change parent PIN.
  5. Enter a new 6-digit parent PIN and tap Next.
  6. Confirm the new parent PIN and tap Done.

When a parent PIN is changed, a confirmation alert will show in the activity feed for your child’s account. Learn more about activity alerts in this article.

About parent-managed accounts

On iPhone

Web

Parent-managed accounts are rolling out gradually and may not be available in your region.

Parent-managed accounts allow children under 13 (or older, as required by your country or region) to communicate with their family and friends on WhatsApp with parental supervision.

[Embedded video omitted]

0:00 / 3:00

Parent-managed accounts have built-in parental controls over contacts and privacy settings. By default, only saved contacts can message or call parent-managed accounts. These accounts focus on messaging and calling only, which means they don’t have access to some features.

Parent-managed accounts can’t use:

  • Meta AI
  • Channels
  • Status
  • Chat Lock
  • App Lock
  • Linked devices
  • Location sharing
  • View once messages
  • Disappearing messages in individual chats

Additionally, ads aren’t shown to parent-managed accounts.

Note:

  • When a child with a parent-managed account turns 13 (or older, as required by your country or region), their parents or guardians will receive a notification to transition out of a parent-managed account. At that time, the child’s account will have access to WhatsApp’s features without parental controls. Learn more in this article.
  • If a parent account is deactivated or banned, all linked parent-managed accounts are deactivated until they’re linked to an active parent account.

Privacy settings

By default, only saved contacts can see parent-managed account’s profile photo, about, and when they’re online. Only parents are able to change these settings.

Learn more about privacy settings.

Messaging and groups

By default, only saved contacts can message and call parent-managed accounts and only parents can add them to groups. Messages and group invites from unknown contacts are sent to a requests folder for parent approval.

Personal messages are end-to-end encrypted, which means no one, not even WhatsApp, can read them.

Learn more about messaging and groups.

Note:- Messages and group invites from unknown contacts are sent to the parent account for approval - Groups can include unknown contacts of parent-managed accounts. If you allow a parent-managed account to join a group with unknown contacts, they will be able to see group messages from those members.

Activity and notifications

Parents will be notified about important account activity on managed accounts, like when a contact is added or when there is a new message request.

Learn more about account activity and notifications.

How to protect your account from malware

On iPhone

Copy link

Android

iOS

More

Android

iOS

Malware is a software used with malicious intent to steal information, disrupt, and damage devices. It can be installed on someone’s device without them knowing it.

How to protect your account from malware

To better secure your phone and remove harmful software:

  • Don’t use jailbroken phones.
  • Reset your phone to factory settings.

You may contact your Operating System manufacturer or phone service provider to learn how to remove harmful software.

Best practices to protect your account

Never use unofficial versions of the WhatsApp app

Unofficial apps are fake WhatsApp apps, which means they’re developed by third-parties and violate our Terms of Service. These apps put your privacy, security, and safety at risk. If you’re using them, there’s no guarantee your messages or your data, like your location or the files you share, will be private and secure. Learn more about unofficial apps in this article.

Remove untrusted apps

Apps downloaded from unknown sources might infect your device with malicious software.

Look out for suspicious links

When receiving links, carefully review the content of the message.

Be careful of suspicious files

When receiving a file, you might get an error message. This could mean that there’s an issue with the format or that the file is malicious. Make sure you trust the sender before opening it. Learn more in this article.

How to re-link to an unlinked account

On iPhone

Copy link

Android

iOS

More

Android

iOS

Parent-managed accounts are rolling out gradually and may not be available in your region.

Parent-managed accounts must be linked to a parent or guardian’s account to work. Sometimes, a parent may want to unlink to allow another parent to manage their child’s account.

A child can’t use their parent-managed account until it’s re-linked to a parent or guardian’s account. If a managed account is not linked to another parent’s account within 30 days, it will be automatically deleted.

Note: If a parent account is deactivated or banned, all linked parent-managed accounts are deactivated until they’re linked to an active parent account.

How to unlink

As a parent, you can unlink your child’s account.

  1. Open WhatsApp on your device.
  2. Tap Settings > Parental controls.
  3. Select your child’s account.
  4. Tap More options > Unlink account.

Note: You can also unlink from your child’s device by going to WhatsApp > Settings > Account > Unlink.

How to link to an unlinked account

As parent, you can re-link your child’s account if it becomes unlinked.

  1. Open WhatsApp on your child’s device.
  2. Tap Continue.
  3. Scan the QR code with your phone’s camera and tap the link to be taken to WhatsApp. You can also send an invite link.
  4. Tap Agree and continue.
  5. Verify you’re an adult.
  6. Create a 6-digit parent PIN.
  7. This PIN is required to access and make changes to your child’s privacy settings.
  8. Confirm your parent PIN > Next.
  9. Tap Done and finish the account setup on your child’s device.

Received verification code without requesting it

Copy link

To protect your account, WhatsApp will send you a push notification when someone tries to register a WhatsApp account with your phone number.

When you receive this notification without requesting for a verification code, it means that someone has entered your phone number and requested the registration code. This often happens if another user mistakenly typed your number when trying to enter their own number to register, and can also happen when someone attempts to take over your account.

To keep your account safe, you should never share your WhatsApp verification code with others. If someone is trying to take over your account, they need the SMS verification code sent to your phone number to do so. Without this code, any user attempting to verify your number can’t complete the verification process and can’t use your phone number on WhatsApp. This means you remain in control of your WhatsApp account. Learn more about two-step verification, an optional feature that adds more security to your WhatsApp account.

If you’re the previous owner of the phone number, learn how to learn how to change numbers.

Note:

  • WhatsApp doesn’t have sufficient information to identify the individual who is attempting to verify your WhatsApp account.
  • WhatsApp is end-to-end encrypted and messages are stored on your device, so someone accessing your account on another device can’t read your past conversations.

How to recover a compromised account

Copy link

You should never share your registration code with others, not even friends or family. Please note, WhatsApp can’t deactivate accounts for others due to verification constraints.

If your account is compromised, or if you lost access to your account, follow the steps below to recover your account.

  1. Tap Log back in > Continue.
  2. If prompted, enter your full international phone number and tap Next > Ok.
  3. Enter the 6-digit code you receive via SMS or phone call.

When you re-register your account with the 6-digit code, all devices logged into your WhatsApp account are automatically logged out of your account.

You might be asked to enter a two-step verification PIN. If you don’t know your PIN, in rare cases, someone else using your account might have enabled two-step verification. If you don’t have the PIN, wait 7 days and try again. Whether you know the PIN or not, anyone using your account is automatically logged out of your account after you enter the 6-digit SMS code. Learn more about two-step verification.

If you suspect that your WhatsApp account is compromised and someone else is using it, you should notify family and friends as this person could impersonate you in chats and groups. To help protect your account, WhatsApp will notify you when someone tries to register an account with your phone number.

Once you re-register your account, we recommend you turn on security features to protect your account. It’s also recommended to review the devices linked to your account. You can learn more about security features in this article.

If you report the compromised account you’re trying to recover, we might ban it for violating our Terms of Service and you could lose access to your WhatsApp account or data. We recommend trying to recover your account before reporting it.

WhatsApp can’t block or unblock contacts on your behalf; however, you can block or report a user or content. Learn more about blocking and reporting in this article.

Note:

  • WhatsApp can’t block or unblock contacts on your behalf; however, you can block or report a user or content. Learn more about blocking and reporting in this article.
  • WhatsApp is end-to-end encrypted and messages are stored on your device, so someone re-registering your WhatsApp account on a new device can’t read your past conversations.
  • A WhatsApp account can only be registered with one phone number at a time.
  • It’s not possible to recover an account without a SIM card with the same phone number as your account.
  • In some cases, WhatsApp can automatically verify your phone number without using manual verification methods such as SMS or voice call. Learn more in this article.
  • If you create a backup using Google Account, or iCloud, you might be able to restore your chat history. Learn how to restore messages.
  • WhatsApp can’t provide information about who accessed your account or the time and location it was accessed.
  • If you recently started using a new SIM card, but are still using the WhatsApp account associated with your old phone number, you need to use the change number feature to transfer your WhatsApp account information to your new phone number. If you fail to do this, you could permanently lose access to your WhatsApp account. Learn how to change your phone number in this article.

How to recover a WhatsApp account from a lost or stolen device

On iPhone

Copy link

Android

iOS

More

Android

iOS

If your device is lost or stolen, or if you lost access to your SIM card or phone number, you will need to recover your account through the following steps:

  1. Call your mobile provider as soon as possible and ask them to block your SIM card.
  2. Request a new SIM card with the same phone number.
  3. Activate your new SIM card and insert it into your device.
  4. Open WhatsApp and follow the steps to re-register an account. Refer to the following article: How to register your phone number.

It’s not possible to recover an account without a SIM card with the same phone number as your account. Once you’ve re-registered your WhatsApp account, your lost or stolen device is automatically logged out of your account.

Once you re-register your account, we recommend you turn on security features to protect your account. It’s also recommended to review the devices linked to your account. You can learn more about security features in this article.

Note:

  • WhatsApp can’t deactivate your account for you because there’s no way to verify that you’re the owner of the phone number associated with that account.
  • A WhatsApp account can only be registered with one phone number at a time.
  • If you create a backup using iCloud, you might be able to restore your chat history. Learn how to restore messages.
  • WhatsApp can’t help you locate your phone. Remote WhatsApp deactivation from another device is not possible.
  • It’s not possible to log out of your WhatsApp account using WhatsApp web or desktop.

How to register your phone number

Copy link

Android

iOS

More

Android

iOS

To activate your WhatsApp Account, you must register an active phone number for verification. We will send you a registration code to confirm that you own the phone number you want to use on WhatsApp. You must be able to receive the registration code through SMS or phone call. The registration code is unique and changes each time you register a new phone number or device.

If you’re logging in to your existing WhatsApp account using your phone number, you can get the verification code through email. This is possible if you’ve added your email address to your account in your WhatsApp settings, during your initial registration, or two-step verification setup.

Registration requirements

  • You can only register a phone number you own.
  • You must be able to receive phone calls and SMS to the phone number you are trying to register.
  • Make sure you’re using the latest version of WhatsApp on your phone.
  • You must have any call-blocking settings, apps or task killers disabled.
  • You must have a working internet connection through mobile data or Wi-Fi. If you’re roaming or have a bad connection, registration may not work. Try opening a web page to make sure.
  • Don’t use an unsupported device to register, such as an iPad.
  • Make sure your device isn’t jailbroken.
  • If you want to use both WhatsApp Business and WhatsApp, you’ll need to use a unique phone number for each app.
  • You must use a supported phone number. Unsupported phone numbers include: VoIP, toll-free numbers, paid premium numbers, universal access numbers (UAN), and landlines (landlines are only supported on the WhatsApp Business app).

Register your phone number

You can register your phone number with an SMS or phone call. Depending on your carrier, you might receive charges for SMS and phone calls.

  1. Open WhatsApp.
  2. Tap Agree and continue to accept the WhatsApp Terms of Service.
  3. Tap Allow if you want to receive notifications for calls and messages.
  4. Select your country from the dropdown and enter your phone number in full international format.
  5. You’ll receive a 6-digit registration code by SMS. Enter the 6-digit code to complete registration.

If you don’t receive a code, tap Didn’t receive a code? and select SMS or Phone call to receive a new code. Wait for the progress bar to finish before you retry registration. The wait time can vary, but usually takes a few minutes. If it’s taking more than a few minutes, or if you still have issues registering your phone number, try these troubleshooting tips.

After registering your phone number, you’ll be asked to set up your account. Follow the steps on your device to restore an existing WhatsApp account or set up a new account.

Note:

  • By entering your phone number, you authorize your wireless carrier to share data from your account and wireless device to WhatsApp or its service providers for phone number verification and fraud prevention purposes. To learn more about the data we collect and how we use it, view our Privacy Policy
  • Don’t guess the registration code, or you’ll be locked out for a period of time.

Secure your account with passkey

After registering your phone number and setting up your profile, you can create a passkey to help protect your account. With a passkey, you can use your fingerprint, face, or screen lock to verify your identity. Learn how to create a passkey.

Add account to Accounts Center

If you have a Facebook or Instagram account, you can link your accounts by adding your Whatsapp account to the Accounts Center. Learn more about WhatsApp in Accounts Center.

To activate your WhatsApp Account, you must register an active phone number for verification. We will send you a registration code to confirm that you own the phone number you want to use on WhatsApp. You must be able to receive the registration code through SMS or phone call. The registration code is unique and changes each time you register a new phone number or device.

If you’re logging in to your existing WhatsApp account using your phone number, you can get the verification code through email. This is possible if you’ve added your email address to your account in your WhatsApp settings, during your initial registration, or two-step verification setup.

Registration requirements

  • You can only register a phone number you own.
  • You must be able to receive phone calls and SMS to the phone number you are trying to register.
  • Make sure you’re using the latest version of WhatsApp on your phone.
  • You must have any call-blocking settings, apps or task killers disabled.
  • You must have a working internet connection through mobile data or Wi-Fi. If you’re roaming or have a bad connection, registration might not work. Try opening a web page to make sure.
  • Don’t use an unsupported device to register, such as an iPad.
  • Make sure your device isn’t jailbroken.
  • If you want to use both WhatsApp Business and WhatsApp, you’ll need to use a unique phone number for each app.
  • You must use a supported phone number. Unsupported phone numbers include: VoIP, toll-free numbers, paid premium numbers, universal access numbers (UAN), and landlines (landlines are only supported on the WhatsApp Business app).

Register your phone number

You can register your phone number with an SMS or phone call. Depending on your carrier, you might receive charges for SMS and phone calls.

  1. Open WhatsApp.
  2. Tap Agree and continue to accept the WhatsApp Terms of Service.
  3. Select your country from the dropdown and enter your phone number in full international format.
  4. Tap Next.
  5. You’ll receive a 6-digit registration code by SMS. Enter the 6-digit code to complete registration.

If you don’t receive a code, tap Didn’t receive a code? and select SMS or Phone call to receive a new code. Wait for the progress bar to finish before you retry registration. The wait time can vary, but usually takes a few minutes. If it’s taking more than a few minutes, or if you still have issues registering your phone number, try these troubleshooting tips.

After registering your phone number, you’ll be asked to set up your account. Follow the steps on your device to restore an existing WhatsApp account or set up a new account.

Note:

  • By entering your phone number, you authorize your wireless carrier to share data from your account and wireless device to WhatsApp or its service providers for phone number verification and fraud prevention purposes. To learn more about the data we collect and how we use it, view our Privacy Policy
  • Don’t guess the registration code, or you’ll be locked out for a period of time.

Secure your account with passkey

After registering your phone number and setting up your profile, you can create a passkey to help protect your account. With a passkey, you can use your fingerprint, face, or screen lock to verify your identity. Learn how to create a passkey.

Add account to Accounts Center

If you have a Facebook or Instagram account, you can link your accounts by adding your Whatsapp account to the Accounts Center. Learn more about WhatsApp in Accounts Center.

About registration and two-step verification

Copy link

When you create a WhatsApp account, you’ll see two different screens:

  • Registration: This screen appears when you’re creating a new account or re-registering your existing account. To confirm that you own the phone number, you’ll be prompted to enter a 6-digit registration code sent to you via SMS or phone call.
    • Note: You can get a registration code through email if you are re-registering and have previously set up two-step verification with an email address. Verifying your phone number with a registration code is the only way you can activate your account, and you must be able to receive the code on your phone. Learn how to register your phone number in this article.
  • Two-step verification: This screen appears after you successfully register your phone number on WhatsApp. Two-step verification (2FA) is an optional feature that adds more security to your WhatsApp account. When enabling this feature, you create and confirm a unique PIN that’s required to access your account. The two-step verification PIN is different from the 6-digit registration code you receive via SMS or phone call. For security purposes, when you re-register an existing account, there may be a delay before you can turn on two-step verification. You can learn more about two-step verification in this article.

Remember: Never share your 6-digit registration code or two-step verification PIN with anyone.

If you didn’t enable two-step verification, but are prompted to enter a PIN, the previous owner of the phone number might have enabled it. In this case, you’ll need to wait 7 days before resetting the PIN to access your account.

If you forgot your PIN and you’ve successfully registered your phone number on WhatsApp, tap Forgot PIN? to create a new one. You can manage your two-step verification PIN settings at any time by going to your WhatsApp settings > Account > Two-Step Verification.

Note: After you successfully register your phone number on WhatsApp, anyone who might be using your account is automatically logged out and your account is protected.

Note: In some cases, WhatsApp can automatically verify your phone number. Find out more.

You can use the request account information feature to request a report of your WhatsApp account information and settings. Account information reports don’t include your personal messages or information about channels or ads.

Note: You can’t request account info on WhatsApp for Windows or Mac. You must switch to your primary device or WhatsApp Web.

Request report

  1. Tap WhatsApp Settings or your profile picture, then tap Account > Request Account Info.
  2. Tap Request Account Report. The screen will update to state Request Sent.

Your report will typically be available three days after the date you requested it. You can refer to the Ready by date while waiting for your report.

Parents and guardians

Depending on where you live, parents and guardians may have certain rights related to their minor’s data, for example:

  • The right to access, delete, or correct data, with some exceptions (for example, when we need to protect the safety, security or rights of others).
  • To provide parental or guardian consent on behalf of their minor.

If you are a parent or guardian of a WhatsApp user who is a minor, and you’d like to make a data privacy inquiry or request, please contact us through our privacy form.

Create reports automatically

You can request to automatically create a report every month.

  1. Tap WhatsApp Settings or your profile picture, then tap Account > Request Account Info.
  2. Under Account Information, toggle on Create Reports Automatically.

This will create a new report every month until you choose to turn off automatic reports.

Turn off automatic reports

  1. Tap WhatsApp Settings or your profile picture, then tap Account > Request Account Info.
  2. Under Account Information, toggle off Create Reports Automatically.

When you turn off automatic reports, you won’t receive a new report every month.

Note:

  • Once you request a report, you can’t undo or cancel your pending request.
  • If you change your phone number or delete your account, your pending request will be voided and you’ll have to request another report.
  • If you uninstall WhatsApp, automatic reports are not created and you’ll need to turn automatic reports on.

Download and export report

When the report is available to download, you’ll receive a WhatsApp notification on your device, stating “Your Account Info Report is now available”. The Request Account Info screen in WhatsApp will tell you the amount of time you have to download the report before it’s deleted from our servers. Because this report contains your information, you should be careful about storing, sending, or uploading it to any other services.

  1. Tap WhatsApp Settings or your profile picture, then tap Account > Request Account Info.
  2. Tap Download report. A ZIP file will be downloaded to your phone, which includes HTML and JSON files.
  3. Once the file is downloaded, tap Export report > Export or Export Report. You’ll be unable to view the downloaded report within WhatsApp.
  4. In the share tray that appears, tap the external app you want to export your report to. For example, you can email a copy of the report to yourself.

After you download the report to your device, you’ll have the option to permanently delete the downloaded copy from your phone by tapping Delete report > Delete or Delete Report on the Request account info screen. Deleting the report won’t delete any of your WhatsApp account information.

Learn how to export your chat history in this article.

  • To export a copy of your personal messages, you can export your chat history.
  • To get information about your channels, you can request a channels report.
  • To get information about ads seen on status or channels, you can request an ads report.

How to reset your two-step verification PIN

Copy link

Two-step verification is an optional feature that adds more security to your WhatsApp account. You can learn more about two-step verification in this help article.

You can reset your two-step verification PIN anytime in your WhatsApp settings, or when re-registering your WhatsApp account using your email address or an SMS OTP. You need a stable Internet connection and an active SIM card to reset your two-step verification PIN.

Keep in mind, deleting or reinstalling WhatsApp won’t disable or reset the PIN for two-step verification.

Reset PIN in Settings

If you forgot your PIN, you can reset it in your WhatsApp Settings > Account > Two-step verification > Change PIN.

Reset PIN during re-registration with an email address

If you provided an email address when you set up two-step verification or added it in your WhatsApp Settings, you can reset the PIN immediately by requesting a reset link.

To reset the PIN:

  1. Open WhatsApp > tap Forgot PIN? > Send Email. A reset link will be sent to the email address you provided.
  2. In the email, follow the reset link and tap Confirm.
  3. Open WhatsApp > tap Forgot PIN? > Reset.

Reset PIN during re-registration with SMS OTP

If you received your 6-digit registration code via email when registering your account, you can reset your PIN with an SMS OTP.

  1. Open WhatsApp > tap Forgot PIN? > tap Send code.
  2. Enter the SMS OTP.

Reset PIN after 7-day wait period

If you can’t reset your two-step verification PIN, you’ll need to wait 7 days to reset it. You may not be able to reset your PIN right away if:

  • You didn’t provide an email address to reset the PIN.
  • You forgot or don’t have access to the email address provided to reset the PIN.
  • You received your 6-digit registration code via email when registering your account.
  • You can’t receive your OTP via SMS on the number associated with your account.
  • Someone else might have set up the two-step verification PIN before you started using this phone number.
    • Note: Whether you know this PIN or not, the other individual is automatically logged out of your account once you’ve entered the 6-digit SMS code.

No one can access your account during the 7-day wait period, which begins from the last time your account successfully connected to WhatsApp.

After the 7-day period, you can access your account by tapping Forgot PIN? > Reset Account.

Note: For security purposes, there isn’t an option for us to speed up the 7-day timeframe or disable your account after two-step verification is enabled. The two-step verification PIN is different from the 6-digit registration code you receive via SMS or phone call.

About restricted accounts

Copy link

If you received the in-app message “Your account is restricted right now” or “Your account may be restricted soon,” you don’t need to take any action to remove the account restriction. The restriction automatically ends once the allocated time passes and you’ll receive a notification in WhatsApp when it ends.

To check the time remaining in your restriction, tap New Chat, then select a contact that you’ve never chatted with before. The pop-up shows the time remaining if your account is still restricted. Any user engaging in spam, automated, or bulk messaging could have their account banned. Learn how to use WhatsApp responsibly in this article.

When your account is restricted, recent activity on your account might be showing signs of engaging in spam, automated, or bulk messaging, which violates our Terms of Service. You can continue to communicate with contacts and groups you’ve exchanged chats or calls with previously. However, you can’t start chats or calls with new contacts, create new groups, add new members to groups, or use linked devices. You may also be logged out of some companion devices.
