Parent-managed accounts are rolling out gradually and may not be available in your region.

Parents or guardians can view and receive timely notifications about their child’s activity on a parent-managed account.

  • View activity: Parents can easily see updates about their child’s activity in parental controls, such as when their child adds a new contact or if a group they’re in grows in size.
  • Receive and prioritize notifications: Parents will receive notifications about important activity, like when their child receives a message request from an unknown contact. They can customize the notifications they receive about other activities, such as when their child leaves a group.

Note: Personal messages are end-to-end encrypted, which means no one, not even the parent or WhatsApp, can read them.

View activity

As a parent, you can view your child’s activity from your phone.

  1. Open WhatsApp on your phone.
  2. Tap Settings > Parental controls.
  3. Select your child’s account to view their activity.

Note: You can also view your child’s activity from their phone by going to WhatsApp > Settings > Parental controls and entering your parent PIN.

Receive and prioritize notifications

Parents can choose what types of notifications they receive about their child’s activity. Notifications for critical alerts are always turned on.

Notification types include:

  • Critical alerts: When a contact is added, blocked or reported.
  • Chats and contacts: When a new chat request is received or when a chat or contact is deleted.
  • Groups: When a group chat is created, joined or exited.
  • Disappearing messages: When disappearing messages are turned on in a group chat.
  • Disappearing messages: When disappearing messages are turned on in a group chat
  • Account updates: When their child’s name or profile picture is changed.

As a parent, you can turn notifications on or off:

  1. Open WhatsApp on your phone.
  2. Tap Settings > Parental controls.
  3. Select your child’s account.
  4. Tap More options > Manage notifications.
  5. Find the notification type and toggle on or off.

Seeing “You have been logged out for your account security”

On iPhone

Copy link

Android

iOS

More

Android

iOS

When you open WhatsApp and see “You have been logged out for your account security”, this means that someone might be trying to register a WhatsApp account with your phone number.

To better secure your account and log back in, simply re-register your phone number:

  1. Enter your phone number:
  • Choose your country from the drop-down list. This will automatically fill your country code below the country.
  • Enter your phone number in the box on the right of the country code. Don’t put any zeros before your phone number.
  1. Tap Next to request a code.
  2. A pop up will appear asking you to confirm if the number you entered is correct, tap Yes.
  3. You can automatically verify with a SMS or a phone call. Enter the 6 digit code given to you.

If the automatic verification process did not go through:

  • Choose Didn’t receive a verification code. You can choose to get the verification code from SMS or Voice call > Continue and follow the onscreen instructions.
  • Wait for the timer to finish and retry. This may take up to 10 minutes.
  • Don’t guess the code, or you will be locked out for a period of time.

Protect your WhatsApp account

  • Never share your 6-digit registration code or two-step verification PIN with others.
  • Enable two-step verification and provide an email address in case you forget your PIN.
  • Set a voicemail password on your phone that’s difficult to guess to prevent anyone from accessing your voicemail.
  • Check your linked devices regularly. Go to WhatsApp >Settings > Linked Devices.
  • To remove a linked device, tap the device > Log Out > Log out.
  • Set a device code and be aware of who has physical access to your phone. Someone who has physical access to your phone could use your WhatsApp account without your permission.

We recommend you share this advice with friends and family to help secure their WhatsApp accounts.

Beware of suspicious emails or messages

Be careful if you receive a message or an email asking you to share or reset your two-step verification PIN or registration code. If you didn’t request this, don’t click on the link. Someone could be trying to access your phone number on WhatsApp.

Seeing “Your phone number was registered with WhatsApp on a new device”

Copy link

If someone tries to use your phone number to register a WhatsApp account on their device, you can use your phone to log them out and recover access to your WhatsApp account. All other devices will be logged out and the account will be returned to you.

How to recover your account

If you see the message “Your phone number was registered with WhatsApp on a new device,” tap Log back in > Continue. If prompted, enter your phone number and tap Next > Ok.

For extra security, turn on two-step verification, which will require a PIN when registering your phone number with WhatsApp again. Learn more about two-step verification in this article.

For more information about account recovery, read this article.

About seeing your phone number already in WhatsApp

Copy link

All WhatsApp accounts are tied to mobile phone numbers. Since it’s common for phone numbers to be recycled by mobile providers, it’s possible that the previous owner of your current phone number used WhatsApp.

If the WhatsApp account of the previous owner of your phone number hasn’t been deleted:

  • You and your contacts may see your phone number in WhatsApp before you activate a new account.
  • You may see someone else’s profile photo and About section attached to your phone number.

There’s no need to worry. This only means that the previous account wasn’t deleted, so old information still exists in the system. This does not mean that the previous owner of the phone number has access to your WhatsApp account. Your conversations and other WhatsApp data are secure. Even if a number was previously owned by someone else, only the user with an active SIM card for that number can access and register to WhatsApp.

To update the account with your information, start by completing the verification process. Once that’s complete, you can enter your profile information. We recommend that you leave all groups that your current account number is tied to and block all unknown contacts.

To help eliminate confusion with recycled phone numbers, we monitor account inactivity. A recycled number is identified when an account is unused for 45 days, then reactivated on a new mobile device. If that’s the case, we’ll remove the old account data tied to the phone number, like the profile photo and About section.

Notes:

  • If the previous owner of your phone number set up two-step verification, you may need to reset the pin.
  • If you don’t have access to an active SIM card for the number you are trying to verify, you will not be able to activate the number. You have to be able to receive an SMS or voice call on the number you want to activate. No exceptions will be made.
  • The same verification process is used for WhatsApp Business accounts.

Parent-managed accounts are rolling out gradually and may not be available in your region.

Parent-managed accounts are available to users under 13 years old (or under the minimum age required in their country or region to use WhatsApp) and must be set up by a parent or guardian 18 years old or older.

Parent-managed accounts require the latest version of WhatsApp for iPhone or Android.

Download WhatsApp on your child’s phone

As a parent, you can download WhatsApp and set up a parent-managed account for your child.

  1. Download WhatsApp Messenger in the Google Play Store or Apple App Store on your child’s device.
  2. Choose your language and tap Agree and continue.
  3. Tap More options and select Create a parent-managed account.
  4. Register and verify your child’s phone number.
  5. Enter your child’s birthday and confirm their age.
  • Note: Depending on legal requirements where you live, app stores from Apple or Google may share your child’s age range with us instead. If you want to learn more or think the wrong age range was shared with us, you can visit the Apple or Google help centers, or check their device settings.
  1. Tap Continue to link to a parent’s account.

Link to your child’s account from your phone.

  1. Scan the QR code displayed on your child’s device with your phone’s camera and tap the link to be taken to WhatsApp.
  • Note: If you don’t already have an existing WhatsApp account, you’ll be asked to download WhatsApp Messenger in the Google Play Store or App Store.
  1. Tap Agree and continue.
  2. Verify you’re an adult.
  3. Create a 6-digit parent PIN.
  • This PIN is required to access and make changes to your child’s privacy settings and should not be shared with your child.
  1. Confirm your parent PIN > Next.
  2. Tap Done and finish account setup on your child’s device.

Finish account setup on your child’s device

  1. Enter your parent PIN.
  2. Tap Continue.

Your child’s managed account is now set up. They’ll be able to enter their name and profile photo.

How to switch accounts on WhatsApp

On iPhone

Copy link

Android

iOS

Web

Mac

Windows

More

Android

iOS

Web

Mac

Windows

Note: Account switching isn’t currently available on the WhatsApp Business app.

WhatsApp’s multiple account feature allows you to have two different accounts on a single mobile device. To register a second account on WhatsApp, you will need to have a separate phone number. Once both accounts are registered, you can easily switch between them on the same device.

Your active account is the one you’re currently logged into, while your idle account is the one you’re not currently using. Even when your account isn’t being used, you will still get alerts about messages and phone calls. To see the content, just switch to the appropriate account.

For each account, you have the ability to customize your accounts by setting unique pictures, about fields, notification settings, and privacy settings.

Note:

  • Secondary accounts can only be created from your primary mobile device.
  • You can pair a companion device to your secondary account.
  • Only mobile companion devices can switch between accounts.

Create a second account

  1. Tap Settings.

  2. Next to your name, tap

    [Image: Add (plus sign in circle)]

    Add Account.

  3. Tap Agree and Continue to agree to the Terms of Service and Privacy Policy.

  4. Select your country and enter your phone number in international phone number format.

    • Tap Continue to get your code.
    • Tap Verify another way to get your code by text or phone call.

  5. Enter your 6-digit code.

  6. Enter your name and tap Next.

    • You can add a profile photo and fill in the about field.
    • Tap Skip to create your profile later.

Note: Some features, such as connecting a payment method, are not available for secondary accounts on iOS at this time. We recommend keeping WhatsApp updated on your device so you can get all features as soon as they’re available.

Switch account

  1. Tap Settings.

  2. Next to your profile, tap

    [Image: More (down chevron)]

    then tap the other account.

Note:

  • This feature supports a maximum of two accounts.
  • Users can see activity on idle accounts. You will need to switch accounts in order to see the content.

Can’t add second account

If you can’t add a second WhatsApp account, try these troubleshooting steps:

  • Restart your phone.
  • Switch between Wi-Fi and cellular data.
  • Make sure you have the latest version of WhatsApp installed. Learn how to manually update WhatsApp.

Respond to notifications on idle accounts

You will receive notifications for new messages and calls on your idle account. You must switch accounts to access the content.

  1. When someone calls your idle account, you will get a push notification.
  • Tap Ignore to ignore the call.
  • Tap Switch Accounts to switch to your idle account.
  1. Select Answer or Decline the call.

Remove account

  1. Tap Settings > Account > Remove account.
  • Tap Go to chat backup to back up chat history.
  1. Confirm the number and tap Remove.

Note:

  • If you remove an account, it will only be removed from the device you’re currently using.
  • If you remove an account from your primary device, your companion devices will be logged out from that account after 14 days.
  • Your WhatsApp groups and channels won’t be deleted by removing this account from your device.
  • You’ll lose any messages or data not backed up. Learn more about backing up your data.

Delete account

  1. Tap Settings > Account > Delete account.
    • Tap Change number to change your account number.
  2. Enter your country code and phone number and tap Delete account.
  3. Select the reason for deleting the account and tap Delete account > Delete account.

Note:

  • If you delete an account the account will be deleted from WhatsApp and all your devices.
  • Your message history will be erased.
  • You will be removed from all your WhatsApp groups.
  • Your Google Account backup will be deleted.
  • Any channels you created will be deleted.

About temporarily banned accounts

Copy link

If you received a “Temporarily banned” in-app message, it could mean you’re using an unofficial version of WhatsApp or harvesting information, known as scraping.

Switch to the official app or stop engaging in scraping after being temporarily banned. If you don’t, your account might be permanently banned from using WhatsApp.

About unofficial apps

Unofficial apps are fake WhatsApp apps, developed by third-parties which violate our Terms of Service. We don’t support these apps because we can’t validate their security practices. Learn more about unofficial apps in this article.

About scraping

Scraping is the automated extraction of information, both targeted and at scale, for any unpermitted purposes. Scrapers might attempt to search for and save users’ information. This can include phone numbers, user profile pictures, and statuses from the WhatsApp platform. Acquiring user information through scraping violates our Terms of Service. Learn more about scraping in this article.

About the official WhatsApp chat account

Copy link

You can hear directly from us with our official WhatsApp chat account. In this chat, we’ll share what’s new, helpful tips, and information to help you make the most out of WhatsApp.

Note:

  • You can’t call or send a message to WhatsApp on this chat.
  • This feature might not be available in your area yet.

How can you tell this is an official WhatsApp account?

  • The official WhatsApp chat is marked with

    [Image: Wa Verified Checkmark (blue sticker with white checkmark)]

    and has the description “Official WhatsApp Account”.

  • When you receive a chat from the WhatsApp official channel you’ll see this system message: “This is an official account of WhatsApp. Tap to learn more”.

  • You can’t message this chat. We won’t ask you to share any personal information.

If you receive a chat message from an account without

[Image: Wa Verified Checkmark (blue sticker with white checkmark)]

claiming to be WhatsApp, it’s a scam. You should never reply to anyone pretending to be WhatsApp. Please report and block this number.

Does WhatsApp have any other official chat accounts?

WhatsApp has three other official chat accounts:

  • WhatsApp Support to assist you when you need help with your account.
  • WhatsApp Surveys to get feedback to help improve WhatsApp.
  • WhatsApp Business to share news, tips, and information that helps you make the most of the WhatsApp Business app.

Learn how to identify accounts for WhatsApp support in this article and WhatsApp Surveys in this article. Learn more about the official WhatsApp Business in this article.

Choose to not receive messages about new features and tips

You have control over the messages you receive from WhatsApp about new features, tips, and information to help you make the most out of WhatsApp. If you’d prefer not to hear from WhatsApp, you can archive or block this chat to stop receiving these types of messages at any time. You always have the option to unblock the chat to receive messages again in the future. In some rare cases, we might send you messages about important and timely information related to your account, even if you block the chat.

Learn how to block and report someone in this article.

If you have additional questions and would like to contact WhatsApp, open WhatsApp Settings then tap or click Help > Contact Us.

How to transfer your WhatsApp account to a new phone

On iPhone

Copy link

Android

iOS

More

Android

iOS

You can transfer your WhatsApp account to a new phone. If you have have your old phone and your new phone with you, and have both devices connected to the Internet, you can begin the transfer by following these steps on your new phone:

To begin the transfer, follow these steps on your new phone:

  1. Download WhatsApp and tap Agree & Continue to agree to WhatsApp’s Privacy Policy and Terms of Service.
  2. Enter your phone number and tap Next > Continue.
  3. If prompted, connect to your local Wi-Fi network.
  4. Use your old phone’s camera to scan the QR code that’s displayed on your new phone.
  • Note: Don’t close the app until the transfer is complete.
  • Follow the Start Transfer prompts, then tap Done > OK.
  1. Enter your two-factor authentication PIN, if you have one.
  2. Confirm your profile information.
  3. Tap Next on the Transfer complete screen. You’ll be redirected to the Chats tab.

Your chats will now be restored from your old phone to your new phone.

Note:

  • If you will use the same phone number on your new phone, transfer your SIM card to your new device and log in to WhatsApp using your old number. When you log in to your new phone, you will be logged out on your old phone as soon as re-registration is complete.
  • If you will use a new phone number and want to transfer your chat history, you must first change numbers on your old phone before transferring your account. If you register with a new number on a new phone without completing this step, you’ll lose your chat history.
  • If you want to log into your old WhatsApp account on your new phone but no longer have access to your old phone number and device, you will need to recover your account first.

Web

Strict account settings is an advanced security feature that turns on privacy and security controls to help protect accounts from sophisticated cyber attacks.

This feature is built for the very few users who may be the target of such attacks. Therefore, you should only turn this on if you think you may be a target of a sophisticated cyber campaign. Most people are not targeted by such attacks.

What is Strict account settings?

Strict account settings is an optional, lockdown-style security feature that, when enabled, reduces your vulnerability to cyber attack by limiting functionality. Your account is locked to more private settings and your chats with others outside your contacts will have limitations.

How Strict account settings protects your account

Here’s how Strict account settings protects your account and changes your WhatsApp experience:

  • Account security: Two-step verification is turned on. Security notifications are turned on and locked. End-to-end encrypted backups are encouraged for users with backups enabled.
  • Messaging and media: Attachments and media from unknown senders are blocked. Link previews are turned off. Blocking high volumes of unknown account messages is turned on.
  • Calls: Calls from unknown numbers are silenced. Your IP address is also hidden during calls.
  • Profile and presence: Your Last seen and online, Profile photo, About details, and links on your profile are locked to contacts only or to your pre-established, more-selective list of people.
  • Groups: Only known contacts or a pre-established, more-selective list of people can add you to groups.

Turn Strict account settings on or off

  1. Tap Settings > Privacy > Advanced.
  2. Tap to turn Strict account settings on or off.

You can only turn on and off Strict account settings from your primary device. When Strict account settings is enabled, you can view all your locked settings by tapping Settings > Privacy > Advanced > Strict account settings > View locked settings.

Your WhatsApp account can only be verified with one registered phone number. It’s not possible to add a second phone number to your account. There is no option to have a verified WhatsApp account with two different phone numbers.

WhatsApp’s multiple account feature allows you to have two different accounts on a single mobile device. To register a second account on WhatsApp, you will need to have a separate phone number. Once both accounts are registered, you can easily switch between them on the same device. Learn more about how to switch accounts on WhatsApp.

You can switch your WhatsApp account to a new phone without receiving an SMS code.

If your phone number is eligible, you can verify it using your old device. WhatsApp will send a push notification to the old device that will provide the 6-digit code to enter on your new device.

If you don’t choose this option, you’ll be prompted to verify your phone number via SMS.

If you attempt to frequently switch your WhatsApp account between different devices, at a certain point, you may be blocked from re-verifying your account. Please don’t repeatedly switch between different devices and numbers.

How to verify your number by SMS

Copy link

When you register your account on WhatsApp, you can verify your phone number by SMS.

Verify by SMS when registering

  1. Select your language.
  2. Tap Agree and continue to accept the Terms of Service.
  3. Select your country and enter your phone number.
  4. Tap Continue.
    • If prompted tap Allow to let WhatsApp to send a one-time SMS message to verify your account. Carrier charges may apply.
  5. WhatsApp will automatically verify your account.
  6. Follow the rest of the steps to complete registration.

Security check

In some cases, you might be asked to complete an additional SMS verification as a security precaution. To continue, you must send an SMS code to WhatsApp to verify your identity.

If prompted to verify by SMS:

  1. Tap Send code.
  2. Tap the send icon to send the pre-written message to WhatsApp.
    • Carrier charges may apply.
  3. WhatsApp will send you an SMS to automatically verify your account.
  4. Follow the rest of the steps to complete registration.

If you have issues registering, try these troubleshooting tips.

Note:

  • You can only register a phone number you own.
  • You must be able to receive and send SMS messages to the phone number you are trying to register.

How to view and manage privacy settings for parent-managed account

On iPhone

Copy link

Android

iOS

More

Android

iOS

Parent-managed accounts are rolling out gradually and may not be available in your region.

Parents or guardians can control the Privacy settings for their child’s parent-managed account.

By default, privacy settings on managed accounts are set to:

  • Only saved contacts can see their profile photo, about, and when they’re online.
  • Only saved contacts can message or call them.
  • Only parents can add them to groups. They cannot create groups of their own.

How to change privacy settings

As a parent, you can access and make changes to your child’s privacy settings by using your parent PIN.

  1. Go to your child’s phone and open WhatsApp.
  2. Tap Settings > Privacy.
  3. Enter your parent PIN.
  4. Tap the privacy setting you want to change.
  5. Select Everyone, (Managed account’s) contacts, (Managed account’s) contacts except…, Selected contacts…, or Nobody, based on the setting.

Privacy setting options

  • Everyone: All users on WhatApp.
  • (Managed account’s) contacts: All WhatsApp users saved to your child’s contacts.
  • (Managed account’s) contacts except: All WhatsApp users saved to your child’s contacts except ones you choose to exclude.
  • (Managed account’s) Selected contacts: Only WhatsApp users saved to your child’s contacts that you’ve selected.
  • Nobody: No WhatsApp users.

Additional privacy settings

  • Learn more about Read receipts settings in this article.
  • Learn how to silence unknown callers in this article.

About WhatsApp in Accounts Center

On iPhone

Copy link

Android

iOS

Web

More

Android

iOS

Web

Your Accounts Center will become your Meta Account. We are gradually rolling out this update so you may see either Accounts Center or Meta Account settings as the place to manage your settings across apps. Learn more About Meta Accounts.

WhatsApp can be added optionally and will not be in a Meta Account unless you previously added it to your Accounts Center or choose to add it to your Meta Account when it’s available to you.

Accounts Center is a place where you can centrally manage account settings and connected experiences across your Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp and Meta accounts. To add your WhatsApp account to Accounts Center and enable connected experiences, you’ll need to add it with an existing Facebook or Instagram account.

Adding your WhatsApp account to Accounts Center is completely optional. You can choose to add or remove accounts from an Accounts Center at any time. Learn about adding or removing WhatsApp in Accounts Center in this article.

Even if you choose to add your WhatsApp account to Accounts Center, your personal messages and calls are protected with end-to-end encryption, meaning no one outside of the chat, not even WhatsApp or Meta, can read, listen to, or share them. We don’t share your WhatsApp contact lists with any other Meta Company.

By adding your WhatsApp account to Accounts Center, you can:

  • Use experiences that work across our apps, like the ability to easily share your Status created on WhatsApp to Stories on Facebook or Instagram or the option to promote your Instagram and Facebook accounts on your WhatsApp profile with verified profile links.
  • Manage some account settings centrally, like your birthday, ad preferences, and the ability to add or remove accounts.
  • Import your WhatsApp profile picture from Facebook or Instagram.

You can find Accounts Center in the app settings on Facebook, Messenger, Instagram or from your WhatsApp account. You can view which accounts are in the same Accounts Center by going to your WhatsApp Settings > Accounts Center. From there, you can remove or add accounts. Adding WhatsApp to Accounts Center means WhatsApp and Meta will share information to provide these experiences, which we explain in this article.

Information used by Meta AI

Note: This feature is currently only available in limited countries and might not be available to you yet, even if other users in your country have access.

To provide you with more relevant responses, Meta AI may use information from across accounts you’ve added in Accounts Center, such as Facebook or Instagram, and things like your interests, age, location, and profiles. This information may also be used to improve AI at Meta. Learn more in this article.

About ads in WhatsApp Status and Channels

Copy link

If you’re only using WhatsApp for personal messaging, you won’t see ads. Ads will appear in Status and Channels, separate from your personal chats and calls.

Ads in WhatsApp Status and Channels are rolling out gradually and may not be available in your region yet.

How WhatsApp protects your personal messages

As always your personal messages, calls, and status updates are end-to-end encrypted and can’t be used to show you ads. End-to-end encryption keeps your personal messages and calls between you and the person you’re communicating with. No one outside of the chat, not even WhatsApp, can see, hear or share them.

WhatsApp collects very limited information about you to operate our Services. We don’t keep logs of who everyone is messaging or calling and don’t track the personal messages people are sending one another for ads. That means we don’t use the following information to show you ads:

  • Your personal messages, calls, and status.
  • Location shared in chats.
  • Your device contacts.
  • Your membership in groups with friends and family.

How WhatsApp decides which ads to show you

When it comes to delivering ads in Status and Channels you might be interested in, WhatsApp uses information including:

  • Basic account information: This includes information you provide such as country code and age (where applicable).
  • Device information: This includes your device information such as device language.
  • General location: This includes your general (not precise) location, like city or country.
  • Status and Channels activity: This includes activity information like channels you follow, content you engage with in channels, and ads you’ve clicked on in Channels or Status.

If you choose to add WhatsApp to an Accounts Center with other Meta Company Product accounts, your ad preferences will apply and information across your accounts will be used for ads. Learn more about WhatsApp in Accounts Center.

Personal data stays with WhatsApp

We anonymize your information: WhatsApp uses Meta’s technology to show people ads. We don’t share personal information (like phone number) with Meta, so Meta cannot identify you and is only able to suggest ads that may appeal to people who share broad characteristics such as a general area.

You decide whether to share personal information with Meta for ads: Access to your WhatsApp personal information is restricted, so Meta will not use it for ads on WhatsApp unless you choose to use optional features that work across Meta Company Products, like Accounts Center.

Learn more about what information WhatsApp and Meta share through Accounts Center.

You control your ads experience

We clearly label ads in Status and Channels and make it easy for you to understand why specific ads are shown and what kinds of information are used.

  • See why we’re showing you an ad: Tap or click “Why you’re seeing this ad” to view some of the factors we consider when showing you a certain ad. Like, when an advertiser wants to show their ad to people in the country that matches your phone’s country code.
  • Manage your ad preferences: See a list of all recent ads and advertisers shown to you in Status and Channels and manage what advertisers you want to see ads from. If you use Accounts Center, you’ll manage your ad preferences (along with other settings) in Accounts Center.
  • Control the ads you see: If you want to hide or report an ad, you will be able to provide that feedback.

Learn more about ads and privacy in our Status and Channels Supplemental Privacy Policy.

On iPhone

Copy link

Android

More

iOS

If you’re only using WhatsApp for personal messaging, you won’t see ads. Ads will appear in Status and Channels, separate from your personal chats and calls.

Ads in WhatsApp Status and Channels are rolling out gradually and may not be available to you yet.

You can give feedback about the ads you see in WhatsApp Status or Channels to make your ad experience more relevant. If you see an ad that isn’t relevant to you, simply share the feedback by telling us you’re not interested.

Tell us about an ad you’re not interested in

If you see an ad you don’t like, there are a few things you can do to remove the ad you see in Status and Channels.

  • For a channels ad:: On the promoted channel, tap the word Ad > Hide ad.

  • For a status ad: From the ad itself, tap

    [Image: More (three horizontal dots)]

    Not interested and then select a reason.

You can also hide all ads from an advertiser when viewing your recent ad activity by tapping the ad or advertiser and then tapping Hide ads from this advertiser. Learn more about viewing your recent ad activity.

Report an ad from WhatsApp Status or Channels

If you think an ad includes problematic content, you can report it.

To report a status ad:

  1. View the ad and tap

    [Image: More (three horizontal dots)]

    Report ad.

  2. Tap Report.

  • Tap View Report to view your active and complete reports.

To report a channels ad:

  1. Below the promoted channel, tap Ad > Report ad.
  2. Tap Report.
  • Tap View Report to view your active and complete reports.

To view your active and complete reports, tap Settings > Help and feedback > Reports.

Report a website accessed from an ad from WhatsApp Status

If you think a website accessed from an ad includes problematic content, you can report it.

To report a website accessed from an ad:

  1. Open the website and tap

    [Image: More (three horizontal dots)]

    Report website.

  2. Select a reason for your report:

  • Misleading content or scam
  • Sexually inappropriate or adult content
  • Excessive or disruptive ads
  • Other
  1. Tap Submit.
  2. Tap Close.

Report a channels ad when logged out

You can report ads when logged out of WhatsApp in the Meta Ad Library.

  1. In your browser, open the Meta Ad Library.

  2. Choose the ad category and search for the ad by keyword or business name.

  3. Find the ad and tap

    [Image: More Options (three horizontal dots)]

    Copy Ad Link to copy the link to your clipboard.

    • Tap Filters to refine your search or clear active filters.

  4. Open the WhatsApp Channel and Promoted Channel EU Legal Reporting Form.

  5. Tap and hold the URL 1 entry field > tap Paste.

  6. Fill in the rest of the form and tap Submit.

Reporting ads that might be problematic helps keep WhatsApp safe. Read more about the standards we have to keep ads safe across all Meta Company Products in the Advertising Standards and on WhatsApp in the WhatsApp Business Messaging Policy.

  • To access your account and settings information, you can request a copy of your account report. Learn how to in this article.
  • To access your channels information, you can request a copy of your channels report. Learn how in this article.

Request an ads report

  1. Tap WhatsApp Settings or your profile picture, then tap Account > Request account info.
  2. Under Ad activity, tap Request ads report. The screen will update to state Request sent.

Your ads report will typically be available three days after the date you requested it. You can refer to the Ready by date while waiting for your ads report.

Parents and guardians

Depending on where you live, parents and guardians may have certain rights related to their minor’s data, for example:

  • The right to access, delete, or correct data, with some exceptions (for example, when we need to protect the safety, security or rights of others).
  • To provide parental or guardian consent on behalf of their minor.

If you are a parent or guardian of a WhatsApp user who is a minor, and you’d like to make a data privacy inquiry or request, please contact us through our privacy form.

Create an ads report automatically

You can request to automatically create an ads report every month.

  1. Tap WhatsApp Settings or your profile picture, then tap Account > Request account info.
  2. Under Ad activity, toggle on Create reports automatically.

This will create a new ads report every month until you choose to turn off automatic reports.

Turn off automatic reports

  1. Tap WhatsApp Settings or your profile picture, then tap Account > Request account info.
  2. Under Ad activity, toggle off Create reports automatically.

When you turn off automatic ads reports, you won’t receive a new ads report every month.

Note:

  • Once you request an ads report, you can’t undo or cancel your pending request.
  • If you change your phone number or delete your account, your pending request will be voided and you’ll have to request another ads report.
  • If you uninstall WhatsApp, an automatic ads report is not created and you’ll need to turn automatic ads reports on.

Download and export report

When the ads report is available to download, you’ll receive a WhatsApp notification, stating “Your Ads report is now available”. The Request account info screen in WhatsApp will tell you the amount of time you have to download the ads report before it’s deleted from our servers. Because this ads report contains your information, you should be careful about storing, sending, or uploading it to any other services.

  1. Tap WhatsApp Settings or your profile picture, then tap Account > Request account info.
  2. Tap Download report. A ZIP file will be downloaded to your phone, which includes HTML and JSON files.
  3. Once the file is downloaded, tap Export ads report. You’ll be unable to view the downloaded report within WhatsApp.
  4. In the share tray that appears, tap the external app you want to export your ads report to. For example, you can email a copy of the ads report to yourself.

After you download the ads report to your phone, you’ll have the option to permanently delete the downloaded copy of the adfs report from your phone by tapping Delete report on the Request account info screen.

Note: Deleting the report won’t delete any of your information relating to your ads activity.

About WhatsApp chats that start from Facebook and Instagram ads

Copy link

When you start a chat with a business after interacting with their ad on Facebook or Instagram, WhatsApp’s parent company Meta receives limited info. This helps improve Meta ads and promotes a safer experience across those apps—for example, by detecting potential scams.

You can either start a chat with the business directly from the ad, or click on any part of the ad and then start a chat with the business from Instagram or Facebook. For instance, if you want to learn more about a business after clicking on their ad, you can visit their Facebook or Instagram profile and begin a chat directly from there.

Note: Meta will receive information if you open a WhatsApp chat with a business within seven days after interacting with their ad.

Your privacy is our priority

  • This icon

    [Image: Single Chevron (right chevron within circle)]

    means Meta may receive limited info. You can tap on this icon

    [Image: Single Chevron (right chevron within circle)]

    to learn more or decide to not chat with the business, so no information is shared.

  • The content of your message and calls isn’t shared by WhatsApp and neither is your name or phone number. Learn more about the privacy and security of messages with businesses.

  • Meta may receive limited information like:

  • Interactions with businesses or business threads (like feedback you submit)

  • Your interactions with a business, such as the number of chats and calls you make with the business, when you browse their products and services, or when you interact with their ordering information and links (including calls to action)

  • Browser interactions from links shared by businesses in WhatsApp, like how long the browser was open.

  • Businesses may also share your activity information with Meta. You can review your Ad settings and choose whether Meta can show you ads on Facebook or Instagram based on your activity information from Ad partners. Learn how to update ad settings.

  • You are in control of the conversation. You can stop chatting with the business or block them at any time. Learn about controls you have when messaging businesses.

Backup and Restore

Back Up or Restore Your Chats

Copy link

If you’re using WhatsApp on your phone, you have the ability to back up and restore your chat history in case you lose your phone or switch to a new one. You can back up your chats at any time or set up regular backups for added convenience.

Backing up your chats

You can back up your chat history using your Google Account on Android devices, or iCloud on iPhone. To avoid the loss of any backups, we recommend backing up your WhatsApp data often. To learn how to back up your chats, read this article.

Restoring your chats

To successfully restore your chats, you need to use the same phone number and Google Account or iCloud account you used to create the backup. We recommend performing a backup before uninstalling WhatsApp or moving to a new device. To learn how to restore your chats, read this article.

Note: Unfortunately, we can’t restore your chats for you because your chat history isn’t stored on our servers.

Transferring your chats

If you don’t want to back up your chats, you can still transfer them between devices. While restoring from a backup can recover all of your chat data, transferring your chats allows you to move your full account information to your new device, including all of your messages and media.

To learn how to transfer your chats between two Android devices or iPhones, read this article.

To learn how to transfer your chats from an Android device to an iPhone, read this article.

To learn how to transfer your chats from an iPhone to an Android device, read this article.

How to back up your chat history

On iPhone

Copy link

Android

iOS

More

Android

iOS

On iPhone, you have two ways to back up your WhatsApp chat history:

  • WhatsApp in-app backup to iCloud: learn more in the article below
  • iPhone backup to iCloud: learn more from Apple’s Help Center

You can choose either option, or use both.

Note:- If you use both options, it will require additional iCloud storage to store both copies of WhatsApp backup. - If you choose to use encrypted backups through WhatsApp in-app backup, it is not possible to use iPhone backup too.

WhatsApp in-app backups to iCloud

You can back up your WhatsApp chat history and media using your iCloud account. Before you get started, check if:

  • You’re using the same phone number and iCloud account that the backup was created on.
  • Your iPhone is updated to the latest iOS.
  • Your available iCloud account and iPhone storage is at least 2.05 times bigger than the size of your backup.

Set up automatic backups

To back up chats to your iCloud account:

  1. Tap WhatsApp Settings or your profile picture.
  2. Tap Chats > Chat backup.
  3. Tap Auto backup and choose your backup frequency.
  • You can choose to include or exclude videos from the backup.

Manually back up your chats at any time

  1. Tap WhatsApp Settings or your profile picture.
  2. Tap Chats > Chat backup > Back up now.

Note:

  • Backups include messages and media sent and received in communities. They also include updates shared over WhatsApp Channels, but they do not include media unless you are the channel admin. In some cases, all previously followed channels may not be included in back-up files. Learn more here.
  • WhatsApp chats and media can only be restored from the last successful backup that occurred on your iPhone.
  • The only way to recover your WhatsApp backup or transfer it to another iPhone is with iCloud.

Create an end-to-end encrypted backup

  1. Tap WhatsApp Settings or your profile picture.
  2. Tap Chats > Chat backup > End-to-end encrypted backup.
  3. Tap Turn on.
  4. Use a passkey, or a 64-digit encryption key instead, or create a password.
  5. Tap Create to create your end-to-end encrypted backup.

Note: Make sure to remember your password or key as it’s the only way to access your backup in the future.

Can’t back up or restore your chat history

On iPhone

Copy link

Android

iOS

More

Android

iOS

Having access to your chats is crucial. We recognize that they contain valuable information and cherished memories, and we understand how distressing it can be to lose them, or accidentally delete them.

Note: Unfortunately, we can’t restore your chats for you because your chat history isn’t stored on our servers.

If your backup gets stuck while uploading or downloading, or you receive any of the following error messages:

  • “WhatsApp seems to be having trouble reading your chat history and will try to recover it. This can take several minutes.”
  • “Unfortunately WhatsApp was unable to recover your chat history. Please delete and reinstall WhatsApp.”
  • “Sorry something went wrong while trying to recover your chat history. Please try again.”
  • “Couldn’t restore your chat history.”
  • “Couldn’t complete backup.”

Try these troubleshooting tips to resolve the issue:

  • Turn your Wi-Fi off and on, try connecting to a different Wi-Fi network, or try using mobile data.- Note: Switching between different Wi-Fi networks can cause the backup to timeout.
  • Check your device has enough storage space to restore or create a backup. To have enough space, your available iCloud account storage must be at least 2.05 times bigger than the size of your backup. Learn how to reduce your backup size here.
  • Check that your iPhone is updated to the latest iOS and WhatsApp version. Learn how to manually update WhatsApp here.
  • Close and reopen WhatsApp.
  • Check that your device’s battery is fully charged or plugged into a power source.
  • Turn iCloud Drive off and back on. Go to iPhone Settings > tap your name > iCloud > iCloud Drive > Sync this iPhone
  • Check that iCloud Drive is turned on for WhatsApp. If it is, turn it off and then back on again. Go to iPhone Settings > tap your name > iCloud > iCloud Drive > Apps Syncing to iCloud Drive > check that WhatsApp is turned on.
  • Check that you’re restoring data from the same phone number and iCloud account that the backup was created on.
  • If you’re restoring an end-to-end encrypted backup, check that you’re using the correct password or 64-digit encryption key. Learn more here.

If none of these troubleshooting tips work:

  • Sign out of iCloud entirely and restart your iPhone by turning it off and on. Then, sign back into iCloud and attempt to back up or restore again.
  • If backing up continues to fail or get stuck, try deleting your backup from iCloud and starting a new one. Your chats won’t be deleted as long as you don’t uninstall and reinstall WhatsApp.

Resolving corrupted backups

If you’ve tried all the recommended troubleshooting steps and are still unable to restore your backup, your backup is most likely corrupted. Backups can become corrupted due to an interruption in the backup creation process, force-closing WhatsApp, sending or receiving corrupted files, or for other reasons. Unfortunately, WhatsApp can’t restore a corrupted backup for you or determine what caused the corruption.

Note:

  • Partial or incomplete backups can be caused by an unstable internet connection, insufficient storage space on your device, or interruptions during the backup process.
  • iCloud only stores one backup per account. Each new backup overwrites the old one, so there’s no way to restore a previous iCloud backup.
  • If your chat history has been corrupted, you can’t restore your backup.

To provide an additional layer of security, WhatsApp protects end-to-end encrypted backups with a password or 64-digit encryption key. This password or backup key is the only way for you to access your encrypted backup or transfer it to a new device.

Note: If you can’t remember your password and don’t have access to your WhatsApp chats, you won’t be able to access your backup. WhatsApp can’t reset your password or help restore your backup.

Change your password

You can change the password for your encrypted backup even if you can’t remember your old password.

  1. Tap Settings or your profile picture.
  2. Tap Chats > Chat backup > End-to-end encrypted backup > Change password.
  3. Tap I forgot my password, then verify your identity with your biometrics or device PIN.
  4. Create a new password for your backup.

Turn off end-to-end encrypted backup

If you can’t remember your password, you can turn off end-to-end encrypted backup.

  1. Tap Settings or your profile picture.
  2. Tap Chats > Chat backup > End-to-end encrypted backup > Turn off.
  3. Enter your password, then tap Turn off.
  4. Tap Done.

You can turn on end-to-end encrypted backup at any time.

Password attempts

You can attempt to enter your password or backup key a total of five times. After five incorrect tries, you’ll have to wait before you can try again.

If you don’t restore your backup

If you choose to use WhatsApp without restoring a backup, that backup will still be available for you to access if you choose to reinstall WhatsApp on another device.

Note: This article is about encrypted backups. If you are looking for information about your username key, learn more in this article.

Can’t transfer chat history

Copy link

Note: Confirm data transfer to your new phone before deleting data, resetting, or uninstalling WhatsApp on your old phone. In case your transfer fails, gets stuck, or you receive an error, your data will still be available on your old phone.

If you’re having issues transferring your chats between two iPhones or two Android devices, the most common reasons why are:

QR code issues

During the transfer process, you will be asked to scan a QR code. Make sure you’re scanning the correct QR code that’s shown after you complete registration.

If the QR code doesn’t appear, ensure both phones are on the same Wi-Fi, live location is active, and all requested permissions are accepted.

WhatsApp is already active on my new device

You can only transfer your chats before you’ve activated WhatsApp on your new phone. Before starting the transfer from your old device, make sure you uninstall WhatsApp on your new device. Learn how here.

Note: You can’t merge new chats from your new phone and old chats from your old phone.

My new device has a different phone number

It’s not possible to transfer your chats to a new phone number. You’ll need to change your phone number on your old device to your new phone number before transferring chats to your new phone. Learn how here.

Verification issues

If you’ve attempted to transfer your chats multiple times and are experiencing wait times for a verification code, there’s no way to speed up the process. You may be able to receive a code by email. Learn more here.

Using WhatsApp Chats Transfer to transfer chats between two different types of devices

Chats can only be transferred between two of the same type of device using WhatsApp Chat Transfer. To transfer chats from an Android device to an iPhone, read this article. To transfer chats from an iPhone to an Android device, read this article.

Note:

  • If you’re having issues with the chat transfer, try restarting both phones. Turn them off, wait 30 seconds, and turn them back on. Then, try the chat transfer again.
  • Don’t delete your old phone’s data, reset your old phone, or uninstall WhatsApp on your old phone until you can confirm the data has successfully transferred to your new phone. In case your transfer fails, gets stuck, or you receive an error, your data will still be available on your old phone.
  • If you receive an error message, restart both phones and start the transfer process again.
  • Using non-WhatsApp chat transfer apps isn’t supported and may cause loss of chats.
  • WhatsApp doesn’t delete your chats during a transfer and your chats aren’t lost if an error occurs.

About end-to-end encrypted backup

On iPhone

Copy link

Android

iOS

More

Android

iOS

End-to-end encryption means that only you and the person you’re talking to can read your messages, and no one in between. With end-to-end encrypted backup, you can add that same layer of protection to your Google Account and iCloud backups.

Note: This article is about encrypted backups. If you are looking for information about your username key, learn more in this article.

Protecting your backup

When you create an end-to-end encrypted WhatsApp chat backup for Android or iCloud, your messages and media are stored in the cloud. These backups are protected by either a passkey, a 64-digit encryption key, or a password.

Passkey

A passkey is a modern, secure authentication method that works with password managers such as the Password app on iOS.

With a passkey, you can use your fingerprint, face, or screen lock to verify it’s you.

To use passkeys your device must be:

  • iOS 18 or higher.
  • Your device must have a screen lock set up such as PIN, password or pattern.

64-digit encryption key

A 64-digit encryption key is a long string of characters generated by WhatsApp.

Password

Using a password which you create yourself is another option available to protect your backup.

Note:

  • You cannot access your encrypted backup if you don’t have your password, encryption key, or passkey.
  • You cannot restore your backup if you lose access to your WhatsApp account and forget your password or encryption key. WhatsApp cannot send you a copy, reset it, or restore your backup for you.
  • If you’ve forgotten your password and still have access to your WhatsApp, you can change your password. Learn how here.

Turn on end-to-end encrypted backups

  1. Tap WhatsApp Settings or your profile picture, then tap Chats > Chat Backup.
  2. Tap End-to-end encrypted backup.
  3. Tap Turn on, then tap Create a passkey and follow the prompts.
  • Alternatively, tap More options to create a password or use a 64-digit encryption key.

Note: To switch from password or encryption key protection to passkey protection, you must first turn off end-to-end encryption, and then re-enable using a passkey.

Turn off end-to-end encrypted backups

  1. Tap WhatsApp Settings or your profile picture, then tap Chats > Chat Backup.
  2. Tap End-to-end encrypted backup.
  3. Tap Turn off, then follow the prompts.
  4. Tap Turn off again to confirm.

Device-level backups on iPhone

When end-to-end encryption is turned on for WhatsApp backups, your chat history is not included in your iPhone’s device backup.

You can restore your chat history as long as you have an existing iCloud backup. Learn how to backup your chat history.

If your old phone is broken or lost, you can restore your chats on a new device from your backup. Learn how to recover a WhatsApp account from a lost or stolen device.

To check if you have an existing iCloud backup:

  1. Open Settings.
  2. Tap Chats > Chat Backup.
  3. If your chats are backed up, you’ll see the time and size of your last backup.

Once you’ve confirmed you have an iCloud backup, you can start the restoring process.

If you don’t have an iCloud backup, you can still restore chats on a new device by transferring chats from your old device. Learn how to transfer your chat history.

Note: After 365 days of inactivity, your account will be deleted. Should this happen, you will be asked to register as a new user and will not have the option to restore backup. However, if you have an iCloud backup, you can restore your chat history by reinstalling WhatsApp.

[Embedded video omitted]

0:00 / 1:38

To restore your chat history from your iCloud backup:

  1. Uninstall and reinstall WhatsApp.
  • Learn how to uninstall WhatsApp.
  1. Verify your phone number and Apple ID.
  2. Tap Restore Chat History.

For additional security, you may be prompted to verify your identity to restore your chats. You can do this by receiving a code by text or a call if you haven’t enabled two-step verification or end-to-end encrypted backups. Learn how to turn on two-step verification here and enable end-to-end encrypted backups here.

You also restore your chat history by transferring chats from your old device. Learn how to transfer your chat history.

Note:

  • Unfortunately, we can’t restore, transfer, or delete your chats, contacts, or media files for you because your chat history isn’t stored on our servers.
  • Any messages sent and received after the latest backup can’t be restored.
  • There must be enough free space on both your iCloud and iPhone to restore your chat history. A partial backup can occur if your iPhone does not have enough storage. If backup restore fails due to storage, then delete the app and try to restore your backup again.
  • The phone number used for backing up and the one used for restoring must be the same.
  • Videos will only be restored if you toggled on Include videos before creating your latest backup.
  • Backups include messages and media sent and received in communities. They also include updates shared over WhatsApp Channels, but they do not include media unless you are the channel admin.

How to transfer your chat history

On iPhone

Copy link

Android

iOS

More

Android

iOS

If you’re moving from an iPhone to another iPhone, you can transfer your full chat and media history using WhatsApp’s Chat Transfer feature.

While restoring from a backup can recover all of your chat data, the Chat Transfer feature allows you to transfer your full account information including all of your personal messages, photos, videos, documents, etc. However, you can’t transfer peer-to-peer payment messages and your call history, or media received over WhatsApp Channels.

[Embedded video omitted]

0:00 / 2:53

What you need

  • The latest iOS version available on both of your devices.
  • The latest version of WhatsApp from the App Store.
  • Use the same phone number as your old phone on your new phone.
  • Your new phone must not be registered on WhatsApp until you start the migration on your old phone.
  • Your phones must be close to each other.
  • Both of your phones should be connected to a power source.
  • Both of your phones need to have WiFi and be connected to the internet.
  • Both of your phones must have local network permissions.

Transfer your chat history

Old phone

  1. Open WhatsApp on your old phone.
  2. Tap your profile picture > Chats > Transfer Chats to iPhone > Start.
  3. Tap Allow to “WhatsApp would like access to the camera” if it’s not enabled. You’ll use the camera on your old phone to scan the QR code on your new phone.

New phone

  1. Open WhatsApp on your new phone.
  2. Tap Agree & continue, then verify your phone number.
  3. Tap Continue on Transfer chat history to iPhone and accept local network permissions.
  4. Use the WhatsApp camera on your old phone to scan the QR code on your new phone.
  5. When prompted, accept local network permissions.
  6. While your chat history is transferring, a percentage bar will track the progress. Keep your phones near each other, unlocked, and don’t leave WhatsApp. Messaging is paused during the chat history transfer. You can Cancel the process at any time.
  7. When you see Transfer completed, tap Next. You’ll see the Setup Profile page where you’ll enter your name. After that, you’ll see the Chats list with all of your existing chats.

What happens to my data?

  • Transferred data doesn’t go to cloud storage as a result of the migration unless you create an iCloud backup.
  • WhatsApp can’t see the data you transfer.
  • Your old iPhone will still have your data on it unless you delete WhatsApp or reset your old phone.

Note:

  • Don’t delete your old phone’s data, reset your old phone, or uninstall WhatsApp on your old phone until you can confirm the data has successfully transferred to your new phone. In case your transfer fails, gets stuck, or you receive an error, your data will still be available on your old phone.
  • If you’re having issues with the chat transfer, try restarting both phones. Turn them off, wait 30 seconds, and turn them back on. Then, try the chat transfer again. Learn more about how to troubleshoot issues with transferring chats here.
  • It’s currently not possible to transfer chats on the WhatsApp Business app.

You can send and receive voice messages on Ray-Ban Meta to keep connected with your loved ones and easily communicate on the go.

If your account is banned, you’ll see the following message when you open the WhatsApp Business app: “This phone number can’t use WhatsApp: [phone number]. You can request a review of this number. Most reviews are completed within 24 hours.”

Note: A banned account automatically loses its Meta Verified subscription.

If your account violates our Meta Verified for Business Terms of Service, the WhatsApp Business Messaging Policy or Meta Commerce Policy, for example if it involves spam, tries to sell items prohibited by our policies, and/or if it puts WhatsApp users’ safety at risk, your subscription will be canceled and a refund will be unavailable. Learn more in this article, or view WhatsApp Business Messaging Policy or Meta Commerce Policy.

We recommend carefully reviewing this article to understand how to comply with the Business Messaging and Commerce policies and to learn more about the appropriate uses of WhatsApp and the activities that violate the WhatsApp Terms of Service.

How to request account review

If you think your WhatsApp Business account was banned by mistake, tap Request review in the app to submit the request. We’ll get back to you as soon as we complete our review. If you don’t see an option to request a review, it means the ban is final and can’t be appealed.

You can check the status of your request by opening the WhatsApp Business app. Please keep in mind that contacting WhatsApp outside of the review process or through another user’s account won’t expedite the review process or impact the decision. After your request is reviewed, you’ll receive a notification from WhatsApp and can view this decision in the WhatsApp Business app.

Please note, third party services can’t ban your WhatsApp Business account or remove your account ban. Only WhatsApp can ban or unban a WhatsApp Business account.

Learn what to do after your account is unbanned here.

About ad performance metrics on the WhatsApp Business app

Copy link

Businesses that advertise using the WhatsApp Business app can access performance metrics that can help them understand the impact of their messaging campaigns and how effectively they’re connecting with customers.

Note:

  • Some metrics for businesses and ads delivered to and from Europe and Japan will be unavailable.
  • Certain factors, such as user behavior, privacy settings, technical delays, or ad targeting, can affect ad performance.

See your ad details

To see an ad’s performance metrics:

  1. Tap Tools > Manage ads.
  2. Tap the ad you want to see metrics for. This will take you to the ad details screen, where you can view some key metrics. To see additional metrics and breakdowns, tap See all to open Ad Performance where you can access a wider range of metrics.

Performance metrics

Performance analytics provide an overview of how many people saw and interacted with an ad, and include information such as:

  • Reach: The total number of individual users that have seen an ad. If one user sees an ad multiple times, they will only be counted once under this metric.

  • Note: During ad creation, you’ll see an estimated reach for your campaign. This number may not match the actual reach.

  • Ad clicks: The amount of times an ad is clicked or tapped.

  • Cost per link click: The average cost for each link click on an ad. This metric is calculated by dividing the total amount spent on an ad by the total amount of link clicks.

  • Note:

  • This metric can include amounts that may not have been invoiced yet.

  • If your ad is currently running, this number may be an approximation. It can take up to 48 hours for results to be processed.

  • Conversations started: The number of chats that started from your ads.

Ad details

  • Status: The current state of an ad. An ad’s status can be:

  • Active: Currently being shown to your audience.

  • In review: Before your ads become active, we automatically review them against Meta Advertising Standards. Most ads are reviewed within 24 hours, although in some cases it may take longer.

  • Not delivering: An ad that is not currently being shown to your audience for reasons like the payment threshold is too low or you’ve already reached it for the day. There could also be an issue with your payment.

  • Completed: Ad ad that has reached its scheduled end date and is no longer running.

  • Paused: An approved ad that you have chosen to stop running. Learn how to pause an ad that’s currently running.

  • Rejected: An ad that doesn’t comply with Meta advertising policies.

  • Budget & duration: How much you spend on an ad each day and how many days that ad runs.

  • Audience: The type of users that an ad will be shown to. Businesses can target their ads toward users based on factors like age, gender, and location.

  • Start date: The day and time that the ad first became active.

  • End date: The day and time that the ad will no longer be active.

  • Placements: The platforms that your ad is on, such as Facebook.

Payment details

  • Ad account: The account associated with the payment.
  • Payment method: Payment method used to pay for your ad.

How to add a WhatsApp Business account to a Facebook Page

On iPhone

Copy link

Android

iOS

More

Android

iOS

When using the WhatsApp Business app, you can link your Facebook Page with your WhatsApp Business account.

Linking your WhatsApp Business account enables customers visiting your Facebook Page to message you directly on WhatsApp with just one click.

To link these accounts, you must have the following:

  • A Facebook page for your business.
  • An account on the WhatsApp Business app.
  • The latest versions of the mobile apps.

You can also link your Facebook or Instagram accounts to an account with a Meta Verified subscription. Learn more about Meta Verified.

Link your WhatsApp Business account to a Facebook Page

You can link your accounts from within the WhatsApp Business app.

  1. From the Tools tab, tap Facebook & Instagram.
  2. Tap Facebook > Continue. This will open the Facebook login page.
  3. Enter the login information for your Facebook account. Tap Log In.
  4. Select the Facebook Page you want to link to your WhatsApp Business account. Tap Connect WhatsApp. .
  • If you don’t have a Facebook Page, you’ll have the option to create one.

You’ll now see a WhatsApp button on your Facebook page.

Once you return to the WhatsApp Business app, you’ll see your linked Facebook Page at the top of the Facebook & Instagram screen.

Remove your linked Facebook account from the WhatsApp Business app

If you no longer want your accounts to be connected, you can unlink your Facebook and WhatsApp accounts from the Whatsapp Business app.

  1. From the Tools tab, tap Facebook & Instagram.
  2. Tap your linked Facebook account > Remove WhatsApp > Remove.

Once you’ve removed your account, it’ll no longer be visible on the Facebook & Instagram screen.

Troubleshoot issues linking or unlinking your Instagram account with the WhatsApp Business app

If you experience issues linking or unlinking your WhatsApp Business account with Instagram, make sure that:

  • You use the phone number associated with your WhatsApp Business account on the WhatsApp Business app.
  • You’re an admin on your Facebook Business Manager account.
  • Your Instagram Profile and your Catalog are linked to the same Business Manager account.
  • You have Manage Page permissions for the Instagram Profile and Manage Catalog permissions for the catalog on Business Manager.
  • You entered the correct registration code when registering the phone number associated with your WhatsApp Business account.

For additional information on linking a WhatsApp Business account to an Instagram Profile, read this article.

Can’t link your Facebook page to WhatsApp Business

If you’re having trouble linking your Facebook page to WhatsApp Business, there are a few things to check.

Make sure you meet the requirements

To link your Facebook page to WhatsApp Business, you need the following:

  • You must be an admin of the Facebook page you want to link.
  • The Facebook page can’t already be connected to a different WhatsApp Business account. Each page can only be linked to one WhatsApp Business account at a time.
  • Your Facebook page must be a business page, not a personal profile or pro-mode profile.
  • If your page is connected to a Meta Business Manager, you must also be a business admin.
  • Your WhatsApp Business account can’t already be linked to a different Facebook page.

Try these steps:

  • Make sure you’re logged into the correct Facebook account that owns the page you want to link.
  • Update both the WhatsApp Business app and the Facebook app to the latest version.
  • Check your internet connection and try again.
  • Force close the WhatsApp Business app, then reopen it and try linking again.
  • If you see the error, “We could not connect your Facebook account,” wait a few minutes and try again. This can be caused by a temporary server issue.

If your ad is promoting the wrong Facebook page

If you created an ad and it’s promoting from the wrong Facebook page, you need to change which page is linked to your WhatsApp Business account.

  • Unlink the current page: On the Tools tab, tap Facebook & Instagram. Tap your linked Facebook account, then tap Remove WhatsApp account > Remove.
  • Link the correct page: On the Tools tab, tap Facebook & Instagram. Tap Facebook > Continue. Log in to Facebook and select the correct page you want to promote your ads from.

Note: After changing your linked page, any active ads will continue to run with the previous page until the ad set ends or you update the ad in Meta Ads Manager.

If you still can’t link your page

If you’ve tried the steps above and still can’t link your Facebook page, it might be because:

  • Your Facebook page is already linked to another WhatsApp Business account. A page can only be linked to one WhatsApp account at a time.
  • Your advertising access is restricted due to a policy violation.
  • You’ve reached the limit for the number of businesses you can create.
  • Your business account isn’t allowed to advertise.

For more help with these issues, contact Meta Business Support.

When using the WhatsApp Business app, you can link your Instagram account with your WhatsApp Business account.

Linking your Instagram Professional account with your WhatsApp Business account enables the Click to WhatsApp button on your Instagram profile. The Click to WhatsApp button makes it easier for customers to connect with your business and increases customer engagement.

To link these accounts, you must have the following:

  • A Professional account for your business on Instagram.
  • An account on the WhatsApp Business app.
  • The latest versions of the mobile apps.

You can also link your Facebook or Instagram accounts to an account with a Meta Verified subscription. Learn more about Meta Verified.

Link your Instagram account to the WhatsApp Business app

You can link your Instagram and WhatsApp Business accounts from within the WhatsApp Business app.

  1. From the Tools tab, tap > Facebook & Instagram.

  2. Tap Instagram > Continue. This will open the Instagram login page.

  3. Enter the login information for your Instagram account. Tap Log In. You can also tap Continue with Facebook to log in using your Facebook account.

  4. If you already have a Professional Account on Instagram, continue to the next step. If you don’t have a Professional Account, you’ll need to update your account type.

  5. Tap Next.

  6. Select Business or Creator. Then, tap Next > Next > Next.

  7. Confirm your account information. Tap Add > Back to WhatsApp.

Once you return to the WhatsApp Business app, you’ll see your linked Instagram Professional account at the top of the Facebook & Instagram screen.

Remove your linked Instagram account from the WhatsApp Business app

If you no longer want your accounts to be connected, you can unlink your Instagram and WhatsApp accounts from the Whatsapp Business app.

  • Not all Instagram business categories are supported by the WhatsApp Business app. If you see an error message that says “Your Instagram business category isn’t supported on WhatsApp,” you’ll need to change your Instagram business category to comply with the WhatsApp Commerce Policy to successfully link your accounts.

  • In order to link your accounts, WhatsApp shares the following information with Facebook:

  • Your WhatsApp business category is used to set your Professional business category on Instagram if you don’t have a Professional Account on Instagram. If you already have a Professional Account on Instagram, your WhatsApp Business category isn’t shared.

  • Your WhatsApp Business phone number is used to enable customers to message you on WhatsApp from your Instagram profile.

Troubleshoot issues linking or unlinking your Instagram account with the WhatsApp Business app

If you experience issues linking or unlinking your WhatsApp Business account with Instagram, make sure that:

  • You use the phone number associated with your WhatsApp Business account on the WhatsApp Business app.
  • You’re an admin on your Facebook Business Manager account.
  • Your Instagram Profile and your Catalog are linked to the same Business Manager account.
  • You have Manage Page permissions for the Instagram Profile and Manage Catalog permissions for the catalog on Business Manager.
  • You entered the correct registration code when registering the phone number associated with your WhatsApp Business account.

How to add and manage your business username key

On iPhone

Android

Usernames on WhatsApp Business is rolling out gradually over the next few months and might not be available to you yet. In the meantime, you can reserve your business username. We recommend keeping WhatsApp Business updated on your device so you can get the latest feature updates.

A username key is an optional code that gives you more control over who can message your business using your username. If you turn on a username key, new customers will need your username and your key to message you for the first time.

Who needs your username key?

Needs your key:

  • New customers contacting you by username for the first time

Doesn’t need your key:

  • Customers you’ve already chatted with
  • Customers who have your phone number Customers in a group with you
  • Customers who scanned your QR code
  • Customers you messaged first

Set up a username key

  1. Go to the Tools tab > Profile.
  2. Tap Username.
  3. Tap Contact me by username.
  4. Select People who know my key. This generates a key.
  • Note: To generate a different key, tap Get a different key.
  1. Tap Save key.

Change username key

  1. Go to the Tools tab > Profile.
  2. Tap Username.
  3. Tap Contact me by username, then select People who know my key.
  4. Tap Save key.
  5. Tap the back arrow to return to the username tab. You’ll see your new username key under your username.

Note: Customers who have your phone number and customers you’ve already chatted with don’t need your username key.

How to share your username key

When sharing your username, include your key so customers can reach you:

  • On business cards: “Message us on WhatsApp: @YourBusiness (key: 1234)”
  • On receipts or packaging
  • Verbally: “My WhatsApp is @YourBusiness, the key is 1234”

Your username key is not a password — it’s a lightweight filter to reduce unwanted first-contact messages. If you’re receiving unwanted messages, generate a new key at any time. Remember to share the new key with customers you want to hear from.

WhatsApp is helping business to be discovered by new customers through the WhatsApp Business directory. For businesses using the WhatsApp Business app, you can increase the visibility for your business by applying to the directory.

Businesses must apply to be included in the Business directory and must comply with all applicable terms and policies, including the WhatsApp Business Messaging Policy and the WhatsApp Commerce Policy.

The WhatsApp Business directory is currently only available in Brazil and may not be available in your area yet.

Apply to the WhatApp Business directory

To be included in the Business directory, your business must:

  • Be located in Brazil, in one of several supported regions.
  • Be part of a supported business category.

Learn more about Business directory requirements.

You can find the Business directory in the Business Tools menu.

  1. Tap Tools > Business directory.
  2. Tap Add your business and follow the steps to complete your application.

Businesses can update their location and coverage area in the business profile.

Once your application is reviewed, you’ll receive a WhatsApp notification confirming if your business has been added to the directory, if more information is required, or if your application wasn’t approved. Once approved, the business information shared by you will be visible to all users.

If an account is determined to violate the WhatsApp Business Messaging Policy and/or the WhatsApp Commerce Policy, your application to the Business directory will be rejected and the business account will be actioned as per the current applicable policies. You will receive a message informing you of this decision and will have the ability to appeal through the appeal process.

Withdraw application from the WhatApp Business directory

To withdraw your application, go to the Chats screen and tap Tools > Business Directory > Remove Your Business > Remove your business.

Remove business from Business directory

You can remove your business account from the Business Directory at any time through the Meta Business Suite or WhatsApp Business Manager. You can also re-list yourself from the same location, if eligible.

You will need to allow 30 minutes for the visibility of your business to be adjusted in WhatsApp users’ phones.

Business removed from the Business directory

Your company might be removed from the Business directory if your business category changes.

You can re-apply to the Business directory with a different category by following the instructions in this article, but your application might not be approved.

Note: Once your account is removed, we unfortunately can’t manually add it back.
