About usernames on WhatsApp Business

Copy link

Usernames on WhatsApp Business is rolling out gradually over the next few months and might not be available to you yet. In the meantime, you can reserve your business username. We recommend keeping WhatsApp Business updated on your device so you can get the latest feature updates. To learn more about reserving your username, read this article.

Usernames on WhatsApp Business are an optional feature that lets you create a unique identifier for your business (for example, @YourBusinessName) to help customers easily find and recognize your business. Customers can use your username to start a chat with your business more easily without needing your phone number. Usernames will be searchable in WhatsApp with exact match search, so your customers need to know your exact username to message you using username.

Your business phone number will still be visible on your business profile.

Your business username is different from your Business name (the name that appears in your Business profile).

Note:

  • A phone number is still required for your WhatsApp Business account.
  • Even if you have a username set up for your Business, customers can still contact you by your phone number if they have it.

Who can see my Business username?

  • Customers who don’t have your business phone number saved will see your username instead. This includes when you message a customer directly, participate in group chats, or make WhatsApp calls. Your username always appears with an @ symbol.

How do customers contact me by my Business username?

Customers can enter your exact username directly in WhatsApp to start a conversation. There’s no searchable directory. They need to know your exact username, which is why sharing it on your marketing materials, signage, and social media is important. You can also share via QR code or a direct link.

How are usernames for consumers different from usernames on WhatsApp Business?

Usernames for people make their phone number private. When a consumer adopts a username, their phone number will not be visible when they message or call anyone who doesn’t already have it saved in their contacts.

Consumers who adopt a username, may message your business without ever sharing their phone number. If you need it for workflows like shipping or customer support, you can set up a quick reply that prompts them to share their contact information directly in the chat. To learn more about quick reply, read this article.

What is a username key?

A username key is an optional code that gives you more control over who can message your business using your username. If you turn on a username key, new customers will need your username and your key to message you for the first time.

This can help protect against unwanted messages from people who only know your username. Customers who already have your phone number won’t need your key to message you.

Can I change or delete my username?

Having a Business username is completely optional. You can change your username or delete it at any time. Keep in mind that once you change or delete a username, it may become available for others to claim.

Can someone take my username?

Usernames are unique to each account. If the username you want is already taken, you’ll need to choose a different one. Certain usernames are held for businesses, governments, or public figures and can’t be claimed by others.

About using Meta Business Agent to chat with customers

Copy link

Note:

  • This feature is currently only available in limited countries to select businesses. It might not be available to you yet. If you are unable to turn on Meta Business Agent using the steps in this article, you can add yourself to the waitlist here.
  • At this time, not all languages are supported. The language that Meta Business Agent uses is determined by your business’s phone number.

Meta Business Agent is an artificial intelligence (AI) service from Meta for businesses. Businesses on WhatsApp can use Meta Business Agent to enhance parts of their conversations with customers who choose to use AI from Meta.

When your business connects Meta Business Agent, it can perform the following actions for your customers based on the information you or your customers provide:

  • Respond to customer questions about basic business information like your business hours or location
  • Provide answers to customer questions about specific products or services
  • Recommend products or services to your customers
  • Provide customers with details about pricing
  • Respond to customer questions about discounts, payment, and shipping

If at any point you choose to respond to your customers’ messages manually, the AI will stop generating responses on your behalf unless you unmute it or update your settings for AI replies. Messages sent or received in chats that have connected Meta Business Agent will still be collected by Meta to improve AI at Meta, even when you mute Meta Business Agent. When you delete Meta Business Agent, you will no longer be sharing your messages with Meta to improve AI at Meta.

We will let customers know the first time they start chatting with a business that has AI connected. When messaging with your business, customers will see the following message if you’re using Meta Business Agent in a chat: AI from Meta receives chats to improve AI quality and generate messages for this business. When your business begins using Meta Business Agent, Meta Business Agent uses information about your business, such as catalog, public profiles, websites, business description, address, and hours, to answer your customers’ questions. WhatsApp’s parent company Meta may use this information, as well as your messages in chats where AI has been turned on, to improve AI at Meta.

Note:

  • Turning on Meta Business Agent may impede your ability to use certain features of the WhatsApp Business app, including broadcast lists, disappearing messages, and greeting and away messages. You can always delete Meta Business Agent to restore access to those features.
  • Turning on Meta Business Agent will disconnect any existing linked devices. You can re-link most devices, with the exception of WhatsApp for Windows, WhatsApp for Android tablets, and WhatsApp for WearOS, after completing the onboarding process.
  • You will receive a notification on your device if Meta Business Agent determines that a customer needs your attention.
  • AI-generated messages may not be accurate or appropriate. To learn how to provide feedback about a message created by Meta Business Agent, view this article.
  • Meta offers additional optional services you can use in the WhatsApp Business app. When you use these services, different data processing terms may apply. You can read the terms for each service to find details.
  • Meta Business Agent uses your public profiles, websites, and catalog to answer questions.

How to turn on Meta Business Agent

Businesses using Meta Business Agent on the WhatsApp Business app can turn on Meta Business Agent through the app. Tap the Tools tab > AI agent. Then, follow the instructions to get started.

How to download your Meta Business Agent data

To view the information shared with Meta to improve AI:

  1. Tap Tools > Your AI agent.
  2. Under Other things you can do, tap Download your data > Request report. A downloadable file will be generated for you.

Note: Meta Business Agent’s data cannot be downloaded using WhatsApp Web. You can download Meta Business Agent’s data using the WhatsApp Business mobile app.

How to delete Meta Business Agent

If you no longer want to use Meta Business Agent, you can delete it.

To learn how to delete Meta Business Agent, view this article.

Note: Businesses using Meta Business Agent on the WhatsApp Business Platform can learn more about using Meta Business Agent in the developer documentation provided to them.

Verified account visibility within WhatsApp Discover businesses

Copy link

Note: This article is intended for businesses in Brazil using the WhatsApp Business Platform.

Discover businesses is a feature that helps users in Brazil find and connect with businesses that use the WhatsApp Business Platform. To use this feature, users can tap> Discover Businesses > Verified Accounts > View All. Only verified business accounts will be displayed.

To help customers find great businesses, Discover businesses will display businesses that must meet the following criteria:

  • Accounts must have a Verified or Official Business Account status.
  • Accounts must have a Connected status in the WhatsApp Business Manager, indicating that their phone numbers are connected.
  • The WhatsApp Business Account must be using the WhatsApp Business Platform.
  • Visible phone numbers in a WhatsApp business account must have different account profile names.
  • The display name for a given phone number must be unique for the given country because duplicate names are not allowed.
  • The phone number must have the prefix +55 for Brazil.
  • The phone number must be responsive to at least 80% of incoming user messages in the last seven days.
  • On average, the account must reply to the first message in a user-initiated conversation within 24 hours.

We also recommend that businesses take the following steps to improve the quality of their accounts:

  • Use a clear business logo as the account profile photo.
  • Select the relevant business category.
  • Add their business address.
  • Add a description of their business.

We reassess account eligibility every 24 hours. If an account doesn’t meet the criteria, it will no longer be visible in Discover businesses. This change is automated and business owners will be able to see the reason for the ineligibility in the WhatsApp Business Manager or Business Management API.

Opting out and in

Visibility in Discover businesses is automatic for businesses meeting the criteria above. Businesses can remove their account(s) from Discover businesses at any time through the WhatsApp Business Manager or Meta Business Suite. Businesses can also re-list themselves from the same locations, if eligible.

Businesses will need to allow 30 minutes for their visibility to be adjusted in WhatsApp users’ phones.

Note: If an account was previously visible in Discover businesses, it’s possible that customers who found the account there will continue to contact the business. Charges could apply.

Understanding search results

Search results will match in full or in part the text the user has entered. The results displayed will only show businesses registered in the user’s country.

Note: Global business accounts are not yet eligible to be listed in Discover businesses.

Popular businesses

The Popular businesses section in Discover businesses will highlight up to 25 verified business accounts for users to discover. To be featured in this section, business accounts must be responsive to at least 90% of incoming user messages. Business accounts must also have received the most messages through business search in their country in the last seven days.

Understanding the pricing model

The WhatsApp Business Platform is priced by each conversation. There are two rates, one for user-initiated and one for business-initiated conversations. User-initiated conversations are only charged once a business replies to the user, and standard pricing will apply. More information about the WhatsApp Business pricing model is available here. Rates are based on the end-recipient’s phone number.

As part of the initial rollout, businesses won’t know the:

  • Exact point of origin for the customer-initiated conversation
  • Total number of customer-initiated conversations

Business account information

Business account information will be used in accordance with the WhatsApp Business Terms of Service and the WhatsApp Business App Privacy Policy.

About verified business accounts

Copy link

Some verified accounts are owned by a notable person, brand, or entity while others are subscribed to one of Meta’s subscription products like Meta Verified or Meta One.

  • A verified badge means Meta has verified the account based on their activity across Meta technologies, or information or documents they provide.
  • Meta Verified is a paid monthly subscription that comes with features like the verified badge, account support, impersonation protection, and more. Learn more about Meta Verified for Business on WhatsApp here.
  • Meta One is an optional paid subscription from Meta that bundles benefits across different Meta apps, including WhatsApp, Instagram, Facebook, Messenger, and Meta AI, depending on what’s available to your account. Learn more about Meta One subscription plans here.

Verified business accounts have been authenticated using a multi-step verification process to help you know whether you’re chatting with the right business.

About verified badges

A verified badge

[Image: Meta Verified Badge (sticker with a checkmark)]

on a business profile gives customers more confidence when engaging with a business on WhatsApp. The badge means Meta has verified the account based on their activity across Meta technologies, or information or documents they provide.

A verified badge

[Image: Meta Verified Badge (sticker with a checkmark)]

can be visible in:

  • Calls tab
  • Business profiles
  • Context cards
  • Chats
  • Incoming calls from verified businesses

For more information about chatting with a business, read this article.

Staying in control while communicating with businesses

Remember, you’re always in control of your interactions with businesses on WhatsApp. If you’d like to stop a business from contacting you, learn how to block them in this article.

Note: Every WhatsApp message is protected by the same Signal encryption protocol that secures messages before they leave your device. When you connect with a WhatsApp business account, your message is delivered securely to the destination chosen by the business.

Your web page address and username

Your existing WhatsApp web page address is now synced to your WhatsApp username. No action is needed to claim it. Going forward, your username and web page address will always be the same. Any changes you make to your username will automatically apply to your web page. Learn more about usernames here.

For Meta Verified businesses who claimed a web page address before usernames were available on WhatsApp, your Business username will automatically match your web page address. Your username is already reserved and you don’t need to take any action.

You can create a professional web page on WhatsApp with a custom link to help customers more easily find and engage with your business.

Without WhatsApp web page With WhatsApp web page
Link based on your phone number Customizable, easy-to-remember link
A web page with your business name and profile picture An indexable web page with your business name, profile picture, hours, address, website, catalog, and more
Easy way to create and manage a professional web page

Your business’s WhatsApp web page showcases information from your business profile and catalog. It’s easy to manage your web page by updating the information on your business profile. A WhatsApp web page helps you build credibility and an online presence for your business. It makes it easier for customers to discover your business on search engines.

Create your web page

  1. Tap Tools > Subscriptions.
  2. Tap Meta Verified or Meta One, depending on your subscription.
  3. Tap Web Page > Get Started.
  4. Complete the steps to create or reserve your username. Learn more about creating usernames here.
  5. Tap Create web page.
  6. Once your web page is created successfully, it’ll open in WhatsApp.

The link to your web page will appear on your Business Profile.

Note:

  • This feature might not be available to you yet.
  • Your web page address:
    • Must follow the WhatsApp Business Messaging Policy and Business Terms of Service.
    • Must represent your business and not impersonate another business.
    • Must have a minimum of 5 characters.
    • Can’t exceed 30 characters.
    • Can only contain letters [a-z], numbers [0-9], periods and/or underscores
    • May not start with www., and it may not end with .com or .org or .net or .int or .edu or .gov or .mil or .arpa or .html or .htm or .txt or .xml.
    • May not start or end with a period “.”
    • Can’t have consecutive periods “..”
    • Can’t contain only numbers. Likewise, a web page name can’t just have underscores or some combination of only underscores, period and digits.
  • You can’t have more than one web page address.
  • Customers can still find you at your short link in addition to your web page address.

Share your WhatsApp web page

  1. Tap

    [Image: Share (rectangle with up arrow)]

    next to your business name.

  2. Tap the person or group you’d like to share it with.

Change or delete your web page

  1. To update your web page, you’ll need to update your username. Then, your web page will update automatically.

  2. To delete your web page, tap

    [Image: More (three horizontal dots)]

    Delete web page > Delete.

Note: Deleting your web page will not delete your username. However, deleting your username will delete your web page.

After you delete your web page, customers can still find you at your short link.

Note: You can only change your web page address once every 90 days. Deleting your web page address removes it from the web, making the address available for others.

What are Business Solution Providers and how can you work with them?

Copy link

Explore our help content library to find answers and troubleshoot issues.

If you are not a developer, or would like to connect WhatsApp to the rest of your technology stack, such as an omnichannel inbox, customer support software, or a bot platform, you can work with a Business Solution Provider (BSP) to manage communications to and from customers. If you’re not sure who to contact, check our Partner Showcase. BSPs are a global community of third-party solution providers with expertise on the WhatsApp Business Platform. These BSPs can help you communicate with your customers on the WhatsApp Business Platform for the approved use cases of customer support and time-sensitive, personalized notifications.

Some businesses and BSPs1 will use WhatsApp’s parent company, Meta, to securely store messages and respond to customers. Meta will not automatically use your messages to inform the ads you see, however, businesses will be able to use chats they receive from you for their own marketing purposes, which may include advertising on Meta. You can always contact the individual business to learn more about their privacy practices.

Third parties offering unauthorized services on our platform, such as automated or bulk messaging, are doing so in violation of our Terms of Service. If you have been working with a third party offering an unauthorized service, you may not be able to send messages with them on WhatsApp. We recommend you work with our authorized BSPs instead.

Note: The shared list of partners is for reference only. We recommend that you conduct your own due diligence of the company you choose to work with.

Importantly, your customers can do all of these things without having to leave WhatsApp.

Building Private, Safe, and Secure WhatsApp Channels

Copy link

Channels are a simple, reliable, and private way to receive important updates on the topics you care about from people and organizations, right within WhatsApp. Anyone can choose to follow a channel by browsing and following the channels they’re interested in. To help make Channels a great experience for users, with the privacy, safety, and security that they expect from WhatsApp, we set out to build Channels thoughtfully with several key principles in mind:

Be the most private broadcast service

We’re aspiring to build the most private broadcast service available. Our privacy approach allows users to follow channels without sharing their phone number to any new people that are not in their contacts. Users can choose channels with the confidence that other users won’t see the channels they choose to follow or be able to contact them through a channel. And, anyone can create a channel without revealing their phone number or profile photo to those who choose to follow it.

Give users choice and control over the information they receive

WhatsApp users have full choice and control over their Channels experience. If a user decides not to follow any channels, their existing WhatsApp experience will remain the same. Users can’t be added to a channel without choosing to follow it and they will only see updates for the channels they choose. WhatsApp will not recommend channels based on users’ personal messaging activity, which remains private and end-to-end encrypted. It’s also simple for users to unfollow a channel at any point.

Keep the experience simple and clutter-free

We’ve designed Channels to be simple and clutter-free for users. For example, channel notifications are muted by default to limit information overload, while also giving users the option to turn on notifications for those updates that they don’t want to miss. We’ll show a limited history of each channel before a user follows it, so that users can make an informed choice about whether they want to follow the channel. Channel updates show up in chronological order to make it easier for users to go back to find an update they’re looking for.

Prevent and address abuse

We are providing tools and resources for Channel admins to safely and effectively manage their channels, and for users to easily unfollow and report problematic channels. As the owners of their channels, admins are responsible for maintaining an age-appropriate and safe experience for their followers. We’ve published guidelines for Channel admins to understand what isn’t allowed on their channel. Channels will be reviewed against these Guidelines, and those engaged in abuse may be subject to suspension or other action. We’ll also continue to receive and be responsive to valid legal orders from authorities in countries where we operate.

WhatsApp will continue to build support for Channel admins and followers and, as always, we will continue to listen closely to feedback from users about how we can help people get the information they want – privately, safely, and securely.

About channel admin controls

Copy link

Channel owners can invite additional channel admins to help manage their channel.

Channel admins can:

  • Change channel info and settings: Admins can change things like the channel name, icon, description and channel settings, like which type of emojis are allowed for reactions to channel admins.
  • Create, edit, and delete channel updates: Updates made by admins are shared immediately, they don’t need the approval of the channel owner. Admins can delete or edit the updates made by themselves, other admins, or the channel owner for up to 30 days after sending. Some channel updates can’t be edited, learn more here.
  • See all available channel metrics: Like channel owners, all channel admins have access to available insights like number of followers, top regions, accounts reached and more. Learn more about channel metrics.
  • Create an admin profile: Admins can create a custom admin profile with a name and photo that’s separate from their personal WhatsApp profile. When admin profiles are turned on for the channel, this profile will appear on any updates the admin posts. The admin’s number and WhatsApp account information aren’t visible to channel followers.
  • Turn on admin profiles: Any channel admin can turn on admin profiles for their channel from channel settings.

Channel owners can take the same actions as admins and can also:

  • Invite and dismiss other channel admins: Other admins can’t add or remove admins.
  • Delete their channel: Only channel owners can choose to delete their channels.
  • Transfer ownership of their channel: Only channel owners can choose to transfer ownership of their channel.

Note:

  • It’s not possible to remove channel followers.
  • All channels are public. You cannot create a code or password for a channel.

Channel admins are visible to each other. Learn more about safety and privacy as a channel admin.

How to become a channel admin

To become a channel admin, you’ll need to receive and accept an invitation from a channel owner. Becoming a channel admin is voluntary, and you can dismiss yourself at any time. If you don’t want to be an admin, simply ignore the invitation, and it will expire.

If you’re a channel owner and want to learn how to invite or dismiss admins, read more here.

Note:

  • Channel verification isn’t publicly available yet. We’re working on an application process, so stay tuned.

About creating a WhatsApp Channel

Copy link

Create a channel to use WhatsApp to share updates and information with your current followers and connect with new ones. With a channel, you can share one-way updates to an unlimited audience.

[Embedded video omitted]

0:00 / 1:43

Share updates and information with your followers

Use your channel to share things like:

  • Text
  • Images
  • Videos
  • Stickers
  • Links
  • Audio
  • Polls

While some features might feel familiar to WhatsApp chats, channel updates are a one-way broadcast rather than a conversation. Followers can’t reply directly to updates or send messages to channel admins. Instead they can show their interest in a channel’s content by adding emoji reactions to channel updates or voting on polls.

Updates are sent from your channel, which is in a separate part of the app away from chats and calls. Followers won’t see your WhatsApp profile name, picture, or your phone number.

Channel admins are visible to each other. Learn more about safety and privacy as a channel admin.

As the channel owner, you and all channel admins are responsible for keeping the content on your channel safe, relevant, and age-appropriate for your followers, learn more in the Channels Guidelines.

Attract new followers

People can find your channel several ways.

  • External link: Share a link to your channel on other websites or apps. Your channel and updates will be viewable in WhatsApp.
  • In-app sharing: Followers can share channels they like with their WhatsApp contacts.
  • Browsing in the app: WhatsApp users can search for channels or find them by browsing the directory. For easier browsing, some channels are sorted into categories within the directory.

Measure engagement

See metrics about your channel like:

  • Insights about your channel’s growth and reach for the last 30 days like:

  • Accounts reached

  • Top regions

  • Number of follows/unfollows

  • Number of channel followers. Also see which followers are contacts by viewing your channel follower list.

  • Update reaction details like number and type of emoji reactions and poll vote results.

Learn more about channel metrics here.

Get started by creating a channel and see the resources linked below to learn more.

How to delete a channel

Copy link

Deleting your channel is permanent. If you delete your channel, you won’t be able to make updates from it again.

  • Followers will still be able to find your channel but will see a system message that your channel was deleted. Your past updates will still be available from their phones.
  • Non-followers (e.g. viewers) will no longer be able to see your channel or updates. They won’t be able to find your channel in search anymore. New people can no longer follow your channel, and your sharing link won’t work.

Delete your channel

  1. From the Updates tab on mobile or the Channels page on web, find and tap or click your channel to open it.
  2. Tap or click your channel name > Delete channel > Delete.
  3. Enter your phone number to confirm, and tap or click Delete.
  • This helps ensure you don’t delete the channel by accident.

Once successfully deleted, you’ll see the message “You deleted your channel” in the Updates tab or the Channels page.

Note:

  • Only the channel owner can delete a channel, not other admins.
  • If you want to delete your channel and your WhatsApp account, delete your channel first. Your channel won’t be automatically deleted if you’ve assigned additional admins before you delete your channel and your WhatsApp account. Instead the admin who has followed the channel longest will become the new channel owner.

Note: You can’t search for channels that you’ve unfollowed or deleted.

Note:

  • Updates can be deleted by any of the channel’s admins.
  • When you delete your channel, it doesn’t affect channel information and content that other users may continue to have. For example, a copy of channel content saved locally on their device or that has been forwarded to other users or shared outside of WhatsApp.

Easily share interesting channels or channel updates with friends and family by forwarding them on WhatsApp. You can forward from a channel to individual or group chats, or to your WhatsApp Status.

If you’re a channel admin or owner, you can also forward channel content to your own channel.

Forward channel updates

To share a single channel update:

  1. Tap

    [Image: Forward (right arrow with curved tail)]

    underneath the update you want to forward.

  2. Choose where to forward:

    • Chats: Select or search for the chats you want. Pick up to 5 individual or group chats.
    • Status: To forward to your status, tap My status.
    • Channels: If you’re a channel admin, search for your channel to forward to it. It will be labeled “Forwarded” and link back to the original channel. Learn more.

  3. Add a message for context on what you’re sharing. This will be sent as a separate message in chats or as a note at the bottom in a status update.

  4. Tap Forward.

To forward multiple updates at one time:

  1. Tap and hold one of the updates you want to forward, then tap Forward.

  2. Tap the checkbox to the left to add additional updates to forward.

  3. Tap

    [Image: Forward (right arrow with curved tail)]

    , then choose where to forward:

    • Chats: Select or search for the chats you want. Pick up to 5 individual or group chats.
    • Status: To forward to your status, tap My status.
    • Channels: If you’re a channel admin, search for your channel to forward to it. It will be labeled “Forwarded” and link back to the original channel. Learn more.

  4. Add a message for context on what you’re sharing. This will be sent as a separate message in chats or as a note at the bottom in a status update.

  5. Tap Forward.

Note:

  • Forwarded channel updates will be labeled “Forwarded” and link back to the original channel.
  • Everyone can see the total number of forwards in a forward button below the update.
  • You can’t see the names of people who forward channel updates.

Forward a channel share link

You can share a link to a channel to your chats, status, and outside of WhatsApp.

  1. Tap Updates.
  2. Tap the channel > the channel name.
  3. To share within WhatsApp: Tap Forward and choose where to forward:
    • Chats: Select or search for the chats you want. Pick up to 5 individual or group chats.
    • Status: To forward to your status, tap My status.
    • Channels: If you’re a channel admin, search for your channel to forward to it. It will be labeled “Forwarded” and link back to the original channel. Learn more.
    • Tap Forward.
  4. To share outside of WhatsApp: Tap Share and choose where you’d like to share.

Note:

  • If an update or share link has already been forwarded you can forward it to five more chats, including a maximum of one group chat.
  • If an update has already been forwarded many times, you can only forward it to one chat at a time.

About how WhatsApp recommends channels

Copy link

When you explore or search for channels, we recommend channels based on things like:

  • Channel information including:

  • Channel updates

  • Number of followers

  • Reactions to channel updates

  • Frequency of channel updates

  • Similarity of content (channel name, channel info and channel updates) among popular channels

  • Your general location information (e.g. country/city) and language preference.

  • Device and connection information, such as your device type and app version.

  • Information about your activity on channels, including:

  • The types and content of channels you follow, view or interact with it.

  • The searches you make on channels.

  • The channels features you use and how you use them.

  • Your time spent and activities on channels.

We use this information, like your channel activity, to help us recommend channels that might be more relevant to you.

As always, your personal chats and calls remain end-to-end encrypted. They aren’t used to recommend channels.

You can see the channels recommended to you by:

  • iOS and Android: scrolling to the bottom of the Updates tab to view the Find channels to follow section.
  • Web and Desktop: scrolling to the bottom of the Channels or Updates page to view the Find channels to follow section.

Note:

  • Some channels may pay to promote their channel. These promoted channels are clearly labeled as “Ad”. Learn more about ads on WhatsApp in Channels.

How to invite and dismiss channel admins

On iPhone

Copy link

Android

iOS

Web

More

Android

iOS

Web

As a channel owner, you can invite up to 16 admins at a time to help you manage your channel and channel updates. You can invite anyone from your contacts. Any admin can choose to dismiss themselves (see instructions below).

When inviting someone to be an admin, keep in mind:

  • Invited admins can see your phone number: When you invite someone to be a channel admin, the invitation is sent as a chat message from your personal WhatsApp account, not your channel.
  • Any admin can make updates or manage channel info: Once an invitation is accepted, an admin can manage your channel info and create, edit, and delete any channel updates. Only you, as the channel owner, can delete the channel. Learn more about channel admin controls.
  • All admins should enable two-step verification: As the channel owner, encourage all admins to turn on two-step verification for their account to protect the security of your channel.

Note:

  • Channel admins who aren’t the owner can’t invite or dismiss additional admins.

  • As the channel owner, you can see the list of current admins at the top of your follower list on the channel info page. You can see the list of invited admins under {number} admins invited on the channel info page.

  • Channel invitations expire:

  • After seven days if not accepted

  • If accepted by the invited admin

  • If the invitation is revoked by the channel owner

You can invite, dismiss, and revoke invitations for channel admins from your channel info page.

To get to your channel info page:

  1. Go to the Updates tab.
  2. Tap your channel to open it.
  3. Tap your channel name.

How to invite channel admins

You can invite an admin by tapping on them from the follower list and tapping Invite as Channel Admin. Add a message to your invite and tap. Alternatively, you can:

  1. Tap Invite admins.

  2. Select the contacts you would like to invite to be admins, then tap Invite.

  3. Add a message to your invite, and tap

    [Image: Send (paper airplane within green circle)]

    to send it.

You can invite multiple admins at one time, and each invitation will open a separate chat between you and the invited admin. You’ll get a notification if the invitation is accepted.

To revoke an admin invitation, go to your channel info page. Under {number} admins invited, tap on an invited person and select Revoke Invite > Revoke. You can also revoke an invite from your chat with the invited person by tapping View invite > Revoke > Revoke.

How to dismiss channel admins

If you’re the channel owner: Tap the admin you want to dismiss, then select Dismiss as admin > OK.

If you’re a channel admin and want to dismiss yourself: At the bottom of the channel info page, tap Dismiss yourself as admin > Dismiss and unfollow or Dismiss > Dismiss.

Note:

  • The channel owner or admin will be notified whenever someone is dismissed by the owner or dismisses themselves.
  • The dismissed admin will remain a follower of the channel, unless they opt to unfollow the channel when dismissing themselves.

To listen to voice updates from a channel you follow:

  1. Go to the update.

  2. Tap

    [Image: Play (right-facing arrowhead)]

    .

Note:

  • Tap 1x while listening to a voice update to increase the playback speed to 1.5x or 2x.
  • To listen to a voice update from a specific point in the recording, tap and hold the dot located on the waveform, then drag it to the desired timestamp.
  • Voice updates will continue to play even if you go to another screen within WhatsApp.
  • When you play a voice update and leave the channel, a mini player will appear at the top of your screen. You can pause, play, and close the voice update from this mini player, or you can tap the channel name to go back to the original channel.

Voice update transcripts

You can convert voice updates into text transcripts for easy access. Voice transcripts are disabled by default and must be enabled.

To turn voice update transcripts on:

  1. Tap Settings or your profile picture, then tap Chats.
  2. Turn Voice Message Transcripts on.
  3. Tap Choose language, then select the language most of the voice messages you receive are in.
  4. Tap Change to {language}.

To see voice update transcripts, you must turn on Siri. Learn how to use Siri with WhatsApp.

Note: Supported languages depend on your OS:

  • iOS 16+ supports: English, Spanish, French, German, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, Russian, Turkish, Chinese, and Arabic.
  • iOS 17+ supports these additional languages: Danish, Finish, Hebrew, Malay, Norwegian, Dutch, Swedish and Thai.

To see voice update transcripts:

  • Turn on Voice message transcripts.

  • Tap and hold a voice update, then tap Transcribe.

  • Tap

    [Image: Open Close Menu (down chevron)]

    in the voice message to expand the transcription.

  • Ensure that your operating system is iOS 16 or newer and Siri is enabled. Learn how to use Siri with WhatsApp.

Learn more about voice update transcripts for WhatsApp Channels.

Keep in mind, channels are not end-to-end encrypted—so anything shared on a channel, including voice updates or transcripts, is public. You can learn more about who can see channel content here.

We’re rolling out channel subscriptions gradually to specific countries and channels, so it may not be available to you yet. We’re working to make it available to more people.

You can see channel subscription details, like renewal date, and cancel subscriptions in WhatsApp from the Updates tab. Payment methods can be viewed or changed on the Google Play or Apple App stores, depending on the device you used to subscribe.

How to see when your channel subscription renews

To see your renewal date on the channel info page:

  1. Tap the channel name or tap

    [Image: More (three horizontal dots)]

    Channel info.

  2. Tap Manage subscription.

How to manage the payment method for your channel subscription

You can view, update, or change your payment method used for your subscriptions by visiting the Apple App Store on the device you used to subscribe.

How to cancel your channel subscription

If you no longer wish to subscribe, you can cancel at any time. Channel subscriptions are month-to-month starting on the date of your original purchase.

When you choose to cancel your channel subscription:

  • You’ll still have access to seeing subscriber-only updates through the end of the current billing period.
  • You won’t be partially or fully refunded for your current billing period.
  • To avoid being charged for the next month, cancel your subscription at least 24 hours before your subscription renewal date. You can see your renewal date by going to the channel’s info page and then Manage subscription.

Cancelling your subscription doesn’t automatically unfollow the channel. Learn how to unfollow a channel.

To cancel your channel subscription:

  1. Tap on the channel name or tap

    [Image: More (three horizontal dots)]

    Channel info.

  2. Tap Manage subscription.

  3. Tap Cancel subscription. After you cancel, you’ll have access to your subscription until the listed “next payment date.”

You can also cancel your channel subscription from the Apple App store. Learn more in the Apple Help Center.

Note: Unfollowing a channel you’re subscribed to will automatically cancel your subscription.

Privacy at a Glance: Additional Information about using Status and Channels

Copy link

Note: Channel subscriptions are only available in certain countries and may not be available to you yet.

Status and Channels are a separate space from your personal chats and calls. When you use Status and Channels, we collect and process limited information about you. We hope this guide, together with our main Privacy at a Glance guide, will help you to understand what information we collect, what we do with it, and how your privacy rights work.

How does Status work?

Status is an optional feature for users to share and re-share ‘status updates’ like photos, videos, voice notes and text with their mutual contacts that last 24 hours. Status updates are end-to-end encrypted when shared on WhatsApp.

Note: Channel statuses are public. This means they can be seen and shared by anyone.

How does Channels work?

Channels is an optional, one-way public broadcasting feature which allows ‘admins’ to create their own channel and share ‘channel updates’ for others to view. Both followers and non-followers of a channel can view and react to channel updates.

Learn how to create a WhatsApp channel, how to find and follow WhatsApp channels, and about privacy and safety on WhatsApp channels.

Channels are public, which means if you create a channel, others may be able to find, follow, and view your channel and see your channel updates.

In some countries and for some channels, you can support your favorite channels by paying for a subscription. When you subscribe to a channel, you can access channel updates only for subscribers. Learn more about channel subscriptions here.

Additionally, in some countries, admins will be able to pay to promote their channel to other users. A promoted channel will show up higher in the Channels directory and will be shown to users who may be interested in that type of channel if we show you ads in Status and Channel.

Channels is separate from messaging on WhatsApp. Using channels has no impact on the privacy of your personal WhatsApp messages, which continue to be end-to-end encrypted.

Information we collect

When you use WhatsApp, we collect information from you as described in Privacy at a Glance. If you choose to use Status and Channels, we collect some additional information from you. This could be:

When you share a status update or view other users’ status updates:

  • How you use Status, like how often you share, reshare, view or react to status updates

If you’re a channel admin:

  • The name that you choose for your channel
  • Other information that you choose to add to the channel, such as a profile picture, a channel description, or links to other websites
  • Channel updates that you share, such as text or audio content, videos, photos, images, documents, links, gifs, stickers, and polls

If you’re a follower or a non-follower viewing channel updates:

  • Channels you follow
  • Your reactions to channel updates (for example, poll votes, emojis or questions)
  • Your language settings

If you’re subscribed to a channel where such features are available in your location:

  • Payment information related to your subscription, like your payment type and amount and time of payment
  • Subscription details, like when your subscription to a channel starts or when your monthly renewal is due

If we show you ads in Status or Channels:

  • How you interact with the ads you see, like whether you view or tap the ad, follow a promoted channel, or make a purchase on WhatsApp
  • How you interact with advertisers, like whether you send them a message after seeing an ad

If you add your WhatsApp account to Accounts Center:

  • Information from your other accounts in the same Accounts Center, which you can learn about here

For all Status and Channels users:

  • Your activity on Status and Channels such as which channels and channel updates you follow or review and your reactions to or engagement with channel updates and status updates
  • Usage information, such as which Status and Channels features and settings you use, your searches within the channels directory, and the date, time, frequency, and duraction or your activity on Status and Channels
  • Technical information relating to how well Status and Channels are working when you use them, such as crash data, performance logs, and error messages
  • User reports made by others about your channel, specific channel updates or status updates, or user reactions

Sharing your information

Your information may be shared by you, or by us, with other people or organizations when you use Status or Channels. For example:

  • It’s important to remember that channel updates shared by admins are public and can be seen by others. You should be careful about what information you share on channels. Anyone can take screenshots or make recordings of channel updates and send them to other people or post them in other places online. Learn more about safety and privacy on channels for admins.
  • Status updates can be seen by your audience. Status updates are end-to-end encrypted when shared on WhatsApp, but they too can be recorded or screenshotted and shown to others and can also be reshared.
  • Admins, subscribers, followers and non-followers who view channel updates can share links with other people and invite them to follow or view a channel. If these links are shared on other Meta Company Products or on other services, Meta and those services will receive information about the channel, such as the name, description, picture, and number of followers.
  • We work with other Meta Companies to help keep you safe when you use Status and Channels. For example, this could be to help protect you against harmful conduct or to investigate possible violations of our policies or the law. We also share information with other Meta Companies to help us provide channels, as described in Privacy at a Glance.
  • If you’re a channel subscriber, we work with other companies like Google, Apple, and other Meta Companies to help you pay for your subscriptions.
  • If we show you ads on Status and Channels, we provide advertisers with reports about the performance of their ads. If you choose to add WhatsApp to Accounts Center, your ad preferences will apply and info from across your accounts will be used for ads. Learn more about WhatsApp in Accounts Center.
  • When you’re a channel follower or non-follower viewing channel updates, you’re not visible to other viewers or followers of that channel, and they can’t see how you interact with channel updates. This means they can’t see your name, phone number, or profile picture.
  • Channel admins may see your profile picture (if your privacy setting permits) and your profile name if you interact with their channel updates and questions. Channel admins can’t see your full phone number unless they have you saved as a contact.
  • Users who post status updates can see who views, reacts to them and also reshares them.
  • If you become an admin of a channel that has one or more admins, your phone number will be shared with the other channel admins. Learn more about safety and privacy on Channels.
  • If you have added your WhatsApp account to an Accounts Center with other Meta Company Product accounts, your information will be shared as described in this article.

What we do with your information

As described in Privacy at a Glance, we use your information in line with legal requirements. This could be:

  • To meet the terms of our contractual agreement with you
  • Where you have consented to us using your information
  • Where we believe we have a legitimate business reason that is not outweighed by any impact on your privacy rights
  • To protect the key interests of you and other people, including physical and mental health, well-being, and safety

How we use your information will vary depending on how you use Status and Channels. For example, this may include:

For all Status and Channels users:

  • Providing and improving the features, like enabling you to share, view and react to channel updates and status updates
  • Understanding how users are using Status and Channels
  • Detecting, preventing and investigating suspicious activity, harmful behavior, and breaches of our terms and guidelines
  • Personalizing your experiences on Status and Channels. For example, we show or recommend Channels and channel updates or display statuses (including your status music search) in an order that’s more relevant to you.

If you use Status:

  • Enabling you to share, reshare, view and react to status updates
  • Display statuses (including your status music search) to you in an order that might be more relevant to them. Learn more about Status here.

If you are a channel admin:

  • Enabling you to create and manage your channels and to share and edit channel updates. Learn how to edit channel updates and how to delete channel updates.
  • Providing you with access to information relating to your channel, such as the number of views of channel updates, reactions to channel updates, and your WhatsApp contacts following your channel.

If you are a follower or a non-follower viewing channel updates:

  • Enabling you to follow/unfollow, view, or mute/unmute a channel and to forward or react to channel updates.
  • Creating and maintaining a directory of channels by category, so that you can search for channels that might be of more interest to you.
  • Recommending and showing you channels that may be more relevant to you when you search or explore. Learn more about how WhatsApp recommends channels.

If you subscribe to channels where that feature has been made available in your location:

  • Facilitating your payments to pay for your channels subscriptions.
  • Managing your channel subscriptions start and end dates and to renew your subscription.

If we show you ads on Status and Channels:

  • Showing you ads based on information about you like your country and language, the channels you follow, and how you have interacted with ads in the past.
  • Measuring how you interact with ads, like whether you tap an ad or make a purchase on WhatsApp, and informing advertisers about how their ads are performing.

Your privacy rights

You have certain rights when we use your information in connection with using Status and Channels. You can find out more about these rights in Privacy at a Glance.

You can request a copy of your channels information or move this information using the ‘Request channels report’ option under the ‘Request account info’ feature (in WhatsApp, go to Settings > Account). You can also request a report with information about the ads you’ve seen in the same settings menu.

Learn more about how to manage channel info and settings and about ads on WhatsApp in Status and Channels.

If an admins deletes a channel, this will:

  • Remove the channel
  • Remove all channel updates from the admin’s WhatsApp account, which will no longer be accessible to other users
  • Cancel all subscriptions to that channel

Learn more about how to delete a channel.

Note: If other users have copies of channel updates on their device, or have forwarded the channel updates to other people, these will not be deleted when a channel is deleted. It is important to remember this when sharing or posting channel updates.

Thank you for using Status and Channels, we hope you’ve found this guide helpful.

You can find more details about your privacy rights and about how we use your information in our Teen Information Center, Privacy at a Glance and our Status and Channels Supplemental Privacy Policy.

How does channels work?

What we do with your information

You can react to channel updates with emojis.

When you react to updates, channel admins can see your profile name and, depending on your privacy settings, might be able to see your profile photo next to emoji reactions or poll votes.

People viewing a channel can see how many reactions an update has and the count of each type of emoji shared. They won’t see what emoji you chose.

You can view the number of reactions by tapping the emojis at the bottom of an update. It’s not possible to hide reactions or reaction counts.

How to react to channel updates

You can add or remove a reaction to updates made in the past 30 days.

  • Add a reaction: To add a reaction to an update, long press the update you want to react to, and tap to select one of the displayed emojis.
  • Change your reaction: You can change your reaction to a different emoji by long pressing the update you reacted to again and choosing a different one.
  • Remove a reaction: Remove a reaction from an update by long pressing the update you reacted to and tapping the emoji you reacted with to remove it.

Note:

  • You can only add one reaction per update.
  • Your reactions aren’t deleted when you leave a channel.
  • Admins can limit what emojis you can use to react in their channel.
  • Channel admins might see your reaction before you remove it or if removing it wasn’t successful. You won’t be notified if removing a reaction wasn’t successful.

If you believe Channel content is harmful or violates our policies, you can report the Channel or individual updates.

Report an individual update

  1. Tap

    [Image: Updates (circle within three part speech bubble)]

    .

  2. Open the channel.

  3. Tap and hold the update.

  4. Tap Report > Report.

  • Tap Report and unfollow to stop receiving updates from this channel.
  1. Tap Close.

Report a channel

  1. Open the channel.

  2. Tap

    [Image: More (three horizontal dots)]

    Report.

  3. Tap Report.

  • Tap Report and unfollow if you’d also like to stop receiving updates from this channel.
  1. Tap Close.

To track the status of reports, tap Settings or your profile picture, then tap Help and feedback > Channel reports. Reviews in progress are labeled Report in review. Completed reviews are labeled Report reviewed. Tap the report to view WhatsApp’s decision. Report review typically takes 24 hours. No one in the channel will know about this report nor is the admin notified of your request. Once a report is submitted, it can’t be cancelled. If the reported content doesn’t violate our Channels Guidelines, the channel will not be affected. Our Channels Guidelines describe the enforcement actions we may take.

If we take enforcement action against your channel, you can dispute our decision by requesting a review. Learn more about how to request a review for a closed channel.

File a dispute

If WhatsApp determines that a reported channel follows the Channels Guidelines, users in the European Region can also file a dispute with a Dispute Settlement Body using a reference number. To find your reference number and file a dispute:

  1. Tap Settings or your profile picture > Help and feedback.
  2. Tap Channel reports > Report reviewed > See options.
  3. Tap Refer to Dispute Settlement body > Continue > Get reference number.
  4. Copy the reference number and then tap Close.
  5. Choose a Dispute Settlement Body and navigate to the website of the one you choose.
  6. On their website, provide your reference number to the Dispute Settlement Body, and pay a processing fee if requested.

How to request a review for a closed channel

On iPhone

Copy link

Android

iOS

Web

Mac

More

Android

iOS

Web

Your channel might be closed if an update violates our Channel Guidelines. To help keep your channel open, you can follow our Channel Guidelines and local laws.

When your channel is closed, followers can’t see your channel history and you can’t share new updates.

Information about why your channel was closed

For more information, tap Channel alerts > Your channel is closed. On this page, you can see an explanation of why your channel is closed.

Under What you need to know, you can find additional resources like:

  • How to keep your channel open
  • How we made this decision
  • Information for people in the EU

You can reopen your channel by deleting the update, or you can request a review or submit an appeal to dispute the enforcement action.

Delete a reported update

You can delete an update that violates our Channel Guidelines.

  1. Open your channel.
  2. Tap Channel alerts > Your channel is closed.
  • If you don’t see Channel alerts, tap the channel name > Channel alerts > Your channel is closed.
  1. Tap Delete from channel > Delete. The update will be permanently deleted for all followers and your channel will be reopened.

Request review or submit an appeal

Channel admins can request a review or submit an appeal if you think your channel was closed by mistake.

  1. Open your channel.
  2. Tap Channel alerts > Your channel is closed > See options.

  • Request a review: Tap Request a review > Request review.

  • Submit an appeal: Tap Submit an appeal, then fill in the appeal form and submit.

If your dispute is successful, your update will be restored and your channel will be reopened.

To see the status of your request, tap Channel alerts > Update in Review or Update Review Completed.

File a dispute

Users in the European Region can also file a dispute with a Dispute Settlement Body using a reference number. To find your reference number:

  1. Open your channel.
  2. Tap Channel alerts > Your channel is closed > See options.
  3. Tap Refer to Dispute Settlement body > Continue > Get reference number.
  4. Copy the reference number and then tap Close.

Note:

  • All channel updates are removed from our servers after 30 days. This means that even if your channel is restored, your updates might not be available.
  • Review requests can only be submitted once per alert, and only channel admins can submit requests. While only one of the admin can submit the review request, all admins can see the progress.

Learn more about our Channel Guidelines.

You can delete an update that violates our Channel Guidelines.

  1. Open your channel.
  2. Click Channel alerts > Your channel is closed.
  • If you don’t see Channel alerts, click the channel name > Channel alerts > Your channel is closed.
  1. Click Delete from channel > Delete. The update will be permanently deleted for all followers and your channel will be reopened.

Request review or submit an appeal

Channel admins can request a review or submit an appeal if you think your channel was closed by mistake.

  1. Open your channel.
  2. Click Channel alerts > Your channel is closed > See options.

  • Request a review: Click Request a review > Request review.

  • Submit an appeal: Click Submit an appeal, then fill in the appeal form and submit.

If your dispute is successful, your update will be restored and your channel will be reopened.

To see the status of your request, click Channel alerts > Update in Review or Update Review Completed.

File a dispute

Users in the European Region can also file a dispute with a Dispute Settlement Body using a reference number. To find your reference number:

  1. Open your channel.
  2. Click Channel alerts >Your channel is closed > See options.
  3. Click Refer to Dispute Settlement body > Continue > Get reference number.
  4. Copy the reference number and click Close.

Note:

  • All channel updates are removed from our servers after 30 days. This means that even if your channel is restored, your updates might not be available.
  • Review requests can only be submitted once per alert, and only channel admins can submit requests. While only one of the admin can submit the review request, all admins can see the progress.

Learn more about our Channel Guidelines.

Note: Channel subscriptions are only available in certain countries and may not be available to you yet.

You can submit a request for a channels report to see your channels information.

The channels report will include information like:

  • A list of your followed channels
  • A list of your channel subscriptions (if applicable)
  • Notification settings for followed channels
  • Your interactions with channels, like emoji your reactions or poll votes

If you are the admin of any channels, the report will include information like:

  • Channel name, description, and profile picture
  • Number of followers
  • Verification status
  • Channel updates shared in the past 30 days
  • Channel subscription information

Request report

  1. Tap WhatsApp Settings or your profile picture, then tap Account > Request Account Info.
  2. Under Channels Activity, tap Request Channels Report. The screen will update to state Request Sent.

Your channels report will typically be available three days after the date you requested it. You can refer to the Ready by date while waiting for your report.

Parents and guardians

Depending on where you live, parents and guardians may have certain rights related to their minor’s data, for example:

  • The right to access, delete, or correct data, with some exceptions (for example, when we need to protect the safety, security or rights of others).
  • To provide parental or guardian consent on behalf of their minor.

If you are a parent or guardian of a WhatsApp user who is a minor, and you’d like to make a data privacy inquiry or request, please contact us through our privacy form.

Create reports automatically

You can request to automatically create a report every month.

  1. Tap WhatsApp Settings or your profile picture, then tap Account > Request Account Info.
  2. Under Channels Activity, toggle on Create Reports Automatically.

This will create a new channels report every month until you choose to turn off automatic reports.

Turn off automatic reports

  1. Tap WhatsApp Settings or your profile picture, then tap Account > Request Account Info.
  2. Under Channels Activity, toggle off Create Reports Automatically.

When you turn off automatic reports, you won’t receive a new channels report every month.

Note:

  • Once you request a channels report, you can’t undo or cancel your pending request.
  • If you change your phone number or delete your account, your pending request will be voided and you’ll have to request another report.
  • Your channels report does not include your account information and settings. To access your account information and settings, you can request a copy of your account report. Learn how to request your account information in this article.
  • If you uninstall WhatsApp, automatic reports are not created and you’ll need to turn automatic reports on.

Download and export report

When the report is available to download, you’ll receive a WhatsApp notification on your phone, stating “Your Channels report is now available”. The Request Channel Report screen in WhatsApp will tell you the amount of time you have to download the report before it’s deleted from our servers. Because this report contains your information, you should be careful about storing, sending, or uploading it to any other services.

  1. Tap WhatsApp Settings or your profile picture, then tap Account > Request Account Info.
  2. Tap Download Report. A ZIP file will be downloaded to your phone, which includes HTML and JSON files.
  3. Once the file is downloaded, tap Export Channels Report > Export Channels Report. You’ll be unable to view the downloaded report within WhatsApp.
  4. In the share tray that appears, tap the external app you want to export your channels report to. For example, you can email a copy of the report to yourself.

After you download the channels report to your phone, you’ll have the option to permanently delete the downloaded copy from your phone by tapping Delete Report > Delete Report on the Request Account Info screen. Deleting the report won’t delete any of your information relating to your activity and use of channels.

About safety and privacy on channels

Copy link

WhatsApp Channels help people get information they care about in a way that is private and secure.

There are controls in place to protect the privacy of channel followers, viewers and admins.

Please note, if you choose to become a channel admin, you’ll be visible to other admins within the channel you manage, even if they aren’t already contacts. Learn more about safety and privacy for channel admins here.

When you’re a channel follower or viewer (and not an admin of a channel):

  • You’re not visible to people viewing a channel, including other channel followers, and they can’t see how you interact with channel content. They can’t see your name, phone number, profile picture, reactions to channel content, or how you vote on polls (except admins, see more below).
  • Your contacts can’t see which channels you follow or how you interact with channel content (unless they are an admin of a channel you follow).

Your profile and channel interaction information may be visible to channel admins, but admins who aren’t contacts only see limited information (unless you choose to become a channel admin):

  • Admins can see your profile name and, depending on your profile settings, your profile photo and how you interact with their channel content.
  • Channel admins who’re also contacts can see all parts of your profile like your name, full phone number, and profile photo.

Channel updates are kept in a separate tab from your chats. As always, your personal messages and calls are protected with end-to-end encryption. No one outside of the chat, not even WhatsApp or Meta, can read, listen to, or share them.

Channel admins are responsible for maintaining an age-appropriate and safe experience for their followers. Anyone can report problematic content - whether they’re a follower or not. If you think a channel is sharing problematic content or spam, report it.

WhatsApp uses a combination of automated tools, manual review and user reports to detect potentially problematic content and reserves the right to take action on violating channels. Read more about the standards we have to keep channels safe in the WhatsApp Channel Guidelines.

About safety and privacy on channels for admins

Copy link

WhatsApp Channels help admins share updates and information with their followers in a way that is secure.

As a channel admin:

  • People see the channel, not you: Channel updates are sent from the channel, so followers and other viewers won’t see your WhatsApp profile name, picture, or your phone number. If you’re a channel owner and invite someone to be an admin, your full phone number, profile picture,depending on your privacy settings, and profile name is shared with the invitation.
  • Admins can see each other: To help admins work together and manage channels more easily, the owner and all admins of a channel can see each other’s phone number, profile picture (depending on your privacy settings), and name. This means other admins may contact you, such as through WhatsApp private messaging.

To help keep the channels you manage secure:

  • Don’t share personal information on a channel, like your full name or phone number, or the information of other admins.
  • All admins should turn on two-step verification for their WhatsApp accounts.

Note: All channels are publicly accessible. It’s not possible to create a private channel.

Channel updates are public, and you’re responsible for them

Remember, anything you share on a channel is public and will be visible to:

  • All followers: Followers can see all channel updates shared 30 days before they followed your channel.
  • People who don’t follow the channel: Anyone can see 30 days worth of update history on the channel.
  • WhatsApp: Channel updates are reviewed against the Channels Guidelines.

Channel updates should be used to share information with followers and viewers, not as a way for admins to communicate back and forth.

As a channel admin, you’re responsible for keeping the content on your channel safe, relevant, and age-appropriate for your followers. Learn more in the Channels Guidelines.

How to see channel metrics and insights

Copy link

As a channel owner or admin, you can see metrics and insights about your channel, like:

  • Growth, reach, and number of net follows
  • Additional info about followers
  • Emoji reactions and poll results

About channel insights

Channel insights are available from your channel info page and show detailed breakdowns of growth, reach, and followers.

Note:

  • Insights are in development and we’re testing to find the best way to measure and report them. As we learn more, we may make adjustments. We’ll remove the “in development” label once we’re done testing.
  • Reported numbers may be delayed by about a week.
  • All channel admins have access to available insights.
  • Channel insights aren’t available for channels with fewer than 100 followers.

In the Growth tab, you can see insights like:

  • Net follows: The number of follows minus the number of unfollows of your channel in the past 30 days. This includes unfollows resulting from WhatsApp account deletion.
  • Follows: The number of times WhatsApp accounts followed your channel in the past 30 days.
  • Unfollows: The number of times WhatsApp accounts unfollowed your channel in the last 30 days. This includes unfollows resulting from WhatsApp account deletion.

In the Reach tab, you can see insights like:

  • Accounts reached: The number of WhatsApp accounts who viewed any of your updates at least once in the past 30 days. The total:
    • Doesn’t include multiple views by the same account.
    • Includes admin views.
    • Includes both followers and non-followers.
  • Top regions: Regions with the highest concentration of reached WhatsApp accounts for your channel.
    • Up to 10 regions where your channel is the most popular.
    • A region only appears as a top region if your channel reaches more than 100 local accounts in the last 30 days.

In the Followers tab, see insights like:

  • Total followers: See how many followers you have and the percent of change over the last 30 days.
  • Top regions: See up to 10 regions with the highest concentration of your followers.

How to see reach, growth, and followers insights for your channel

Channel insights are available on the channel info page.

To get to your channel info page:

  1. Tap or click your channel to open it.
  2. Tap or click your channel name.
    • You can see the number of accounts reached and net follows for the past 30 days.
  3. Tap or click See all for a more detailed breakdown.
    • Tap or click Reach to see a detailed breakdown of the accounts and regions reached by your channel.
    • Tap or click Growth to see a detailed breakdown of your net follows for the last 30 days.
    • Tap or click Followers to see a detailed breakdown of your channel’s total followers.

How to see your follower list

The follower list is available on the channel info page.

To get to your channel info page:

  1. Tap or click your channel.
  2. Tap or click your channel name.

From the follower list you can:

  • See how many people follow your channel.

  • See followers and details about them like:

  • Profile name

  • Profile photo, depending on their privacy settings

  • Quickly interact with followers who are also your contacts — clicking on a contact will open a new private message in the Chats tab and messages will come from your WhatsApp profile, not your channel.

How to see reaction details for channel updates

On each channel update you can see how people reacted to it.

Emoji reactions: Tap and hold or click the update you want to see reaction details for to see:

  • Number of each type of emoji reaction.

  • Details about who reacted with emojis like:

  • Profile photos, depending on their privacy settings

  • Profile name

Poll votes: Tap and hold or click the poll to view the poll details like:

  • Number of votes for each option.
  • Details about who voted for each option like:
    • Profile photos depending on their privacy settings
    • Profile name
    • When they voted

Note: There are controls in place to protect the privacy of channel followers, viewers and admins. Learn more about safety and privacy on channels.

How to share a channel update

Copy link

Sharing updates through your channel is similar to how you might already use WhatsApp to send messages to your friends and family, but there are key differences.

Updates appear in a separate tab of the app, away from your personal chats and calls. Channel updates are a one-way broadcast rather than a conversation. Updates are always shared from your channel, and followers won’t see your name or phone number.

Most importantly, channels aren’t end-to-end encrypted.

Your updates are public

Anything you share is public and visible to:

  • All followers: Followers can see all channel updates, including updates shared 30 days before they began following your channel.
  • People who don’t follow your channel: Anyone can see channel updates from the past 30 days.
  • WhatsApp: Channel updates are reviewed against the Channels Guidelines.
  • People on other channels: If your update was forwarded to another channel.

Create updates to keep your channel followers engaged by:

  • Keeping written updates short, concise, and focused on a specific topic.
  • Providing helpful information like tips and tricks, time-saving hacks, or the latest how-to’s.
  • Sharing timely and up-to-date information.

You’re responsible for keeping the content on your channel safe, relevant, and appropriate for your followers. Learn more in our Channels Guidelines.

To use WhatsApp Web to manage your channel, you’ll have to first link the device you use for channels.

How to share updates

Share written notes to your followers

  1. From the Channels page, click your channel.
  2. Enter a written update. You can add:

  • Formatting: Add formatting like underline, bold, or strikethrough.

  • Emojis: Click

    [Image: Emoji (smiley face)]

    to open the emoji selection menu in WhatsApp.

  • Links: Enter a link to your update. The link appears with a preview of the content and an image, when available.

  1. When your update is ready, click

    [Image: Send (paper airplane)]

    .

You can also forward messages from chats to your channel. Learn how to forward a channel update to your channel.

Share media

  1. Click

    [Image: Add Item (plus sign)]

    to share images or video.

  2. Select:

  • Camera to take a picture or video with your computer’s camera.
  • Photos & Videos to select an existing photo or video from your computer. You can select multiple images.
  1. You can also:
  • Edit: Learn how to edit your photos and videos before sharing.
  • Add captions: Click the photo you want to add captions to each one.

  1. Click

    [Image: Send (paper airplane)]

    .

Note:

  • Followers can save any media you share.
  • You can’t share PDFs to your channel.

Share stickers

Click Stickers > Add to share a sticker to your channel. The sticker is shared to your channel immediately.

You can download more sticker packs or create your own stickers.

Share voice updates

  1. Clickand start speaking.

  2. Once finished, click

    [Image: Check (checkmark within circle)]

    .

  3. While recording an audio update, you can:

  • Click X to cancel it.

  • Click

    [Image: Pause (two parallel vertical lines within circle)]

    to pause recording or preview a draft of your update. Clickto continue recording.

Note: If the beginning of your audio updates aren’t being recorded, wait a second before speaking.

Channel polls and quizzes are easy ways to engage with your channel audience. Like all channel updates, polls are public and anyone using channels can vote on them.

Create a channel poll

  1. Tap Updates > your channel.

  2. Tap

    [Image: Attach (plus sign)]

    Poll.

  3. Tap Ask Question to enter your poll question. Questions are limited to 255 characters.

  4. Tap Add text or photo to enter up to 12 poll options. Options are limited to 100 characters.

  • Tap and hold

    [Image: Drag Item (three parallel horizontal lines)]

    to change the order of your poll options by sliding up or down.

  • Tap

    [Image: Gallery (photo with landscape)]

    to add a photo to an option.

  • To limit users to one vote, turn off Allow multiple answers.

  1. Tap Send.

Note:

  • You can delete a poll for up to 30 days.
  • You can’t edit polls, but you can delete them and create a new one.

Create a photo poll

You can add photos to your poll options to create eye-catching photo polls.

  1. Tap Updates > your channel.

  2. Tap

    [Image: Attach (plus sign)]

    Poll.

  3. Tap Ask Question and enter your poll question. Questions are limited to 255 characters.

  4. Tap Add text or photo to add text for each photo >

    [Image: Gallery (photo with landscape)]

    .

  5. Select a photo for each option, up to 12 total. Tap Next.

  6. Tap the photo previews to add captions and tap

    [Image: Check (checkmark within circle)]

    .

  7. To reorder your poll options, tap and hold

    [Image: Drag Item (three parallel horizontal lines)]

    and slide up and down.

  8. Tap Send.

Note: You can’t forward photo polls.

View channel poll details

Tap View votes to view the poll details.

As a channel admin, you can see responders profile name, when they voted, and profile photo depending on their privacy settings.

Share quiz to your channel

Challenge your followers by sharing multiple-choice quizzes to your channel.

  1. Tap Updates > your channel

  2. Tap

About the WhatsApp Channels Terms and Privacy Policy

Copy link

  • Channels are a one-way broadcast feature that anyone on WhatsApp can discover, follow, and view. In order to share public content with unlimited audiences, channels are not end-to-end encrypted.
  • Channel admins are responsible for maintaining an age-appropriate and safe experience for their followers, and their channels are reviewed against the Guidelines in our Terms.

WhatsApp keeps your privacy in mind:

  • Followers or viewers can’t see who else is following a channel.
  • Other followers or viewers can’t see your phone number. Admins of the channels that you follow can’t see your full phone number unless they have you saved as a contact.
  • Channels are optional and kept in a separate tab from your chats. As always, your personal messages and calls are protected with end-to-end encryption. No one outside of the chat, not even WhatsApp, can read, listen to, or share them.

Please note, if you choose to become a channel admin, you’ll be visible to other admins within the channel you manage, even if they aren’t already contacts. Learn more about safety and privacy for channel admins here.

Learn more about getting started with WhatsApp Channels.
