How to troubleshoot issues with channel subscriptions

Copy link

We’re rolling out channel subscriptions gradually, so it may not be available to you yet. We’re working to make it available to more people.

Use these tips to help troubleshoot or better understand issues with your channel subscription.

Channel subscription payment issues

Here are some common reasons you might face issues with payments for your channel subscription, and some steps to try to fix them.

Payment declined or failed

If your payment for a channel subscription failed or was declined, verify your payment details in the Google Play Store or Apple App Store.

Double check to make sure you:

  • Used a supported payment method.
  • Entered your payment information correctly.
  • Used a payment method that hasn’t expired.
  • Used a payment method with enough funds in your account to cover the subscription cost.

We recommend adding a second payment method to your Google Play Store or Apple App Store account as a backup. If your default payment method fails for any reason, your backup payment will be charged to keep your subscription active.

Note: Sometimes your financial institution may have declined your payment. If this happens, please contact your financial institution for more information.

Multiple charges and pending payments

Channel subscriptions are charged on a monthly basis and automatically renew every month. If you notice multiple charges in the same month, we recommend that you check the payment status. If your payment shows as “Pending,” this is likely an authorization hold from your financial institution that will drop off later.

Automatically canceled channel subscriptions

Your subscription may be automatically canceled if you:

  • Switch your number from WhatsApp Messenger to the WhatsApp Business App. Channel subscriptions aren’t available on the WhatsApp Business App yet.
  • Choose to unfollow a channel you subscribe to. You’ll still have access to your subscription until the end of the current month you paid for.
  • Delete your WhatsApp account.

Your subscription may also be canceled due to issues with the channel you subscribed to, like if a channel changes owners, decides not to offer subscriptions anymore, or gets suspended. In these cases, you’ll receive a refund for the current month and won’t be automatically charged again.

About voice update transcripts on Whatsapp Channels

On iPhone

Copy link

Android

iOS

More

Android

iOS

Right now we’re seeing issues with voice mail transcription. We’re working to fix it as soon as possible. In the meantime, we encourage you to keep WhatsApp updated on your device. Updates are released regularly and may contain fixes for bugs and other issues.

You can get text versions of voice updates on WhatsApp Channels for easy access by turning on voice transcripts.

Voice transcripts are off by default. Enable transcripts on your device to use it. Once enabled, you can read voice transcripts for both channel updates and personal voice messages. Learn more about voice transcripts for personal messages.

Voice updates on channels, like all channel updates, are public. Learn more about channel updates.

Note: Voice update transcripts aren’t supported for linked devices including WhatsApp Web, WhatsApp for Mac, and WhatsApp for Windows.

Turn voice update transcripts on

To see voice update transcripts, you must turn on Siri. Learn how to use Siri with WhatsApp.

  1. Tap Settings or your profile picture, then tap Chats.
  2. Tap Voice message transcripts > Choose Language.
  3. Select language and tap Set up now.

Alternatively, you can turn on voice update transcripts when you receive a voice update in one of your channels.

  1. Go to the voice update.
  2. Tap Get started > Choose language.
  3. Select your Transcript language.

Note:

  1. Voice update transcripts are disabled by default.
  2. If Siri isn’t turned on when you turn on voice update transcripts, you’ll need to download your transcript language.
  3. Currently supported languages depend on your OS:
    • iOS 16+ supports: English, Spanish, French, German, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, Russian, Turkish, Chinese, and Arabic.
    • iOS 17+ supports additional languages: Danish, Finish, Hebrew, Malay, Norwegian, Dutch, Swedish and Thai.

How to see voice update transcripts

  1. Turn on Voice message transcripts.
  2. Go to the voice update.
  3. Tap and hold the voice update > Transcribe.

Note: Your transcript might take a moment to process.

Some voice update transcripts might be inaccurate. If you receive a “Transcript unavailable” error, it might be because:

  • Your operating system is older than iOS 16.
  • Siri isn’t turned on. Learn how to use Siri with WhatsApp.
  • Your transcript language doesn’t match the language of the voice update.
  • Some words aren’t recognized, possibly due to background noise.
  • The voice message language isn’t supported.

How to vote on channel polls

Copy link

Responding to channel polls shows admins how you feel about topics in real-time. Anyone viewing a channel, including channel admins, can respond to polls.

People viewing or following a channel can only see how many people voted for each option.

Channel admins may be able to see limited profile information next to your vote:

  • Admins may view your profile photo next to your poll vote, depending on your privacy settings. Learn how to change your profile photo visibility and other privacy settings here.
  • If an admin has saved you as a contact, they can see the name they’ve assigned to you in their address book next to your vote.

How to respond to channel polls

  • To vote: Tap or click the options you want to vote for.
  • To remove a vote: Tap or click the option again.

Note:

  • If admins have turned off the option to select multiple answers, tapping or clicking an option will deselect any options that you previously selected.
  • You can’t copy channel polls.

About WhatsApp Channels

Copy link

Get information and relevant updates directly in WhatsApp by following channels. Follow the channels of people and organizations that interest you to get updates from them, including text, links to information, photos, and videos.

Channel updates appear in a separate tab of the app (the Updates tab), away from your personal chats and calls. While some features might feel familiar to WhatsApp chats, channel updates are a one-way broadcast rather than a conversation. Followers can’t reply directly to updates or send messages to channel admins. Instead, they can show their interest in a channel’s content by voting on polls or adding emoji reactions to channel updates.

Get the updates you want, when and how you want them

You can choose how you want to hear from the channels you follow:

  • Notifications are muted by default. To get notified about new updates, you can turn on notifications for each channel.
  • Channels appear in a separate tab, so you can choose to look at them when you want.
  • Follow people or organizations you’re interested in. You’re not automatically subscribed to channels. You can browse before you follow, and you can unfollow a channel at any time.

Note:

  • People viewing a channel can’t see who is following a channel. Your profile information and interactions with channel content, like emoji reactions or poll votes, aren’t visible to them. They can’t see your name, phone number, or profile picture.
  • Channel admins can see your profile name and, depending on your privacy settings, might be able to see your profile photo next to emoji reactions or poll votes.

Read more about safety and privacy on channels.

Chats and Messaging

About “Waiting for this message. This may take a while.”

Copy link

At times, you might see the above message in place of a message.

WhatsApp protects your personal messages and calls with end-to-end encryption. This means that only you and the person you’re communicating with can read, listen to, or share messages sent between you.

There are a few issues that might cause an incoming message to be replaced with “Waiting for this message. This may take a while.”

  • The message failed to deliver.
  • You or the sender recently reinstalled WhatsApp.
  • You or the sender aren’t using the latest version of WhatsApp.
  • You replaced your primary device and installed WhatsApp on a new device with the same number.

If you receive this message, there are a few troubleshooting steps you can try.

Get online

Ask the sender to open WhatsApp and make sure you’re both online at the same time.

Check your connection

Make sure you have a good internet connection. Try switching between Wi-Fi and mobile internet. If you have no Wi-Fi or a poor mobile internet connection, try moving to a different location.

Learn more about how to fix WhatsApp connection issues in this article.

Update WhatsApp

Make sure both you and the sender have the latest version of WhatsApp installed. Learn how to update WhatsApp in this article.

Ask the sender to resend the message

If the message failed to deliver, ask the sender to resend the message.

Switch to your primary device

Switch to your primary iOS or Android phone. This is the phone you used to register your WhatsApp account.

Note: You need to log in to your primary phone every 14 days to keep linked devices connected to your WhatsApp account.

Unlink and relink a linked device

Unlink and relink a linked device following the steps in this article.

Apply a chatlist filter

    [Image: Search (magnifying glass)]

About authentication messages

Copy link

Note:

  • This feature is currently only available to users in Brazil.
  • Card payments to businesses directly on WhatsApp have been discontinued as of January 15th, 2026. Learn more about making payments to businesses on WhatsApp.

Businesses on the WhatsApp Business Platform can send authentication messages that ask customers to verify their identities with a passkey. This helps businesses to streamline transactions that require sensitive personal or financial customer information.

About broadcast limits

Copy link

People in some countries might see a monthly broadcast limit. This feature is rolling out gradually and might not be available everywhere. If you do not yet see a limit on your broadcasts, you can find everything you need to know about broadcast lists in the main broadcast list article.

Broadcasts can help people receive important messages like holiday notes, daily greetings or event invites, but they can also be a source of overload. To help people manage the number of messages they get, you can only send a limited number of broadcasts per month.

Check your broadcast limit

  1. Tap

    [Image: More (three vertical dots)]

    Settings.

  2. Tap Broadcasts.

Note:

  • WhatsApp will notify you when you are about to reach the limit.
  • If you want to send more messages to more people, you can use status updates and channels to message many people at once.
  • Businesses can get more advanced messaging tools on the WhatsApp Business app.

Can’t send or receive messages

Copy link

Sometimes messages take a while to send or receive. Having a message in a single check mark state is normal.

There are many reasons why a message might take a while to be delivered or only display a single check mark:

  • You or your contact are having connection problems.
  • The other person’s phone might be turned off.
  • They might be out of the coverage area or roaming.
  • They might be out of data on their phone.
  • They might have seen a notification, but didn’t launch WhatsApp.
  • Their notifications might be slow or disabled.
  • They might have blocked you.

Steps to try

Here are some steps to try if your device can’t send or receive messages:

  • Update to the latest version of WhatsApp.
  • Try updating your phone’s operating system.
  • Make sure you’re connected to the internet.
  • Restart your device.
  • Make sure you’ve completed the verification process for your phone number.
  • Make sure you’ve saved your contact’s phone number in full international format on your device.

Can’t move chats from an Android device to an iPhone

Copy link

If you’re having issues moving your chats from an Android device to an iPhone, the most common reasons why are:

Device setup

Check the list below before moving chats:

  • Both devices are plugged in.
  • Both devices are connected to the same Wi-Fi.
  • Your iPhone is a new one or factory reset.
  • You’re using the same phone number on your old phone and new phone.
  • Android 5 or above is installed on your Android device.
  • iOS 15.5 or above is installed on your iPhone.
  • Move to iOS app is installed on your Android device.

WhatsApp is already active on my iPhone

You can only move your chats before you’ve activated WhatsApp on your iPhone. If you want to retrieve your old chat history:

  1. Factory reset your iPhone.
  2. Reinstall WhatsApp on your Android device.
  3. Start a new transfer with the Move to iOS app on your Android device.

Note: You can’t merge new chats from your iPhone with old chats from your Android device.

My iPhone has a different phone number

It’s not possible to move your chats to a new phone number. You first need to change your phone number on your Android device to your new number before moving chats to your iPhone. Learn how here.

Error messages

If you receive the error message “Something went wrong,” unfortunately this means your chat history may be corrupted. You have the options to either Retry or Skip Import.

If you receive the error message “An unknown error occurred. Please try again later,” your chat history may be corrupted. We recommend restarting both phones and trying again.

If while moving your chats, importing stops before completion, you’re likely experiencing a connection error. Get help here.

Verification issues

If you’ve attempted to move your chats multiple times and are experiencing wait times for a verification code, there’s no way to speed up the process. You may be able to receive a code by email. Learn more here.

Can’t scan QR code or receiving Invalid QR code error

If you’re unable to scan the QR code, we recommend:

  • Increasing your iPhone’s brightness to maximum.
  • Cleaning your Android device’s camera.
  • Checking that you’re scanning the correct QR code.
  • Removing any screen protectors from your iPhone.

Move to iOS app force quit, failed, or canceled

Please contact Apple Support with issues using the Move to iOS app.

Note:

  • Using any other apps to move chats isn’t supported and may cause loss of chats.
  • You can’t move chats to or from the WhatsApp Business app using this feature.
  • If the process completes successfully but not all chats were moved, unfortunately we are unable to retrieve them for you.

Can’t move chats from an iPhone to an Android device

Copy link

If you’re having issues moving your chats from an iPhone to an Android device, the most common reasons why are:

Device setup

Check the list below before moving chats:

  • Both devices are plugged in.
  • Both devices are connected to the same stable Wi-Fi.
  • Your Android device is a new one or factory reset with Android 10 or above.
  • The latest WhatsApp Android version available in the Google Play Store is installed on your phone.
  • iOS 15.5 or above is installed on your iPhone.
  • You’re using the same phone number on your old phone and new phone.

WhatsApp is already active on my new device

You can only move your chats before you’ve activated WhatsApp on your Android device. If you want to retrieve your old message history:

  1. Factory reset your Android device.
  2. Reinstall WhatsApp on your iPhone.
  3. Start a new transfer.

Note: You can’t merge new chats from your Android device with old chats from your iPhone.

My Android device has a different phone number

It’s not possible to move your chats to a new phone number. You’ll first need to change your phone number on your iPhone to your new number before moving chats to your Android device. Learn how here.

How do I transfer from an iPhone to an Android device?

Follow these steps to transfer from an iPhone to an Android device.

What messages can I transfer to my new phone?

You can transfer:

  • Personal messages

You can’t transfer:

  • Peer to peer payment messages

Error messages

If you receive the error message “Something went wrong with your chat history,” unfortunately this means your chat history is corrupted and can’t be moved to your Android device.

If you receive the error message “Could not import,” your chat history may be corrupted, but you can retry the process.

If while moving your chats, importing stops before completion, you’re likely experiencing a connection error. Get help here.

Verification issues

If you’ve attempted to move your chats multiple times and are experiencing wait times for a verification code, there’s no way to speed up the process. You may be able to receive a code by email. Learn more here.

Samsung Smart Switch or Google’s Data Restore Tool force quit or failed

We’re unable to resolve issues with third party apps. Please contact Samsung or Google for support.

Can’t scan QR code

If you’re unable to scan the QR code, we recommend:

  • Increasing your Android device’s brightness to maximum.
  • Cleaning your iPhone’s camera.
  • Checking that you’re scanning the correct QR code.
  • Removing any screen protectors from your Android device.

Can’t record voice messages

Copy link

If you’re unable to record voice messages, try these steps to fix the issue:

Check your connection

You must be connected to a Wi-Fi or cellular network to record and send voice messages. Try connecting to mobile data if you’re on Wi-Fi or Wi-Fi if you’re on mobile data. We also recommend restarting your phone. If you’re still having issues, contact your mobile provider for assistance.

Update WhatsApp

Make sure you’re updated to the latest version of WhatsApp on Google Play for Android and the Apple App Store for iPhone. Latest versions contain the newest features and bug fixes. Learn how to manually update WhatsApp here.

Check your phone’s proximity sensor

WhatsApp uses your phone’s proximity sensor to play audio through the earpiece when you’re holding your phone to your ear. However, some screen protectors and cases can disrupt this. Remove any screen protectors or cases and try recording your voice message again.

Check permissions

You can’t record a voice message if WhatsApp doesn’t have permission to use your microphone. You can change this in your phone’s settings.

Check Bluetooth pairing

Your voice message might be playing on a connected Bluetooth device. If there’s no wired audio device plugged into your phone, go to your phone’s settings and disable Bluetooth connectivity.

Free up storage space

You may not have enough space on your phone to record your voice message. You can free up storage space by deleting items. To check how much storage space you have available, and review and delete items, read this article.

How to create and send a marketing message

Copy link

Marketing messages is now business broadcasts in some countries. Business broadcasts might not be available to you yet. If you’re seeing business broadcasts, please refer to this article.

Marketing messages are especially good for keeping your existing customers engaged with offers, deals and promotions, but you can create and send marketing messages for other communications: sharing new items, announcements, thanking customers and asking for their feedback, or even sending appointment reminders or birthday greetings.

[Embedded video omitted]

0:00 / 2:48

Getting started

  1. Tap

    [Image: shopping (storefront)]

    Marketing messages

If this is your first time using marketing messages, you’ll see an intro screen. Tap Get started to begin your first message.

If you’re coming back to marketing messages, you’ll go straight to your list of previous messages and drafts. Tap the plus sign to start creating a new one.

Creating a message

When creating a message, you first edit its draft. This involves adding media, text, and an action button, and picking the audience to whom you want to send the message.

Add photos or video media

You can enhance your message by adding a photo or video to it. All messages require at least a photo.

  1. In the Edit draft screen, tap Add media:
  • From your media library: Choose an image from your device.
  • From your catalog: Choose a product image from your catalog.
  • From your archived statuses: Use a previous status update. Learn more about archived status updates here.
  • Recently shared: Choose a previously shared photo or video again.

  1. Tap

    [Image: Alternate Checkmark (white checkmark within circle)]

    to insert the image into your message > Next step.

Add text and customer names

  1. Tap Add text if you want to enter text for your message.

You can make your message feel more personal and engaging by having it automatically show each contact who receives it their own name:

  • For example, you could say:

    Hi {receiver name}, we would love to see you again! Get 10% off on your next purchase with coupon code SS10.

  1. Tap

    [Image: Alternate Checkmark (white checkmark within circle)]

    to add the text to your message.

Add an action button

Your message can contain a button to let customers take certain actions:

  • View catalog: Tapping this takes customers to a selected catalog item or your entire catalog.
  • Tap to reply: This allows customers to respond to your message with a single tap that will send you a message you pre-filled.
  • Phone call: This lets customers tap to call you at your business’s phone number.
  • Website: Tapping this takes customers to a website of your choice, such as your business website.

Message preview

While you’re creating your draft, you can see how the message will look to those who will receive it - simply tap Preview. To go back to editing the draft, tap Edit.

When you’re done creating your draft and are ready to choose your audience, tap Next.

Note: Your messages are subject to review by Meta

To help keep WhatsApp users safe, your marketing messages are subject to review by Meta before you send them in WhatsApp chats. Meta can’t access your messages once they’re sent in chats on WhatsApp.

Select audience

There are several ways to select the contacts to whom you want to send your marketing message. On the Select audience screen, you’ll see pre-populated lists:

  • Your full contact list from your address book, and from your various broadcast lists.
  • Lists: Send your message to select contacts by selecting the relevant list.

You can add everyone in from any of these lists with a single tap, or choose individual contacts from any or all of them for your message.

When you’re done selecting your audience, tap

[Image: New Chat Arrow (right arrow within square)]

to review and pay for and send or schedule your message.

Review and send or schedule your message

Review your message, its pricing, and the audience you selected. You can edit your draft by tapping it at the top of the screen. You can modify the audience by tapping the audience row. If you’re ready, you can send or schedule the message; you’ll be charged when you do so (you’ll be refunded for any contacts to whom the message can’t be delivered).

To send your message, tap Send.

To schedule your message to automatically send at a later time, tap Schedule. On the Schedule screen, select a date > tap OK > select a time > tap OK > Done.

Note: Your device must be connected to the internet at the time your message is scheduled to send. If it isn’t connected, the app will attempt to send your message after one minute, and then every 10 minutes. The app will try to send your message up to 10 times.

Paying for marketing messages

To send marketing messages, you need to have added a payment method and added some available funds to your account. You will only pay for successfully delivered messages, but we will reserve an amount in your account equal to the total number of contacts you initially select. Your available funds will be credited for any messages that cannot be delivered successfully.

To add a payment method:

  1. Enter your email address > tap Send code. You’ll receive a six-digit code at this email address.
  2. Enter the six-digit code.
  3. Select your country or region, currency, and time zone > tap Next.
  4. Add a payment method > tap Save.
  5. Enter the required information, such as your email or business address.
  6. Review your estimated total and add a payment method.

If a message can’t be delivered, funds will be credited back to your account for future use. Learn more about how payments for marketing messages work in this article.

Processing

When you send or schedule your message, there may be a slight processing delay. This is typically no more than a few seconds, but could be as long as 3 hours.

About sending spam

WhatsApp will be monitoring reports of messages marked as spam. Businesses must provide all necessary data disclosures and notices (such as maintaining a privacy policy or labeling marketing messages) and secure all necessary rights, consents, and permissions (for example, opt-in) to communicate with its customers via WhatsApp as stated in the WhatsApp Business Terms of Service. Businesses must also honor and comply with all customer requests to stop or opt-out of receiving certain or all types of WhatsApp messages from the business.

Failure to comply with the Meta Terms for WhatsApp Marketing Messages Features, which incorporate the WhatsApp Business Terms of Service, may result in temporary or permanent suspension of your account’s access to the marketing messages feature. Follow our best practices to create a quality experience and avoid any inconvenience.

Add to a sticker pack

  1. Tap

    [Image: Edit Sticker (pencil)]

    .

  2. Select the stickers you’d like to add.

  3. Tap

    [Image: More (three horizontal dots)]

    Add to sticker pack.

  4. Select an existing sticker pack or tap New to create a new one.

  • For a new sticker pack, enter the Sticker Pack name, then tap Create.

Upload stickers

Stickers must meet the following requirements to be uploaded.

Static sticker requirements

  • The maximum image file size is 100KB.
  • Sticker media files can be both .png or .webp
  • Each sticker pack must have between 3 and 30 stickers
  • Each sticker image must be 500x500 px
  • Emojis are optional
  • Each sticker must have max 2 emojis

Animated sticker requirements

  • Max sticker size = 500KB
  • Every sticker in the pack must be animated, you can share up to 30 stickers in a pack
  • Frame rate should be less than 125 frames per second (each frame should animated for more than 8 ms)
  • Total duration of animation should not last more than 10 seconds
  • Stickers should be 512 x 512 in pixels

Share your sticker pack

You can also share your sticker packs directly in the chat.

  1. Open an individual or group chat.

  2. Tap

    [Image: Stickers (square with folded corner)]

    .

  3. Tap

    [Image: More (three horizontal dots)]

    .

  4. Tap Send.

Note: WhatsApp stickers must be legal, authorized, and acceptable. Learn more about acceptable uses of our services in our Terms of Service.

Delete an individual chat

  1. In the Chats tab, swipe left on the chat you want to delete.
  2. Tap More > Delete chat > Delete chat.

Alternatively, tap

[Image: More (three vertical dots within a circle)]

Select chats. Select the chats you wish to delete, then tap Clear > Clear all messages.

Delete a group chat

To delete a group chat, you first need to exit the group:

  1. In the Chats tab, swipe left on the group chat you want to delete.
  2. Tap More > Exit group > Exit group.
  3. Swipe left on the group chat and tap More > Delete group > Delete group.

Note: If a group is part of a community, you can find that group by tapping on the community. You can also search for it by typing the group name into the search bar.

Delete all chats at once

  1. Tap your profile picture, tap Chats > Delete all chats.
  2. Enter your phone number and tap Delete all chats.

Individual chats will be deleted from your Chats tab. However, group chats will still be visible in your Chats tab, and you’ll still be part of them unless you exit them.

Note: When you delete a chat, it can’t be undone. WhatsApp is unable to recover deleted chats for you. You can only recover deleted chats if your latest backup occurred prior to deleting a chat. Please be aware that you’ll lose any chats that occurred after the latest backup.

How to delete chats from your old phone

Copy link

When you register your phone number on a new phone, you will be logged out of WhatsApp on your old phone. However, your chats will remain on the device. To help keep your chats private, you can delete your chats on your old phone.

Note: Before deleting, make sure you transfer your chats or recover your chat history from backup.

Delete chats on old phone

  1. Register your phone number on your new phone.
  2. Open WhatsApp on your old phone.
  • You’ll see “You have been logged out.”
  1. Tap Delete chats.
  2. Check the box and tap Delete chats.

How to delete messages

On iPhone

Copy link

Android

iOS

Web

Windows

Mac

More

Android

iOS

Web

Windows

Mac

Note: This article explains how to delete individual messages. To delete an entire conversation, view this article.

You can delete messages you sent just for yourself or request that messages be deleted for everyone. If you want to edit a message instead, you can for up to 15 minutes after sending.

When you delete a message, there’s no way to get it back unless you’ve included the message in a backup.

Delete messages for everyone

Deleting messages for everyone allows you to delete specific messages you’ve sent to an individual or group chat. This is particularly useful if you sent a message to the wrong chat or if the message you sent contains a mistake. Group admins can remove problematic messages sent by other members in the chat.

Messages you’ve sent that are deleted for everyone will be replaced with:

“This message was deleted”

To delete messages you’ve sent for everyone

To delete messages you sent:

  1. Open WhatsApp and go to the chat containing the message you want to delete.

  2. Tap and hold the message > choose Delete from the menu. Optionally, select more messages to delete multiple messages at once.

    • If prompted, tap

      [Image: More (three horizontal dots)]

      choose Delete from the menu.

  3. Tap

    [Image: Delete Message (trash can)]

    Delete for Everyone.

Group admins can delete messages sent by another group member. This enables admins to manage their private groups and communities by deleting inappropriate messages or media for all members. When an admin deletes a message for everyone, it will be replaced with:

“This message was deleted by admin [admin name]”

To delete a message sent by another group member

Group admins can delete messages sent by other group members:

  1. Open WhatsApp and go to the chat containing the message you want to delete.

  2. Tap and hold the message.

  3. Tap Delete >

    [Image: Delete Message (trash can)]

    Delete for Everyone > Delete.

Note:

  • You and the message recipients must be using the latest version of WhatsApp.
  • Recipients using WhatsApp for iOS might still have media you sent saved to their Photos, even after the message is deleted from the WhatsApp chat.
  • Recipients might see your message before it’s deleted or if deletion wasn’t successful.
  • You won’t be notified if deleting for everyone wasn’t successful.
  • You have two days after you’ve sent a message to request to Delete for Everyone.
  • Only group admins can delete messages sent by other group members.
  • Group admins have two days after someone else sends a message to request to Delete for Everyone.
  • Group members will be able to see which admin chose to Delete for Everyone.
  • Messages deleted by a group admin are not recoverable and can’t be appealed.
  • When you delete a message for yourself or for everyone in a chat, the deletion will sync across all online devices where you are logged into WhatsApp.

Delete messages for yourself

You can delete your copy of messages you’ve sent or received from your phone. This has no impact on your recipients’ chats. Your recipients will still see the messages in their chat screen.

  1. Open WhatsApp and go to the chat containing the message you want to delete.

  2. Tap and hold the message > then tap Delete >

    [Image: Delete Message (trash can)]

    Delete for Me. Optionally, select more messages to delete multiple messages at once.

Note: After choosing Delete for Me, you have 5 seconds to undo this action by pressing Undo before the message is permanently deleted. After 5 seconds, you can’t recover the deleted messages. Please be advised that WhatsApp is unable to recover deleted messages for you.

Delete media from a chat

You can delete your copy of media you’ve sent or received from your phone. This has no impact on your recipients’ chats. Your recipients will still see the media in their chat screen.

  1. Tap and hold the media file.

  2. Tap Delete >

    [Image: Delete Message (trash can)]

    .

  3. After selecting the first message, you can select other messages to delete before tapping

    [Image: Delete Message (trash can)]

    .

  4. Tap Delete for everyone.

There’s no way to delete all media from a chat in one step. The easiest way to delete multiple media is to do the following:

  1. Open the chat.

  2. Tap the name of the chat to enter the chat info screen.

  3. Tap Media, Links, and Docs.

  4. Tap Select.

  5. Tap any media to add it to your selection.

  6. Tap

    [Image: Delete Message (trash can)]

    Delete for everyone.

  • Only group admins can delete messages sent by other group members.
  • Group admins have two days after someone else sends a message to request to Delete for everyone.
  • Group members will be able to see which admin chose to Delete for everyone.
  • Messages deleted by a group admin are not recoverable and can’t be appealed.
  • When you delete a message for yourself or for everyone in a chat, the deletion will sync across all online devices where you are logged into WhatsApp.

Delete messages for yourself

You can delete your copy of messages you’ve sent or received from your phone. This has no impact on your recipients’ chats. Your recipients will still see the messages in their chat screen.

  1. Open WhatsApp and go to the chat with the message you want to delete.

  2. Click

    [Image: Menu (down chevron)]

    within your chat message.

  3. Click Delete > Delete > Delete for me.

Note: After choosing Delete for me, you have 5 seconds to undo this action by clicking Undo before the message is permanently deleted. Please be advised that WhatsApp is unable to recover deleted messages for you.

Delete media from a chat

You can delete your copy of media you’ve sent or received from your device. This has no impact on your recipients’ chats. Your recipients will still see the media in their chat screen.

  1. Hover over the media file and then click

    [Image: Menu (down chevron)]

    .

  2. Click Delete > Delete.

  3. Click Delete for me.

There’s no way to delete all media from a chat in one step. The easiest way to delete multiple media is to do the following:

  1. Open the chat.

  2. Click the name of the chat to enter the chat info screen.

  3. Click Media, Links, and Docs.

  4. Select any media to add it to your selection.

  5. Click

    [Image: Delete Message (trash can)]

    Delete for everyone > Delete for everyone.

Design custom stickers

You can create your own custom stickers from a photo or using AI and package them in an app to be published in the Apple App Store. Once your app is published, users can download and install the app to use your sticker pack in WhatsApp.

You can drop in your sticker art and build an app with minimal development or coding experience. Advanced developers can also make richer sticker apps using the set of APIs and interfaces that WhatsApp supports. Refer to the README files associated with the sample apps for requirements and tips when creating your sticker app.

Note: When creating an iOS sticker app, develop a unique user interface (UI) and don’t use our sample apps’ UI. A unique user interface (UI) is required to comply with the Apple App Store Review Guidelines.

Custom stickers must meet the following requirements:

  • Each sticker has a transparent background.
  • Stickers must be exactly 512x512 pixels.
  • Each sticker must be less than 100 KB.

If you want to create a custom sticker with AI, refer to this article.

Provide an icon to represent your sticker pack in the WhatsApp sticker picker or tray. This image should be 96x96 pixels and must be less than 50 KB.

In addition to the requirements above, we strongly recommend the following:

  • Stickers will render on a variety of backgrounds, including white, black, colored, and patterned. We recommend adding an 8-pixel #FFFFFF stroke to the outside of each sticker. View a sample Photoshop (PSD) file here.
  • There should be a 16-pixel margin between the sticker image and the edge of the 512x512 pixel canvas.

Note: WhatsApp stickers must be legal, authorized, and acceptable. Learn more about acceptable uses of our services in our Terms of Service.

You can learn how to create and share your own sticker packs in this article

As an advanced security measure, you can turn on Disable link previews. If you turn on Disable link previews, the links you send to others won’t generate a link preview. We’re currently experiencing a problem with chats appearing out of order on some iOS devices, including iPhones. We’re working on fixing it at the moment. In the meantime, we recommend keeping WhatsApp updated to the latest version available in the app store on your device. Updates are released regularly and may contain fixes for bugs and other issues.

Here are some ways you can fix common problems with the timestamp on your WhatsApp messages. A timestamp indicates the time a message was sent or received.

If the timestamp on messages you’ve sent or received is wrong, please check the time and time zone configuration on your device and adjust them.

This can also help to fix incorrect last seen times.

Setting date and time

We recommend setting your date and time to Set Automatically. This means your mobile provider will set your phone to the correct time.

  1. Go to device Settings.
  2. Tap General > Date & Time.
  3. Turn on Set Automatically.

Configure your time zone

You can also modify your date and time settings and correct your time zone manually.

Visit the Apple support website for instructions.

WhatsApp allows you to format text inside your messages. Please note, there’s no option to disable this feature.

Italic

To italicize your message, place an underscore on both sides of the text:

_text_

Bold

To bold your message, place an asterisk on both sides of the text:

*text*

Strikethrough

To strikethrough your message, place a tilde on both sides of the text:

text

Monospace

To monospace your message, place three backticks on both sides of the text:

text

Bulleted list

To add a bulleted list to your message, place an asterisk or hyphen and a space before each word or sentence:

* text

* text

Or

  • text

  • text

Numbered list

To add a numbered list to your message, place a number, period, and space before each line of text:

  1. text

  2. text

Quote

To add a quote to your message, place an angle bracket and space before the text:

text

Inline code

To add inline code to your message, place a backtick on both sides of the message:

text

Alternatively, you can use shortcuts. Double tap the text you’ve entered in the text field > Format. Choose Bold, Italic, Strikethrough, or Monospace.

The forward feature allows you to forward messages from an individual or group chat to another individual or group chat. Forwarded messages are indicated with a “Forwarded” label, which helps you know if your friend or family member wrote the message they sent or if the message originally came from someone else.

You can forward a message with up to five chats at one time. If a message has already been forwarded, you can forward it to up to five chats, including a maximum of one group chat. When a message is forwarded many times, it can only be forwarded to one chat at a time.

About forwarding limits

Copy link

You can forward messages to up to five people or groups at a time.

If you’re forwarding a message or update that was forwarded to you, it can only be shared with one additional group chat.

If a message or update is forwarded through a chain of five or more chats it will:

  • Be labeled as: “Forwarded many times.”

  • Show the

    [Image: Frequently Forwarded (two overlapping right arrows with curved tails)]

    icon.

This helps keep conversations on WhatsApp intimate and personal. This also limits and helps prevent spamming and misinformation.

If you want to share content with multiple users in your network, we suggest creating a group chat or sharing links. Learn about creating a group.

Forwards and end-to-end encryption

WhatsApp messages contain a counter that keeps track of how many times a message is forwarded. This counter is end-to-end encrypted, so WhatsApp can’t tell how many times a message is forwarded. End-to-end encryption means only yours and the recipient’s device can access this information.

As always, WhatsApp can’t see the content of any of your personal messages in end-to-end encrypted chats. While channel updates are public, when you choose to forward them to individual and group chats, these forwarded updates are end-to-end encrypted.

You can forward messages to Meta AI to ask questions or learn more. Meta AI can only read messages people share with it. Meta can’t read any other messages in your personal chats, as your personal messages remain end-to-end encrypted.

Learn more about end-to-end encryption.

Troubleshooting issues with forwarding limits

If you’re having issues with forwarding messages and haven’t reached the forwarding limit, we recommend you:

  • Restart your phone, or turn it off and on.
  • Update WhatsApp to the latest version.
  • Update your phone to the latest version.
  • Try connecting to mobile data if you’re on Wi-Fi or Wi-Fi if you’re on mobile data. If that doesn’t work, try these connection troubleshooting steps.

Getting started on WhatsApp

Copy link

Messaging on WhatsApp is by its nature private and our Privacy at a Glance provides details about how we use your information and help keep our service and users safe.

When you join WhatsApp, you must meet the minimum age of use requirements. We encourage you to review these guidelines on how to use WhatsApp responsibly.

You must be at least 13 years old (or such greater age required in your country) to register for and use WhatsApp.

You’re in control

It’s important to us that you know how to control your own privacy when using WhatsApp. You can change your privacy settings at any time. You can also use privacy checkup directly in your app by going to your Settings > Privacy to manage your privacy settings.

About harvesting personal information

Copy link

Harvesting information at scale, also known as scraping, through the use of an automated tool for any unpermitted purpose violates the WhatsApp Terms of Service. Scrapers might attempt to search for and save users’ information. This can include phone numbers, user profile pictures, and statuses from the WhatsApp platform.

Accounts could be temporarily or permanently banned if suspected of scraping personal information from WhatsApp. For more information on how to use WhatsApp responsibly, read this article.

Keeping WhatsApp Users Safe in Indonesia

Copy link

WhatsApp is an industry leader among end-to-end encrypted messaging services in preventing abuse and promoting online security. At WhatsApp, the safety of our users is at the core of everything we do.

WhatsApp has made significant product changes to help enhance security and privacy. Besides continuous product innovations, over the years we have also consistently invested in state-of-the-art technology, artificial intelligence, data scientists, experts, and in processes, to support user safety.

The private nature of WhatsApp

Privacy and security is in our DNA, which is why we built end-to-end encryption into our app in 2016. When end-to-end encrypted, your messages, photos, videos, voice messages, documents, status updates and calls are secured to help protect them from falling into the wrong hands.

End-to-end encryption helps ensure only you and the person you’re communicating with can read, listen to, or share what is sent, and nobody in between, not even WhatsApp. This is because with end-to-end encryption, your messages are secured with a lock, and only the recipient and you have the special key needed to unlock and read them. All of this happens automatically with no need to turn on any special settings to secure your messages.

Preventing abuse in Indonesia

WhatsApp has no direct visibility into the content of personal messages sent on our service. Hence, we rely on behavioral signals from accounts and available unencrypted information including user reports, profile photos, group photos and descriptions. We deploy a combination of security measures and processes to help keep our users safe. We apply spam detection technology to spot and take action on accounts engaging in abnormal behavior to stop spam.

Resources for WhatsApp users in Indonesia, including how to submit complaints or reports of abuse, can be found here (contact_id@meta.com). Users in Indonesia can also submit reports via the Ministry of Trade’s WhatsApp chat (+62 853 1111 1010) or the Ministry of Communications & Informatics (Kominfo) reporting line (aduankonten.id).

Working with law enforcement

WhatsApp continues to work closely with law enforcement agencies and carefully reviews law enforcement requests based on applicable laws and our policies. In coordination with the Government of Indonesia we have provided law enforcement training on how to use WhatsApp to respond to citizens and to make legal requests in the process of investigating a crime. More information on the process can be found here.

Product features to keep you safe

  • Two-step verification: We recommend users add an extra layer of security to their WhatsApp account by enabling two-step verification, which requires a six-digit PIN for resetting and verifying your WhatsApp account, in the event of your SIM card being stolen or your phone being compromised.
  • Block and report: Unlike traditional SMS, WhatsApp provides a simple way for users to block accounts and make reports to WhatsApp if they encounter problematic messages. We encourage users to report problematic contacts to us. In addition, we now provide the option for users to keep reported messages on their phone if they want to share them with fact checkers or law enforcement officials. Users can also now report accounts to WhatsApp by flagging a specific message. Users simply need to long press a message to either report or block a user.
  • Lock your WhatsApp with Touch ID or Face ID: WhatsApp offers its users the ability to add another layer of security to their accounts with Touch ID and Face ID for iPhone, and fingerprint lock for Android.
  • Group privacy settings: WhatsApp’s privacy settings and group invite system allow users to decide who can add them to groups. This significant change increases user privacy and helps prevent users from being added to unwanted groups. Users can also exit a group privately without notifying the entire group. Only the admins will be notified.
  • Guidelines for users to protect themselves from scams by taking simple steps like turning on two-step verification, not sharing their PIN, never clicking on suspicious links, and never sharing personal details with someone they do not know or sending money to anyone without verifying that it is genuinely that person, even if the phone number is in their contacts.
  • Forward limits: We have set limits on forwarding messages, making us one of the few messaging services to intentionally constrain sharing. These labels help users identify forwarded messages and the number of times you can forward them. If a message has already been forwarded, you can forward it to up to five chats and if a message has a “forwarded many times” label, it can only be forwarded to one chat at a time. We have also introduced new group forwarding limits where messages that have the “forwarded label” can only be forwarded to one group at a time, rather than five.
  • Control your online presence: For the moments you want to keep your online presence private, users can select who can and can’t see when you’re online.
  • Disappearing messages: We have launched ‘Disappearing Messages’ to let users send messages that disappear from WhatsApp. Once enabled, new messages sent in the individual or group chat will disappear twenty-four hours, seven days or ninety days after the time they are sent, depending on the duration users select. We launched the feature ‘View Once’ - photos and videos that disappear from the chat after they’ve been opened, giving users even more control over their privacy. We have also enabled screenshot blocking for View Once messages for an added layer of protection.
  • Admin controls: We have made a number of changes to WhatsApp groups that empower users with additional controls. For example, we launched a setting that enables administrators to decide who can send messages within groups.
  • End-to-end encrypted backup: Users can now add the same layer of end-to-end encryption to protect their chat backups on iCloud or on their Google Account. With end-to-end encrypted backup, messages and media are stored in the cloud and secured by a password or a 64-digit encryption key.

About kept messages

When you use disappearing messages in your WhatsApp chats, you can choose to keep messages in the chat to prevent them from disappearing, as long as the duration time has not passed. Once the message has been kept, it will be visible to everyone in the conversation and not disappear when its duration expires. All messages that are kept will appear in the Kept messages folder in your WhatsApp settings.

Your privacy is our priority

If someone keeps a message you’ve sent, you’ll get a notification. As the sender of a message, you have the ultimate control over who can keep your message. If you decide to unkeep your message, no one else in the chat can keep it again.

Keep a message

Anyone in the chat can keep a message. Group admins can restrict this based on the group admin settings, and limit it to only admins if they choose.

To keep a message, click or long press on the message you want to keep and tap or click Keep.

To view your kept messages, tap or click on the chat info > Kept messages.

Unkeep a message

  1. Long press on the message you want to unkeep.
  2. Tap Unkeep > OK.

Note: You can’t unkeep messages after 25 days past the disappearing message’s duration time.

About lists

Copy link

Lists are customizable filters that can help you keep your chats organized. Go to Chats and swipe down to view your lists.

You have four default lists:

  • All: The default view of all your messages.
  • Unread: Chats with messages that you mark as unread or haven’t opened yet.
  • Favorites: Chats from your favorite contacts.
  • Groups: All your group chats in one place.

When selected, lists are highlighted in green. Lists remain applied until you change the filter view, or exit and re-open WhatsApp.

Notes:

  • Chats can’t be reorganized within All, Unread, or Groups.
  • Contacts added as favorites appear in the Chats tab, the Favorites list, and the Calls tab under Favorites. Learn more in this article.

Create custom lists

You can create custom lists to sort your chats into separate, accessible categories. To view your custom lists, go to the chats tab and swipe down.

Message privately and safely

Copy link

Whether it’s in conversation with friends, family or a business, your personal messages are secure, and you are in control. WhatsApp has a number of privacy settings, tools and controls to help keep you and these messages safe.

Safeguard your account

1. Activate two-step verification Add another layer of security to your WhatsApp account by requiring a unique PIN for access using two-step verification.

2. Look out for suspicious behavior Scams can affect anyone anywhere. We want to help you recognize suspicious behaviors and ways you can protect yourself.

Common things to watch out for include:

  • Messages from unknown phone numbers
  • Requests for money or personal information

Explore more examples of suspicious links, files, and spam.

3. Avoid unknown or unwanted calls and messages Focus on conversations that matter to you by silencing calls from unknown numbers. Unsure if the contact is someone you know? You can find which of your contacts use WhatsApp by accessing your phone’s address book. When you receive messages from someone that is not in your contacts, we’ll show you if you have groups in common, and if their phone number is registered in a different country from yours. From there, you can decide if you should reply, add them as a contact, block them or report them.

Safeguard your privacy

1. Complete the privacy checkup Choose your level of privacy with a privacy checkup. Follow the step-by-step guide to add more layers of security to your account and customize your privacy settings all in one place.

2. Check your privacy settings Control who sees your information by adjusting your privacy settings. You can adjust your last seen and online, profile photo, about, live location,status, or who can add you to groups. You can explore these topics and more to help you stay safe on WhatsApp here.

3. Report unwanted conversations or content You control who you chat with on WhatsApp. You can block specific contacts to stop unwanted calls and messages at any time. You can also report messages and contacts to us. Learn more about how to block and report contacts here.

Note: If you think a channel is sharing illegal or harmful content or spam, you can report them or report specific updates.

Learn more account security tips here.

About message summaries

Copy link

You can quickly catch up on conversations by asking Meta AI to summarize unread messages you’ve received. If you choose to use this feature, only you can see your message summaries and they’ll disappear when you scroll away from the summary or exit the chat. Responses from Meta AI are generated by artificial intelligence (AI), using a service from Meta.

To enable message summaries, Meta AI uses Private Processing, a secure technology from Meta. This technology allows Meta AI to generate a summary of your unread messages while ensuring no one, not even Meta or WhatsApp can read your personal messages or Meta AI’s response. Using Meta AI through WhatsApp, including features that use Private Processing, is always optional.

Note:

  • Meta AI and some experiences are currently only available in limited countries and might not be available to you yet, even if others in your country have access.
  • At this time, only English, Indonesian, Portuguese, and Spanish are supported.

As always, your personal messages are protected with end-to-end encryption, meaning no one outside of the chat, not even WhatsApp or Meta, can read, listen to, or share them.

How it works

About Private Processing

To enable message summaries, Meta AI uses Private Processing, a secure technology from Meta. Personal messages needed to complete your request are sent encrypted to secure Meta AI servers, where they’re used to complete your request without any data being stored. You can learn more about Private Processing in this article.

You can request to create and download a report of your Private Processing activity at any time. Learn how in this article.

Summarize your messages

To summarize your messages, you’ll be prompted to accept terms and will need to tap Continue. You’ll need to turn on Private Processing features and will be prompted to accept terms if you haven’t already for other Private Processing features. Learn how in this article.

Note:

  • Some messages generated by AI might not be accurate or appropriate.
  • Meta uses AI chats consistent with Meta’s Privacy Policy. By using this feature, you agree to Meta’s AI Terms of Service. When you share your personal messages with AI features that use Private Processing technology, Meta can’t read or access the messages you have shared.

How to move chats from an Android device to an iPhone

Copy link

When switching from Android to iPhone, you can transfer your WhatsApp account info, profile photo, chats (individual, group, communities), Channel updates, chat history, media, and settings. You can’t transfer your call history or display name, or media received over WhatsApp Channels.

Note: It’s currently not possible to transfer chats from an Android device to an iPhone on the WhatsApp Business app.

What do I need?

  • Android OS Lollipop, SDK 21 or above, or Android 5 or above installed on your Android device.
  • iOS 15.5 or above installed on your iPhone.
  • Move to the iOS app installed on your Android phone. Note: Using other data migration apps is not supported, and will cause migration issues.
  • Latest WhatsApp iOS version available in the App Store and latest WhatsApp Android version available in the Google Play Store.
  • Use the same phone number as your old phone on your new device.
  • Your iPhone must be factory new or factory reset to pair with the Move to iOS app and move data from your Android phone.
  • Both of your devices must be connected to a power source.
  • Both of your devices need to be connected to the same Wi-Fi network or you’ll need to connect your Android device to your iPhone’s hotspot.

Move chats from Android to iPhone

  1. Open the Move to iOS app on your Android phone and follow the on-screen prompts.
  2. A code will be displayed on your iPhone. When prompted, enter the code on your Android phone.
  3. Tap Continue and follow the on-screen prompts.
  4. Select WhatsApp on the Transfer Data screen.
  5. Tap Start on your Android phone, and wait for WhatsApp to prepare the data for export. You’ll be signed out from your Android phone once the data is prepared.
  6. Tap Next to return to the Move to iOS app.
  7. Tap Continue to transfer the data from your Android phone to your iPhone and wait for Move to iOS to confirm the transfer is complete.
  8. Install the latest version of WhatsApp from the App Store.
  9. Open WhatsApp and log in using the same phone number used on your old device.
  10. Tap Start when prompted, and allow the process to complete.
  11. Finish activating your new device and you’ll see your chats waiting for you.

Note: Going to Files and selecting the WhatsApp folder in the Move to iOS app isn’t supported during migration.

What happens to my data?

  • Transferred data doesn’t go to cloud storage as a result of the migration until you create an iCloud backup.
  • WhatsApp can’t see the data you transfer.
  • Your Android phone will still have your data unless you delete WhatsApp or wipe your phone.

What messages can I transfer to my new phone?

You can transfer:

  • Personal messages

You can’t transfer:

  • Peer to peer payment messages

Can I transfer my call history?

Your WhatsApp call history can’t be transferred from an Android phone to an iPhone.

What if WhatsApp is already active on my new device?

You can only restore your WhatsApp history before you’ve activated WhatsApp on your new device. If you want to get back your old message history, you need to wipe your new device and start over. It’s not possible to merge the new and old history.

What if my new device has a different phone number?

It’s not possible to transfer your WhatsApp data to a new phone number. You can however change your new phone number on your old device before moving to your new device. Learn how to change your WhatsApp number on your old device in this article.

How to move chats from an iPhone to an Android device

Copy link

Transferring your WhatsApp messages from iPhone to Android is easy and secure. WhatsApp handles the process directly, so your messages stay protected with end-to-end encryption throughout the transfer.

If you’re moving from an iPhone to an Android device, you can transfer your:

  • Account information
  • Individual chats
  • Group chats
  • Communities
  • WhatsApp Channels updates
  • Chat history
  • Call history
  • Media and settings

You can’t transfer your display name, status updates, or media received over WhatsApp Channels.

Before you start the transfer, make sure you have:

  • An Android device with Android 6 or above.
  • The same phone number on the new device as the old device.
  • The latest WhatsApp Android version available in the Google Play Store.
  • The latest WhatsApp iOS version available in the App Store.
  • A stable Wi-Fi connection.
  • Don’t delete your WhatsApp data from your old phone (iPhone) until after your transfer has completed.

Next, follow these steps to move your chats from an iPhone to an Android device:

  1. On your iPhone, open WhatsApp and go to Chats > Transfer chat history > Transfer to Android.
  2. When the chats are prepared, tap Continue.
  3. If prompted, tap Allow to enable access to the camera.
  4. Keep your iPhone unlocked during the transfer.
  5. On your Android device, open WhatsApp and verify your account with the same number you use on your iPhone
  6. When prompted, tap Allow to enable your devices to connect. A QR code is displayed.
  7. Use your iPhone camera to scan a QR code.
  8. When prompted, tap Join to connect to the Wi-FI network and start the transfer.
  9. When the transfer completes, tap Next on your Android device to view your chats and start using WhatsApp.

Note:

  • The time it takes to transfer your data depends on how much you’re moving. If you have a lot of data, the transfer might take longer to finish.
  • You can only transfer your chats before you’ve activated WhatsApp on your new Android device. If you want to restore your old chats, you’ll need to first uninstall WhatsApp on your new device. You can’t merge new chats from your new phone and old chats from your old phone.
  • It’s currently not possible to transfer chats from an iPhone to an Android device on the WhatsApp Business app.
  • Your old device will still have your data unless you wipe it or delete WhatsApp.
  • Transferring chats by local Wi-Fi connection means transferred data doesn’t go to cloud storage. However, you might have sent this data to your cloud storage separately by backing up chats to your iCloud account.
  • WhatsApp can’t see the data you transfer.
  • It’s not possible to transfer your chats to a new phone number. You’ll need to change your phone number on your old device to your new phone number to transfer chats. Learn how here.
  • You can transfer personal messages, but you can’t transfer peer-to-peer payment messages.
  • Your status updates can’t be transferred from an iPhone to an Android device.

You can pin up to four messages to the top of a chat. Once pinned, the message stays at the top of the chat as a banner for 24 hours, 7 days, or 30 days. Tap on the pinned message banner to navigate to the message in the chat.

If more than one message is pinned, the banner shows how many messages are pinned. The most recent pinned message appears first in the banner. Tap the banner to see the next pinned message.

Pin a message

A pinned message is displayed as a banner at the top of the chat until it’s unpinned.

  1. Tap and hold the message.
  2. Tap Pin.
  3. Select the pin duration (24 hours, 7 days, or 30 days).

Unpin a message

You can unpin a message at any time. If a pin isn’t unpinned, it will automatically unpin when the set duration expires.

  1. Tap and hold the pinned message.
  2. Tap Unpin.

Pin a message in group chats

Group admins can choose to allow members to pin messages in a group chat.

  1. Open the group chat and tap the group name.
  2. Tap Group permissions.
  3. Turn Edit group settings on or off.

When you pin a message in a group chat, a system message is shared with everyone in the chat indicating that a message was pinned and who pinned it. Users can’t see a pinned message if they join a group after a pinned message is sent, if they lost or cleared their chat history, or if they deleted the message before it was pinned.

  4. You can also:

    • Long press the dot located on the waveform, then
    • Drag it to the timestamp of the message you want to start playing from.

  5. Voice messages will continue to play even if you go to another chat or group within WhatsApp.

    • When you play a voice message and leave the chat, a mini player will appear at the top of your screen.
    • You can pause, play, and close the voice message, or go back to the original chat.

Note:

  • When you receive two or more voice messages in a row, WhatsApp will automatically play them in order when you tap Play. To stop your voice messages from playing in order, simply tap the Pause button of the voice message currently playing.
  • “Hey Siri” must be turned on for voice message transcripts to display.
  • Once voice message transcripts are enabled, the message recipient can see voice message transcripts. The sender can’t see the transcripts.
  • You can’t delete, edit, or copy and paste voice message transcripts.

How to prevent the spread of misinformation

Copy link

You can help prevent the spread of misinformation by following the tips below.

[Embedded video omitted]

0:00 / 0:17

Learn about the Forwarded message labels

Messages with the “Forwarded” label show that they originally came from someone other than the person who sent them to you. When a message is forwarded through a chain of five or more chats, a double arrow icon

[Image: frequently forwarded (two overlapping right arrows with curved tails)]

and the “Forwarded many times” label is displayed. To learn more about forwarding limits, read this article.

Check your biases

Watch out for information that confirms your pre-existing beliefs; review the facts yourself before sharing information. Stories that seem hard to believe are often untrue.

Fact check information with other sources

Fake news often goes viral, and photos, audio recordings, and videos can be edited to mislead you. Even if a message is shared many times, this doesn’t make it true. If you receive information that’s fake, inform the sender that they sent you incorrect information. You can also recommend they verify messages before sharing them.

If you’re unsure whether a message is true, we recommend checking trusted news sites to see where the story came from. When a story is reported in multiple places and from trustworthy sources, it’s more likely to be true. You can consult fact-checkers, or people you trust, for more information. For a list of fact-checkers affiliated with the International Fact-Checking Network, see this article.

If a contact is constantly sending fake news, report them. To learn how to report a message, contact, or group, read this article.

Look for messages that look different

Many unwanted messages and links have spelling or grammar mistakes, or ask you to share personal information. To learn how to identify and handle these types of messages, read this article.

Note: If you feel that you or someone else is in emotional or physical danger, please contact your local law enforcement authorities. Local law enforcement authorities are equipped to help in these cases.

About pricing for marketing messages

On iPhone

Copy link

Marketing messages is now business broadcasts in some countries. Business broadcasts might not be available to you yet. If you’re seeing business broadcasts, please refer to this article.

With marketing messages, you only pay for each message that is delivered to a contact within five days of being sent. The balance for each delivered message is accumulated. After the balance exceeds a set amount or you reach your billing date, you’ll be charged for the outstanding balance.

You can also pay for marketing messages through prepaid funds. You must have enough funds in your account to cover the cost of the marketing messages. Funds will be deducted daily as messages are delivered. Your payment method is charged for the total number of recipients you choose, and the funds are credited back to your account for any receivers to whom your message couldn’t be delivered.

Pricing for messages is based on the country code of each message recipient. Marketing messages is available in all of the currencies listed on this page through USD-based exchange rate conversion. We use rate cards for the following specified currencies:

  • IDR rate card
  • TRY rate card
  • MXN rate card
  • PKR rate card
  • AED rate card
  • PEN rate card
  • INR rate card
  • BRL rate card
  • USD rate card
  • CLP rate card
  • COP rate card
  • AUD rate card
  • HKD rate card
  • NZD rate card
  • SGD rate card
  • TWD rate card
  • MYR rate card
  • SAR rate card

Total cost, estimated tax, and estimated total will be displayed in the app before you checkout.

Note: Final cost may be lower if some messages are not delivered. Marketing messages is currently available in limited countries and might not be available to you yet.

You can react to messages in individual and group chats with emojis. You can view all reactions to a message by tapping the emoji below the message.

React to a message

  1. Tap and hold a message.

  2. Tap an emoji to react or tap

    [Image: Black Add (plus sign within circle)]

    to select an emoji from your keyboard.

Note:

  • When you add a reaction, only the sender of the message being reacted to will receive a notification.
  • You can only add one reaction to a message.
  • Reactions to disappearing messages will disappear when the message disappears.
  • It’s not possible to hide reactions or reaction counts.

React to a photo, gif, or video

  1. Tap and hold a photo, gif, or video.

  2. Tap an emoji to react or tap

    [Image: Black Add (plus sign within circle)]

    to select an emoji from your keyboard.

Alternatively, tap on the image to open the media viewer. Select one of the displayed emojis or tap the add emoji icon to select an emoji from your keyboard.

Change your reaction

  1. Tap and hold a message, photo, gif, or video you reacted to.

    • Alternatively, tap the emoji below the message.

  2. Tap a different emoji or tap

    [Image: Add (plus sign within circle)]

    to select an emoji from your keyboard.

Remove your reaction

  1. Tap and hold a message, photo, gif, or video you reacted to.
    • Alternatively, tap the emoji below the message.
  2. Tap your reaction to remove it.

Note:

  • A notification won’t be sent to the sender of the message if you remove a reaction.
  • Recipients might see your reaction before you remove it or if WhatsApp fails to remove it. You won’t be notified when removing a reaction fails.

To react to a message while using the Voice-Over feature on your iPhone:

  1. Touch the message you want to react to.
  2. Flick down until Voice-Over says “react.”
  3. Double tap your screen. A list of reactions will appear.
  4. Swipe left and right to navigate the list of reactions.
  5. When you find your desired reaction, double tap your screen to react.

When you’re in a community, you’ll be added to an Announcements group.

Admins can use this group to send announcements to all community members.

Only community admins can send announcements in the Announcements group.

As a member, you can react, report and reply to announcements.

How to reply to announcements

  1. Tap your community.

  2. Tap Announcements.

  3. Tap and hold an announcement.

  4. Tap

    [Image: Reply (left arrow with curved tail)]

    .

  5. Type your reply and tap Send.

You can see other members’ replies by tapping and holding Replies.

Note: If the community is deactivated, you can still see previous replies on an announcement. You won’t be able to add any new replies though.

How to react to announcements

Reacting to an announcement is the same as reacting to other messages on WhatsApp. Learn how to send message reactions.

You can’t react to other members’ replies to an announcement.

How to report announcements

  1. Tap your community.
  2. Tap Announcements.
  3. Tap and hold an announcement.
  4. Tap More > Report > Report.
  • To block and report, tap Report and block.

Note: To protect user privacy, your phone number is only visible to community admins, people who have saved your number in their contacts, or those who have your number from your other chats.

You can find and join events in individual and group chats to help organize gatherings and stay connected.

You can’t see or join events created before you join a group. The event creator has to delete the event and create a new one to let you see the event and respond.

Find events

When members add an event to an individual or group chat, it’ll appear as an event message in the chat.

You can see all upcoming events in your chat or group info. In an individual or group chat: Tap the group name > Events.

Note: You can only see events in groups you’re a member of.

Respond to an event

  1. Tap Respond.
  2. Tap Going, Going with guest, Maybe, or Not going.

If you respond Going, Going with guest, or Maybe, you’ll receive a notification when the event creator edits or cancels the event. A notification about event changes will also be sent to the individual or group chat.

How to search WhatsApp

On iPhone

Copy link

Android

iOS

Web

More

Android

iOS

Web

You can search chats for messages, groups in common, photos, videos, links, GIFs, audio, documents, and polls using the WhatsApp search feature. You can use search from the Chats tab or within individual or group chats.

The Chats tab is on the navigation bar at the bottom of your screen. It’s the first screen you see when you open WhatsApp.

Search by keyword

The search feature allows you to search your chats with a keyword. Search by keyword in an individual or group chat, or from the Chats tab.

Chats tab

  1. In the Chats tab, tap the search bar.
  2. Type the word or phrase you’re looking for in the search field.
  3. Tap a result to open that message in the chat.

Individual or group chat

  1. Open the chat you want to search.
  2. Tap the chat name, then tap Search.
  3. Type the word or phrase you’re looking for in the search field.
  4. Tap search.

Note: On iPad, open the chat > tap the More menu > tap Search.

Search by date

You can also search by date in an individual or group chat.

  1. Open the chat you want to search.

  2. Tap the chat name, then tap Search.

  3. Tap

    [Image: Search By Date (calendar with magnifying glass in bottom right corner)]

    .

  4. Select the date you want to search.

  5. Tap Jump to date.

Note: On iPad, open the chat > tap the More menu > tap Search.

Search for media with filters

You can also search your chats for media such as photos, videos, links, GIFs, audio, polls, and documents, by using filters in the search feature. This is only available on the Chats tab.

  1. Tap the search field at the top of the Chats tab.
  2. Select the media type you want to search.
  3. Tap a result to open that message in the chat.

Filter media by content type

You can view all photos, videos, links, GIFs, audio, polls, and documents. This is only available on the Chats tab.

  1. In the Chats tab, tap the search bar.
  2. Tap Photos, GIFs, Links, Videos, Documents, Audio, or Polls to view media in that category.

Search for groups

Groups that you’re a part of can be found in the Chats tab. You can also search for a group by its subject, contents or a contact you know is in it.

  • When you type a contact’s name in the search bar, you can see a list of groups that you’re both in under Groups in common.
  • If you can’t find a group, be sure to check the Archived Chats section within the Chats tab.
  • If you don’t see the group you’re looking for in the Chats tab, you might not be a member.
  • If you’d like to join a group, you’ll have to ask the group admin to add you or send you an invite link.
  • You can’t separate groups from individual chats in the Chats tab.
  • You can pin a group for easy access. Learn how to pin a chat in this article.

Note: If you’ve recently restored your WhatsApp chat history, it can take time to recreate the search database, depending on the size of your chat history. All restored chats can be searched in the app after the backup is complete. Don’t force-close WhatsApp during this time.

Search with Meta AI

Note: This feature is currently only available in limited countries and might not be available to you yet, even if other users in your country have access.

You can also use search to ask Meta AI a question. Learn how in this article.

Seeing “Devices out of sync” message

On iPhone

Copy link

This feature isn’t available on the iPhone app, but it is available on these devices. Select a device to learn more about this feature.

Web

On WhatsApp Web

Copy link

Web

More

Web

If you’re seeing the warning “Devices out of sync,” you may need to update your phone clock to the correct time. The date, time, and time zone settings on your phone should match your current location. If they don’t, you can update your clock in your phone’s settings. If your clock is set correctly but the warning persists, check your internet connection and restart your phone.

If the clock remains incorrect on your phone, your linked devices may be automatically removed after some time. You can always relink your devices.

For the future, we recommend setting your date and time to Automatic. With this setting enabled, your mobile provider will set your phone to the correct time. If the incorrect time is displayed even with this setting enabled, then there might be an issue with your network. Please contact your mobile provider to address the issue.
