About WhatsApp contacts

Copy link

With WhatsApp contacts, you can save your contacts to your WhatsApp account so they can be restored and managed across your devices.

WhatsApp contacts allows you to manage your contact list directly within WhatsApp, independently from your phone’s address book. This means you can save contacts to your WhatsApp account. They won’t appear in your phone’s address book or be shared with other apps.

You have two types of contacts:

  • WhatsApp contacts: Saved only to your WhatsApp account. They won’t appear in your phone’s address book or be accessible by other apps. When you add a new contact on WhatsApp, it’s saved as WhatsApp-only by default.
  • Synced contacts: Saved to both your WhatsApp account and your phone’s address book. You can choose to sync any contact to your phone by turning on the Sync to phone toggle when adding or editing a contact.

Turn WhatsApp contacts on or off

When WhatsApp contacts is on:

  • You can save contacts using just their username, without needing to have their phone number.
  • You’ll have the option to choose which contacts to sync to your phone, which means you can choose to add or edit contacts that will only be saved on WhatsApp and not in your phone’s address book. There’s no limit on the number of contacts you can save. Learn more about adding and editing contacts in this help article.
  • You can choose to create contacts that are specific to each WhatsApp account. For example, if you have multiple accounts on the same phone, such as a work account and personal account, you can customize WhatsApp contact lists for each account, rather than using the same phone contact list for multiple accounts.
  • If you change phones or reinstall WhatsApp, all of your contacts will be automatically restored.
  • You can add, edit, and delete contacts on WhatsApp Web and the Windows desktop app.

When WhatsApp contacts is off:

  • Any contacts saved only to WhatsApp will be deleted.
  • Any contacts you create or edit in WhatsApp will be saved to your phone’s address book. You won’t have the option to save contacts to WhatsApp only.
  • You won’t have the option to choose which contacts to sync to your phone or save to WhatsApp only.
  • If you change phones or reinstall WhatsApp, your contacts won’t automatically be restored.
  • You won’t be able to manage contacts on WhatsApp Web or Windows.

You can turn off WhatsApp contacts in your account settings, which will delete your contacts saved to your WhatsApp account. To turn WhatsApp contacts on or off:

  • iPhone: Tap Settings or your profile picture, then tap Privacy > Contacts > turn WhatsApp contacts on or off.

  • Android: Tap

    [Image: More (three vertical dots)]

    Settings > Privacy > Contacts > turn WhatsApp contacts on or off.

If you delete your WhatsApp account, contacts saved with your WhatsApp account will also be deleted.

How contact names are displayed

WhatsApp displays contact names based on where the contact is saved:

  • Synced contacts: WhatsApp displays the name saved in your phone’s address book. If you update the name in your phone’s address book, the change will be reflected in WhatsApp.
  • WhatsApp contacts: WhatsApp displays the name you saved within WhatsApp.
  • Unsaved contacts: If you haven’t saved someone as a contact, you’ll see the profile name they’ve set on their own WhatsApp account.

Note: Contact profile photos are set by each person on their own WhatsApp account. Saving someone as a contact doesn’t change their profile photo.

How to tell if a contact is WhatsApp-only or synced

Edit the contact and check the Sync to phone toggle. If the toggle is on, the contact is synced to your phone’s address book.

If the toggle is off, the contact is a WhatsApp contact only.

If your contacts appear incorrectly after changing phone settings

WhatsApp-only contacts are not affected by changes to your phone’s address book because they’re stored securely in your WhatsApp account. If contacts appear incorrect:

  • Check your phone’s address book to confirm the names are correct there.
  • For synced contacts, WhatsApp will display whatever name is in your phone’s address book. Update the name in your phone’s address book, and it will update in WhatsApp.
  • You can edit contacts directly in WhatsApp. If you’d like to manage a contact’s name entirely within WhatsApp, turn off the Sync to phone toggle to make it a WhatsApp-only contact. If multiple contacts in your phone’s address book share the same phone number, you might see different names appear in WhatsApp (for example, in the new chat picker). However, WhatsApp will only allow you to access and edit one contact per phone number.

WhatsApp contacts and phone permissions

  • If you haven’t granted WhatsApp permission to access your phone’s contacts, you can still create WhatsApp-only contacts. The Sync to phone option will be unavailable until you grant permissions.
  • If you revoke contact permissions while WhatsApp contacts is turned on, your phone contacts will be kept in WhatsApp as WhatsApp-only contacts. You won’t lose your contact list.
  • If you revoke contact permissions while WhatsApp contacts is turned off, phone contacts will be removed from WhatsApp.

You can find more technical details about how your contacts are securely stored and saved to your WhatsApp account in our engineering blog.

General

How to link to WhatsApp from a different app

On iPhone

Copy link

iOS

More

iOS

There are several ways to have your iPhone application interact with WhatsApp: universal links, custom URL schemes, share extension, and the Document Interaction API.

Universal links

Universal links are the preferred method of linking to a WhatsApp account.

Use https://wa.me/<number> where the <number> is a full phone number in international format. Omit any brackets, dashes, plus signs, and leading zeros when adding the phone number in international format.

Examples:

Use: https://wa.me/15551234567

Don’t use: https://wa.me/+001-(555)1234567

Universal links can also include a pre-filled message that will automatically appear in the text field of a chat. Use https://wa.me/whatsappphonenumber/?text=urlencodedtext where whatsappphonenumber is a full phone number in international format and URL-encodedtext is the URL-encoded pre-filled message.

Example: https://wa.me/15551234567?text=I'm%20interested%20in%20your%20car%20for%20sale

To create a link with just a pre-filled message, use https://wa.me/?text=urlencodedtext

Example: wa.me’m%20inquiring%20about%20the%20apartment%20listing`

Custom URL Scheme

Opening whatsapp:// URL with one of the following parameters, will open our app and perform a custom action.

URL Parameters Opens
app - The WhatsApp Messenger application
send New chat composer
text If present, this text will be pre-filled into message text input field on a conversation screen.

The Objective-C call to open one of these URLs is as follows:

NSURL *whatsappURL = [NSURL URLWithString:@“whatsapp://send?text=Hello%2C%20World!”]; if ([[UIApplication sharedApplication] canOpenURL: whatsappURL]) { [[UIApplication sharedApplication] openURL: whatsappURL]; }

Be sure to include WhatsApp URL scheme in your application’s Info.plist under LSApplicationQueriesSchemes key if you want to determine whether WhatsApp is installed on the user’s iPhone using -[UIApplication canOpenURL:].

Share Extension

Introduced in iOS 8.0, Share Extension provides a convenient way for any app to share content with other applications installed on user’s iPhone. This is now the preferred way of sharing your content onto WhatsApp. The Share extension allows you to share up to 30 mixed media files. To use Share Extension, create an instance of UIActivityViewController and present it in your app. WhatsApp accepts the following types of content:

  • text (UTI: public.plain-text)
  • photos (UTI: public.image)
  • videos (UTI: public.movie)
  • audio notes and music files (UTI: public.audio)
  • PDF documents (UTI: com.adobe.pdf)
  • contact cards (UTI: public.vcard)
  • web URLs (UTI: public.url)

Note: Editing when sharing from another app isn’t supported. If you’d like to make changes to your files before sharing them, you’ll need to first make changes in the app.

File size limits

You can upload up to 30 files at a time. The file size limits are:

  • All Files: 2 GB
  • Videos: 200 MB
  • Images: 16 MB

Group admins can add or remove members from their group. Admins can also allow other members to add people into the group. Groups can have up to 1024 members.

Add members

When you add a new member to a group, you may have the option to send message history to them. You can send up to 100 messages from the last 14 days.

When message history is sent, the new member will receive a notification. All members will see a system message notifying them that message history was sent to the new member.

  1. Open the WhatsApp group chat, then tap the group subject.
    • Alternatively, swipe the group to the left in the Chats tab. Then tap More > Group Info.
  2. Tap Add Members or Invite to Group via Link.
  3. Search for or select contacts or a phone number to add to the group.
  • You’ll see Frequently contacted contacts as potential contacts to add to your group.
  1. Turn on Message history.
  2. Select the number of recent messages you’d like to send, then tap Done.
  3. Tap Add > Add.
  4. If the group has Approve New Members turned on, and there are pending requests to join the group, an admin can review these requests.

Note:

  • Group admins have the option to turn off the ability for members to send message history. If Send message history is turned off, group members won’t see the option to send message history when they add a new member to the group.
  • Certain contact names won’t appear when you try to call, message, or view a status if you haven’t allowed full access to the contacts in your phone’s address book. You can grant access by going to your phone’s Settings > Apps > WhatsApp > Contacts.

Add someone not saved as a contact

You can add people or phone numbers that aren’t saved in your contacts.

  1. Open the WhatsApp group chat, then tap the group subject.
  • Alternatively, swipe the group to the left in the Chats tab. Then tap More > Group Info.
  1. Tap + Add members.

  3. Tap Add.
  4. Tap Add to group.

Invite contacts who don’t have WhatsApp to a group

  1. Open the group chat and tap the group name.

  • If prompted, select Allow to be able to send and view SMS messages through WhatsApp.
  1. Enter a message.

Remove members

  1. Open the WhatsApp group chat, then tap the group subject.

You can hide an individual or group chat from your Chats tab by archiving it.

By default, archived chats will stay archived when you receive a new message. You can access your archive at the top of the Chats tab.

Archive an individual chat or group

  1. In the Chats tab, swipe left on the individual or group chat you want to archive.
  2. Tap Archive.

Archive all chats at once

  1. Tap Settings or your profile picture, then tap Chats.
  2. Tap Archive all chats > Archive all.

View archived individual or group chats

At the top of the Chats screen, tap Archived.

Note: If you’ve archived all chats, you will see this message: “**All of your chats are archived. Tap

[Image: Add Chat Green (plus sign within circle)]

to start a new chat.” Tap Archived** below this message to see your archived chats.

Unarchive an individual or group chat

You can access your archived chats and decide to unarchive a chat at any time.

  1. At the top of the Chats tab, tap Archived.
  2. Swipe left on the chat you want to unarchive.
  3. Tap Unarchive.

Alternatively, or if you’d like to unarchive more than one chat:

  1. At the top of the Chats tab, tap Archived > Edit > Select chats.
  2. Select the chats you’d like to unarchive, then tap Unarchive.

You can also manually unarchive a chat by searching for a contact name or message from that contact:

  1. In the Chats tab, tap the search bar.
  2. Enter the name of the chat or contact name you want to unarchive.
  3. Swipe left on the chat you want to unarchive.
  4. Tap Unarchive.

More archive settings

When you receive a new message in the archived chat, the chat remains archived by default. To automatically unarchive a chat when new messages are received:

  1. Tap Settings or your profile picture, then tap Chats.
  2. Turn off Keep chats archived.

Note:

  • Archiving a chat doesn’t delete the chat.
  • You won’t receive notifications for archived chats unless you’re mentioned or replied to. You can’t adjust notifications for archived chats.
  • Archived individual or group chats will unarchive when you receive a new message from that individual or group chat unless Keep Chats Archived is turned on.
  • The number next to Archived shows how many individual or group chats have unread messages.
  • An **@** symbol shows when someone has replied to or mentioned you in an archived group chat.

If you’re a group admin, you can make a group member an admin or remove a member as an admin.

Unable to add or remove an admin

If you’re unable to make another member an admin or remove them as an admin, it might be because:

  • You’re not a group admin.
  • You and the member aren’t on the latest version of WhatsApp.
  • The member is already an admin.
  • The member is no longer in the group.
  • There’s a network issue.

Note: WhatsApp can’t interfere with group administration functions. For example, we can’t make someone an admin.

How to change group admin settings

On iPhone

Copy link

Android

iOS

Web

Windows

Mac

More

Android

iOS

Web

Windows

Mac

Group admins can change settings to allow either only admins or all members to edit group info, send messages, send invite links, or add people to a group.

If a group was started with fewer than 33 members, all group members can:

  • Add others to the group.
  • Send invite links.

If a group has more than 256 members, Edit group settings will default to Only admins.

Change group info settings

  1. Open the group chat, then tap the group name.
  2. Tap Group permissions.
  3. Choose to turn on Edit group settings.
    • When turned on, members can edit group settings, including name, icon, and description.
    • When turned off, only admins can edit group settings.

Change group message settings

  1. Open the group chat, then tap the group name.
  2. Tap Group permissions.
  3. Choose to turn on Send messages.
    • When turned on, all members can send messages in the group.
    • When turned off, only admins can send messages in the group.

Change who can add members

By default, all group members can add others to a group. Group admins can change group settings to allow members to add others to a group.

  1. Open the group chat, then tap the group name.
  2. Tap Group permissions.
  3. Turn Add other members on or off.
    • When turned on, all members can add other members to the group.
    • When turned off, only admins can add other members to the group.

Change who can share a group invite link or QR code

By default, members in groups with fewer than 33 members can send a group link to invite others to the group. Group admins can change group settings to allow members to invite others to a group.

  1. Open the group chat, then tap the group name.
  2. Tap Group permissions.
  3. Choose to turn on Invite via group link or QR code.
    • When turned on, any member of the group can share a link to invite people to join the group.
    • When turned off, only admins can create a link to invite people to join the group.

Note:

  • If Approve new members is turned on, admins will still need to approve new members.

Allow members to send message history

If you’ve allowed any member to add others to the group, you can also allow them to send message history when they add a new member.

  1. Tap the group name.
  2. Tap Groups permissions.
  3. Turn Send message history on or off.

Change who can approve new members

If you turn on Approve new members, new members must be approved by group admins before they’re added to the group.

  1. Open the group chat, then tap the group name.
  2. Tap Group permissions.
  3. Choose to turn on Approve new members.
    • When turned on, admins must approve anyone who wants to join the group.
    • When turned off, this group is open for people to join without admin approval.

Change who can be group admin

  1. Open the group chat, then tap the group name.

  2. Tap Group permissions.

  3. Tap Group admin.

  4. Select other members of the group who can be group admin.

  5. Tap

    [Image: Approve CheckMark (checkmark)]

    .

Note:

  • If you’re the only group admin and leave the group, another member is chosen at random to become the new admin.
  • If you rejoin the group and would like to be an admin again, you need to ask the group admin to make you one.
  • You can contact an admin of a group you’re in by tapping Group Info, then tapping the name of the admin you want to message.

How to change group privacy settings

On iPhone

Copy link

Android

iOS

Mac

Web

More

Android

iOS

Mac

Web

We work diligently to reduce spam and unwanted contact on WhatsApp. However, just as anyone with your contact information can send you an SMS message or email, anyone with your phone number can add you to a group on WhatsApp.

By default, your group privacy settings are set to Everyone, to let you easily connect with friends and family, even if they’re not in your contacts list. For additional privacy, you can control who can add you to a group by adjusting your WhatsApp Settings. Learn more about how to change privacy settings.

Group admins can also turn on Advanced chat privacy to control how messages and media in your group are shared outside of WhatsApp, learn more in this article.

Note:

  • Changes to group privacy settings can’t be made on WhatsApp Web or Desktop. When you change the settings on your phone, they sync with WhatsApp Web and Desktop.
  • Group privacy settings don’t affect community Announcements. When you’re in a community, you’re always added to community Announcements.
  • You can’t directly block a group chat, but you can exit the group and block the group admin.

How group invite links work with privacy settings

  • Your group privacy settings only apply when someone tries to add you directly to a group. Your privacy setting does not prevent someone from sending you a group invite link. If someone does share a group invite link with you, you can choose to join regardless of your privacy settings. Joining a group through an invite link is always your choice.
  • Changing your group privacy settings only controls who can add you to new groups in the future. It doesn’t remove you from groups you’re already in.
  • Using the option to Exit group only removes you from the group you want to leave. It doesn’t stop other people from adding you to any groups in the future. Learn more about how to exit a group in this article.

Stop others from adding you to groups

If someone repeatedly adds you to groups you don’t want to be a part of, go to your group privacy settings and choose My contacts except… to exclude them. This prevents that person from adding you to groups in the future. You can also block the contact entirely, which stops all communication including group adds.

Change group privacy settings

  1. Tap WhatsApp Settings or your profile picture.
  2. Tap Privacy > Groups.
  3. Select one of the following options:
  • Everyone: Everyone, including people outside of your phone’s address book contacts, can add you to groups without your approval.
  • My Contacts: Only contacts in your phone’s address book can add you to groups without your approval. If a group admin who’s not in your phone’s address book tries to add you to a group, they’ll get a pop-up that says they can’t add you and will be prompted to tap Invite to Group or press Continue, followed by the send button, to send a private group invite through an individual chat. You’ll have three days to accept the invite before it expires.
  • My Contacts Except…: Only contacts in your phone’s address book, except those you exclude, can add you to groups without your approval. After selecting My Contacts Except… you can search for or select contacts to exclude. If a group admin you exclude tries to add you to a group, they’ll get a pop-up that says they can’t add you and will be prompted to tap Invite to Group followed by the send button to send a private group invite through an individual chat. You’ll have three days to accept the invite before it expires.
  1. If prompted, tap Done.

Learn more about how to change group admin settings.

How to create and edit events in groups

On iPhone

Copy link

Android

iOS

Web

Windows

Mac

More

Android

iOS

Web

Windows

Mac

You can create events in individual and group chats to help organize gatherings and stay connected. Events contain useful information that can be easily accessed by people.

Create an event

  1. Open your individual or group chat and tap

    [Image: Add item (plus sign)]

    Event.

  2. Enter the event name, date, and time.

  3. Add additional details to make your event more informative.

    • Description: Describe your event in up to 2,048 characters.
    • End time: Choose an end time for your event.
    • Location: Add a location to help guests find your event.
    • WhatsApp call link: Add a call link to host your event on a video or voice call. Call links can’t be added to events more than 12 months in advance.
    • Allow guests: Turn on to allow guests to bring an additional guest.- Tap Send.

Once created, the event will be shared in the individual or group chat. People can tap the message to respond and view event information. They can respond Going, Maybe, or Not going.

People who respond Going or Maybe will receive a notification when the event begins.

Note:

  • Events are hosted by the event creator. It’s not currently possible to have a co-host.
  • If Disappearing messages is turned on, you might not be able to create events in advance. To use the full calendar, turn Disappearing messages off.
  • You can’t invite people who aren’t in the individual or group chat to the event. You also can’t forward an event to another chat.
  • New members can’t see events created before they joined the group. To include new members, delete the old event and create a new one.

Edit an event

Only event creators can edit and cancel events.

  1. Open your individual or group chat and tap the chat name.
  2. Tap Events and select the event you want to edit.
  3. Tap Edit.
  • Edit your event name, date, and time, location, and description. Tap Save to save changes.
  • To cancel the event, tap Cancel event > Yes.

People who respond Going, or Maybe will receive a notification when you make changes to your event. A notification about your event changes will also be sent to the individual or group chat.

Pin an event

You can pin an event to the top of an individual or group chat to help remind people about the upcoming event.

  1. Go to the Chats tab and tap the individual or group chat with the event.
  2. Tap and hold the event notification and tap Pin.
  3. Choose to pin the event for 24 hours, 7 days, or 30 days.
    • If the event has an end time, you can select Until event ends.
    • If the event doesn’t have an end time, you can select Until 3 hours after event starts.

To unpin an event, tap and hold the pinned event and tap Unpin.

Note:

  • Only event creators can pin an event.
  • New members can’t see events created before they join the group, even if they’re pinned.

You can create a WhatsApp group with up to 1024 members.

Create a group

  1. Tap

    [Image: Add Chat Green (plus sign within circle)]

    New group.

  2. You have the option to:

    • Search for or select contacts to add to the group. If a contact doesn’t have WhatsApp, they’ll be sent an SMS invite.
    • Add members later.

  3. Tap Next.

    • Tap Group name (optional) to create a name for the group. The name limit is 100 characters.

    • Tap

      [Image: Camera Tab (camera)]

      to add a group icon. Tap Take photo, Choose photo, Emoji & sticker, or Search web to add an image. You might also have the option to generate and use an AI image.

    • Tap Disappearing messages to turn on messages that disappear after a selected duration. Select 24 hours, 7 days, or 90 days.

    • Tap Group permissions to edit permissions for members and admins.

  4. Tap Create.

Note:

  • If you don’t add a group name, the name will be a list of the users in the group.
  • Some names won’t appear in your contacts until you allow full access to your phone contacts. To grant access, open your phone’s Settings and tap WhatsApp > Contacts.

Invite contacts to group

  1. Open the group chat and tap the group name.
  2. Tap Add and select contacts.
    • If a contact doesn’t have WhatsApp, they’ll be sent an SMS invite.
  3. Tap Add.

Invite contacts without WhatsApp to group

  1. Open the group chat and tap the group name.
  2. Tap Add and select contacts.
  3. Tap Send invites on the confirmation screen.

WhatsApp will send an SMS invite to the contact including your name and the group name. You’ll see a confirmation that your invite was sent.

Note:

  • When your contact receives the SMS, they can tap the link to join WhatsApp and your group directly. The invite expires after 3 days.
  • If WhatsApp can’t send the invite for you, you’ll see an Invite directly option with a pre-written SMS that you can send yourself.

Invite to group with link or QR code

Admins and members in groups with fewer than 33 members can create group links to invite new members to a group.

  1. Open the group chat and tap the group name.
  2. Tap Invite via link or QR code
    • Tap Send link via WhatsApp to send to link through WhatsApp. Select contacts, and tap Send.
    • Tap Share to my status to share the link to your status.
    • Tap Send link via SMS to share the link through text message.
    • Tap Send link via email to share the link through email.
    • Tap Copy link to copy the link. Paste the link to share.
    • Tap Share link to share the link through another app.
    • Tap QR code to generate a scannable QR code.

Reset a group invite link

If you’re a group admin, you can deactivate a group invite link and create a new one.

  1. Open the group chat and tap the group name.
  2. Tap Invite via link or QR code.
  3. Tap Reset link > Reset link.

Note: Once an invite link has been reset, the previous link can’t be restored.

Allow members to create group links

If you’re a group admin, you can change group permissions to allow members to invite others with group links.

  1. Open the group chat, then tap the group name.
  2. Tap Group permissions > turn on Add other members.
    • When turned on, group members can create group invite links.
    • When turned off, only admins can create group invite links.

Note: By default, members in groups with fewer than 33 members can create invite links. Learn more about how to change group admin settings.

Manage group invitations

If you’re a group admin, you can check if the group has any pending invites. Group members who create a group link can also check the status of their invitation.

  1. Open the group and tap the group name.
  2. Pending invites are displayed under Invites.

Note: Groups may work differently if you’re invited to a group by a business using authorized third-party providers to help them manage WhatsApp. Learn more.

How to exit a group as a member

On iPhone

Copy link

Android

iOS

You can exit or exit and delete a group if you no longer want to be in it.

What happens when you exit and delete a group

When you exit a group, group admins will see “{contacts name or phone number} left.” in the group. It’s not possible to disable this notification.

When you delete a group, you’ll no longer see it in your Chats list and the group chat history will be erased from your phone.

Your profile name and phone number will be shown in the Past members list in Group info. Your profile photo may also be shown, depending on your settings. Group members can see your information in the Past members list for up to 60 days after you leave the group.

It’s not possible to restore a group once it’s been deleted. To rejoin a group chat you’ve left, you’ll need to ask the group admin to re-invite you. Learn more in this article.

Note:

  • Only admins can delete groups for all members. If you’re an admin, you can learn how to exit and delete a group in this article.
  • For additional privacy, you can control who can add you to a group by adjusting your WhatsApp group privacy settings. Learn how in this article.

Community groups

If the group is part of a community, you’ll also exit the community and any groups in the community.

Exit a group or exit and delete a group

  1. Open the group chat, then tap the group name.
  2. Tap Exit group.
  3. You have the option to report the group. If you select Report group, the last five messages in the chat are sent to WhatsApp.
  4. Choose from one of the following options:

  • Exit group: To exit the group but keep your chat history.

  • Exit and delete for me: To exit and delete the group from your Chats tab.

Delete a group you exited

You can also delete a group you previously exited.

  1. Open the group chat, then tap the group name.
  2. Tap Delete group > Delete group.

Note:

  • You can’t restore a group once it’s been deleted. You’ll need to create a new group. Learn how in this article.
  • When you delete a group, media received in the chat will also be deleted from your device.
  • Only group admins will be notified that you left the group.
  • When you report a group, WhatsApp receives up to five of the last five messages sent to you by a reported group. No one in the group will be notified. WhatsApp also receives the reported group ID, information on when the message was sent, and the type of message sent (image, video, text, etc.), as well as how the first contact was initiated between you and the reported group.

How to exit and delete groups as an admin

On iPhone

You can delete a group for all members if you’re the group admin. Before you can delete the group, you’ll need to remove all group members.

If you’re a group member, you can exit a group and delete it from your device. Learn how in this article.

What happens when you remove a group member or delete a group

When you delete a group, you won’t see the group in your Chats list. The group chat history will also be erased from your phone.

Removing a member or deleting a group won’t delete the group on other members’ devices. Other members will still see the group in their Chats list and see all previous content unless they delete it themselves. However, one will be able to send messages.

The removed member’s profile name and phone number will be shown in the Past members list in Group info. Their profile photo may also be shown, depending on their settings. Group members can see this information in that list for up to 60 days after a member leaves the group.

If you exit a group without removing all group members, you’ll only be able to delete the group from your device. The group won’t be deleted for other group members.

If you’re the only group admin and leave the group, another member will be chosen at random to become the new admin. If you rejoin the group and would like to be an admin again, you’ll need to ask the group admin to make you one. Learn how in this article.

Remove group members

Before you can exit and delete a group, you’ll need to remove all members.

  1. Open the group chat, then tap the group name.
  2. Tap the member’s name.
  3. Tap Remove {member} > OK.

Exit or delete a group

After removing all group members, you can exit the group.

  1. Open the group chat, then tap the group name.
  2. Tap Exit group.
  3. You might see the option to report the group. If you select Report group, the last five messages in the chat are sent to WhatsApp.
  4. Choose from one of the following options:

  • Exit group: To exit the group but keep your chat history.

  • Exit and delete for me: To exit and delete the group from your Chats tab.

Note:

  • When you exit a group that’s part of a community, you’ll also exit the community. If you exit a community, you’ll also exit groups in the community.
  • Deleting groups also deletes media received in the chat from the device gallery.
  • You can’t restore a group once it’s been deleted. You’ll need to create a new group. Learn how in this article.
  • When you report a group, WhatsApp receives up to five of the last five messages sent to you by a reported group. No one in the group will be notified. WhatsApp also receives the reported group ID, information on when the message was sent, and the type of message sent (image, video, text, etc.), as well as how the first contact was initiated between you and the reported group.

About group join requests

On iPhone

Copy link

Android

iOS

Web

Mac

Windows

More

Android

iOS

Web

Mac

Windows

The Approve new members setting empowers admins to help grow, moderate, and protect their groups. Turning on the setting in Group permissions requires the admin to review every request to join the group before a member is allowed to join.

Note: The Approve new members setting is turned off by default. In this case, every member that requests to join the group will be granted admission.

There are several ways a member can join a group:

  • Group invite link
  • Added by another member in the group
  • Group directory in a community
  • QR code

As a member

To request to join a group, you must have been invited by a current member or have found the group through a Group invite link, Group directory in a community, or QR code. When admin approval is required to join the group, members will see the message “An admin must approve your request” above the Request to join button. Members will be able to cancel their request to join at any time by tapping Cancel request. When a member’s request has been approved, the chat will reflect which group admin added the member or if they joined through the group’s invite link.

As a group admin

Group admins will be notified when they have pending requests to review. An admin might see a banner in the group chat or can access the Pending requests screen from the Group info page.

When reviewing a request, group admins can see the source of the request to better help them make decisions. The admin can choose to approve or reject the request. If a group admin doesn’t have enough information about the person requesting access, they can tap on the user to go to their contact info and start a chat with that person.

About group suspensions

Copy link

Group members and admins might see the message “This group is suspended” when a group violates our Terms of Service. In addition to relying on reports from users, WhatsApp uses advanced machine learning to identify and ban accounts engaging in bulk or automated messaging, and to evaluate basic information about a group – like its subject, or profile photo – to determine if a group or a group admin might have violated our Terms of Service. Using community announcements instead of sending repeated messages to groups or members may help reduce the risk of being flagged as spam. We may prevent further activity in chat groups to comply with our legal obligations.

Only group admins can request a review of a suspended group. Learn more in this article.

There are different types of groups on WhatsApp. Some you’ll need to request to join, and some you can join right away. To join a group, you’ll need to ask a group admin to add you to the group, or send you an invite link or QR code.

Once you receive the group invite, you’ll need to tap Join Group > Join Group. When you join a group, your profile name may be visible to other members in the group.

You can control who can add you to groups in your privacy settings. Learn how in this article.

Message history in groups

When you’re added to a group, the member who added you may choose to send message history to you. They can send up to 100 messages from the last 14 days.

You’ll receive a notification if message history is sent.

  • New members who joined the group through a group invite link or QR code won’t be able to view message history.
  • Groups may work differently if you’re invited to a group by a business using authorized third-party providers to help them manage WhatsApp. Learn more.

  • Click Safety tools to learn how to stay safe in groups.
  • Click Ok to join the group.
  • Click Exit group to leave the group.

You can also control who can add you to groups in your privacy settings. Learn how in this article.

Message history in groups

Add a contact to a call through a chat thread

  2. Select a chat thread.
  3. Tap.
  4. Tap Add to call.
  • If you’re currently in a call with only one other user, tap Add to current call again to confirm you want to upgrade to a group call.

Join a group voice call

Join an incoming group voice call

  1. You’ll receive a notification when someone invites you to join a group voice call.

  • Tap Ring to send a notification to people who’ve already been invited.

Join a missed group voice call

  1. Open WhatsApp, then tap the Calls tab.
  2. If the call was started from a group chat, you can join by opening that chat and tapping Join.
  3. If the call is ongoing, tap the call you’d like to join. This will open the call info screen.
  4. Tap Join.

Mute someone else

You can mute other people in a group call. To do so, tap and hold on the person’s name. Then press Mute.

The person can unmute themselves at any time by tapping the microphone icon. You can message a person directly on a group call by tapping and holding their tile.

Group voice calling tips

  • Make sure you’re using the latest version of WhatsApp. If your call isn’t going through, it’s possible the other person is on an older operating system or WhatsApp version.
  • You can’t switch a group voice call to a video call.
  • You can only mute someone three times.
  • To save data, make and answer calls when connected to Wi-Fi. You can also turn Use Less Data for Calls on or off by tapping Settings or your profile picture, then tapping Storage and data.
  • You can’t remove a contact during a group voice call. The contact would need to hang up their phone to disconnect from the call.
  • It’s possible to be in a group voice call with someone you’ve blocked. However, you can’t add someone you’ve blocked or who has blocked you to the call. Ignore or decline the call if you don’t want to connect with a blocked contact.
  • You can’t access emergency service numbers through WhatsApp, such as 911 in the United States.
  • Voice message transcripts aren’t available during group voice calls.

If you’re a group admin, you can make another group member an admin.

A group can have an unlimited number of admins, and any admin can make a member an admin. The creator of a group can’t be removed and will remain an admin unless they exit the group.

Note: WhatsApp can’t interfere with group administration functions. For example, we can’t make someone an admin, even if they were previously an admin and removed by another admin.

Make a member an admin

  1. Open the WhatsApp group chat, then tap the group subject.
  2. Tap the member you want to make an admin.
  3. Tap Make group admin.

Make multiple members admins at the same time

  1. Open the WhatsApp group chat, then tap the group subject.
  2. Tap Group permissions > Group admins.
  3. Select the members you want to make admins.
  4. Tap Done.

Dismiss an admin

  1. Open the WhatsApp group chat, then tap the group subject.
  2. Tap the admin you want to dismiss > Dismiss as admin.

Dismiss multiple admins at the same time

  1. Open the WhatsApp group chat, then tap the group subject.
  2. Tap Group permissions > Group admins.
  3. Uncheck the admins you want to dismiss.
  4. Tap Done.

Note: Groups may work differently if you’re invited to a group by a business using authorized third-party providers to help them manage WhatsApp. Learn more.

Learn how to mute @all messages in this article.

Note:

If you’ve been mentioned or replied to in a group

You’ll see a notification with **@** in your chats list next to an unread message if you’ve been mentioned or someone has replied to your message.

You can see messages you were mentioned in or replied to when you open the chat.

Note:

  • Mentioning or tagging someone in a group will override any mute notifications that member has set for the group, unless they’ve also muted @all mentions. They also may have muted your individual chat.
  • The name of the member you’re mentioning might be displayed differently for other group members, depending on the way their name is saved in their address book.

About messaging and groups on parent-managed accounts

On iPhone

Copy link

Android

iOS

More

Android

iOS

Parent-managed accounts are rolling out gradually and may not be available in your region.

With a parent-managed account, parents or guardians can choose who can contact their child, decide which groups they can join, and review message requests from unknown contacts.

Individual messaging

By default, managed accounts can only message with people saved in their contacts.

If a user with a managed account wants to message someone new, they must first add the person as a contact, which will send an alert to their parent.

If a managed account receives a message from someone not saved in their contacts, the message will be sent to a Requests folder for parent approval. Parents will also receive an alert for new message requests.

Only parents are able to change contacts settings for managed accounts, learn more in this article.

Group messaging

By default, only parents can add a managed account to groups, and managed accounts are not able to create groups themselves.

If a managed account receives a group invite, a parent will need to review and accept it using their parent PIN on the child’s device. Parents will receive alerts for group invites and when groups their child is already in grows in size.

Only parents are able to change groups settings for managed accounts, learn more in this article.

Review message requests

As a parent, you can review and approve message requests by using your parent PIN.

  1. Go to your child’s phone and open WhatsApp.
  2. Tap Settings > Parental controls.
  3. Enter your parent PIN.
  4. Tap the Requests folder.
  5. Tap the chat you want to review.
  6. Tap Approve to add the person to your child’s contacts and allow them to chat. Or tap Decline.

Review group and community invites

When a group invite is received from a saved contact, a parent PIN is required before your child can join the group chat or community.

Note: Only a parent can directly add their child to a group chat or community.

  1. Go to your child’s phone and open WhatsApp.
  2. In the Requests folder, tap the group or community invite.
  3. Enter your parent PIN.
  4. Tap Join group or Join community.

Note:

  • Parent-managed account users can block or report someone on WhatsApp to stop receiving their messages and calls.
  • Personal messages are end-to-end encrypted, which means no one, not even the parent or WhatsApp, can read them.

You can mute individual or group chat calls and messages for a specified period of time. You can choose 8 hours, 1 week, or Always. You’ll still receive messages, but your device won’t vibrate or make noise to notify you.

Mute notifications for individual chats

  1. Open an individual chat.
  2. Tap the name of the individual.
  3. Tap Notifications > Mute notification, then select the length of time you’d like to mute notifications for.

Mute notifications for group chats

  1. Open a group chat.
  2. Tap the name of the group.
  3. Tap Notifications.
  4. Tap Mute notifications under Messages or Calls to mute notifications for messages or calls from the group.
  5. Select the length of time you’d like to mute notifications for.

Tap Muted > Unmute on a chat that has been muted to unmute notifications for that chat.

Note: When you mute message notifications for a chat, your device won’t alert you of incoming notifications. However, it’s important to remember:

  • Contacts aren’t notified that you’ve muted the chat.
  • If you’ve enabled read receipts, contacts will still receive read receipts when you read their messages.
  • You’ll still have the unread message count next to the chat.

Mute notifications for lists

To mute notifications for lists:

  1. Tap Settings or your profile picture > Lists.
  2. Tap the list you’d like to edit.
  3. Tap Mute to mute chats from contacts and groups in this list. You can choose to mute them for 8 hours, 1 week, or Always.

Alternatively, from the Chats tab, tap and hold a list > Mute or select a list and tap Manage > Mute to update notification preferences.

Note:

  • Your contacts won’t see that you muted the chats.
  • You’ll still be notified if you’re mentioned.

Learn more about how to use lists in this article.

Mute WhatsApp notifications on your device

  1. Tap iPhone Settings > Notifications.
  2. Under Notification style, tap WhatsApp and turn on or off Allow Notifications.

Note: If you disable or silence WhatsApp notifications from device settings, updates made to notification settings in WhatsApp won’t override them. If you enable custom notifications in WhatsApp, a new notification category will be added in your device settings, with notifications enabled for that custom setting.

How to rejoin a group chat

Copy link

To rejoin a group chat you’ve left or deleted, you’ll need to ask the group admin to re-invite you. In some cases, if the group admin has allowed them to in settings, other group members can re-invite you.

Note:

  • If you’re the only group admin and leave the group, another member is chosen at random to become the new admin. If you rejoin the group and would like to be an admin again, you need to ask the group admin to make you one.
  • When your account is deleted, you’re removed from all of your WhatsApp groups.

Rejoin a group you’ve left twice

If you want to rejoin a group you’ve left twice, you’ll need to wait 24 hours before the group admin or other members can re-invite you.

To avoid the wait time to re-invite a member, the admin or another member can share a group invite link with you.

Note: Every time you leave a group, the amount of time you must wait to be re-added by the group admin increases. The maximum amount of time you’d have to wait would be 81 days.

Access groups in a community

There are a few ways to access groups in a community.

You can tap or click the community the group is part of from the Chats tab. Then, tap or click the group under Groups you can join.

Alternatively, you can search for your group by typing the group name into the search bar.

Recover groups you deleted

It’s not possible to see or recover groups you’ve exited and deleted or your group history. You’ll need to ask the group admin to re-invite you.

WhatsApp uses various signals, such as group metadata or user reports, to identify groups that may be harmful or show signs of spam or scams. If a group is suspended no one in the group can send messages, add members, download or forward media. You can learn more in this article.

If you’re a group admin and you think the suspension was a mistake, you can request a review.

Request a review

  1. Tap the suspended group.
  2. In the popup This group is suspended, tap Request review.
  3. Tap Ok

We’ll notify you when the review is complete, typically within 24 hours.

If the review was successful, the group can resume activity. If the review was unsuccessful, the group will remain suspended and the group admin(s) and members can tap Delete group.

Note: You can only request a suspension review once.

About sending message history in groups

Copy link

This is a new feature we’re building and testing out and may not be available to you yet. In the meantime, we recommend keeping WhatsApp updated on your device so you can get the feature as soon as it’s available.

When you add a new member to a group, you may have the option to send message history to them to help them quickly get up to speed. You can send all available pinned messages and up to 100 messages. When you send message history, the new member will receive a notification. All members of the group will see a system message notifying them that message history was sent to the new member.

Group admins have the option to turn off the ability for members to send message history. If Send message history is turned off, group members won’t see the option to send message history when they add a new member to the group.

Messages in message history are end-to-end encrypted, meaning no one outside of the group, not even WhatsApp, can read them.

Messages not included in message history

  • Messages that disappeared when disappearing messages was turned on.
  • Live location, view once messages, and business transactions.

Note:

  • Message history can’t be sent to new members who join the group through a group invite link or QR code.
  • If someone you sent message history to reports content that was sent as part of the message history you sent, you’ll be reported. The original sender of the message won’t be reported.

How to stay safe in groups on WhatsApp

On iPhone

Copy link

Android

iOS

Web

More

Android

iOS

Web

Mac

At WhatsApp, we believe that you should have control over who you communicate with and what groups you join. That’s why we provide tools for you to leave or report groups that you don’t want to be a part of.

When you’re added to a group by someone not saved in your contacts, we show you information about the group so you can decide if you want to exit the group. Tap Stay to stay in the group, or Exit group to leave the group. After tapping Exit group, you can also tap Report to WhatsApp if you would like to report the group.

Group privacy settings

By default, your group privacy settings are set to Everyone. For additional privacy, you can control who can add you to a group by adjusting your WhatsApp Settings. You can select Everyone, My contacts, or My contacts except…. Learn how to change your group privacy settings in this article.

Report a message

You can report a message in a group and block the member. The message will be sent to WhatsApp, and the sender or group won’t be notified. WhatsApp also receives the reported user ID, information on when the message was sent, and the type of message sent (image, video, text, etc.).

  1. Tap and hold the message.
  2. Tap More….
  3. Tap Report > Report and block or Report.

If you believe a group has been compromised, you can report the group or report the admin or member involved.

Block a group

It’s not possible to block a group, however you can block and report group admins and members. For example, if you think they’re sending problematic content or spam. Learn what happens when you block and report someone in this article.

Report a group

  1. Tap the group name > Report group.
  2. Tap Report and exit or Report.

When you report a group, WhatsApp receives up to five of the last messages sent to you in the reported group. No one in the group will be notified. WhatsApp also receives the reported group ID, information on when the message was sent, and the type of message sent (image, video, text, etc.).

Block a group admin or member

You can stop receiving messages from group admins or members by blocking them.

Learn how to block a group admin and how to block and report someone.

Exit a group

  1. Tap the group name > Exit group.
  2. Tap Exit group.

How to turn disappearing messages on or off in a group

On iPhone

Copy link

Android

iOS

Web

Mac

More

Android

iOS

Web

Mac

You can send messages that disappear on WhatsApp by turning disappearing messages on.

  • When you enable disappearing messages, you can choose to have messages disappear after 24 hours, 7 days, or 90 days, unless the messages are kept.
  • Disappearing messages can be kept in the chat so that they won’t disappear. Learn more about kept messages in this article.
  • You can turn on disappearing messages for multiple existing chats, and new messages sent in the chat will disappear after the duration you select. The most recent duration you select controls new messages in the chat, not previous messages you’ve sent or received.
  • You can choose to turn disappearing messages on for all of your chats, or select specific chats.

Turn on disappearing messages

In a group chat, any group member can enable disappearing messages. However, a group admin can change group settings to allow only admins to enable disappearing messages. Learn how to change group admin settings in this article.

  1. Go to the Chats tab and tap a group chat.
  2. Tap the group name to see Group Info.
  3. Tap Disappearing Messages.
  • If prompted, tap Continue.
  1. Select 24 hours, 7 days, or 90 days.

You can also turn on disappearing messages when creating a new group chat.

Turn off disappearing messages

Anyone in a group chat can disable disappearing messages at any time, unless a group admin has limited that action to admins only. You can choose to keep specific messages to prevent them from disappearing, as long as the duration time hasn’t passed. If you decide to disable disappearing messages, you won’t have the option to keep them.

  1. Go to the Chats tab and tap a group chat.
  2. Tap the group name to see Group info.
  3. Tap Disappearing Messages.
  • If prompted, tap Continue.
  1. Select Off.

The Code Verify web browser extension provides an additional layer of security on the web by verifying that you are using an authentic and untampered version of WhatsApp Web. The extension is available on the following browsers:

  • Google Chrome
  • Mozilla Firefox
  • Microsoft Edge

To install the Code Verify extension on your web browser, follow the instructions provided by your browser. For additional support, contact your web browser’s support team.

Note:

  • For the best user experience, pin the Code Verify browser extension to your toolbar once downloaded so that you can easily see the extension and confirm whether it was able to validate WhatsApp Web.
  • If you’re using WhatsApp Web on an incognito or private tab, you should follow your browser’s instructions to enable the extension on incognito tabs.
  • The Code Verify browser extension won’t access any other browser tabs or windows you have open.
  • The extension doesn’t log any data, metadata, or user data, and it doesn’t share any information with WhatsApp. It also doesn’t read or access the messages you send or receive.

There is a known issue for some linked devices not displaying up to one year of chat history. We’re working to fix this as soon as possible. In the meantime, you can still see your chat history on your primary device. We encourage you to keep WhatsApp updated on your linked device. Updates are released regularly and may contain fixes for bugs and other issues.

Linked devices provide a reliable, secure way to access WhatsApp from any of your devices. You can stay connected by linking up to four devices at a time to your primary phone. You’ll still need your primary phone to register your WhatsApp account and link new devices. Learn how to link a device here.

Supported linked devices include:

  • Windows
  • Mac
  • Web
  • Android tablet
  • iPad
  • WearOS
  • Apple Watch
  • Companion Phones
  • Meta AI glasses
  • VR

Benefits of linked devices

[Embedded video omitted]

0:00 / 0:46

  • Use WhatsApp on your computer even when your phone is off.
  • Be more productive with multi-tasking and faster typing on a larger keyboard.
  • Use WhatsApp on a bigger screen to view and share your media and files with others.
  • Use the WhatsApp Mac or Windows app to make voice and video calls with up to 32 people.

Your personal messages, media, and calls are end-to-end encrypted. Each linked device connects to WhatsApp independently, maintaining the same expected level of privacy and security through end-to-end encryption.

Learn more about end-to-end encryption in this article. For information on how we collect, process, and share your data, please see the WhatsApp Privacy Policy.

Keep your account safer

  • Enable push notifications on your phone. By enabling push notifications, you can remove devices you don’t recognize from being linked to your account. If you don’t recognize the device, tap the notification to review and remove it.

  • Check your linked devices regularly. To review all devices linked to your account, tap

    [Image: Settings Tab (gear)]

    Linked devices. To log out of a linked device, tap the device > Log out. We’ll also automatically disconnect linked devices after 30 days of inactivity.

  • You can scan a WhatApp QR code or use your phone number to link a new device to your account. Only link on WhatsApp Web, WhatsApp for Windows and Mac, WhatsApp Android Tablets, WhatsApp companion phones, or AI glasses.

  • Linking your device through unofficial apps or websites may put your account at risk. Unofficial apps and websites are fake WhatsApp apps and websites developed by third-parties. They aren’t supported because we can’t validate their security or privacy practices. If you link your account to an unofficial app or website, or have done so in the past, your account could be temporarily or permanently banned. These unofficial apps or websites could compromise your account, meaning that your account could be used to send spam and scams to other WhatsApp users. Learn more about unofficial apps in this article and how you can protect yourself from scams in this article.

Note: Your phone doesn’t need to stay online to use WhatsApp on linked devices, but your linked devices will be logged out if you don’t use your phone for over 14 days.

Unsupported features

These features aren’t currently supported:

  • Viewing a live location.
  • Creating and viewing broadcast lists.
  • Interacting with businesses using WhatsApp Flows.

On WhatsApp Web

Copy link

Web

More

Web

Code Verify adds an extra layer of security to end-to-end encryption when people use WhatsApp on the web. If you have downloaded the Code Verify web browser extension, you might see a warning that says: “Cannot validate the page due to another browser extension. Consider pausing the other extension(s) and re-trying.”

This might occur for the following reasons:

  • You have another extension installed that is interfering with our ability to verify the page.
  • Your other active browser extensions might be able to read or modify content that you see on WhatsApp Web. The best way to ensure the security of your messages on WhatsApp Web is to disable any extensions that cause this warning.

To resolve the issue:

  • Try pausing your other extensions, going through the validation process again, and unpausing your other extensions once finished. You might have to reload WhatsApp Web to clear the warning.
  • If the error persists, disable any extensions you’re unsure of while using the page. You might have to reload WhatsApp Web to clear the warning.
  • If you trust your other active extensions, no action is required.

If you’re seeing this error, it could be caused by browser issues on your computer. WhatsApp Web uses your browser’s database to securely store your messages. There may be a problem with your browser’s database causing device linking issues on WhatsApp Web. You can find the solutions below to resolve the issue.

Use another browser

The easiest solution is to try using another browser. Go to web.whatsapp.com on a browser from the list below.

    [Image: More (three vertical dots)]

  1. Check the boxes next to Cookies and other site data and Cached images and files.

Reset browser settings to default

On Chrome:

Restart your computer

About WhatsApp Web

Copy link

WhatsApp Web lets you message privately from any browser on your desktop, keeping you connected. It offers the convenience and benefits of a bigger screen, but doesn’t require you to download a desktop app.

Benefits of WhatsApp Web

  • Convenience: Login from any browser to stay in touch with your contacts, use keyboard shortcuts for efficient navigation.
  • Increased productivity: Quickly switch between conversations, organize your chats in folders, and pin frequent chats.
  • Improved collaboration: Create groups for teamwork, coordinate in real time, and share files and links easily.
  • Flexible workspace: Larger screen, multiple tabs, and flexible configurations for keyboard and mouse.

Log in

  1. Go to web.whatsapp.com on your desktop browser.
  2. Follow the on-screen instructions to scan the QR code with your phone.
  3. Now you can use WhatsApp on your browser.

This feature is rolling out gradually and may not be available to you yet. In the meantime, we recommend keeping WhatsApp updated on your device so you can get the feature as soon as it’s available.

You have the option to add your Instagram profile link to your WhatsApp profile, allowing people who view your profile to tap the link directly to visit your Instagram profile. You can also select who can see your link by going to your WhatsApp Settings, then tapping Privacy.

Add your Instagram profile link

  1. Tap WhatsApp Settings or your profile photo, then tap your profile photo again.
  2. Under Links, tap Add links.
  3. Tap Instagram and type your Instagram username.
  4. Tap Save.

Remove your Instagram profile link

  1. Tap WhatsApp Settings or your profile photo, then tap your profile photo again.
  2. Under Links, tap Instagram.
  3. Next to Instagram, tap X.
  4. Tap Remove link.

Manage who can see your Instagram profile link

Your contacts can see your Instagram profile link by default, but you can change your privacy settings at any time to manage who can see it. If you block a contact, that person won’t see any updates to your profile link.

To update your privacy settings:

  1. Tap WhatsApp Settings or your profile photo, then tap Privacy.
  2. Tap Links and choose Everyone, My contacts, My contacts except…, or Nobody.

You can learn more about changing your privacy settings in this help article.

If you can’t download or update WhatsApp from the App Store, it’s probably due to one of the following error codes:

  • “There’s insufficient space on the device”
  • “This app is incompatible with your device”
  • “This item isn’t available in your country”

Learn more about each of these error codes below.

Note: Before deleting WhatsApp data or clearing cache on your device, consider backing up your chats to save your chat history. Learn more about backing up your chat history here.

“There’s insufficient space on the device”

If you’re unable to install WhatsApp due to insufficient space on your device, try the following:

  • Delete data and apps you no longer use.
  • Clear cached data.

A minimum of 1 GB of free space is recommended when installing or updating apps.

Note: If you delete your WhatsApp photos, voice messages, or videos, you can’t see or listen to them anymore.

“This app is incompatible with your device”

Read about supported iOS devices in this article.

“This app is currently not available in your country or region”

If an error says the app isn’t available in your country, please check Apple Support for specific troubleshooting steps.

Note: You may see an error message “This file format is not supported”. We’re working on fixing this. In the meantime, please keep WhatsApp updated.

Media include photos, videos, audio, video messages, voice messages, location, reactions, documents, stickers, gifs, and emojis. Supported video formats include 3GP, AVI, FLV, MKV, MOV, and MP4.

If you can’t download, open, or send media files, the most common reason why is a weak internet connection. We recommend you:

  • Restart your phone, or turn it off and on.
  • Update WhatsApp to the latest version.
  • Try connecting to mobile data if you’re on Wi-Fi or Wi-Fi if you’re on mobile data.
  • Contact your mobile provider.

Note: If you see question marks instead of pictures in Media, Links, and Docs or blank boxes instead of media in your chats, this might mean that the media was not properly backed-up to iCloud. Unfortunately, this means that the media can’t be recovered through this backup.If a photo appears blurry, it means that WhatsApp can’t find the photo on your device.

Can’t hear audio

If you’re experiencing issues with audio playback, try the following:

  • Close other applications that might be using your audio output and interfering with WhatsApp’s audio playback.
  • Test the file using an audio player outside of WhatsApp.

Can’t open PDF

If you’re unable to open a downloaded PDF file on your phone, try the following:

  • Make sure you have a PDF reader installed on your phone. Without a PDF reader, you won’t be able to open a downloaded PDF file.
  • If the file is password-protected, confirm that you have permissions to view the file.
  • If the file still won’t open, try turning your phone off and then back on.

Note: You can’t share PDFs to channels.

If you can’t download, open, or send media files, the most common reason why is a weak internet connection. We recommend you:

Can’t hear audio

If you’re experiencing issues with audio playback, try the following:

  • Close other applications that might be using your audio output and interfering with WhatsApp’s audio playback.
  • Test the file using an audio player outside of WhatsApp.

Can’t open or preview PDF

Note: PDF preview and editing is powered by Adobe Acrobat.

PDFs open in a full-screen preview directly in WhatsApp. If a PDF isn’t loading, try the following:

  • Check your internet connection. PDF preview requires an active connection.

  • Refresh the page or try reopening the PDF.

  • Make sure you’re using the latest version of WhatsApp Web.

  • If the preview still won’t load, click

    [Image: down arrow with horizontal bracket underneath]

    to save the PDF and open it with your device’s PDF viewer.

  • If the file is password-protected, confirm that you have permissions to view the file.

Can’t use Edit PDF or Edit in Acrobat

If the PDF editing tools aren’t working or Edit in Acrobat isn’t opening, try the following:

  • Make sure pop-ups aren’t blocked in your browser settings.
  • Try using a different browser.
  • Check your internet connection.

Note: You don’t need an Adobe account to use the editing tools. You can’t share PDFs to channels.

You can set WhatsApp to automatically download photos, voice messages, videos, and documents when using mobile data, Wi-Fi, and when roaming.

To enable or disable media downloads, follow these instructions:

Configure automatic photo, video, or voice message downloading

  1. Tap WhatsApp Settings or your profile picture, then tap Storage and data.
  2. In the Media auto-download section, tap the type of media you’d like to configure your auto-download settings for and select:
  • Never: Media won’t automatically download. You will need to manually tap each file to download it. Note: If you set your Auto-Download settings to Never, your videos won’t automatically download. However, once you tap the play button, the video will play and continue the download process in the background.
  • Wi-Fi: Media will automatically download when you’re connected to a Wi-Fi hotspot such as your home internet.
  • Wi-Fi and cellular: Media will automatically download whenever you have an internet connection.

Note:- If you have a limited data plan, we suggest you restrict media to auto-download when connected to Wi-Fi only. - YouTube videos are unable to auto-download. - To manually download photos and videos, tap and hold the photo or video, then tap Save.

You can personalize your photos and videos by adding stickers, emojis, text, freehand drawings, filters, and more.

Edit photos and videos

Take a new photo or video

  1. Tap, then take a new photo or video.
  2. Start editing your photo or video.

Use an existing photo or video

  1. Tap

    [Image: Add (blue plus sign)]

    [Image: Photo Video Library (photo with landscape)]

    , then choose an existing item from your Albums.

  2. Start editing your photo or video.

Live Photos

Live Photos include a video and audio recording of the moments before and after the photo was taken. Tap

[Image: Live Photo (circle within circle within dotted circle)]

to turn it on or off. Tap

[Image: Mute Video (volume icon)]

to turn off the audio in your Live Photo. If you edit a photo, Live Photos will be turned off.

Adjust the quality of your photo or video message

Tap

[Image: HD Media (the letters H-D within a rectangle with a gear in the bottom right corner)]

, then tap:

  • Standard quality to send a standard quality photo or video. Standard quality photos and videos use less data and are sent faster than HD quality photos and videos.
  • HD quality to send a high quality photo or video. HD quality photos and videos are clearer than Standard quality photos and videos, but use more data and take longer to send.

Note: HD media isn’t currently available for status updates or profile pictures.

Crop or rotate your photo or video

  1. Tap

    [Image: Crop Rotate (overlapping corners with curved arrow)]

    .

    • Tap the

      [Image: Aspect Ratio (composite of three rectangles of different sizes)]

      button to select one of the presets.

    • To manually crop your media, tap and hold any of the handles, then drag them in or out to the desired size.

    • To rotate your photo or video, tap

      [Image: Rotate Left Two (square with left arrow with curved tail in top right corner)]

      repeatedly.

    • Tap Reset to undo all your changes and revert to the original size and rotation.

  2. Tap Done when you’ve finished.

Trim a video

  1. Drag the slider at the top to trim the video.

  2. Tap

    [Image: Play (right-facing arrowhead)]

    to preview your newly trimmed video.

Apply a filter to your photo or video

  1. Swipe up on your photo or video.
  2. Select a filter.
  3. Tap Done to continue editing.

Add stickers or emojis to your photo or video

  1. Tap

    [Image: Sticker (sticker with upturned corner)]

    [Image: Emoji (smiley face)]

    or

    [Image: Sticker (sticker with upturned corner)]

    .

  2. Tap the item that you’d like to use.

    • To move the item, tap and hold it, then drag it.
    • To resize the item, pinch in or out to make it smaller or larger.
    • To rotate the item, pinch and turn it.

  3. To delete an emoji or sticker, tap and hold it, and drag it to

    [Image: Delete Editing Status (trash can)]

    .

Add text to your photo or video

  1. Tap

    [Image: Text (pencil within circle)]

    .

  2. Enter your text in the text field.

  3. Tap Done when you’ve finished.

  4. To delete a text box, tap and hold it, and drag it to

    [Image: Delete Editing Status (trash can)]

    .

Change the appearance of your text

  1. Tap the text box.
    • To change the text and background color, slide your finger up and down the Color selector.
    • Tap the font type at the bottom of the screen to select a font.
  2. Tap Done to make other changes to your text.
    • To resize the text, pinch in or out to make it smaller or larger.

Add a caption

Enter a caption in the text box.

Draw on your photo or video

    [Image: Draw (pencil)]

    .

      [Image: Pen Width Medium (squiggle)]

      icons below your photo.

    • To delete a line, tap

      [Image: Undo (left arrow with U-shaped tail)]

      .

Blur all or part of your photo

    [Image: Draw (pencil)]

    .

[Image: Mute Video (volume icon)]

to turn off the audio in your video.

Send your media

Once you’ve finished editing your media, tap

[Image: Send (paper airplane within green circle)]

to send.

You can customize your profile by editing your profile picture, name, and About. You can also set an avatar alongside your profile picture.

Note:You can edit your username at any time. Learn more about how to create or manage your username.

Edit your profile picture

  1. Tap your profile picture to get to settings. Tap your profile picture again, then tap Edit.

  • Tap Take photo > Use Photo > Done to take a photo with your camera.

  • Tap Choose photo > Choose to select an existing photo.

  • Tap Create Ai image > type your prompt >

    [Image: right arrow within circle]

    [Image: checkmark within circle]

    .

  • Tap Delete photo > Delete to remove your current profile photo.

Import profile picture from Facebook or Instagram

You can import your WhatsApp profile picture from Facebook or Instagram if you choose to add your accounts to Accounts Center.

Accounts Center allows you to manage account settings and connected experiences across Facebook, Instagram, and WhatsApp. Learn more about WhatsApp in Accounts Center.

To import your profile picture from Facebook or Instagram:

  1. Tap Settings or your profile picture, then tap Edit.
  2. Tap Import from Facebook or Import from Instagram.
    • If prompted, follow the instructions to add your accounts to Accounts Center.
  3. Move and resize the circle to crop the image for your profile picture.
  4. Tap Choose.

Sync profile picture with Facebook and Instagram

You can use the same picture across WhatsApp, Facebook, Instagram if you add your accounts to Accounts Center.

  1. Tap Settings or your profile picture, then tap Account Center.
  2. Tap Syncing profile pictures > Start a new sync.
  3. Select profiles and tap Continue.
  4. Choose a profile picture.
  5. Tap Save.

Note: When you change your profile picture on a synced account, your other synced accounts will be updated also.

To remove an account from syncing profile pictures:

  1. Tap Settings or your profile picture, then tap Account Center.
  2. Tap Syncing profile pictures.
  3. Tap Your synced profiles.
  4. Uncheck profile and tap Continue.
  5. Tap Save.

To stop syncing profile pictures:

  1. Tap Settings or your profile picture, then tap Account Center.
  2. Tap Syncing profile pictures.
  3. Tap Your synced profiles.
  4. Tap Stop syncing profile pictures > Confirm

Set your avatar as your profile picture

You can use your avatar as or alongside your profile picture.

If you already created an avatar:

  1. Tap Settings or your profile picture, then tap Edit.
  2. Tap Add avatar.
  3. Tap Continue.
  4. Select an avatar.
  5. Tap Save.

If you haven’t created an avatar, learn more here.

Use an AI-generated image for your profile photo

You might have the option to generate an AI image to use as your profile photo. Learn how in this article.

Note:

  • This feature is currently only available in limited countries and might not be available to you yet, even if other users in your country have access.
  • At this time, only prompts in English, Arabic, French, Hindi, Indonesian, Portuguese, Spanish, Tagalog, Thai, and Vietnamese are supported.

Edit your profile name

  1. Tap your profile picture twice, then tap your name.
  2. Enter your new name.

How to free up storage on WhatsApp

On iPhone

Copy link

Android

iOS

More

Android

iOS

To ensure that WhatsApp works properly, make sure that your phone has storage space available. You can clear up storage space by deleting stored media or chats or freeing up storage on your phone outside of WhatsApp.

It’s possible that there might be a difference in the storage usage noted by your WhatsApp app and iPhone. This is mainly because of the difference in the way WhatsApp calculates storage versus your iPhone.

Note: We recommend creating a backup before deleting any content from your iPhone. Learn how in this article.

View storage

  1. Tap your profile picture.
  2. Tap Storage and data > Manage storage.

The amount of space taken up on your device by WhatsApp is displayed at the top of the screen.

You can also directly manage storage from any chat.

  1. Tap any chat.
  2. Tap the chat name.
  3. Tap Manage storage.

This will show you how much space the chat’s media is taking up, with files sorted from largest to smallest.

Review and delete items

You can free up storage by deleting items that are large or have been forwarded many times. You can also delete items per chat.

Review items

  1. Tap your profile picture.
  2. Tap Storage and data > Manage storage.
  • Note: The amount of space taken up on your device by WhatsApp is displayed at the top of the screen.
  1. Select a chat or channel. You can tap Search to search for chats or channels.
  • Tap the sort icon to sort by Newest, Oldest, or Largest. The file size of the item is displayed in the top right corner of the item.
  1. Tap an item to review.
  • From this screen, you can share, forward, star or unstar, reply to, and draw on the item.

Delete items

If you delete an item, it’ll be deleted from your WhatsApp media. Deleted items might still be saved on your device. If you have multiple copies of an item, you’ll also need to delete all copies to free up space.

  1. Tap your profile picture.
  2. Tap Storage and data > Manage storage.
  3. Select a chat or channel.
  • Tap Search to search for chats or channels.
  1. Tap the item you want to delete or tap Select to select multiple items.
  • Tap Select all to delete all items.

  1. Tap

    [Image: Delete Message (trash can)]

    .

  • If your selection includes starred items, you can choose to Delete all except starred or Delete all.
  • If your selection includes duplicate items, and doesn’t include starred items, you can choose to Delete items or Delete items and any copies.

Note: Media will be deleted from your device if you select Delete media in this chat while clearing the chat. This won’t remove you from any groups or remove the chat from the Chats tab.

Delete items through search

You can also delete individual items by using the search feature.

  1. On the Chats tab, tap

    [Image: Search (magnifying glass)]

    .

  2. Tap Photos, Videos, or Documents.

  3. Tap the item you want to delete.

  4. Tap

    [Image: Delete Message (trash can)]

    Delete for me.

Delete contents from an individual or group chat

You can free additional space by clearing media files from any chat.

  1. Tap and hold the chat you wish to clear.
  2. Tap Clear chat.
  3. Select Clear all media.
  4. Check or uncheck Videos and GIFs, Photos, Stickers, Documents, and Audio to determine what items are deleted.
  • Select Clear starred messages to delete starred messages.
  1. Tap Clear media.

You can also delete the entire contents of a chat, including media, links, files, and messages.

  1. Open the chat you’d like to clear.
  2. Tap the contact name or group name.
  3. Tap Clear chat > Clear all messages.

Note: Clearing a chat won’t delete the chat itself or remove you from a group. The chat will still be listed on the Chats tab unless you delete it. Learn how to delete a chat.

Low storage alerts

If the available storage amount on your device reaches critically low levels, WhatsApp might not work properly. If this happens, WhatsApp might prompt you to free up space to continue using the app.

To learn how to free up storage on your phone outside of WhatsApp, visit the Apple Support website.
