This article explains how billing, payments, and cancellations work for Meta One.

Meta One is a paid subscription that gives you a set of exclusive benefits across Meta technologies, including Instagram and Facebook. You can subscribe through a supported Meta mobile app on iPhone or Android.

Learn how to subscribe to Meta One.

Meta One billing cycle and automatic renewal

Meta One renews automatically each month unless you cancel your subscription. You’re charged on the same date each month as your original purchase date.

For example, if you subscribed to Meta One on January 15, you’re charged again on February 15, March 15, and so on.

Note: If your billing date falls on a day that doesn’t exist in a given month (for example, the 31st in a 30-day month), you’re charged on the last day of that month instead.

Accepted payment methods for Meta One

The payment methods you can use for Meta One depend on the store where you subscribe:

  • Apple App Store: See Apple App Store payment methods.
  • Google Play Store: See Google Play Store payment methods.

Your Meta One subscription is linked to the platform, device type, and account you used to subscribe. You need to manage billing and payments through the same platform and account.

Update your Meta One payment method

To update the payment method for your Meta One subscription, go to the store where you originally subscribed:

  • Apple App Store: Update your payment method through your Apple account.
  • Google Play Store: Update your payment method through your Google Play account.

You can also update your payment method from the app you used to subscribe:

  1. Open WhatsApp Settings.
  2. Tap Subscriptions, then tap Meta One.
  3. Tap Payment method, below Your subscription, then follow the prompts to update your payment method.

You must have at least one valid payment method on file to keep your subscription active. Payment method changes take effect at the start of your next billing cycle.

Note: Add a backup payment method to your account. If your default payment fails, your backup method is charged automatically. If you don’t have a backup and your payment fails, you may get a short grace period to fix the issue before your subscription is canceled.

View your Meta One payment history

To check your Meta One payment history, including the payment amount, date, and status, go to the store where you originally subscribed:

  • Apple App Store: View your payment history in your Apple account.
  • Google Play Store: View your payment history in your Google Play account.

Note: Make sure you’re signed into the same Apple or Google account you used for your original Meta One purchase. If you use a different account, you won’t see your Meta One subscription or payment history.

Meta One promotions

A promotion may be available for first-time Meta One subscribers to try the subscription before being charged.

You’re automatically charged the monthly subscription fee when your trial ends. To avoid being charged, cancel at least 24 hours before the promotion ends.

If you cancel and resubscribe to Meta One before your original trial period ends, your trial picks up where it left off. You won’t be charged until the original trial end date.

Note: The free trial may not be available in all regions. Eligibility and availability may change.

Cancel your Meta One subscription

Meta One renews automatically each month unless you cancel. If you cancel, your subscription stays active until the end of your billing cycle. After that, you lose access to all Meta One benefits across Facebook, Instagram, and WhatsApp.

If you purchased Meta One through the Apple App Store or Google Play Store, follow that store’s cancellation process. To avoid being charged for another billing cycle, cancel your Meta One subscription at least 24 hours before your current billing period ends.

Learn how to cancel your Meta One subscription.

If you have trouble with billing or payments for Meta One, visit Troubleshoot Meta One subscription issues.

Note: This article is about Meta Verified, a paid subscription for businesses. If you’re looking for help with two-step verification (a security PIN for your account), see this article instead.

Note: This feature may not be available to you yet. To check availability, go to Settings or Business Tools in the WhatsApp Business app and tap Meta Verified. If you don’t see the Meta Verified option, it’s not yet available to you.

Meta Verified is a paid subscription that helps your business establish its presence across WhatsApp, Instagram, and Facebook and get a verified badge (blue tick) on your WhatsApp Business profile. Meta Verified provides tools to help you build more confidence with new audiences, protect your brand and more efficiently engage with your audience. If your business has multiple accounts on WhatsApp, we recommend subscribing to a Meta Verified subscription plan that includes the protected business accounts benefit.

Before you apply for Meta Verified

Those interested in signing up for Meta Verified for Business on WhatsApp will need to apply and meet certain eligibility requirements. Prior to applying, please review the WhatsApp Business Policy to ensure compliance with our Terms of Service. We recommend carefully reviewing this article to understand how to comply with the Business Messaging and Commerce policies and to learn more about the appropriate uses of WhatsApp and the activities that violate the WhatsApp Terms of Service. We recommend having your business information ready before you begin the application process.

If your WhatsApp Business account is linked to a business account on Facebook or Instagram, you may be prompted to log in to the Facebook or Instagram account before completing your subscription. Learn how to link Facebook and Instagram accounts to your WhatsApp business accounts in this article.

Learn more about the steps you need to complete before purchasing a subscription here.

Note:

  • In order to successfully subscribe with these linked accounts, your Facebook or Instagram account must have Full control admin permissions. Learn more in this article.
  • The business name you’d like to use for your Meta Verified subscription needs to match the name reflected on any business documentation you provide during the verification process.
  • Protected accounts can still be banned for violating WhatsApp Business Terms of Service.

How to apply for Meta Verified

To apply for Meta Verified and get the blue tick on your WhatsApp Business profile:

  1. From the Chatlist, tap Tools.
  2. Tap Meta Verified. If you don’t see the Meta Verified option, this means that either it’s not yet available in your country or Meta has determined that your business account doesn’t meet the eligibility requirements.
  3. Tap Continue.
  4. Tap the button for the subscription package we’ve recommended for your business.
  5. Select the account(s) you want to verify. You have the option of bundling your WhatsApp account with linked accounts on Facebook or Instagram and verify them all at the same time.
  6. Tap Continue.
  7. If your business account meets the eligibility requirements, you’ll be prompted to set up your payment method and make your first payment. Tap Pay.
  8. Enter your payment information. Then, confirm payment with your device’s Side Button.
    • Note: This payment will be refunded if Meta is unable to verify your business.
  9. Enter your business details.
    • Note: Once your business details are verified, your profile will be locked. If you need to update your business information after verification, you’ll need to reapply for Meta Verified.
  10. Tap Next.
  11. Select your business. Then, tap Next. If your business account isn’t provided as an option, tap None of these matches my business.
  12. Select a verification method. Then, tap Next.
  13. Provide your verification information, then tap Next or Submit.
  14. Tap Done.

After you apply for Meta Verified

Your application is now submitted. If you’re purchasing Meta Verified for an account that’s connected to a business with accounts on Facebook or Instagram, that business has the option to revoke your request. If the business revokes your request, you’ll receive a notification and your verification will be canceled. You can always resubmit your request if you’d like to start a separate Meta Verified subscription.

If you’re purchasing Meta Verified for your own business, Meta will review your application and provide you with an update. The verification process may take up to three business days, and may take longer in some instances due to high volumes of submissions. Once approved, the blue tick will appear on your business profile.

Note: If your verification is unsuccessful, learn about common reasons why verification may fail in this article.

Add Protected business accounts after subscribing

If your business has multiple accounts on WhatsApp, you’ll need to add those accounts as Protected business accounts after purchasing a subscription for Meta Verified for businesses on WhatsApp. This helps protect associated accounts from being falsely banned for impersonation. Learn more about how to set up Protected accounts in this article.

Meta Verified not appearing after changing your number

If you recently changed your phone number, your Meta Verified subscription was automatically canceled. You’ll need to resubscribe using your new number.

To resubscribe to Meta Verified on your new number:

  1. Open the WhatsApp Business app and go to Settings or Business Tools.
  2. Tap Meta Verified.
  3. Follow the steps to select a subscription plan and complete payment.

If you don’t see the Meta Verified option after changing your number:

  • Make sure your app is updated to the latest version.
  • Confirm that Meta Verified is available in your country for your new number.
  • Check that your new number meets the eligibility requirements.

Note: If you switch your account from the WhatsApp Business app to WhatsApp Messenger, your verified status will be removed.

About updating business information in your Meta Verified profile

Copy link

Before subscribing to Meta Verified for businesses on WhatsApp, verify that the following business and account information are up-to-date. Once you’ve subscribed, updating your business information may require additional reviews.

Business name and profile picture

Before you subscribe to Meta Verified

If we’re unable to complete your verification because those names don’t match, you’ll have the option to tap Update profile name. Once you’ve updated your profile name, tap Update name > Submit. It typically takes about 48 hours for us to review your information. We’ll send you a notification once our review is complete. If you don’t want to change your profile name, you can verify another profile that’s similar to or clearly associated with your business name.

Other WhatsApp business profile information such as business name, category, address, email, or website, will be locked once you’ve subscribed to Meta Verified. You will not be able to update these without losing your verified status.

Businesses with active Meta Verified subscriptions can update their business asset’s profile name and picture. Updating your asset’s profile info will require review and approval. You also have the option of creating a unique business username. Learn more about business usernames in this article.

Once your WhatsApp Business account is verified, your profile information may be locked for up to 20 days. After that, you can make the following updates:

  • Profile picture: Once every three days.
  • Business name: Once every 60 days.

Note: These features may not be available to all regions or businesses.

Managing or changing your linked accounts on Facebook or Instagram

To avoid this, we recommend adding those accounts to your WhatsApp Business account before subscribing. Learn how to link Facebook and Instagram accounts to your WhatsApp business accounts in this article.

Additionally, if your WhatsApp business account is linked to a Facebook or Instagram account in the Meta Business Suite, you may be redirected to sign in to that account and complete the subscription process on Meta Business Suite. Learn more about linked accounts in this article.

Note that canceling your Meta Verified subscription removes all but your 4 most recently used linked devices and removes your web page from the web 15 days after your subscription expires. The link address becomes available for others to claim 30 days after your subscription expires. If your subscription is canceled, you’ll need to resubscribe to get your verified badge, re-link your devices, and create a new web page link address. Quick replies for WhatsApp calls on Meta Quest allows you to quickly respond to incoming calls using predefined responses.

Using quick replies means you can respond to contacts without leaving your immersive experience.

Use quick replies in WhatsApp on Meta Quest:

About using Meta Business Agent with Meta One

Copy link

Meta One is currently in limited testing and isn’t available everywhere yet. The options you see may vary based on your location, account type, and what’s currently available in testing.

This feature may not be available to you yet. Go to WhatsApp Settings > Subscriptions in the WhatsApp Business app to see if you are eligible.

Access to Meta Business Agent is limited. If you reach your free limit on the WhatsApp Business app, you can subscribe to a Meta One plan to get more access to 24/7 responses from Meta Business Agent, or wait for your free limit to refresh.

About Meta Business Agent and how it works

Meta Business Agent WhatsApp is an artificial intelligence (AI) service from Meta designed to help businesses enhance and automate parts of their conversations with customers.

Unlike other business messaging tools like greeting messages or away messages, Meta Business Agent gives users a conversational experience that feels like they’re chatting with a real person, rather than exact canned responses.

You can customize your Meta Business Agent with specific product information and set boundaries for what it should or shouldn’t answer. It continuously improves by learning from your interactions and feedback, and you can tailor its voice to reflect your business’s unique tone and style.

When you set up Meta Business Agent, you’ll share information about your business, like your catalog, business description, address, and hours, so your AI can learn to answer your customers’ questions. When you start using Meta Business Agent to respond to customers, your AI will read, understand and respond to chats in a natural way based on the settings you choose. It can share product recommendations, answer common questions and more. You can continue to teach and test your Meta Business Agent after setup.

Over time, you can add more business information to help your AI agent respond more accurately. You can also give feedback on your Meta Business Agent responses to help it improve.

You can also manually take over a chat with AI at any time, and customers can always request to chat with someone from your team.

Benefits of AI-enabled chats for business messaging

Meta Business Agent helps your business in these key ways:

  • Customize Meta Business Agent to sound like you: Set up your AI agent to sound like you and act like a member of your team. The more information you provide, the better your AI agent will be able to respond like you.
  • Respond to customers anytime: Your AI agent can answer customer questions in a helpful, friendly tone at any time, even when you’re not available.
  • Save time: Spend less time on repetitive tasks and commonly asked questions. Your AI agent can respond to chats while you focus on other ways to grow your business.

Note: Meta uses AI chats consistent with its privacy policy. Some AI messages may be inaccurate or inappropriate. Meta Business Agents are subject to the Meta Business Agents Terms of Service.

Key features

When you set up your Meta Business Agent, it can can help your business in the following ways:

  • Respond to customer questions about basic business information like your business hours or location.
  • Provide answers to customer questions about specific products or services.
  • Recommend your products or services to customers.
  • Provide customers with details about pricing.
  • Respond to customer questions about discounts, payment, and shipping.

You and your customers are in control

You can manually take over a chat with AI at any time. If at any point you choose to respond to your customers’ messages manually, the AI will stop generating responses on your behalf.

We will let customers know when they start chatting with a business that has AI connected. When messaging with your Meta Business Agent, customers will see the following text in a chat: This business uses Al from Meta to generate messages. By chatting, you agree to the AI Terms. People can always request to stop chatting with AI directly in the chat, and the AI will transfer them to someone from your team to respond.

Note:

  • When you turn on Meta Business Agent, certain automations, like away messages, will pause while the AI is active, since they can interfere with how it handles incoming messages. The AI will learn from those automations and incorporate them into its responses where possible. You can also add instructions in Your info to teach it specific automation behaviors. Your automations will resume once the AI exits a chat.
  • You will receive a notification on your device if Meta Business Agent determines that a customer needs your attention.
  • AI-generated messages may not be accurate or appropriate. Users can long press on any Meta Business Agent message to provide feedback.

About using optional Meta Company Products if you opted out of sharing WhatsApp account information with Meta

Copy link

We recognize that some users in 2016 opted out of sharing their WhatsApp account information with Facebook to improve their Facebook ads and product experiences. Since then, we have started to provide new optional features that help connect your WhatsApp experiences with other Meta Companies. These features may require sharing of your information with other Meta Companies as described in the applicable privacy policy. You have the option not to use these features.

About WhatsApp on Meta Quest

Copy link

Note: WhatsApp isn’t available on Meta Horizon operating system (OS) versions older than v62. If your software version is older than v62, please update it.

You can use WhatsApp on Meta Quest to read your chats, send messages, and make calls. Download WhatsApp from the Meta Quest Store on your Quest 2, Quest Pro, Quest 3, or Quest 3S headset.

Your calls and messages remain end-to-end encrypted while using WhatsApp on Meta Quest. No-one, not even WhatsApp or Meta, can listen to or read them.

WhatsApp on Meta Quest is available in light mode or dark mode. WhatsApp defaults to the theme selected on your device. To change your theme, select Settings > Chats > Theme and select a theme.

What can you do with WhatsApp on Meta Quest?

WhatsApps on Meta Quest works like the version on your mobile device in many ways. You can:

  • View and respond to your contacts’ status updates.
  • Respond to incoming call notifications with quick replies.
  • Read chats and reply using voice or text.
  • Make voice and video calls.
  • Answer or decline and ignore calls.
  • Block and report chats and users.
  • Use disappearing messages.
  • Verify end-to-end encryption.
  • Play back voice messages.
  • Send reactions.
  • Use stickers and GIFs.
  • View images.
  • Send polls.
  • Mute a chat.

Note: This list isn’t definitive.

WhatsApp Plus is an optional subscription offered by Meta that is a part of the Meta One subscriptions which gives you access to additional exclusive features across Meta Products or Meta Company Products, including on WhatsApp. We want to be clear about how your information is handled and who is responsible for what. The WhatsApp you know and rely on remains free—simple, reliable, private messaging and calling. This subscription does not change your core experience, and we are committed to ensuring that WhatsApp continues to get better for everyone.

What’s included with WhatsApp Plus

With a WhatsApp Plus subscription you can:

  • Share exclusive stickers with special effects.
  • Choose unique app themes and icons to personalize how your WhatsApp looks.
  • Pin up to 20 chats so important conversations stay at the top.
  • Set exclusive ringtones for your most important contacts.
  • Customize chat lists with custom alerts, ringtones, and themes.

Learn how to subscribe to WhatsApp Plus.

Once subscribed, go to WhatsApp Settings > Subscriptions > WhatsApp Plus to see your list of benefits. Tap a benefit to get started.

WhatsApp Plus availability

WhatsApp Plus is currently available in limited locations and is only available on WhatsApp Messenger, not on the WhatsApp business app.

WhatsApp Plus eligibility

Subscriber requirements:

To subscribe to WhatsApp Plus, you must:

  • Have a phone number from a country where WhatsApp Plus is available.
  • Have an active account on WhatsApp Messenger.
  • Agree to the Meta Subscription Terms of Service and follow applicable product terms and policies.

Only one WhatsApp Plus subscription can be active per WhatsApp account.

Note: WhatsApp Plus subscriptions are only supported on official versions of WhatsApp Messenger downloaded from the Google Play Store or Apple App Store. Using or linking your WhatsApp account to unofficial versions of WhatsApp may result in a temporary or permanent ban on your account. Learn more about unofficial apps.

WhatsApp Plus billing and renewal

  • WhatsApp Plus renews automatically each month unless you cancel.
  • You’re charged on the same date each month as your original purchase date.
  • Cancel at least 24 hours before your next payment date to stop future charges.

Learn more about billing and payments for WhatsApp Plus.

How Meta and WhatsApp work together

When you subscribe to WhatsApp Plus, both WhatsApp and WhatsApp’s parent company Meta play a role in delivering your subscription as explained below.

What is Meta’s role in this subscription?

Meta, WhatsApp’s parent company, offers multiple subscriptions across Meta Company Products as part of Meta One. When you subscribe to any Meta One subscription like WhatsApp Plus or Meta One Plus, use of your subscription information (such as your renewal date and payment information) is subject to Meta’s Privacy Policy.

What is WhatsApp’s role in this subscription?

WhatsApp provides the WhatsApp service, including any exclusive features you subscribe to. Your use of WhatsApp, including the premium features, is subject to WhatsApp’s Privacy Policy.

Issues with notifications can be resolved by trying the steps below.

Internet connection issues

Check if you have an internet connection by opening a browser and going to a website. If that doesn’t work, try these connection troubleshooting steps.

Notifications are turned off or silenced

If you aren’t receiving WhatsApp notifications, check your device’s notification settings. When WhatsApp notifications are turned off in your phone’s settings, incoming WhatsApp call notifications are silenced.

Turn on WhatsApp notifications in your phone’s settings:

  1. Go to your phone’s Settings > Notifications.
  2. Scroll down and tap WhatsApp. Turn on Allow Notifications.

Turn on notifications in WhatsApp:

  1. Tap WhatsApp Settings or your profile picture, then tap Notifications.
  2. Turn on the notifications you’d like to receive.

Background data restricted

  1. Go to your phone’s Settings.
  2. Tap General > Background App Refresh > WhatsApp.

Do not disturb is turned on

Make sure Do not disturb is turned off.

  1. Go to your phone’s Settings > Focus > Do Not Disturb > Apps.
  2. Tap Allow Notifications From > Add Apps.
  3. Select WhatsApp > Done.

Update WhatsApp

Make sure you’re using the latest version of WhatsApp. You can update the app on the Apple App Store.

Restart your device

Turn your device off and back on and check for software updates to resolve any technical issues.

Avoid force closing WhatsApp

When you swipe up to force quit WhatsApp, you might not receive WhatsApp notifications.

Note:

  • Your phone’s settings override WhatsApp settings. Check your phone’s settings if you aren’t receiving notifications.
  • If you’ve tried the troubleshooting options above and still aren’t receiving notifications, we recommend you contact your phone’s manufacturer for further assistance.

You can change your notification settings for all calls and messages in WhatsApp Settings. Learn how to mute individual or group chat notifications in this article.

Note: Your device settings override WhatsApp settings. If you disable or silence all notifications or WhatsApp notifications from your device settings, updates made to notification settings in WhatsApp won’t take effect. However, if you enable custom notifications for a chat in WhatsApp, a new notification category will be added in your device settings, with notifications enabled for that custom setting.

Manage notifications settings for all messages, groups, or calls

  1. Tap Settings > Notifications.
  2. Manage notifications settings by performing one of the following actions:

  • Turn on Show notifications under Message notifications or Group notifications to receive notifications about individual or group messages. Turn off Show Notifications if you don’t want to see these.

  • Tap Sound under Message notifications or Group notifications to change the notification sound of individual or group messages. Select an alert tone, then tap Save.

  • Turn on Reaction notifications under Message notifications or Group notifications to receive notifications about reactions to messages that you send in individual or group chats. Turn off Reaction Notifications if you don’t want to see these.

  • Tap In-app notifications to manage notifications settings for notifications you receive while using WhatsApp. Select and tap None, Banners, or Alerts under Alert style. Then turn Sounds or Vibrate on or off to change these notification settings.

  • Turn on Show preview to show a preview of message text inside new message notifications. Turn off Show Preview to stop showing these.

  • If you turn on Show Preview, previews for messages with suspicious links might still be hidden. Learn more here.

Silence WhatsApp notifications with Focus modes

You can use your iPhone’s Focus modes (Do Not Disturb, Sleep, and others) to silence WhatsApp notifications during specific times or activities.

Visit the Apple Help Center to find out more information.

Note: If you turn off all notifications or WhatsApp notifications from your device settings, changes made to notification settings in WhatsApp won’t take effect.

To reset all notifications settings:

  1. Tap Settings > Notifications.
  2. Tap Reset notification settings > Reset.

Manage notifications for group chats

  1. Open a group chat.
  2. Tap the name of the group.
  3. Tap Notifications.
  4. Manage notification settings by performing one of the following actions:

  • Tap Mute notifications under Messages or Calls to mute notifications from messages or calls. You’ll still get notifications for mentions and replies.

  • Tap Mute @all mentions to mute @all mentions.

  • Tap Notify for to choose which notifications you’d like to receive:

  • Select All to get notifications for every group message.

  • Select Highlights to only get notifications for mentions, replies, messages from contacts, and other relevant messages.

  • Tap Alert tone under Messages to change the notification tone of messages. Select an alert tone, then tap Save.

  • Turn on Clear badge when viewed to show the total unseen message and call count on the WhatsApp icon until you view them.

Note: You can enable and disable Do Not Disturb mode in your phone settings, but WhatsApp notification settings may override Do Not Disturb.

Mute a community or groups within a community

  1. Open the community.
  2. Tap and hold the group you want to mute.
  3. Tap Mute and select the duration: 8 hours, 1 week, or Always.

To mute the announcement group, open the community, tap the announcement group, then tap Mute.

Manage notifications for lists

To manage notifications for lists:

  1. Tap Settings or your profile picture > Lists.
  2. Tap the list you’d like to manage notifications for.
  • Alternatively, you can tap and press the list you’d like to manage notifications for in the Chats tab.
  1. Tap Mute to mute chats from contacts and groups in this list. You can choose to mute them for 8 hours, 1 week, or always.
  • Your contacts won’t see that you muted the chats.
  • You’ll still be notified if you’re mentioned.

Learn more about how to use lists in this article.

An incorrect badge count on the WhatsApp icon is usually caused by an issue with your device.

To troubleshoot an incorrect badge count, try the following steps:

How to pay for ads and business broadcasts on the WhatsApp Business App

Copy link

Marketing messages is now business broadcasts in some countries. Business broadcasts might not be available to you yet. If you’re still seeing marketing messages, refer to this article.

Once you’ve set up an ad in WhatsApp, you can pay for ads and manage your payments by tapping

[Image: More Options (three vertical dots)]

Advertise >

[Image: More Options (three vertical dots)]

Ad account settings > Ad payments.

Once you’ve set up business broadcasts in WhatsApp, you can pay for business broadcasts and manage payments by tapping

[Image: More Options (three vertical dots)]

Business broadcasts >

[Image: More Options (three vertical dots)]

Account settings > Payments

Pay for ads and business broadcasts

Add funds

Prepaid funds can be used to pay for your ads and business broadcasts in advance. We’ll deduct from prepaid funds before charging other payment methods.

To add funds to your account, tap Add funds > select an amount to add > select or add a payment method > tap Next > Confirm.

Add, remove, or edit a payment method

To add a payment method, tap Add payment method > select a payment method > tap Next > enter your payment details > tap Save > Done. If you have multiple payment methods, you can set a primary method and several backup methods.

To edit a payment method, tap the payment method > Edit > enter your new payment details > tap Save.

To delete a payment method, tap the payment method > Remove > Remove > Done or Add payment method.

Verify a payment method

For the safety of your account, you might be asked to verify your payment method. To do so, tap the payment method > Verify card > Verify > enter the four-character code > tap Submit > Done. Your payment method is now ready to use.

See a list of supported payment methods in this article.

Pre-authorization

Sometimes, we ask to place a temporary hold on your payment method before you can run ads or business broadcasts. We might also temporarily place a verification hold on your payment method in order to validate it. These charges will be removed automatically.

Manage your payments

Set an account spending limit

An account spending limit helps you control your ad and business broadcasts costs. If you set an account spending limit, your ads and business broadcasts will pause once you reach that limit. Your ads and business broadcasts won’t run again until you increase, reset, or remove the limit.

To set a limit, tap Account spending limit > Set limit > enter a new spending limit > tap Save > Done. The next time you check your spending limit, you’ll see how much you’ve spent so far.

To edit your limit, tap Account spending limit > Edit > Change > enter a new spending limit > tap Save > Done. You can also remove the limit by tapping Account spending limit > Edit > Remove.

Set a payment threshold

A payment threshold affects how often you’re billed. You’ll be charged each time you reach your payment threshold.

To set or update a payment threshold, tap Payment threshold > enter an amount > tap Save > Done.

View your payment activity and edit your business information

To see your previous bills, tap Payment activity. To edit your business information, tap Business info > update your business information > tap Save.

Failed payments

Learn how to troubleshoot failed payments in this article.

Unauthorized payments

Learn how to troubleshoot unauthorized payments in this article.

Refunds

To request an ads refund, tap

[Image: More Options (three vertical dots)]

Advertise >

[Image: More Options (three vertical dots)]

Ad account settings > Ad payments. Scroll down and tap Get payment support, then follow the prompts.

To request a business broadcasts refund, tap

[Image: More Options (three vertical dots)]

Business broadcasts >

[Image: More Options (three vertical dots)]

Ad account settings > Payments. Scroll down and tap Get payment support, then follow the prompts.

You’ll be notified about the status of your refund through email. Learn more about refunds and types of refunds.

Note: Business broadcasts is currently available in limited countries and might not be available to you yet.

Add, remove, or edit a payment method

To add a payment method, tap Add payment method > select a payment method > tap Next > enter your payment details > tap Save > Done. If you have multiple payment methods, you can set a primary method and several backup methods.

To edit a payment method, tap the payment method > Edit > enter your new payment details > tap Save.

To delete a payment method, tap the payment method > Remove > Remove > Done or Add payment method.

Verify a payment method

For the safety of your account, you might be asked to verify your payment method. To do so, tap the payment method > Verify card > Verify > enter the four-character code > tap Submit > Done. Your payment method is now ready to use.

See a list of supported payment methods in this article.

Pre-authorization

Sometimes, we ask to place a temporary hold on your payment method before you can run ads or marketing messages. We might also temporarily place a verification hold on your payment method in order to validate it. These charges will be removed automatically.

Manage your payments

Set an account spending limit

An account spending limit helps you control your ad and marketing messages costs. If you set an account spending limit, your ads and marketing messages will pause once you reach that limit. Your ads and marketing messages won’t run again until you increase, reset, or remove the limit.

To set a limit, tap Account spending limit > Set limit > enter a new spending limit > tap Save > Done. The next time you check your spending limit, you’ll see how much you’ve spent so far.

To edit your limit, tap Account spending limit > Edit > Change > enter a new spending limit > tap Save > Done. You can also remove the limit by tapping Account spending limit > Edit > Remove.

Set a payment threshold

A payment threshold affects how often you’re billed. You’ll be charged each time you reach your payment threshold.

To set or update a payment threshold, tap Payment threshold > enter an amount > tap Save > Done.

View your payment activity and edit your business information

To see your previous bills, tap Payment activity. To edit your business information, tap Business info > update your business information > tap Save.

Failed payments

Learn how to troubleshoot failed payments in this article.

Unauthorized payments

Learn how to troubleshoot unauthorized payments in this article.

Refunds

To request an ads refund, tap

[Image: More Options (three vertical dots)]

Advertise >

[Image: More Options (three vertical dots)]

Ad account settings > Ad payments. Scroll down and tap Get payment support, then follow the prompts.

To request a marketing messages refund, tap

[Image: More Options (three vertical dots)]

Marketing messages >

[Image: More Options (three vertical dots)]

Ad account settings > Payments. Scroll down and tap Get payment support, then follow the prompts.

You’ll be notified about the status of your refund through email. Learn more about refunds and types of refunds.

About two-step verification and payments

Copy link

Note: WhatsApp is upgrading the 6-digit PIN used in two-step verification to a password. If you already have a PIN protecting your account, you can update to a password by following the steps here.

Two-step verification is a feature that adds more security to your WhatsApp account. If you use payments on WhatsApp, enabling two-step verification will enhance the security of your payment information. It also allows you to restore your protected payment account information if you need to reinstall WhatsApp, or if you install WhatsApp on a new device.

How to restore your payments account information

Two-step verification allows you to safely restore your payment account information if you need to reinstall WhatsApp, or if you install WhatsApp on a new device.

Once you have installed WhatsApp and re-registered using two-step verification, follow the below steps to restore your ability to send money, and to perform additional functions like changing your bank:

  1. Tap Settings or your profile picture, then tap Payments.
  2. On the screen, you’ll see a notification telling you that you must verify your number to use your existing payments information. To proceed, tap Verify.
  3. Tap Continue > Verify on Android, or Next > Verify on iPhone.
  4. Once your number has been verified, tap Done.

Notes:

  • Your two-step verification PIN is different from your UPI PIN. Your UPI PIN is a 4 or 6 digit number you must enter before making each payment. You shouldn’t share your two-step verification PIN or UPI PIN with anyone else.
  • Enabling two-step verification is optional, but you must have two-step verification enabled to restore your payments account information.
  • The ability to restore your payments account information is currently only available to users with a UPI ID linked to certain payment partners. We’re currently working to expand this to additional payments partners.

How to comply with the WhatsApp Business Messaging and Commerce policies

Copy link

Explore our help content library to find answers and troubleshoot issues.

We want businesses to enjoy all the benefits of the WhatsApp Business Platform and WhatsApp Business app. In order to ensure safe, high-quality customer conversations, all businesses and Business Solution Providers must adhere to both the WhatsApp Business Messaging and Commerce policies.

Both of these policies apply to WhatsApp Business. The Business Messaging Policy governs the acceptable use of WhatsApp Business products, outlining what messages businesses can send and setting expectations for a quality customer experience. The Commerce Policy is used to govern whether businesses can sell their products and services using WhatsApp commerce product features like catalog and payments.

We recommend that everyone using WhatsApp Business Services reads both WhatsApp Business Messaging and Commerce policies. We recognize, however, that questions may arise regarding policy components, their enforcement, and business impact.

Businesses selling products and services prohibited by the WhatsApp Commerce Policy can still use WhatsApp for messaging and most features, excluding commerce product features like product catalogs or payments.

Comply with the Business Messaging and Commerce Policies

Many businesses that sell products and services prohibited by the WhatsApp Commerce Policy can still use WhatsApp for business messaging and all other features, except for commerce product features, which currently include but are not limited to:

  • Catalog
  • Payments

Note: Some commerce product features are currently limited to specific regions or products and may not be available to you yet.

These restrictions on the use of commerce product features only apply to the categories prohibited in the Commerce Policy. Any product or service that is allowed to be sold according to the Commerce Policy may use commerce product features. For example, t-shirts aren’t a restricted item, so they can be purchased using the commerce product features available to the WhatsApp Business Platform or WhatsApp Business app.

Establishing communication with customers

Per our Business Messaging Policy, businesses may only contact someone on WhatsApp if the person has:

  • Given the business their mobile phone number
  • Agreed to be contacted by the business over WhatsApp

Confusing, deceiving, defrauding, misleading, spamming, or surprising people with business communications violates our Business Messaging Policy. Additionally, businesses can’t share or ask people to share full length individual payment card numbers, financial account numbers, personal ID card numbers, or other sensitive identifiers.

Customers must opt-in to communication with the business for the business to send them messages outside the 24-hour window on the WhatsApp Business Platform.

Note: A user reaching out to a business doesn’t act as an opt-in. The user must still opt in to receive future proactive messages from the business on WhatsApp. Learn more about opt-in requirements and best practices in the Business Messaging Policy.

Navigate specific Commerce Policy categories

Some WhatsApp Commerce Policy categories are more complex than others. Here is an overview of how to avoid Commerce policy violations for some of those categories.

Drugs, whether prescription, recreational, or otherwise are prohibited by the Commerce policy

Pharmacies and drugstores may use all WhatsApp features for grocery and convenience items, but not for pharmaceuticals. Pharmaceuticals—which we define as prescription drugs, over-the-counter drugs, and medical devices—continue to be prohibited by both the Business Messaging Policy and the Commerce Policy. Businesses cannot promote or transact in Pharmaceuticals (for example, prescription drugs, over-the-counter drugs, and medical devices) in any conversations or product features. Medical services provided by pharmacies, including testing and vaccine administration, are already permitted to conduct business messaging on WhatsApp.

Pharmacies and drugstores are allowed to:

  • Provide purchase confirmation, such as receipts of non-Pharmaceuticals
  • Use commerce product features to sell groceries, convenience items, personal care, and other non-regulated retail products
  • Respond to customer inquiries about groceries, convenience items, personal care, and other non-regulated retail products
  • Provide delivery updates of non-Pharmaceuticals
  • Provide customer service related to non-Pharmaceuticals

We will also continue to support medical services provided by licensed pharmacies for use cases such as:

  • Scheduling appointments and providing appointment updates (excluding scheduling a pick-up or delivery of Pharmaceuticals)
  • Answering questions about medical services, such as testing and vaccines
  • Answering questions about proper use of Pharmaceuticals
  • Sending surveys or bill-pay reminders

Prescriptions written by a licensed medical practitioner can be shared on WhatsApp, as this is considered medical advice. However, neither prescription or over-the-counter drugs can be directly sold or promoted within the WhatsApp business services. It is up to the client to comply with applicable law and regulations.

Supplements

Supplements are prohibited by the Commerce Policy, and aren’t allowed to be sold using commerce product features.

However, businesses in the supplements vertical can now onboard for non-sales use cases. Supplements are defined as ingestible products (excluding over-the-counter, prescription, and illegal drugs) that may provide dietary or other health benefits. Ingestible means the products enter the body (for example, topical, pill, tablet, liquid, suspension, creams).

Unsafe supplements are still prohibited under both the Commerce Policy and the Business Messaging Policy. These include, for example, products that contain any of the following:

  • Anabolic steroids
  • Chitosan
  • Comfrey
  • Dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA)
  • Ephedra
  • Human growth hormones
  • Human chorionic gonadotropin (HCG)

Digital services

Services like mobile recharges, cable TV packages, and internet packs are allowed for sale on WhatsApp.

We will allow any entity engaging in digital subscriptions and services to onboard for business messaging but they can’t use WhatsApp commerce product features.

News Aggregators will continue to be disallowed from onboarding under this policy and News Publishers still have to go through the News Page Index Registration.

Real, virtual, or fake currency

Selling real, virtual, or fake currency is prohibited on the WhatsApp Business Services.

Real money refers to cash or cash equivalent instruments that have real world monetary value. Some examples of prohibited real currency are:

  • US Dollars
  • Checks
  • Prepaid debit cards
  • Gift cards

Virtual currencies are issued by private entities, and don’t commonly have real world monetary value outside of specific communities. Some examples of virtual currency are:

  • Game currency
  • Cryptocurrency

Fake currencies refer to forged or counterfeited currency or financial instruments.

Alcohol

If the business’s primary business model is the sale of alcohol (including alcoholic beverages and kits for producing alcohol), they can’t use WhatsApp Business Services.

However, if a business sells alcohol along with other goods including alcohol-related items (such as glasses, coolers, wine bottle holders, and books or DVDs about alcohol) as part of its business model, then they may use WhatsApp Business Services for messaging that’s not related to alcohol. They can’t list alcohol in product catalogs or promote or advertise alcohol in messaging.

Weapons

If the business’s primary business model and function is the issue, sale, or use of weapons, ammunition, or explosives, they can’t WhatsApp Business Services.

Some examples of prohibited weapons are:

  • Firearms and firearm parts
  • Paintball guns
  • BB guns
  • Fireworks
  • Pepper spray
  • Tasers
  • Gun ranges
  • Gun shows

However, if the sale of weapons is one component of the business model, or if the business promotes safety training or licenses for legal weapons, it may use WhatsApp Business Services for messaging that’s not related to promotion or sales of weapons. They can’t list weapons, ammunition, and explosives in product catalogs.

Compliance with laws

It is up to the business to be compliant with applicable law. Review the Business Messaging and Commerce policies for an up-to-date list of goods and services that are prohibited from being sold or promoted on WhatsApp Business.

If a customer begins a conversation about a prohibited good or service, instruct them to continue that conversation on a different channel.

Does WhatsApp collect or sell your data?

Copy link

From everyday conversations to confidential information, your personal chats are end-to-end encrypted. No one outside of these chats, not even WhatsApp, can read, hear, or share your personal messages. Questions like “What data does WhatsApp collect?”, “Does WhatsApp share my data with Meta?”, and “What happens with backup chats?” come up often. Let’s break them down:

No one outside of your chats, not even WhatsApp, can read, hear, or share your personal messages

Every personal message, call, media, voice message, or document you send on WhatsApp is private and protected with end-to-end encryption by default. That means all your personal messages stay between you and who you send them to—no one else, not even WhatsApp (or Meta), can read, listen to, or share them.

End-to-end encryption is the foundation of your privacy on WhatsApp.

What data does WhatsApp collect?

To work properly, WhatsApp collects some limited information about you. When we say ‘information’, we mean information that could be used to personally identify you, like your name or phone number. This also includes other information that could be linked to you. This is how we collect information:

  • You provide the information to us. For example, you must provide your phone number when you sign up for WhatsApp.
  • When you use WhatsApp, we automatically collect technical information. For example, we need details about your internet connection in order to send messages.
  • Other WhatsApp users provide information about you. For example, your friends and family may add you as a WhatsApp contact.

To learn more about how WhatsApp collects and uses your information, take a look at our Privacy at a Glance.

Does WhatsApp share my data with Meta?

WhatsApp is part of Meta, and we work with other Meta Companies to help provide, improve and support each other’s services. If you choose to integrate your WhatsApp experience with other Meta products, we will share some information with Meta to make this possible. For example, you can choose to share your WhatsApp status updates to Facebook.

Choose the right level of protection for you

WhatsApp privacy checkup allows you to access step-by-step guidance to help strengthen the security of your account and customize your privacy settings in one place. To manage your privacy settings:

  • Tap Settings > Privacy.
  • Choose who can see your info: Everyone, My contacts, My contacts except…, or Nobody.

You can also decide who can add you to groups, enable disappearing messages, and turn on features like chat lock or app lock for extra security.

What happens when you back up your chats?

You can add an extra layer of privacy to your chat backups with end-to-end encryption. When turned on, your messages and media are stored securely in iCloud or your Google Account, protected by a password or a 64-digit encryption key.

Keep in mind: If you lose your password or key—and can’t access your WhatsApp—you won’t be able to restore your backup. Not even WhatsApp can help recover it.

Learn everything you need to know about how to back up your chat history.

Information for Law Enforcement Authorities

Copy link

About WhatsApp

WhatsApp provides messaging, Internet calling and other services to users around the world. You can learn more about WhatsApp by visiting our Help Center.

WhatsApp appreciates the work law enforcement agencies do to keep people safe around the world. We are prepared to carefully review, validate and respond to law enforcement requests based on applicable law and policy.

The following operational guidelines are for law enforcement officials seeking records from WhatsApp. Users seeking information on their own accounts can access WhatsApp’s Request Account Info feature. This information may change at any time.

Responding to Law Enforcement Requests

In addition to this guide, law enforcement officials may also contact WhatsApp with questions or in emergency situations as detailed below. Please do not send law enforcement inquiries to WhatsApp Support or any other channel not intended for law enforcement.

U.S. Legal Process Requirements

We disclose account records solely in accordance with our terms of service and applicable law. This includes the federal Stored Communications Act (“SCA”), 18 U.S.C. Sections 2701-2712. Under U.S. law:

  • A valid subpoena issued in connection with an official criminal investigation is required to compel the disclosure of basic subscriber records (defined in 18 U.S.C. Section 2703(c)(2)), which may include (if available): name, service start date, last seen date, IP address and email address.
  • A court order issued under 18 U.S.C. Section 2703(d) is required to compel the disclosure of certain records or other information pertaining to the account, not including contents of communications, which may include numbers blocking or blocked by the user, in addition to the basic subscriber records identified above.
  • A search warrant issued under the procedures described in the Federal Rules of Criminal Procedure or equivalent state warrant procedures upon a showing of probable cause is required to compel the disclosure of the stored contents of any account, which may include “about” information, profile photos, group information and address book, if available. In the ordinary course of providing our service, WhatsApp does not store messages once they are delivered or transaction logs of such delivered messages, and undelivered messages are deleted from our servers after 30 days. WhatsApp offers end-to-end encryption for our services, which is always activated.
  • We interpret the national security letter provision as applied to WhatsApp to require the production of only two categories of information: name and length of service.

International Legal Process Requirements

We disclose account records solely in accordance with our terms of service and applicable law. Additionally, we will assess whether requests are consistent with internationally recognized standards. These include human rights, due process, and the rule of law. A Mutual Legal Assistance Treaty request or letter rogatory may be required to compel the disclosure of the contents of an account.

Account Preservation

We will take steps to preserve account records in connection with official criminal investigations for 90 days pending our receipt of formal legal process. You may expeditiously submit formal preservation requests via the WhatsApp Law Enforcement Online Request System as indicated below.

Emergency Requests

In responding to a matter involving imminent harm to a child or risk of death or serious physical injury to any person and requiring disclosure of information without delay, a law enforcement official may submit a request via the WhatsApp Law Enforcement Online Request System. For expedited processing of such requests, we recommend including the word “EMERGENCY” in the subject line of your message. You can learn more about government requests for user data in this article.

Note: We will not review or respond to requests submitted by non-law enforcement officials. Please submit emergency requests from an official government-issued email address. Users aware of an emergency situation should immediately contact their local law enforcement directly.

Child Safety Matters

We report all apparent instances of child exploitation appearing on our service from anywhere in the world to the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children (NCMEC), including content drawn to our attention by government requests. NCMEC coordinates with the International Centre for Missing and Exploited Children and law enforcement authorities from around the world. If a request relates to a child exploitation or safety matter, please specify those circumstances in the request and include relevant NCMEC report identifiers to ensure that we are able to address these matters expeditiously and effectively.

Data Retention and Availability

We will search for and disclose information that is specified with particularity in an appropriate form of legal process and which we are reasonably able to locate and retrieve. We do not retain data for law enforcement purposes unless we receive a valid preservation request before a user has deleted that content from our service.

In the ordinary course of providing our service, WhatsApp does not store messages once they are delivered or transaction logs of such delivered messages. Undelivered messages are deleted from our servers after 30 days. As stated in the WhatsApp Privacy Policy, we may collect, use, preserve, and share user information if we have a good-faith belief that it is reasonably necessary to (a) keep our users safe, (b) detect, investigate, and prevent illegal activity, (c) respond to legal process, or to government requests, (d) enforce our Terms and policies. This may include information about how some users interact with others on our service. We also offer end-to-end encryption for our services, which is always activated. End-to-end encryption means that messages are encrypted to protect against WhatsApp and third parties from reading them. Additional information about WhatsApp’s security can be found here.

Form of Requests

We will be unable to process overly broad or vague requests. All requests must identify requested records with particularity and include the following:

  • The name of the issuing authority, badge or ID number of responsible agent, email address from a law enforcement domain and direct contact phone number
  • The WhatsApp account number, including any applicable country codes
  • More information about how to add an international phone number is found this article.

User Consent

If a law enforcement official is seeking information about a WhatsApp user who has provided consent for the official to access or obtain the user’s account information, the user should be directed to obtain that information on their own from their account. Users can access WhatsApp’s Request Account Info feature.

Notification

WhatsApp reserves the right to notify people who use our service of requests for their information prior to disclosure unless we are prohibited by law from doing so or in exceptional circumstances, such as child exploitation cases, emergencies or when notice would be counterproductive.

Testimony

WhatsApp does not provide expert testimony support. In addition, WhatsApp records are self-authenticating pursuant to law and should not require the testimony of a records custodian. If a special form of certification is required, please attach it to your records request.

Cost Reimbursement

We may seek reimbursement for costs in responding to requests for information as provided by law. These fees apply on a per account basis. We may also charge additional fees for costs incurred in responding to unusual or burdensome requests. We may waive these fees in matters investigating potential harm to children, WhatsApp and our users and emergency requests.

Submission of Requests

Online

Law enforcement officials may use the Law Enforcement Online Request System, a law enforcement contact process, for the submission, tracking and processing of requests. A government-issued email address is required to access the Law Enforcement Online Request System.

Law enforcement officials seeking account records from WhatsApp must address their request to WhatsApp LLC.

Address

Attention: WhatsApp LLC, Law Enforcement Response Team

WhatsApp LLC 1 Meta Way Menlo Park, California 94025 United States of America

Law enforcement officials who do not submit requests through the Law Enforcement Online Request System should expect longer response times. Sending requests both electronically and via hard copy might also increase processing time.

Note:

  • Acceptance of legal process by any of these means is for convenience and does not waive any objections, including lack of jurisdiction or proper service.
  • We will not respond to correspondence sent by non-law enforcement officials to the addresses above.

Updates to the Guidelines

WhatsApp may update this information periodically. Please consult the guidelines in this article before making any request.

The threat of traceability in Brazil and how it erodes privacy

On iPhone

Copy link

The Brazilian National Congress is actively considering legislation that would force companies to add a permanent identity stamp to the private messages people send. The proposal is called “traceability.”

If passed, private messaging services like WhatsApp would have to trace who-said-what and who-shared-what for billions of messages sent every day. The proposal inverts law enforcement investigations by forcing private companies to turn over the names of people who say or share something. This could include information about people who forwarded along something just to comment about it.

As we conduct more of our lives online - especially in the middle of this pandemic - protecting our private conversations with friends, family, doctors and clients is more important than ever. That is why we built end-to-end encryption into our app. This security technology protects our users by making sure only the sender and the people they are talking to can see the content of their messages, not criminals, not hackers, not authoritarian governments, and not even WhatsApp.

Traceability is a direct threat to the ability for people to communicate privately and securely. If adopted, Brazil would be a true outlier on the global stage — no other democratic country in the world mandates tracing of private messages. We’ve joined 50 organizations in opposing this proposal and defending freedom of expression, communication, privacy, and digital rights in Brazil and around the world.

In this video, made in collaboration between WhatsApp and SaferNet, we explain the potential privacy and free speech implications of traceability. It is important to understand that in order to trace any messages, we must trace them all.

[Embedded video omitted]

0:00 / 2:15

Viral misinformation is a widespread societal problem that exists in every form of communications, including email, letters and in-person conversations. Weakening privacy for all and putting innocent people at risk is not the solution. WhatsApp has helped tackle misinformation through product changes to reduce bulk and viral messaging, which have yielded a 70% decrease in highly forwarded messages on WhatsApp, and introducing a way to double check forwarded messages by tapping a magnifying glass button in the chat. We will continue to explore impactful changes as well as empowering and educating our users while maintaining people’s privacy and security.

10 myths and facts about traceability can be found here, and more information about traceability can be found below:

  • “Track the viral?”: InternetLab launches new document on privacy risks in the regulation of messaging applications, InternetLab
  • Technical Note on Article 10 of Bill no. 2630/2020 - Private Messaging Applications Traceability, Instituto de Pesquisa em Direito e Tecnologia do Recife
  • 87% of Brazilians are against message tracking in app, DataFolha
  • It is necessary to clarify what WhatsApp is in a debate on the fake news bill, Folha De S. Paulo

On the Windows desktop app

Copy link

The Brazilian National Congress is actively considering legislation that would force companies to add a permanent identity stamp to the private messages people send. The proposal is called “traceability.”

If passed, private messaging services like WhatsApp would have to trace who-said-what and who-shared-what for billions of messages sent every day. The proposal inverts law enforcement investigations by forcing private companies to turn over the names of people who say or share something. This could include information about people who forwarded along something just to comment about it.

As we conduct more of our lives online - especially in the middle of this pandemic - protecting our private conversations with friends, family, doctors and clients is more important than ever. That is why we built end-to-end encryption into our app. This security technology protects our users by making sure only the sender and the people they are talking to can see the content of their messages, not criminals, not hackers, not authoritarian governments, and not even WhatsApp.

Traceability is a direct threat to the ability for people to communicate privately and securely. If adopted, Brazil would be a true outlier on the global stage — no other democratic country in the world mandates tracing of private messages. We’ve joined 50 organizations in opposing this proposal and defending freedom of expression, communication, privacy, and digital rights in Brazil and around the world.

In this video, made in collaboration between WhatsApp and SaferNet, we explain the potential privacy and free speech implications of traceability. It is important to understand that in order to trace any messages, we must trace them all.

What is traceability and why does WhatsApp oppose it?

Copy link

Some governments are seeking to force technology companies to find out who sent a particular message on private messaging services. This concept is called “traceability.”

Technology and privacy experts have determined that traceability breaks end-to-end encryption and would severely undermine the privacy of billions of people who communicate digitally. Reasonable and proportionate regulations for an increasingly digital world are important, but eroding privacy for everyone, violating human rights, and putting innocent people at risk is not the solution. WhatsApp is committed to doing all we can to protect the privacy of people’s personal messages, which is why we join others in opposing traceability.

How does “traceability” break end-to-end encryption?

WhatsApp deployed end-to-end encryption throughout our app in 2016, so that calls, messages, photos, videos, and voice notes to friends and family are only shared with the intended recipient and no one else (not even us).

“Traceability” is intended to do the opposite by requiring private messaging services like WhatsApp to keep track of who-said-what and who-shared-what for billions of messages sent every day. Traceability requires messaging services to store information that can be used to ascertain the content of people’s messages, thereby breaking the very guarantees that end-to-end encryption provides. In order to trace even one message, services would have to trace every message.

That’s because there is no way to predict which message a government would want to investigate in the future. In doing so, a government that chooses to mandate traceability is effectively mandating a new form of mass surveillance. To comply, messaging services would have to keep giant databases of every message you send, or add a permanent identity stamp – like a fingerprint – to private messages with friends, family, colleagues, doctors, and businesses. Companies would be collecting more information about their users at a time when people want companies to have less information about them.

How does traceability violate human rights?

Traceability forces private companies to turn over the names of people who shared something even if they did not create it, shared it out of concern, or sent it to check its accuracy. Through such an approach, innocent people could get caught up in investigations, or even go to jail, for sharing content that later becomes problematic in the eyes of a government, even if they did not mean any harm by sharing it in the first place. The threat that anything someone writes can be traced back to them takes away people’s privacy and would have a chilling effect on what people say even in private settings, violating universally recognized principles of free expression and human rights.

Would traceability work?

No. Tracing messages would be ineffective and highly susceptible to abuse. If you simply downloaded an image and shared it, took a screenshot and resent it, or sent an article on WhatsApp that someone emailed you, you would be determined to be the originator of that content. At another point, someone might copy and paste the same piece of content and send it along to others in an entirely different circumstance. Think of this like a tree with many branches – looking at just one branch doesn’t tell you how many other branches there.

Moreover, traceability inverts the way law enforcement typically investigates crimes. In a typical law enforcement request, a government requests technology companies provide account information about a known individual’s account. With traceability, a government would provide a technology company a piece of content and ask who sent it first.

Can WhatsApp work with law enforcement without traceability?

WhatsApp respects the important work law enforcement does to keep people safe. Our dedicated team reviews and responds to valid law enforcement requests. We respond to valid requests by providing the limited categories of information available to us, consistent with applicable law and policy. We also have a team devoted to assisting law enforcement 24/7 with emergencies involving imminent harm or risk of death or serious physical injury. We consistently receive feedback from law enforcement that our responses to requests help solve crimes and bring people to justice.

It’s also important to understand that depending upon the nature of their investigations, law enforcement officials have multiple investigative tools, and may obtain information from many sources, including different companies, other governments, or from users’ devices. More information about how we work with law enforcement can be found here.

What experts are saying about traceability:

  • Mozilla: “The open internet is fundamentally based on the principles of interoperability and common standards, which may begin to fragment under these rules. Some provisions, such as those enabling traceability of encrypted content and automated filtering, are fundamentally incompatible with end-to-end encryption and will weaken protections that millions of users have come to rely on in their daily lives.”
  • Access Now: “The mandates in the new [Indian IT] rules would result in encouraging internet platforms to over-censor content, require dangerous unproven AI-based content regulation tools, retain vast amounts of user data for handing over to the government, and undermine end-to-end encryption crucial for cybersecurity and individual privacy.”
  • Internet Society: “The Internet Society reiterates its concern, shared by cybersecurity experts, that in order to comply with these traceability requirements, platforms may be forced to undermine end-to-end encryption.”
  • International coalition of civil society organizations and security researchers: “Undermining security features in order to ensure traceability would affect all users of that platform, not just those that are the subjects of the information request. Protections for privacy, data security, and free expression that are derived from the availability of strong encryption would be weakened or eliminated through the use of this amendment.”
  • Center for Democracy and Technology: “The guidelines would require WhatsApp to archive what each user shares, robbing them of the absolute privacy provided by end-to-end encryption, one of the app’s longtime user benefits. One large country, by adopting and enforcing these rules, could make it so that large messaging platforms either pull out or don’t offer encrypted services all over the world.”
  • Stanford Internet Observatory: “Confidentiality and integrity are core underpinnings of data security. Not even the provider of an end-to-end encrypted service can decrypt encrypted information. That’s why end-to-end encryption is incompatible with tracing and filtering content…When intermediaries employ end-to-end encryption, that means stronger security for communities, businesses, government, the military, institutions, and individuals—all of which adds up to the security of the nation. But the new traceability and filtering requirements may put an end to end-to-end encryption in India. The revised intermediary rules put the whole country’s security at risk.”
  • Electronic Frontier Foundation: “Ultimately, any implementation [of traceability] will break users’ expectations of privacy and security, and would be hard to implement to match current security and privacy standards. Such changes move companies away from privacy-focused engineering and data minimization principles that should characterize secure private messaging apps.”
  • Internet Freedom Foundation: “The government will break any type of end-to-end encryption to gain knowledge of who sent what message and also get to know its contents. Also, this specific requirement will break existing protocols for the deployment of end-to-end encryption that has been built through rigorous cybersecurity testing over the years!”

You can limit how other users can share your messages and media outside of WhatsApp. In group chats, group admins can enable Advanced Chat Privacy. In individual chats, either participant can enable Advanced Chat Privacy. When Advanced chat privacy is enabled for a chat, people in the chat:

  • Can’t save media to their device gallery automatically.
  • Can’t ask Meta AI to answer questions, or to create images or summaries in this chat.
  • Can’t export the chat.

Participants in the chat must enable Advanced chat privacy for each individual or group chat you want to apply this setting to. Once it’s turned on, Advanced chat privacy applies to all messages in the chat. In group chats, group admins can enable Advanced Chat Privacy. In individual chats, either participant can enable Advanced Chat Privacy.

Note: All chats are private by default. Your personal messages are always protected with end-to-end encryption.

Meta AI can’t access your chats. It can only read the messages people choose to send it, nothing else. This is true whether Advanced chat privacy is on or off.

Enable or disable advanced chat privacy for individual chats

Anyone in the chat can turn this setting on or off.

  1. Tap the chat you want to edit.
  2. Tap the name.
  3. Tap Advanced chat privacy.
  4. Turn on or off Advanced chat privacy.

Enable or disable advanced chat privacy for groups

This setting applies to every member of the group. Group admins can update this setting.

  1. Tap the chat you want to edit.
  2. Tap the name of the group.
  3. Tap Group permissions.
  4. Turn on Edit group settings.
  5. Go back to the Group info page and tap Advanced chat privacy.
  6. Turn on or off Advanced chat privacy.

Note:- Users who aren’t on the latest version of WhatsApp may still be able to share chats outside of WhatsApp, like auto-downloading media. When enabling this feature, you won’t be notified if someone in the chat isn’t on the latest version of WhatsApp. - Advanced chat privacy isn’t available in chats with businesses that choose to use WhatsApp’s parent company, Meta, to securely store messages and respond to customers on its behalf. Learn more in this article.
