Answering your questions about WhatsApp’s January 2021 Privacy Policy update

Copy link

This page describes how WhatsApp processed and safeguarded users’ data when we updated our privacy policy in 2021. For information on how WhatsApp protects your data and privacy, click here.

Last edited: May 2024

In January 2021 we began rolling out an updated Privacy Policy, and we want to answer some of the common questions people have asked. We go to great lengths to build WhatsApp in a way that helps people communicate privately.

We want to be clear that the policy update does not affect the privacy of your messages with friends or family in any way. The changes are related to optional business features on WhatsApp, and provides further transparency about how we collect and use data. Learn more about new business features and WhatsApp’s Privacy Policy update here.

The privacy and security of your personal messaging

We can’t see your personal messages or hear your calls, and neither can Meta: Neither WhatsApp nor Meta can read your messages or hear your calls with your friends, family, and co-workers on WhatsApp. Whatever you share, it stays between you. That’s because your personal messages are protected by end-to-end encryption. We will never weaken this security and we clearly label each chat so you know our commitment. Learn more about WhatsApp security here.

We don’t keep logs of who everyone is messaging or calling: While traditionally mobile carriers and operators store this information, we believe that keeping these records for two billion users would be both a privacy and security risk and we don’t do it.

We can’t see your shared location and neither can Meta: When you share your location with someone on WhatsApp, your location is protected by end-to-end encryption, which means no one can see your location except the people you share it with.

We don’t share your contacts with Meta: When you give us permission, we access only the phone numbers from your device’s contacts to make messaging fast and reliable, and we don’t share your contacts lists with the other apps Meta offers.

Groups remain private: We use group membership to deliver messages and to protect our service from spam and abuse. We don’t share this data with Meta for ads purposes. Again, these personal chats are end-to-end encrypted so we can’t see their content.

You can set your messages to disappear: For additional privacy, you can choose to set your messages to disappear from chats after you send them. Learn more in this Help Center article.

You can download your data: You can download and see what information we have on your account right from within the app. Learn more in this Help Center article.

Business messaging and how we work with Meta

Every day, millions of people around the world communicate securely with businesses of all sizes on WhatsApp. We want to make this easier and better if you choose to message with businesses. We will always be clear within WhatsApp when you are communicating with any business that uses these features.

Cloud API hosted by Meta: Messaging with businesses is different to messaging with your family or friends. Some large businesses need to use hosting services to manage their communication. Which is why we’re giving businesses the option to use secure hosting services from Meta to manage WhatsApp chats with their customers, answer questions, and send helpful information like purchase receipts. But whether you communicate with a business by phone, email, or WhatsApp, it can see what you’re saying and may use that information for its own marketing purposes, which may include advertising on Meta. To make sure you’re informed, we clearly label conversations with businesses that are choosing to use hosting services from Meta.

Discovering a business: You may see an ad on Facebook or Instagram with a button to message a business using WhatsApp. If you have WhatsApp installed on your phone, you’ll have the option to message that business. Meta may use the way you interact with these ads to personalize the ads you see on Facebook or Instagram.

Meta Pay on WhatsApp: In countries where Payments is available, WhatsApp’s separate payments privacy policies govern, which you can access here. Those privacy policies are not affected by this update.

Being blocked by someone

Copy link

There are a couple of indicators that you may be blocked:

  • If a person has blocked you, you will not be able to see their message read confirmation (double blue check mark). You will still be able to see message sent confirmations (single gray check mark).
  • You can’t see the contacts’ statuses.
  • You don’t see updates to a contact’s profile photo.
  • Any messages sent to a contact who has blocked you will only show one gray check mark to show the message was sent. They won’t show a second check mark.
  • Any calls you attempt to place will not go through.
  • You can’t add them to a group if you’re a group admin.
  • You can no longer see a contact’s last seen or online.

If you see all the indicators above for a contact, this could mean they’re blocking you. But they may also be due to other reasons. We can’t tell you if someone has blocked you, or who has blocked you. WhatsApp also can’t remove blocks on your behalf.

You can stop receiving messages, calls, and status updates from someone by blocking them. You can also report them if you think they are sending problematic content or spam.

When you block someone, the existing chat will remain in your chatlist. You can delete the chat completely if you want to remove it from your chatlist, or archive the chat instead. You can also unblock the sender to receive new messages from them.

You can’t block a group. Alternatively, you can exit a group and block the group admin. Learn how in this article. You can also adjust your privacy settings to prevent unknown contacts from adding you to groups. Learn more in this article.

If you feel you or anyone else is in immediate danger, please contact your local emergency services.

Block a contact, business, or unknown phone number

  1. Click

    [Image: Menu (down chevron)]

    on the chat with the sender you’d like to block. You can also click

    [Image: More Options (three vertical dots]

    at the top right of the chat window.

  2. Click Block > Block. Check the box next to Report to WhatsApp if you also want to report the sender.

Note:

  • Blocked contacts or phone numbers or will no longer be able to call you or send you messages.
  • If you’re concerned about whether a blocked contact will know you’re blocking them, read this article.
  • If you change your phone number and use the same WhatsApp account, your blocked contacts will stay blocked. Learn how to use the change number feature.
  • If you set up a new WhatsApp account, you’ll need to manually block those contacts again.
  • Blocking a contact won’t remove them from your contacts list, nor will it remove you from the list on the contact’s phone. To delete a contact, you’ll need to delete the contact from your phone’s address book.

Block third-party app users

As part of changing laws in Europe, WhatsApp now offers the option for you to chat with others using third-party apps that have integrated with WhatsApp and that you choose to turn on. Chats with third-party apps are only available in select regions and may not be available to you.

Users you’ve previously blocked on WhatsApp might be able to message you through third-party apps. If you receive an unwanted message from a third-party chat, you can block the sender by:

  1. Go to the Chats tab and click the third-party chat with the sender you’d like to block.
  2. Click the sender’s name > Block user.

Learn more about WhatsApp and third-party apps in this article.

Block high volumes of unknown messages

As an advanced security measure, you can block high volumes of unknown messages to help protect your account and improve device performance. Learn how to block unknown account messages.

Unblock someone

You can remove blocked contacts from your blocked list by following these steps:1. Click

[Image: Menu (down chevron)]

on the chat with the person you’d like to unblock. You can also click

[Image: More Options (three vertical dots)]

at the top right of the Chats window. 2. Click Unblock > Unblock.

Note: If you unblock someone, you won’t receive any messages, calls, or status updates the sender sent you during the time they were blocked.

When you report someone

When you report someone, WhatsApp receives up to five of the last messages they’ve sent to you, and, if a call took place, the basic info about the last five calls with this person, such as who initiated the call and the duration of the call. The user or group won’t be notified. WhatsApp also receives:

  • The reported group or user ID.
  • Information about when the message was sent, and the type of message sent such as an image, video, or text.

If you report a group, you’ll be removed from that group. If you’d like to rejoin a group you reported, the group admin will need to invite you again to the group.

Report a contact, unknown phone number, or group

Report a contact, unknown phone number

  1. Click

    [Image: More Options (three vertical dots)]

    at the top right of the Chats window > or Contact info > or Report.

  2. Click Report {contact} or Report {phone number} or > Block {contact} or Block {phone number} or > Report.

Report a group

  1. Click at the top right of the Chats window > Group info or Contact info > Report group, Report {contact} or Report {phone number} .
  2. Select the box if you want to Block {contact}, Block {phone number} or Exit group and clear chat > Report.

As an advanced security measure, you can block high volumes of unknown messages to help protect your account and improve device performance. Learn how to block unknown account messages.

Unblock someone

You can remove blocked contacts from your blocked list by following these steps:1. Tap Settings or your profile picture, then tap Privacy > Contacts > Blocked. 2. Swipe left on the contact’s name. - Alternatively, tap Edit > the red minus sign icon. 3. Tap Unblock.

More ways to unblock someone:

  • Open the chat with the sender you’d like to block. Tap the sender’s name or unknown phone number > Unblock {contact name} or Unblock {unknown phone number}.
  • From the chatlist, swipe left on the chat with the sender. Tap Unblock.

Note: If you unblock someone, you won’t receive any messages, calls, or status updates the sender sent you during the time they were blocked.

When you report someone

When you report someone, WhatsApp receives up to five of the last messages they’ve sent to you, and, if a call took place, the basic info about the last five calls with this person, such as who initiated the call and the duration of the call. The user or group won’t be notified. WhatsApp also receives:

  • The reported group or user ID.
  • Information about when the message was sent, and the type of message sent such as an image, video, or text.

If you report a group, you can either Report group or Report and exit. If you choose Report and exit, you’ll be removed from the group. If you’d like to rejoin a group you reported, the group admin will need to invite you again to the group.

If someone you sent message history to reports content that was sent as part of the message history you sent, you’ll be reported. The original sender of the message won’t be reported. Learn more about sending message history in a group in this article.

Report a contact, unknown phone number, or group

Report a contact or unknown sender:

  1. Open the chat with the sender you want to report.
  2. Tap the contact name or unknown phone number to see Contact Info.
  3. Scroll to the bottom of the screen and tap Report {contact name} or Report {Unknown contact number} > Report and block or Report.

Report a group:

  1. Open the group you want to report.
  2. Tap the group name, then tap Report group > Report and exit or Report.

Alternatively, you can report a group when you exit the group.

  1. Open the group you want to exit.
  2. Tap Exit group.
  3. Select the box to Report group.
  4. Choose from one of the following options:
  • Exit group: To exit the group but keep your chat history.
  • Exit and delete for me: To exit and delete the group from your Chats tab.

Note:

  • If you report a group, you’ll be removed from that group. If you’d like to rejoin a group you reported, the group admin will need to invite you again to the group.
  • When you report a group, the last five messages in the chat will be sent to WhatsApp. No one in the group will know about the report.

Report a view once photo or video

  1. Open the view once photo or video.

  2. Tap

    [Image: more (three horizontal dots)]

    in the bottom corner.

  3. Tap Report.

  4. Tap Report and block or Report.

Learn more about view once media.

How to change your privacy settings

You can adjust your privacy settings to control who can see your information and contact you. By default, WhatsApp sets your privacy settings to:

  • Any user can see your profile photo, read receipts, and when you’re online. It’s not possible to see who viewed your profile.
  • Your contacts can see your statuses, about information, links you share on your profile, and when you were last seen.
  • Any users can add you to groups or mention you in a status. Learn how to change group privacy settings.
  • The default message timer for disappearing messages is turned off.
  • Unknown callers will be able to call you.
  • You will be included in the group online count for all groups you are in.
  • You can block and report contacts on WhatsApp to stop receiving their messages, calls, and statuses.

Note:

  • You can’t set status privacy to Everyone or share your status with people who don’t have your number. You can choose who can see your status by adding them to your status audience or mentioning people or groups in your status. Learn how to manage status privacy.
  • Users you’ve saved as a contact or who you’ve messaged before can see your last seen and online, showing when you were last active on WhatsApp. Learn more about last seen and online.
  • If an unknown phone number can view your statuses, a contact may have changed their number.
  • When someone reshares your status from a status mention, they can edit and reshare the content of your status to their own audience. Your name, profile information and phone number are not displayed in the reshared status. Learn more about status mentions.
  • At this time, it’s not possible to hide group member’s phone numbers in a group.

Change privacy settings

To change who can see your last seen and online, profile photo, about information, statuses or add you to groups:

  1. Go to WhatsApp Settings > Privacy.
  2. Tap the privacy setting you’d like to change.
  3. Select Everyone, My contacts, My contacts except…, or Nobody.
    • You can’t set status privacy to Everyone.

In your privacy settings, you can also change the following settings:

  • Change your read receipts, learn more in this Help Center article.
  • Set your disappearing messages on or off by default, learn more here.
  • Silence unknown caller, learn more in this article.
  • Turn off live location sharing, learn more in this article.
  • Who can see the links you share on your profile, learn more in this article.
  • Advanced settings, such as how to protect your IP address in calls, disable link previews, and the ability to block high volumes of unknown messages from unknown accounts.

Alternatively, you can change your privacy settings through privacy checkup. Learn more about privacy checkup in this article.

Privacy settings options

Select one of the following privacy setting options for who can see your last seen and online, profile photo, about, status, links you share on your profile, or who can add you to groups:

  • Everyone: All users can see your profile photo, about, links, or add you to groups. You can’t set status privacy to Everyone. Learn more about how to manage status privacy.
  • My Contacts: Only contacts from your address book can see your last seen and online, profile photo, about, links, status, or add you to groups.
  • My Contacts Except…: Contacts from your address book, except those you exclude, can see your last seen and online, profile photo, about, links, status, or add you to groups.
  • Nobody: No one can see your last seen and online, profile photo, about, links, or status.

Note:

  • If you don’t share your last seen or online, you can’t see other users’ last seen or online.

  • If you select Everyone in settings for last seen or online, only those you’ve called and messaged before, or who you’ve saved as a contact, can see your last seen and online.

  • If you select Everyone in settings for online, you will be counted towards the group online count.

  • If you turn off read receipts, you can’t see read receipts from other users. Read receipts are always sent for group chats.

  • If a contact turns off read receipts, you can’t see if they’ve viewed your statuses.

  • If you’ve turned off read receipts, you can’t see who viewed your statuses. Instead, you’ll see this icon:

    [Image: Hide Catalog Item (eye with slash)]

    . To see who has viewed your statuses, learn more in turn on read receipts.

  • There is no way to hide your phone number when using WhatsApp. Your phone number will still be visible even if the recipient has not saved your number in their contact list.

Check marks will appear next to each message you send. Here’s what each one means:

  • [Image: Read Receipts Sent (gray single checkmark)]

    The message was successfully sent.

  • [Image: Read Receipts Delivered (gray double checkmarks)]

    The message was successfully delivered to the recipient’s phone or any of their linked devices.

  • [Image: Read Receipts Read (blue double checkmarks)]

    The recipient has read your message.

Note:

  • If the recipient’s phone is off and the message isn’t delivered to any of their linked devices, the second check mark won’t appear.
  • In a group chat, the second check mark appears when everyone has received your message. Two blue check marks appear when everyone has read your message.
  • Read receipts reset when you edit a message, so you can see who viewed your updates.
  • Seeing a clock means the message is not yet sent or delivered. This could be due to connectivity issues.
  • It isn’t possible to change the color of the check marks or clock.

Message info screen

The message info screen displays details of when your sent message was delivered, read, or played by the recipient.

Note: When a member leaves a group, the Message info screen will still show the original information with all members. This includes the member who left the group.

To see the message info screen:

  1. Open an individual or group chat.
  2. Tap and hold your sent message.
  3. Tap Info.

The message info screen shows:

Delivered:

  • Your message was delivered to your recipient’s phone or linked devices, but the recipient hasn’t seen it.

Read or Seen:

  • The recipient has read your message or seen your picture, audio file or video.
  • The recipient has seen your voice message, but hasn’t played it.

Played:

  • The recipient has played your voice message.

Missing read receipts

If you don’t see two blue check marks, a blue microphone, or Opened next to your sent message or voice message:

  • You or your recipient might have disabled read receipts in the privacy settings. Learn more here.
  • The recipient might have blocked you.
  • The recipient might not have opened your conversation.
  • You or the recipient might be experiencing connection issues.
  • When a person gets your message for the first time, a read receipt might not be sent to you.
  • The date and time settings are incorrect on your phone or the recipient’s phone.

Turn off read receipts

  1. Tap Settings or your profile picture.
  2. Tap Privacy.
  3. Turn off Read receipts.

To turn off your read receipts, go to Settings > Privacy and turn off Read receipts.

Note:

  • If you turn read receipts off, you might not be able to see who views your status. Others may also not be able to see when you view their status.
  • This won’t disable the read receipts for group chats or play receipts for voice messages. There’s no way to turn those settings off.
  • If you turn off read receipts, you won’t be able to see read receipts from others.

About disappearing messages

Copy link

Disappearing messages is an optional feature you can turn on for more privacy.

You can set messages to disappear 24 hours, 7 days, or 90 days after they’re sent unless that message is kept. The duration you choose only affects new messages in the chat, not messages you’ve already sent or received.

How to use disappearing messages

You can choose to turn disappearing messages on for all chats or select specific chats. In individual chats, either you or the person you’re messaging can turn disappearing messages on or off. Learn how to turn disappearing messages on or off in this help article.

Anyone can turn disappearing messages on or off in group chats by default. But, group admins can change group settings to allow only admins to do this. Learn how to turn disappearing messages on or off in a group in this help article.

You can set disappearing messages as default for new individual chats by tapping Settings > Privacy > Default message timer and selecting a duration.

Note:

  • You can set messages to disappear after 24 hours, 7 days, or 90 days.
  • Disappearing messages disappear for both senders and recipients, including messages you send to yourself.
  • After the disappearing messages setting is enabled for a group chat, new messages will disappear. Messages sent before the settings change are unaffected.
  • If you don’t open WhatsApp within the time you set messages to disappear, the message will disappear from the chat. But the message preview might still be displayed until the person you’re messaging opens WhatsApp.
  • If a disappearing message is forwarded to a chat with disappearing messages off, the message won’t disappear in the forwarded chat.
  • When you reply to a message on WhatsApp, the original message is quoted in your response. If you have disappearing messages turned on, the quoted message might still be visible in the chat after the duration limit has passed.
  • If a user creates a backup before a message disappears, the disappeared message will be included in the backup. Disappearing messages will be deleted when a user restores from a backup.
  • Disappearing messages aren’t available in certain countries for payment or order-related messages. You can still delete these messages from your own chat history individually.

About kept messages

Anyone in a group chat can keep disappearing messages to stop them from disappearing as long as the set duration time hasn’t passed.

  • A kept message will be visible to everyone in the conversation and won’t disappear when its duration expires.
  • The message sender has ultimate control over who can keep it. If someone keeps a message you’ve sent, you’ll get a notification. If you decide to unkeep the message, no one else in the chat can keep it again.
  • You’ll have approximately 30 days to unkeep a message from the time it was kept.

Learn more about kept messages.

Media in disappearing messages

By default, any media you download in WhatsApp will be automatically saved to your photos. But if disappearing messages are turned on, media sent in a chat will disappear and won’t be saved to your photos.

Explaining Apple and Android App Privacy Reports

Copy link

Apple and Android recently launched privacy reporting dashboards that allow their users to receive information about how an app functions and when an app uses certain features of a phone. We support transparency, which is why for years we have provided a way for people to download information associated with their account.

Since 2016 we have deployed end-to-end encryption, meaning that calls, messages, photos, videos, and voice notes to friends and family are only shared with the intended recipient; no one else (not even us) can read them. We make that clear at the start of every conversation. With end-to-end encryption, messages are not stored on our servers after they’re delivered, and in the normal course of operating our services, we do not keep logs of who everyone is messaging or calling.

To provide a reliable and seamless global communications service, we collect some information. As a matter of principle, we minimize the categories of data that we collect. For the limited kinds of data we do collect, we take measures to restrict access to that information. For example, when you send a live location to a friend on WhatsApp, your location is end-to-end encrypted, which means we cannot see that location and neither can our parent company Meta. We provide further explanations throughout our Help Center, Privacy Policy, and Terms of Service.

Here’s an overview of how WhatsApp functions and the additional services WhatsApp may use. It’s important to understand that when a user downloads WhatsApp on iOS or Android, they have the option to grant WhatsApp permission to access features like contacts and camera. Our users are in complete control over whether they approve these permissions, and are able to change these permissions at any time in the device’s Settings menu.

Contacts

To make it easier for you to message your friends and family, when you sign up for WhatsApp we ask for access to your phone numbers to see which of your contacts are using WhatsApp. If you choose to do so, the app displays the names from your address book. When you elect to do this, we will, for instance, access your phone’s contacts on a regular basis to ensure that your contact list in WhatsApp is up to date. We do not share your contact list with Meta.

Microphone

Your microphone is used for services such as sending voice messages, making and receiving calls and video chats, and recording videos on WhatsApp. You are in full control of when you use it, if at all.

Location

WhatsApp provides options for you to send and receive your location with a friend, and see what is nearby you. These are optional features. When you share your location with someone on WhatsApp, your location is protected by end-to-end encryption, which means no one can see your location except the people you share it with.

Camera

WhatsApp only accesses the camera when you tell us to, for example if you take a photo, make a video call or scan a QR code. You are in full control of when you use this feature.

Photos

WhatsApp accesses your photo library so you can use, share and receive photos seamlessly. We provide additional controls for you to limit this access, such as Save to Camera Roll. Any photos sent or received on WhatsApp are end-to-end encrypted, meaning we can’t see them.

Files + Media

If you want to save or send a photo or file in WhatsApp, WhatsApp helps you do that. You are in full control of whether you allow this. Any files sent on or saved via WhatsApp are end-to-end encrypted, meaning we can’t see them.

Domains

WhatsApp relies on other companies to provide certain features within our app, such as the ability to see someone’s location when they send it to you or enabling you to watch a video directly within WhatsApp. We do not sell your personal information and with end-to-end encryption we do not know what videos you watch.

How safe & secure is WhatsApp? Privacy explained

Copy link

WhatsApp is secure by design. To keep you safe, we’ve created an end-to-end encrypted messaging and calling experience with world-class security, and built innovative tools that put you in control. Here are some features we’ve designed to keep your WhatsApp account safe.

Layers of security

Built-in protection

By default, WhatsApp has three built-in layers of security to give you the peace of mind to focus on connecting with family and friends.

  • Default privacy: No one outside of your chats can read, listen to, or share your personal messages.
  • Automatic spam detection: WhatsApp catches and removes most spam and scam accounts before they can even reach you or before anyone reports them.
  • Proactive security alerts: WhatsApp prompts you to verify your identity if it detects any suspicious or unauthorized attempts to take over your account.

Take control of your experience

Check out these easy steps that will add additional layers of protection to prevent hackers and scammers from stealing your account and data.

  • Enable two-step verification: Set up a secret pin and never share it with anyone to prevent someone from stealing your account.
  • Always use the official WhatsApp: Using fake versions of WhatsApp poses serious privacy and security risks to your account and data.
  • Keep your groups safe: Control who can add you to groups and who can join your groups, and remove members or messages when needed.
  • Learn to spot scams: Get to know common scams and actions you can take to protect yourself and your loved ones.
  • Back up your chat history: You can back up your WhatsApp chat history and media using your iCloud or Google account.

Support tools to guide you through tricky moments

WhatsApp continuously anticipates and adapts to new risks and provides you with tools to support you when you need it. Whether it’s reporting, blocking or recovering your account, here’s what you can do when something doesn’t feel right:

  • Report problematic behavior: Reporting messages, people or businesses helps us keep WhatsApp safe for everyone.
  • Block unwanted contact: If someone you don’t want to chat with is messaging you, simply block them.
  • Recover your account: If you’ve lost access to your account, you can re-register your phone number.

About last seen and online

On iPhone

Copy link

Android

iOS

More

Android

iOS

Last seen and online tells you if a user is online and the last time they used WhatsApp. If a user is online, they have WhatsApp open on their device and are connected to the Internet. However, this doesn’t mean the user has read your message.

Change your last seen and online

You can change who can see your last seen and online:

  1. Tap Settings or your profile picture, then tap Privacy.
  2. Tap Last seen and online.
  3. Choose Everyone, My Contacts, My Contacts Except…, or Nobody.

Can’t see someone’s last seen or online

There are a few reasons why you might not be able to see someone’s last seen or online:

  • You set your privacy settings to not share your last seen. If you don’t share your last seen, you can’t see other contacts’ last seen.
  • You haven’t chatted with them before or saved them as a contact.
  • You might be blocked.
  • They set their privacy settings to hide this information.
  • They haven’t messaged you before or saved you as a contact.
  • There’s a temporary connection issue. Close then reopen WhatsApp to see if this helps.

Note: People online in a chat with you can see when you’re typing.

Privacy at a Glance

Copy link

When you use WhatsApp, we collect some limited information about you. We hope this guide will help you understand what information we collect, what we do with it, and how your privacy rights work.

When we say ‘information’, we mean information that could be used to personally identify you, like your name or phone number. This also includes other information that could be linked to you. This is how we collect information:

  1. You provide the information to us. For example, you must provide your phone number when you sign up for WhatsApp.
  2. When you use WhatsApp, we automatically collect technical information. For example, we need details about your internet connection in order to send messages.
  3. Other WhatsApp users provide information about you. For example, your friends and family may add you as a WhatsApp contact.

To learn more about how we use your information, you can also take a look at our Teen Information Center and our Privacy Policy. Note: This Help Center article is specific to users who use WhatsApp Status and Channels without ads. Learn more about ads on Status and Channels.

Note: Ads in WhatsApp Status and Channels are rolling out gradually and may not be available to you yet. If you can see ads in Status and Channels, you can learn more about ads on Status and Channels here.

Information we collect

We need to collect information from you so you can use the WhatsApp service. This could be:

  • Information you provide to us, including:

  • Your phone number and whatever profile name you choose

  • Your profile picture or ‘about’ information, if you choose to add them

  • Your age information

  • Your contacts

  • Information related to the communities, groups and broadcast lists you join

  • Your WhatsApp settings

  • Information you provide when contacting WhatsApp customer support

This information is not ‘end-to-end encrypted’, which means we are able to see it.

However, when you use WhatsApp to send personal messages, make calls, post status updates, or share your location (when you turn on location sharing in chats) this will be end-to-end encrypted. This means that only you and the people you chat with can read your messages, hear what you talk about, see your status updates, or see your location. No one else can see any of this, not even WhatsApp. Learn more here.

  • Technical information, including information about:

  • How you use WhatsApp

  • How well our services are working when you use them

  • Your device, your internet connection, and your general location (for example, country).

  • Information about you that we receive from others, including:

  • If another user uploads your number to WhatsApp from their address book

  • If another user reports you because they think your messages are against our Terms, our policies, or the law (for example, if you’re sending spam messages).

Sharing your information

Your information may be shared by you or by us with other people or organizations when you use WhatsApp. For example:

  • You share information when you communicate with others through our services. Remember to be careful about what you share on WhatsApp. Other users might take screenshots of your messages or make recordings of your calls with them and then send them to other people or post them online. Learn more about how to use WhatsApp responsibly.
  • Depending on your privacy settings, other users who have your phone number will be able to see your profile picture, your ‘about’ and ‘last seen’ information, and your message read receipts. These users may also be able to add you to groups and communities, which means other members of those groups would then be able to see certain information about you. Learn more about how to change your privacy settings.
  • When you join WhatsApp groups or communities, other members will see certain information about you. For example, when you are added to a group, all members of the group will see your phone number. Learn more about how to change your group privacy settings. To protect your privacy when you join a community, your phone number is only visible to community admins, people who have saved you as a contact, and people who have your number from other chats. Learn more here.
  • If you interact with other services through WhatsApp, some information will be shared with them. For example, if you back up your WhatsApp chats to iCloud or to your Google Account, the providers of these services will receive the information you share with them, including your WhatsApp messages. When you use WhatsApp to view content or use experience from services like YouTube or Facebook, we need to share some technical information with them to make this possible.
  • WhatsApp is part of Meta, and we work with other Meta Companies to help provide, improve and support each other’s services. If you choose to integrate your WhatsApp experience with other Meta products, we will share some information with Meta to make this possible. For example, you can choose to share your WhatsApp status updates to Facebook. We may also receive and share information with other Meta products to make your experience with our products better, including for safety purposes.
  • We also share your information with partners, such as companies that provide telecoms technology or security solutions, so that they can help us provide the WhatsApp service to you. When we share your information, we require that these partners use your information in the way we direct them to.
  • We share your information with law enforcement (for example, the police) or other public authorities if we receive valid legal requests from them.

What we do with your information

We only use your information in line with legal requirements. This could be to:

  • meet the terms of our contractual agreement with you
  • where you have consented to us using certain information
  • where we have a legal obligation that we must meet
  • where we believe we have a legitimate business reason that is not outweighed by any impact on your privacy rights.

How we use your information will vary depending on how you use WhatsApp. For example, this may include:

  • Assisting you in creating and managing your WhatsApp account
  • Ensuring your messages and calls are secure with end-to-end encryption
  • Sending and receiving end-to-end encrypted messages (including voice messages) and calls (including video messages) to and from your contacts
  • Enabling you to broadcast your status updates with the contacts of your choice
  • Helping you find out if your contacts are WhatsApp users if you choose to sync the address book on your device and manage your contacts on WhatsApp
  • Allowing you to create, join, leave and participate in groups and communities
  • Monitoring the performance of our services and fixing issues that occur
  • Assisting you in backing up your chat history in the cloud
  • Providing customer support to you
  • Enabling you to use optional features like Channels, adding your WhatsApp account to Accounts Center or accessing Meta AI through WhatsApp (where such optional features have been made available in your country).
  • Improving our products and services by creating new features and updating existing ones

Your privacy rights

You have certain privacy rights when we use your information. These include your right to:

  • request access to your information
  • receive a copy of it
  • correct it
  • delete it

In some countries, you also have the right to object to how we use your information (under certain circumstances). However, there are some exceptions to these rights, so we may not always be required to comply with your requests.

You can:

  • Request a copy of your information or move your information using the ‘Request account info’ feature (in WhatsApp, go to Settings > Account).
  • Update or delete your information using the ‘Change number’ and ‘Delete my account’ features (go to Settings > Account).

You can also change your privacy settings at any time. Learn more here. Alternatively, you can use the ‘privacy checkup’ feature (go to Settings > Privacy) to change your privacy settings. Learn more about privacy checkup.

We handle your information with care

  • We only keep your information for as long as we need it. For example, we use your information to provide our services to you and to comply with our legal obligations. When we no longer need your information, we delete it within a reasonable time period.
  • When we share your information with other Meta Companies or our partners, we only share what is necessary for our business operations or to provide you with our services or to enable you to use or engage with optional third party experiences. We have safeguards in place to protect the privacy and security of your information if it is sent to other countries.

Thank you for using WhatsApp, we hope you’ve found this guide helpful. You can find more details about your privacy rights and about how we use your information in our Teen Information Center and our Privacy Policy.

About privacy checkup

On iPhone

WhatsApp privacy checkup allows you to choose the right level of protection for you. It allows you to access step-by-step guidance to help strengthen the security of your account and customize your privacy settings all in one place. In privacy checkup, you can:

  • Choose who can contact you.
  • Control your personal info.
  • Add more privacy to your chats.
  • Add more protection to your account.

Where to find WhatsApp privacy settings

  1. Tap Settings or your profile picture, then tap Privacy.
  2. Tap Privacy Checkup.
  3. Tap each option to adjust your privacy setting for that section.

Learn everything you should know about how to change your WhatsApp privacy settings.

Choose who can contact you

In this section, you can choose who can contact you and stop unwanted calls and messages. You can adjust who can add you to groups, silence unknown callers, and manage your blocked contacts.

Control your personal info

Here, you can choose the best audience for your personal information, like online status and activity. You can choose who can see your profile photo, control who can see your last seen and online, and manage read receipts.

Add more privacy to your chats

You can use this section to limit access to your messages and media. Here, you can add a fingerprint lock to open your chats and manage your default message timer and your end-to-end encrypted backups.

Add more protection to your account

In this section, you can help to protect your account by adding an extra layer of security. You can set up two-step verification, add a passkey to log in with your face, fingerprint, or screen lock, or add a recovery email to help access your WhatsApp account.

About profile photo screenshot blocking

Copy link

To help protect user privacy, WhatsApp blocks users from taking screenshots of profile photos. This means that you can’t take a screenshot of another person’s profile picture, and they can’t screenshot your profile picture.

Screenshot blocking is enforced on supported Android and iOS versions. This means only users of these devices are blocked from taking screenshots. You can’t disable this feature.

About reporting and blocking on WhatsApp

On iPhone

Copy link

Android

iOS

Web

Windows

Mac

More

Android

iOS

Web

Windows

Mac

You can report problematic content to WhatsApp. You can also stop receiving WhatsApp messages, calls, and status updates from someone by blocking them. Blocking and reporting problematic users helps keep WhatsApp safe. Learn how to block and report someone in this article.

If you feel you or anyone else is in immediate danger, please contact your local emergency services.

Report a contact, business, unknown number, or group

Reporting a user without blocking them won’t stop you from receiving their messages, calls, and status updates. When you report a user in an individual chat, WhatsApp receives up to five of the last messages they’ve sent to you. When you report a group, WhatsApp receives up to five of the last messages sent to you in the reported group. If a call took place in an individual chat, WhatsApp may also receive basic info about the last five calls with this user, such as who initiated the call and the duration of the call.

The user or group won’t be notified of your report. WhatsApp receives the reported group or user ID, information on when the message was sent, and the type of message sent (image, video, text, etc.).

We might ban accounts if we believe the account activity is in violation of our Terms of Service. Per our Terms of Service, we retain the right to ban the user without notification. Please be aware that a user report of conduct in violation of our Terms of Service won’t necessarily result in us banning the user or otherwise taking action against the user. The only way to report someone is to follow the in-app reporting process. After you’ve submitted a report, you don’t need to take any action or share additional details. Contacting WhatsApp outside of the in-app review process won’t expedite the review process or impact the decision. We’ll acknowledge receipt of your report, but we will not contact you again.

Block a contact, business, or unknown number

When you block someone, you’ll no longer receive their messages, calls, and status updates. Your last seen, online, status updates, and any changes made to your profile photo won’t be visible to contacts you’ve blocked. Blocking a contact won’t remove them from your contacts list, nor will it remove you from the list on the contact’s phone. You’ll need to manuallydelete a blocked contact. The existing chat will remain in your chatlist. You can delete the chat if you want to remove it from your chatlist, or archive the chat to hide it from your chatlist.

After you block someone:

  • You’ll see You blocked this contact under the blocked contact’s name and in your chat with them. They won’t see this.
  • You can choose to Unblock or Delete Chat after blocking someone. You’ll also have the option of archiving the chat instead. Select Block {contact name} only if you don’t want to report the person you’re blocking.
  • Blocked numbers are visible in Blocked, which can be found in Settings or your profile > Privacy > Contacts > Blocked.

Note:

  • Blocking a contact won’t stop that user from seeing your messages in a group you both participate in, and you’ll see their messages in that group as well. Please don’t participate in groups with people you don’t wish to communicate with.
  • Blocking won’t stop you from being counted as online in a group if your privacy settings are set to Everyone. However, a blocked user can’t see if you’re online specifically.
  • We can’t block or unblock contacts on your behalf. If you’re concerned whether a blocked contact will know if you’re blocking them, read about being blocked by someone.
  • Contacts can’t see your status after you’ve blocked them. But, they can see your status if you post it before you block them.
  • You can see a contact’s status if they posted it before you blocked or deleted their number from your phone’s address book. The status will disappear within 24 hours and you won’t see future status updates from that contact.

Block high volumes of unknown messages

As an advanced security measure, you can block high volumes of unknown messages to help protect your account and improve device performance.

If Block unknown account messages is turned on, WhatsApp will block messages from unknown accounts when they exceed a high volume. During this period, your contacts can message you as usual. Message blocking stops after message rates return to normal.

Learn how to block unknown account messages.

How to send and open view once media and voice messages

On iPhone

Copy link

Android

iOS

More

Android

iOS

You can send photos, videos, and voice messages that disappear from a chat after the recipient has opened them once. This is known as ‘view once’.

View once media

View once photos and videos won’t be saved to the recipient’s Photos or Gallery. They won’t be able to forward, share, or copy them. Recipients also won’t be able to take a screenshot or screen recording of your view once media. It’s still possible for someone to take a photo or video of the media, for example with a camera or another device, before it disappears.

Send view once media

  1. Open an individual or group chat.

  2. Tapto take a photo or video, or select one from your Albums.

    Alternatively, tap

    [Image: Attach (plus sign)]

    , then tap:

    • Camera to take a new photo or video with your camera.

      Learn more about duration limits on videos.

    • Photos to select an existing photo or video from your device.

  3. Tap

    [Image: View Once (the number 1 within a solid and dotted circle)]

    .

  • When this turns green, you’re in view once mode.

  1. Tap

    [Image: Send (paper airplane)]

    .

Note: To send media, WhatsApp needs permission to access your device’s Photos and Camera. You can grant these permissions in iPhone Settings > Privacy & Security.

Send view once voice messages

  1. Open an individual or group chat.

  2. Tapand swipe up to lock / start the recording.

  3. Tap

    [Image: View Once (the number 1 within a solid and dotted circle)]

    .

  • When this turns green, you’re in view once mode.

  1. Tap

    [Image: Send (paper airplane)]

    .

If the recipient has read receipts enabled, you’ll see an Opened receipt in the chat when they’ve opened your view once media or voice message.

Open view once media and voice messages

  1. Tap the view once message.

  2. View the photo, video, or listen to the voice message.

  3. Swipe or tap

    [Image: Back (left arrow)]

    to exit the viewer.

You’ll see an Opened receipt in the chat for media or voice messages you’ve already viewed. View once media won’t be saved to your device. Once you exit the media viewer, you can’t view the media again.

About the avatar stickers privacy setting

On iPhone

Copy link

Android

iOS

More

Android

iOS

If you’ve created an avatar, you’ll see a privacy setting called Avatar Stickers. This setting is designed to help you decide how others can use your avatar stickers in a chat.

By default, this is set to My Contacts. To change this setting:

  1. Tap Settings or your profile picture, then tap Privacy > Avatar Stickers.
  2. Tap My Contacts, Selected Contacts or Nobody.

  • My Contacts allows anyone you’ve saved as a contact to feature your avatar sticker with theirs in a chat. The other person must also have saved you as a contact.

  • Selected Contacts allows you to choose certain contacts who can feature your avatar sticker with theirs in a chat. The other person must also have saved you as a contact.

  • Nobody means no-one can feature your avatar sticker with theirs in a chat.

Turn chat lock on or off

On iPhone

Copy link

Android

iOS

Web

Windows

Mac

More

Android

iOS

Web

Windows

Mac

You can lock chats to add an extra layer of privacy to your chats. Locked chats are hidden in a folder behind an extra layer of authentication, such as your phone passcode, Face ID, fingerprint, or a secret code.

Note:

  • Notifications for locked chats hide content and contact information.
  • Notifications for locked chats appear as “WhatsApp: 1 new message.”
  • Depending on language, the feature may appear as Chat lock or Chat block.

Turn chat lock on or off

You can lock any chat, including group chats and muted chats. If you haven’t set up device authentication, like Face ID or a phone passcode, you’ll be prompted to create one before you can lock chats.

To lock and unlock chats:

  1. Tap and hold the chat.
  2. Tap Lock chat or Unlock chat.

When you lock a chat, the other people in the chat aren’t notified. Locked chats are closed when you lock your device.

To open locked chats on iPad, you must to create a secret code on your primary phone. You can manually close locked chats on iPad by tapping

[Image: More (three horizontal dots)]

.

Note:

  • You can save media from locked chats on iPhone, but you can’t turn on Save to Photos for locked chats.
  • Calls from contacts in locked chats won’t be blocked.
  • If you backup and restore WhatsApp on a new phone, your locked chats will still be locked. To access your locked chats you must have device authentication set up.

View your locked chats

  1. Swipe down on your chat list and tap Locked chats.
  • If you’ve hidden your locked chats folder, tap the search bar, enter your secret code, and tap Locked chats.
  1. Unlock your phone with your device authentication or tap Use secret code.

Create a secret code

You can secure your locked chats with a secret code, separate from your phone passcode.

  1. Swipe down on your chat list and tap Locked chats.
  • If you’ve hidden your locked chats folder, tap the search bar, enter your secret code, and tap Locked chats.
  1. Tap Settings > Secret code.
  2. Enter your code and tap Next.
  3. Enter your code again to confirm.
  4. Tap Done.

To turn off your secret code, tap Locked chats > Settings > Secret code > Turn off > Continue.

Hide locked chats

You can hide your locked chats folder, so it only appears when you enter your secret code.

On your primary phone:

  1. Swipe down on your chat list and tap Locked chats.
  • If you’ve hidden your locked chats folder, tap the search bar, enter your secret code, and tap Locked chats.
  1. Tap Settings > Hide locked chats.

To view hidden locked chats, tap the search bar and enter your secret code.

Note: If you forget your secret code, you can recover your hidden chats by unlocking and clearing your locked chats. This will also clear all messages, photos, and videos in locked chats.

Unlock and clear locked chats

If you hide your locked chats and forget your secret code, you can recover your hidden chats by unlocking and clearing your locked chats.

If you unlock and clear locked chats, your secret code will be cleared and all of your locked chats will be returned to your chat list. However, this will also clear all messages, photos, and videos in locked chats.

On your primary phone:

  1. Tap Settings > Privacy.
  2. Tap Chat lock > Unlock and clear locked chats > Unlock and clear.

Note: You can restore cleared chats if your most recent backup happened before you cleared the chats. However, you can only restore messages and media sent before the backup.

  3. Click Continue.

If you’ve hidden your locked chats, click Search, type your secret code, and click Locked chats.

Note: To hide or unhide chats, you must update your locked chats settings on your Android or iPhone.

Create a secret code

You can secure your locked chats with a secret code, separate from your phone passcode. However, you must create your secret code on your Android or iPhone.

Unlock and clear locked chats

If you hide your locked chats and forget your secret code, you can recover your hidden chats by unlocking and clearing your locked chats.

If you unlock and clear locked chats, your secret code will be cleared and all of your locked chats will be returned to your chat list. However, this will also clear all messages, photos, and videos in locked chats.

To unlock and clear locked chats, you use your Android or iPhone.

Note: You can restore cleared chats if your most recent backup happened before you cleared the chats. However, you can only restore messages and media sent before the backup.

You can send messages that disappear after a set period of time on WhatsApp by turning disappearing messages on.

You can turn disappearing messages on for one or many existing chats, or set up disappearing messages by default for all new chats.

When you turn disappearing messages on, you can choose to have messages disappear after 24 hours, 7 days, or 90 days. Disappearing messages can also be kept in the chat so they don’t disappear.

New messages sent in the chat will disappear after the duration you select. This applies to new messages in the chat only, not to previous messages you’ve sent or received.

Turn disappearing messages on or off by default

Anyone can turn on disappearing messages by default. Once turned on, all new individual chats will default to using disappearing messages set to the duration you select.

  1. Tap Settings or your profile picture, then tap Privacy.

  2. Tap Default message timer.

  3. Select 24 hours, 7 days, 90 days, or Off.

  4. If you want to apply the timer to existing chats, tap the chats you want to use disappearing messages in, then tap Apply.

  5. If you don’t want to apply the timer to existing chats, tap

    [Image: Back (left chevron)]

    to apply changes.

Turn on disappearing messages in a specific chat

Anyone can turn on disappearing messages in an individual chat. Once turned on, new messages in the chat will disappear after the duration you select.

  1. Open a chat.
  2. Tap the contact’s name or group subject.
  3. Tap Disappearing messages.
  • If prompted, tap Continue.

  1. Select 24 hours, 7 days, or 90 days.

  2. Tap

    [Image: Back (left chevron)]

    to apply changes.

Turn off disappearing messages in a specific chat

Anyone in the chat can disable disappearing messages at any time. You can keep specific messages to stop them from disappearing, as long as the duration time hasn’t passed.

If you disable disappearing messages, you can’t keep them.

  1. Open a chat.
  2. Tap the contact’s name or group subject.
  3. Tap Disappearing messages.
  • If prompted, tap Continue.

  1. Tap Off.

  2. Tap

    [Image: Back (left chevron)]

    to apply changes.

As an additional security measure, you can use app lock on WhatsApp. When turned on, you must use Touch ID or Face ID to unlock WhatsApp. You can still reply to messages from notifications and answer calls if WhatsApp is locked.

In order to use app lock for WhatsApp, you must first set it up in iPhone Settings.

Turn Touch ID or Face ID on

  1. Tap WhatsApp Settings or your profile picture.
  2. Tap Privacy > App Lock.
  3. Turn on Require Face ID.
  • You can set your app to lock Immediately, After 1 minute, After 15 minutes, or After 1 hour.

Turn Touch ID or Face ID off

  1. Tap WhatsApp Settings or your profile picture.
  2. Tap Privacy > App Lock.
  3. Turn off Require Face ID.

Note: If Touch ID or Face ID doesn’t unlock WhatsApp, you can enter your iPhone passcode.

As an additional security measure, you can turn on app lock on WhatsApp Web. When app lock is turned on, you’ll need to enter your password to unlock WhatsApp Web. Your message contents will be secure when the app is locked. Notifications will not appear when your app is locked.

  • You should use a combination of letters, numbers, and special characters to set a strong password.
  1. Click OK.

Turn app lock off

  2. Deselect App lock.

About view once

Copy link

You can send photos, voice messages, and videos that disappear from a chat after the recipient has opened them once.

[Embedded video omitted]

How to send view once photos and videos on WhatsApp

0:00 / 1:13

Sending view once media and voice messages

You’ll need to select view once each time you want to send a view once photo, video or voice message. Read this article to find out how.

Once you send a view once photo, video, or voice message, you won’t be able to view it again.

To see if a recipient has opened a view once photo, video, or voice message, they’ll need to have read receipts turned on.

Any photos or videos you send won’t be saved to the recipient’s Photos or Gallery.

The recipient also can’t take a screenshot of anything you send using view once.

Note:

  • Only send view once photos, videos, or voice messages to people you trust.
  • Remember that there are other ways your view once media or voice message can be saved or recorded. For example, recipients can take a photo or video of your view once media with a camera or other device before it disappears.
  • Encrypted media may be stored for a few weeks on WhatsApp’s servers after you’ve sent it.
  • If a recipient chooses to report view once media, or voice messages, the media, or voice messages will be provided to WhatsApp. Find out more about reporting messages.
  • It’s possible for iOS or Android users to record audio of view once messages using the native screen recorder.

About receiving view once media and voice messages

Once you receive a view once photo, video, or voice message, you’ll need to open it within 14 days of it being sent. Otherwise, it’ll expire from the chat.

You can’t forward, copy, save, star, or share photos, voice messages, or videos that were sent or received with view once media enabled.

View once media and voice messages can be restored from backups if the message is unopened at the time of back up. If the photo, voice message, or video was opened, it won’t be included in the backup and can’t be restored.

You won’t be able to take a screenshot of any view once media you receive.

How to add and manage your username key

On iPhone

Copy link

Android

iOS

Web

More

Android

iOS

Web

Usernames on WhatsApp are rolling out gradually over the next few months and might not be available to you yet. In the meantime, you can reserve your username. We recommend keeping WhatsApp updated on your device so you can get the latest feature updates. To learn more about reserving your username, read this article.

A username key is an optional code that gives you control over who can contact you by your username. When you turn on a username key, people who haven’t messaged you before will need both your username and your key to contact you for the first time. You can share your key alongside your username when you want someone new to reach you.

Who doesn’t need my key?

Your key is only required for people contacting you for the first time by username. The following people don’t need your key:

  • People who already have your phone number saved
  • People you’ve previously chatted with
  • People in a shared group with you
  • People who scanned your QR code
  • People you messaged first

Set up a username key

  1. Tap You.
  2. Tap the area around your profile photo.
  3. Tap Username > Contact me by username.
  4. Select People who know my key.
  5. A key will be generated for you automatically.
  • To generate a new key, tap Get a different key.
  1. Tap Save key.

Your key will now appear under your username in your profile settings. You can find it at any time by going to your profile and tapping Username.

Share your username key

When you share your username with someone, let them know your key so they can message you. For example: “Message me on WhatsApp! My username is @YourName and my key is 1427.”

Change your username key

  1. Tap You.
  2. Tap the area around your profile photo.
  3. Tap Username > Contact me by username > Username key.
  4. Tap Get a different key. A new key will be generated.
  5. Tap Save key.

Note: After you change your key, you’ll need to share the new key with anyone who hasn’t contacted you yet. People you’ve already chatted with won’t be affected.

Turn off your username key

  1. Tap You.
  2. Tap the area around your profile photo.
  3. Tap Username > Contact me by username.
  4. Select Everyone.
  5. Tap Remove.

Once removed, anyone who knows your username can message you without needing a key.

Review your username key

If you forget your username key, you can check it in your username settings at any time.

  1. Tap You.
  2. Tap the area around your profile photo.
  3. Tap Username > Contact me by username > Username key.

Note:

  • You can’t manually enter a specific code for your username key, WhatsApp generates it for you. You can tap Get a different key to generate a new one.
  • Username keys are optional. You can add, change, or remove your key at any time.
  • If you have connected your WhatsApp account to another Meta account that says you’re under 18, your username key will be turned on by default to help protect your privacy. You can change this at any time.
  • Creating a username key doesn’t affect existing conversations. People you’ve already chatted with can continue to message you without needing your key.
  • You won’t be notified if someone can’t reach you by your username because they don’t have your key.

About backgrounds, filters, and effects

Copy link

Note: These features are currently only available to limited users and might not be available to you yet, even if other users have access.

You can apply effects, filters, and backgrounds on video calls, when sending photos and videos, or when posting a Status to express yourself in rich and fun ways.

When you use some effects, we use certain information so that the effects react to your gestures, expressions and movements. For example, if you select puppy ears, we need to make sure the ears appear on the top of your head and stay there as you move, so we estimate the location of parts of your face. This information is not used to identify you.

Your personal calls and any photos and videos you send in messages remain end-to-end encrypted.

Note:

  • The availability of certain effects may depend on the device you are using.
  • If you have a Samsung device and are experiencing issues removing filters and backgrounds on video calls, contact your phone’s manufacturer.

About Cart

Copy link

If you’re using the WhatsApp Business app, you can help your customers place orders through the cart feature. The cart provides a way for your customers to begin the order process.

The shopping button next to your business name appears in your chat or business profile. Using this shopping button, customers can browse your catalog and add items to their cart from your catalog.

Once added, customers can access their cart by tapping Cart

[Image: Open Cart (shopping cart)]

in the catalog menu or in their message with the business. From there, they can also change the quantity of each item in their cart. When they’re ready to check out, customers can send the items in their cart to your business account as a WhatsApp message.

The feature will allow your existing customers to:

  • Place orders quickly
  • Ask questions about multiple items at the same time
  • Place an order for multiple items simultaneously

About changing phones

On iPhone

Copy link

Android

iOS

More

Android

iOS

You can switch to a new phone and transfer your WhatsApp account. You can either move to the same type of phone (iPhone to iPhone), or move to a different type of phone (iPhone to Android).

Sometimes, we may need to ensure your account is secure while changing devices. In these cases, you’ll need to wait to receive your verification code. We can’t speed up this wait time.

Note: You might get a notification on your old phone to confirm that it’s you trying to change devices. In this case, confirm you’re moving your WhatsApp account to a new device.

Move to the same type of phone

There are three ways to transfer an account from iPhone to iPhone.

  • Account transfer
  • Google Account backups
  • Chat transfer

If you’re moving from one iPhone to another, the process is quite simple. Before you start transferring your WhatsApp account to a new phone, you should back up your chat history. This help will ensure that you don’t lose any important conversations or media files during the transition. You’ll have to have the old device active to scan the QR code for setup. Learn how to transfer your account to a new phone in this article.

Once it’s backed up, you can restore your chat history on your new phone.

Alternatively, you can transfer your chat history.

Move to a different type of phone

If you’re switching from an Android phone to an iPhone, or vice versa, you can keep your account information. This includes your profile photo, about, individual chats, group chats, and settings.

You can transfer chat history from an iPhone to an Android phone or from an Android phone to an iPhone.

Delete chats from your old phone

If you move to a new phone, we recommend deleting the chats on your old phone to help keep your chats private. Learn how to delete your chats from your old device.

Keep your phone number

To keep your phone number when changing phones, simply download WhatsApp on your new phone to re-register your phone number. When you re-register on a new phone, you will be logged out on your old phone as soon as re-registration is complete.

Note: If two-step verification is active on your account, you’ll receive a prompt to enter the PIN created when you set it up. Your PIN is different from your six-digit registration code.

You might experience some delay in setting up two-step verification. This delay is normal and helps us assess that your account is not compromised. Learn more about the delay in setting up two-step verification in this article.

Change to a new phone number

If you’re changing phone numbers and want to keep your chat history, you must first change numbers on your old phone.

Note: If you register with a new number on a new phone without completing this step, you’ll lose your chat history.

To change to a new phone number without keeping your chat history, simply download WhatsApp on your new phone and register your new phone number. You should then delete the WhatsApp account associated with your old phone number.

Note: If you plan to give away your old phone, or return it to your mobile provider, you should wipe all your data beforehand. This includes the SD card, if applicable. This ensures that none of your private data, such as your WhatsApp chat history, will fall into someone else’s hands.

Troubleshooting common issues with changing phones

If you’re having trouble receiving verification codes or logging in on your new phone, try the following:

  • Make sure you’re entering the correct phone number and verification code.
  • Restart your phone and try again.
  • Check your old phone’s settings to ensure that WhatsApp is allowed to send you notifications.

What to do if your phone is lost or stolen

If your old phone was lost or stolen, follow these steps.

By doing so, you should be able to recover your WhatsApp account. Remember to always back up your chat history and take steps to protect your account if your old phone is lost or stolen.

About Code Verify

On iPhone

Copy link

This feature isn’t available on the iPhone app, but it is available on these devices. Select a device to learn more about this feature.

Web

On WhatsApp Web

Copy link

Web

More

Web

Code Verify adds an extra layer of security to end-to-end encryption when people use WhatsApp on the web.

When you download the Code Verify web browser extension from the official Google Chrome, Mozilla Firefox, and Microsoft Edge browser extension stores, it automatically checks whether you’re using an authentic and untampered version of WhatsApp Web so you can be confident that your messages are between you and your intended recipients, and nobody else. If the extension detects that the code you’re using to run WhatsApp Web is not the same as the code that everyone else is using, the extension notifies you so that you can take action.

How to use Code Verify

For the best user experience, ensure the Code Verify browser extension is pinned to your toolbar once downloaded so that you can easily see the extension and its status. Code Verify will then run automatically when you use WhatsApp Web (web.whatsapp.com). When the extension is pinned to your toolbar and the code for WhatsApp Web is fully validated, the extension will show a checkmark in a green circle on the toolbar to show that the code has been fully validated.

If the extension is unable to validate the code you’re being served, you will see one of these three messages:

  • Network Timed Out: If your page can’t be validated because your network has timed out, your Code Verify extension will display an orange circle with a question mark.
  • Possible Risk Detected: If one or more of your extensions is interfering with our ability to verify the page, your Code Verify extension will display an orange circle with a question mark.
  • Validation Failure: If the extension detects that the code you’re using to run WhatsApp Web is not the same as the code everyone else is using, the Code Verify icon will turn red and show an exclamation mark.

If you click on the Code Verify extension icon in your toolbar when it is green, orange, or red, you will be able to see more information. If an issue is detected or a validation error occurs, click on the icon to launch a Learn More button. Click on the Learn More button to see how to solve the issue. You will also be able to download the source code if you want to investigate the issue further. Read more about Code Verify in this article.

Note:

  • The Code Verify browser extension simply confirms the underlying code on WhatsApp Web is the same as the code that everyone else is using. The extension won’t read or access the messages you send or receive, and we won’t know if you have downloaded the extension.
  • The performance of the Code Verify browser extension might depend on pausing or disabling other browser extensions you’re using.
  • The Code Verify browser extension verifies code for WhatsApp Web and doesn’t impact WhatsApp Desktop.
  • The extension doesn’t log any data, metadata, or user data, and it doesn’t share any information with WhatsApp. It also doesn’t read or access the messages you send or receive.

On iPhone

Usernames on WhatsApp are rolling out gradually over the next few months and might not be available to you yet. In the meantime, you can reserve your username. We recommend keeping WhatsApp updated on your device so you can get the latest feature updates. To learn more about reserving your username, read this article.

On WhatsApp, you can create a unique username (for example, @Name123) to keep your phone number private. People will be able to contact you by your username.

Create or reserve your username

  1. Tap You.
  2. Tap your profile.
  3. Tap Create username.
  • In areas where usernames are still rolling out, tap Reserve username.
  1. Tap Create username > Create username.
  2. Enter the username you want.
  • If the username is available, you’ll see a confirmation.
  • If it’s not available, you can generate suggestions based on your input.
  1. Tap Save > Done.

Once reserved, your username will become active when the feature launches in your region. You will receive a notification when your username is ready to use. Learn more about username reservations.

Claim your Instagram or Facebook username

As long as it’s not already taken, you can claim the same username you use on Facebook or Instagram (including professional accounts on Instagram) by adding WhatsApp to the same Accounts Center.

  1. Tap You.
  2. Tap the area around your profile photo.
  3. Tap Create username.
  4. Tap Use Instagram username or Use Facebook username.
  5. Follow the prompts to add your accounts to the same Accounts Center.
  6. Once added, you’ll have claimed your existing Instagram or Facebook username for your WhatsApp account.

Note:

  • Adding your WhatsApp account to Accounts Center is completely optional. You can remove your WhatsApp account from Accounts Center anytime. Learn more about WhatsApp in Accounts Center.
  • If different people use the same username across Instagram and Facebook, it’ll be available on WhatsApp to the first person who claims it.
  • If you claimed your username from Instagram or Facebook, download WhatsApp to keep your username. If you haven’t downloaded WhatsApp, your username may become available for others to claim.
  • If you later change your username on Instagram or Facebook, it won’t automatically update on WhatsApp. You’ll need to update your WhatsApp username separately.
  • If you are a business interested in claiming your Instagram or Facebook username to use on the WhatsApp Business app, read this article.

Change your username

  1. Tap You.
  2. Tap the area around your profile photo.
  3. Tap Username > Edit > Change username.
  4. Enter the username you want.
  • If the username is available, you’ll see a confirmation.
  • If it’s not available, you can generate suggestions based on your input.
  1. Tap Save > Done.

Note:

  • There’s a limit to how many times you can change your username. Once you change your username, your previous username may become available for others to claim.
  • If you want to reclaim a previous username, you can check to see if it’s been taken by someone else by following the same steps to change your username.

Delete your username

  1. Tap You.
  2. Tap the area around your profile photo.
  3. Tap Username > Edit > Delete username > Delete.

Note: If you delete your username, you have 14 days to reclaim it before it becomes available to others.

Username format rules

Your username:

  • Must be between 3 and 35 characters long
  • Can contain lowercase letters (a to z), numbers (0 to 9), underscores (_), and periods (.)
  • Can’t only contain numbers
  • Must be unique
  • Can’t contain restricted words or phrases

Note:

  • Usernames are optional. You can create, change, or delete a username at any time.
  • You can set up a username key to control who can contact you by your username.
  • Your username can be transferred to a different phone number by changing your phone number within the same device. Username transfers across different devices isn’t currently available. To learn more about transferring your phone number on the same phone, read this article.
  • Your phone number stays private: people who don’t have your number saved will see your username instead. Existing contacts who already have your number saved will continue to see it as before.
  • Some usernames are held for businesses, governments, or public figures.If your preferred username isn’t available, you can use the username generator to suggest alternatives.
  • If you delete your username, you have 14 days to reclaim it before it becomes available to others.

About data roaming charges

On iPhone

Copy link

Android

iOS

More

Android

iOS

WhatsApp uses the same internet connection as web browsing and email on your phone. If you use WhatsApp while your phone is roaming, data charges might apply.

Contact your mobile provider for more information about roaming in other countries. Charges may differ from domestic data charges.

You can check your data usage in WhatsApp in Settings. We recommend connecting to Wi-Fi whenever possible to avoid paying for data.

To see how much data you’ve used:

  1. Tap

    [Image: Settings Tab (gear)]

  2. Tap Storage and data.

  3. Tap Network usage.

If you don’t have an international data plan, we recommend you turn off:

  • Mobile data and data roaming to avoid data roaming charges. You can visit your mobile provider’s support website for instructions.
  • Media auto-download over your cellular connection and roaming to avoid extra data charges.

If you use a local SIM card while traveling, you can still use WhatsApp with your home number. But if you need to re-verify your account, you can’t do this on your original WhatsApp number.

To re-verify or verify a phone number, you must have the corresponding SIM card in your device, with phone or SMS service enabled.
