What does “Invite via Link unavailable” mean?

Copy link

WhatsApp occasionally limits groups from using the “Invite to Group via Link” feature in order to address unwanted contact, abuse of our groups feature, spam, or other Terms of Service violations.

WhatsApp uses a number of different methods to detect potential Terms of Service violations, including use of advanced machine learning technology to evaluate information about a group, and user reports.

We recommend carefully reviewing the “Acceptable Use of Our Services” section of our Terms of Service to learn more about the appropriate uses of WhatsApp. You can also learn more about how to use WhatsApp responsibly in this Help Center article.

The “Invite to Group via Link” feature will normally become available again after 7 days.

How we protect your privacy

Your status is end-to-end encrypted, so WhatsApp can’t see what you share, and we don’t know which songs you add to your status.

The music that’s available to add to your status is based on licensed music provided by Meta. Meta receives anonymous information about what songs you’ve added to status to make sure we’re able to pay music rightsholders, and does not know what songs you have chosen.

Can’t create or share status

Copy link

If you can’t create or share a status, below are a few potential solutions to try.

Connectivity

Some issues caused by connectivity problems include photos you upload to status appearing blurry.

To help resolve this:

  • Ensure you and the other person have a strong mobile internet or Wi-Fi connection. Find out what to do if you can’t connect to WhatsApp.
  • Try connecting to mobile data if you’re on Wi-Fi or Wi-Fi if you’re on mobile data.
  • Contact network or mobile service provider.

Device storage

Check that you’ve got enough storage space on your device. You need at least 1GB of free space to share a status.

Check the media file

If you’re trying to upload an image or video to status, check that the file isn’t corrupt. Videos can have a maximum duration of 90 seconds, and can only be uploaded in 3GP or MP4 format. If you attempt to upload a longer video, only the first 90 will be shared to status.

Note: The quality of media, such as images, GIFs, videos, and pictures uploaded into WhatsApp Status may be lower than the original version. This is because media files are usually compressed when shared on WhatsApp.

Restart your device

Restarting your device can help reset apps. Try turning it off and on again.

WhatsApp version

Update WhatsApp to the latest version available for your device.

Can’t hear voice messages, status audio, call audio, or videos

Copy link

If you have no sound or no audio when playing voice messages, status updates, or videos on WhatsApp, or if you can’t hear the other person on a voice or video call, try the following steps to fix the issue:

Turn up your phone’s volume

Check that your phone’s volume isn’t low or muted. Turn up your phone’s speaker volume and try again.

If your device is on vibrate only or silent, you will also have no sound when playing a video status with audio or during a call. Try turning up your volume or taking your phone off vibrate or silent.

If you’re using headphones with a dedicated mute button or slider, check they aren’t toggled off.

Check your phone’s proximity sensor

WhatsApp uses your phone’s proximity sensor to play audio through the earpiece when you’re holding your phone to your ear. However, some screen protectors and cases can disrupt this. Check that the call audio, voice message, or video is being played through your phone’s earpiece rather than the speaker. If you can’t hear the other person on a call, the proximity sensor may be redirecting audio.

If your screen goes black and you’re unable to hear the other person on a call or listen to voice messages, it’s possible that your hand or fingers are accidentally triggering the proximity sensor. Try adjusting your grip or fingers and playing the audio again.

If the issue still persists, try making a phone call from your phone with the proximity sensor uncovered. If your screen turns off immediately, there’s either an issue with your phone’s proximity sensor or with your phone’s software.

Check for connected Bluetooth devices

Your call audio, voice message, or video might be playing on a Bluetooth device connected to your phone. If you’re sure there’s no wired audio device plugged into your phone, go to your phone’s settings and turn off Bluetooth connectivity.

Can’t see someone’s statuses or replies

Copy link

If you can’t see someone’s status or aren’t receiving messages from others on your status, try these potential solutions.

Seeing “this status is no longer available” or trouble viewing a status mention

When trying to view a status, you may see the message “this status is no longer available,” or otherwise not be able to see the status when:

  • It expired. Statuses are only available for 24 hours.
  • It was deleted by the person who shared it.
  • It was taken down for violating our Terms of Service.

If you’re trying to view a status you were mentioned in by someone and can’t see it, you can ask them to share the status with you again.

Read receipts

Turn on read receipts. If you or the person trying to view your status has turned these off, you won’t be able to see status views.

Status privacy

If you can’t see someone’s status, it could be because they’ve changed their status privacy settings. You could ask them to check this, or to check if you’re in their status audience.

Likewise, you won’t be able to see replies or messages from others to your status if your privacy settings don’t allow messages from the contacts you want to receive messages from, or if the person replying isn’t included in your audience.

Blocked

If you’ve blocked someone, you won’t be able to see any messages, replies, or status updates sent by them.

Connectivity

Ensure you and the other person have a strong mobile internet or Wi-Fi connection. Find out what to do if you can’t connect to WhatsApp.

Contacts

Add the other person to your contacts. Ask them to add you to theirs. Find out what to do if you can’t see contacts on WhatsApp.

Check your contacts’ numbers are saved in full international format.

If you have multiple accounts, make sure you’re using the WhatsApp account and phone number your contacts have saved for you.

Certain contact names won’t appear when you try to call, message, or view a status if you haven’t allowed full access to the contacts in your phone’s address book. Learn how to grant access to your phone’s address book.

App permissions

Reset WhatsApp’s app permissions and ensure they’re all turned on.

Restart your device

Restarting your device can help reset apps. Try turning it off and on again.

WhatsApp version

Update WhatsApp to the latest version available for your device.

About information shared when you share status updates to Facebook and Instagram Stories

Copy link

Note: We’re building and testing out new features, like adding your account to Accounts Center and the ability to share status to Instagram, and they may not be available to you yet. Keep WhatsApp updated so you can get features as soon as they’re available.

You can share your status to other apps, like Facebook and Instagram.

WhatsApp in Accounts Center

In available regions, you can add your WhatsApp account to Accounts Center to seamlessly share your status to Facebook and Instagram Stories.

You can use Accounts Center to manage account settings and connected experiences across your Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, and Meta accounts. To add your WhatsApp account to Accounts Center and turn on status sharing, you’ll need a Facebook or Instagram account.

Learn how to add your Whatsapp account to Accounts Center.

Learn how your information will be shared, if you add your WhatsApp account to Accounts Center.

Information shared through status sharing

If you turn on status sharing to your Facebook or Instagram Stories:

  • WhatsApp will receive your Facebook or Instagram profile photo and name to help confirm your account.
  • Facebook or Instagram will receive device information such as language, browser information, and IP address.
  • When you share a status update to Facebook or Instagram, they will receive your WhatsApp status information, such as the content, media type, and caption.
  • Your phone number, contacts and messages on WhatsApp will not be shared. Your personal messages will continue to be end-to-end encrypted.

The information Facebook and Instagram receive might may be used for the purposes outlined in Meta’s Privacy Policy, including for ads and personalization.

Status sharing settings

WhatsApp and Meta won’t share your information related to status sharing without your permission and you can disable status sharing at any time. You can choose to always share your status to Facebook or Instagram Stories or to only share selected statuses. Status sharing is optional and off by default.

When you share your WhatsApp status to Facebook or Instagram Stories, it will use your existing privacy settings for stories and appear in the same places as when you directly post to your stories.

Learn how to update your privacy settings for Facebook Stories and Instagram Stories.

Note:

  • Any status that you share on Instagram and Facebook is subject to Meta’s Community Standards.
  • If you choose to add your WhatsApp account to Accounts Center, you’ll need to keep your account connected to continue to share your status to Facebook or Instagram stories.

How to integrate status with third-party apps

On iPhone

Copy link

Android

iOS

More

Android

iOS

You can use WhatsApp’s Share to Status API to integrate status with your apps and allow your users to share content directly to their status. Your app can use Android Intents and iOS Custom URL Schemes to send photos, videos, and stickers to WhatsApp Status. WhatsApp receives this content and loads it in the status composer, allowing your user to edit and publish it like a regular status.

By accessing and using this functionality, you acknowledge and agree to be bound by the Meta Developer Terms. Additionally, you represent and warrant:

  • Any content made available through your application or website, or shared to WhatsApp from your application or website, does not infringe upon the intellectual property rights of any third party and that you own, control or have otherwise secured all rights necessary to distribute, copy, publicly perform and display, or otherwise use the content via this functionality, including as uploaded and shared on WhatsApp.
  • You have the authority to make the foregoing representations on behalf of your organization.
  • If you do not have such authority or are otherwise unable to make the foregoing representations, you are not authorized to continue and should not do so.

Overview

WhatsApp’s status composer consists of a background layer and a foreground layer.

  • Background layer: Fills the screen and can be customized with a photo, video, solid color, or color gradient.
  • Foreground layer: Contains an image and can be customized within the status composer.

Implement Share to Status API

iOS implementation uses a media share link to launch WhatsApp Status and pass it content.

Your sharing flow should:

  • Check that your app can resolve WhatsApp’s custom URL scheme
  • Assign the content that you want to share to the pasteboard
  • Trigger the WhatsApp media share link

Data

You send the following data when you Share to Status. It should be passed as a single dictionary via the pasteboard using the following pasteboard type: com.whatsapp.media-share-external.data

Parameter name Type Description
bundle_id String Required The bundle identifier of the source app
background_media Data Optional Data for a background media, accepts both images and videos Images Supported formats: JPG, PNG Minimum dimensions: 720x1280 Recommended ratios: 9:16, 9:18 Videos Supported formats: MOV, MP4, WebM Supported resolutions: Up to 1080p Duration: Up to 60 seconds Recommended aspect ratio: 9:16 Recommended file size: Under 64MB. This might get transcoded to 16 MB in some cases. You must pass WhatsApp a background asset, a foreground asset, or both.
background_media_type String Optional The file type of the background media shared Supported formats: JPG, PNG, MOV, MP4, WebM
foreground_media Data Optional Data for a foreground media which appears as a sticker over the background. Accepts only images. Supported formats: JPG, PNG You must pass WhatsApp a background asset, a foreground asset, or both.
foreground_media_type String Optional The file type of the foreground media shared Supported formats: JPG, PNG
background_color [CGFloat] Optional A solid background based on the color is applied to the status. The background color is represented by an array of CGFloat. The array is expected to have four elements, one for each of the RGBA values in this order: red, green, blue and alpha. The values must be in the range [0:1]. If both color and background asset are defined, the asset takes precedence.
background_gradient [[CGFloat]] Optional A gradient background based on the first two colors (top-bottom) is applied to the status. The background color is represented by an array of CGFloat. The array is expected to have four elements, one for each of the RGBA values in this order: red, green, blue and alpha. The values must be in the range [0:1]. See this example for more information. If both gradient and color are defined, the gradient takes precedence. If both gradient and background asset are defined, the asset takes precedence.

Note: The dictionary will silently fail serialization to the pasteboard if it contains a non-serializable type.

Register Custom URL Scheme

You must register WhatsApp’s custom URL scheme to the list of allowed URL schemes. To do this, add ‘whatsapp’ to your application’s ‘LSApplicationQueriesSchemes’ key in your app’s Info.plist.

In the relevant parts of your codebase, you can verify that WhatsApp is installed using the following method: UIApplication.shared.canOpenURL(URL(string:“whatsapp://”)!)

Note: Use the custom url scheme to verify that WhatsApp is installed. For sharing, use the **Media share external** (wa.me) link instead of the custom scheme.

Share background and foreground media

This example sends a background layer image asset and a foreground layer image asset to WhatsApp Status.

`func shouldShowWhatsAppShareButton() -> Bool { // TODO: Make sure to register the custom url scheme first // Step 1 - check if WhatsApp is installed let customSchemeURL = URL(string:“whatsapp://”)! return UIApplication.shared.canOpenURL(customSchemeURL) }

func postToWhatsApp( bundleId: String, foregroundImage: UIImage, backgroundVideo: URL ) { // Step 2 - assign data to pasteboard. guard let imageData = foregroundImage.pngData() else { return } guard let videoData = try? Data(contentsOf: backgroundVideo) else { return }

let dictionary: [String: Any] = [ “bundle_id”: bundleId, “foreground_media”: imageData, “foreground_media_type”: “png”, “background_media”: videoData, “background_media_type”: “mp4”]

let options: [UIPasteboard.OptionsKey : Any] = [ .expirationDate: Date.now.addingTimeInterval(60 * 2)]

UIPasteboard.general.setItems( [[“com.whatsapp.media-share-external.data”: dictionary]], options: options )

// Step 3 - trigger the WhatsApp media share link let url = URL(string:“Media share external (wa.me)”)! UIApplication.shared.open(url) }`

Share background assets

The example sends an image as background to WhatsApp Status.

`func shouldShowWhatsAppShareButton() -> Bool { // TODO: Make sure to register the custom url scheme first // Step 1 - check if WhatsApp is installed let customSchemeURL = URL(string:“whatsapp://”)! return UIApplication.shared.canOpenURL(customSchemeURL) }

func postToWhatsApp( bundleId: String, backgroundImage: UIImage ) { // Step 2 - assign data to pasteboard. guard let imageData = backgroundImage.pngData() else { return }

let dictionary: [String: Any] = [ “bundle_id”: bundleId, “background_media”: imageData, “background_media_type”: “png”]

let options: [UIPasteboard.OptionsKey : Any] = [ .expirationDate: Date.now.addingTimeInterval(60 * 2)]

UIPasteboard.general.setItems( [[“com.whatsapp.media-share-external.data”: dictionary]], options: options )

// Step 3 - trigger the WhatsApp media share link let url = URL(string:“Media share external (wa.me)”)! UIApplication.shared.open(url) }`

Share foreground assets

This example sends a foreground layer image asset and a set of background layer colors to WhatsApp Status. If you don’t specify the background layer colors, the background layer color defaults to the most dominant color.

`func shouldShowWhatsAppShareButton() -> Bool { // TODO: Make sure to register the custom url scheme first // Step 1 - check if WhatsApp is installed let customSchemeURL = URL(string:“whatsapp://”)! return UIApplication.shared.canOpenURL(customSchemeURL) }

func postToWhatsApp( bundleId: String, foregroundImage: UIImage, color: UIColor ) { // Step 2 - assign data to pasteboard. guard let imageData = foregroundImage.pngData() else { return }

var red: CGFloat = 0 var green: CGFloat = 0 var blue: CGFloat = 0 var alpha: CGFloat = 0 color.getRed(&red, green: &green, blue: &blue, alpha: &alpha)

let dictionary: [String: Any] = [ “bundle_id”: bundleId, “foreground_media”: imageData, “foreground_media_type”: “png”, “background_color”: [red, green, blue, alpha]]

let options: [UIPasteboard.OptionsKey : Any] = [ .expirationDate: Date.now.addingTimeInterval(60 * 2)]

UIPasteboard.general.setItems( [[“com.whatsapp.media-share-external.data”: dictionary]], options: options )

// Step 3 - trigger the WhatsApp media share link let url = URL(string:“Media share external (wa.me)”)! UIApplication.shared.open(url) }`

How to manage status privacy

On iPhone

Copy link

Android

iOS

Web

Android

You can choose who can see your status by adding them to your status audience or mentioning people or groups in your status. By default, your status updates are shared with all your contacts.

Note:

  • People or groups you mention in your status can reshare it to their audience.
  • Resharing allows their audience to see the content of your status, but doesn’t reveal your name, profile info or phone number.
  • You can mention people who aren’t in your contacts.

Change your status privacy

You can share your status with all contacts or limit your audience to specific contacts.

  1. Tap Updates.

  2. Tap

    [Image: More (three horizontal dots)]

    Status Privacy.

  3. Select one of the following options:

  • My contacts: All contacts can see your status.
  • My contacts except…: Choose contacts to exclude from your status audience.
  • Only share with…: Choose specific contacts to share statuses with.
  1. Turn on Allow sharing if you want people who can see your status to reshare and forward it.
  2. Turn on Facebook Story and Instagram Story if you want to automatically share your status to Facebook or Instagram stories.

Share statuses to Facebook and Instagram Stories

If you share your status to your Facebook or Instagram Stories, your status will use your existing story privacy settings on Facebook or Instagram. Learn about information shared when you share your status update to Facebook.

Note:

  • Changes to your privacy settings won’t affect status updates you’ve sent already.

  • If you choose to mention people or groups in a status, they can see your status—even if they aren’t in your status audience. When you mention a group, all the group members can see the status. This won’t change the audience settings for future status updates. Learn more about status mentions.

  • If you delete a contact who has viewed an update, the contact will remain on the list of viewers until the update expires.

  • If an unknown phone number can view your status updates, a contact may have changed their number.

  • If a contact has disabled read receipts, you won’t be able to see if they’ve viewed your status updates. This includes statuses where you’ve privately mentioned someone directly.

  • If you’ve turned off read receipts, you can’t see who viewed your status updates. Instead, you’ll see this icon:

    [Image: Hide Catalogue Item (eye with a slash)]

    . To turn on read receipts, click You > Privacy > turn on Read receipts.

You can use status sharing to share your status updates across apps. In available regions, you can add your WhatsApp account to Accounts Center to seamlessly share your status to Facebook and Instagram Stories.

To share individual status updates:

  1. Open your status and tap

    [Image: more (three horizontal dots)]

    .

    • Tap Share to Facebook.
    • Tap Share to Instagram.
    • Tap Share… and select an app.

  2. Tap Share.

In some regions, you might still be able to share updates to Facebook Stories without adding your WhatsApp to Accounts Center. Open your status and tap

[Image: more (three horizontal dots)]

Share to Facebook > Share.

Note:

  • If you share your status update to your Facebook or Instagram story, your status update will use the existing story privacy settings that you’ve chosen on Facebook and Instagram.
  • Learn about status privacy and information shared to Facebook and Instagram Stories.

Add WhatsApp to Accounts Center

Accounts Center allows you to manage account settings and connected experiences across your Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, and Meta accounts. Learn how to add your WhatsApp account to Accounts Center.

Note:

  • To turn on status sharing, you must add your WhatsApp account to Account Center.
  • To add your WhatsApp account to Accounts Center, you’ll need an existing Facebook or Instagram account.

Automatically share updates to Facebook or Instagram Stories

To automatically share status updates to your Facebook and Instagram Stories, you must turn on status sharing.

To turn on status sharing:

  1. Tap Updates >

    [Image: more (three horizontal dots)]

    .

  2. Tap Automatically share your status.

  3. Tap OK.

Note: In some regions, you might be able to turn on sharing to Facebook Stories without adding your WhatsApp to Accounts Center.

  1. Tap Updates >

    [Image: more (three horizontal dots)]

    Status Privacy > Facebook story.

  2. Tap Continue > Allow and continue.

  3. Log into your Facebook account.

  4. Tap Yes, finish adding.

About status

Copy link

WhatsApp Status allows you to share text, photo, video, and GIF updates that disappear after 24 hours.

Note:

  • The maximum duration for status is 90 seconds.
  • WhatsApp supports 3GP and mpeg4 video formats.
  • It’s not possible to turn off or disable WhatsApp Status.
  • It’s not possible to revert to a previous version of WhatsApp Status.

About status archive

On iPhone

Copy link

Android

iOS

Web

More

Android

iOS

Web

This feature is rolling out gradually and may not be available to you yet. In the meantime, we recommend keeping WhatsApp updated on your device so you can get the feature as soon as it’s available.

Your statuses are now archived, so you can relive and share your moments, wherever you want. Your status archive lets you keep your own statuses and details like views, likes, and reactions after the 24-hour viewing window ends. Only you can see the statuses in your archive. They are stored on your phone and remain end-to-end encrypted.

What’s saved in your archive

When a status expires, the following is automatically saved to your archive:

  • The status content (photo, video, or text)
  • The caption and timestamp
  • The audience list
  • Like counts and names, sticker responses, and shares
  • The total number of views

Note:

  • Viewer names are only available for 24 hours after you post a status. After that, only the view count is kept.
  • Archived statuses count toward your WhatsApp storage, but you can delete them at any time.
  • Archived statuses are included in your WhatsApp backup.

How to view your archive

  1. Tap Updates >

    [Image: three vertical dots]

    Status archive.

  2. Tap the status you want to view.

You’ll see the full status with its likes, sticker responses, and view count.

How to share an archived status again

  1. Tap Updates >

    [Image: three vertical dots]

    Status archive.

  2. Tap the status you want to share.

  3. Tap Add to status.

  4. Tap

    [Image: paper airplane within circle]

    to share your status.

The archived status will be shared as a new status.

How to delete archived statuses

Note: Deleting an archived status is permanent.

Delete statuses from your archive:

  1. Tap Settings > Storage and data > Manage storage.
  2. Select archived statuses you want to remove.
  3. Tap Delete.

How to manage archive storage

Archived statuses are stored on your device and count toward your WhatsApp storage. To manage your storage:

  1. Tap Settings > Storage and data > Manage storage.
  2. Select archived statuses you want to remove.
  3. Tap Delete.

How to turn off your status archive

Status archive is turned on by default. To stop saving statuses to your archive:

  1. Tap Settings > Storage and data.
  2. Turn off Status archive.

Note: Turning off your status archive stops new statuses from being archived. It doesn’t delete statuses that are already in your archive.

Privacy

Only you can see your archived statuses unless you choose to share them. Archived statuses are stored on your device and are end-to-end encrypted.

About status mentions

Copy link

Note: This is a new feature we’re rolling out in phases to ensure the best experience for all users. You might notice some users have access before you, but we’re working hard to make sure it’s available to everyone as soon as possible.

Mention someone to let them know you’ve shared a status for them to see. You can mention individual contacts and groups in your status. People or groups mentioned in your status can view the status and reshare it to their audience.

If you’re mentioned individually by someone in their status, other people viewing the status can’t see that you were mentioned. If you’re in a group which was mentioned in a status, all group members can see the status mention.

[Embedded video omitted]

0:00 / 1:51

Mentioning a person or group in your status

You can add up to 5 mentions on a status at a time. People you mention in your status will be notified privately, and other users viewing the status will not be able to see who you mentioned.

When you mention a person or a group in your status:

  • They can see your status, even if they aren’t in your status audience. This won’t change the audience settings for future status updates. Learn more about status privacy settings here.
  • They will get a message from you in the Chats tab saying you mentioned them with a link to the status. When you mention groups, the mention is sent to the existing group chat.
  • The mentioned people or group members can edit and reshare the content of your status to their own audience. Resharing allows their audience to see the content of your status, but doesn’t reveal your name, profile info or phone number.

Learn how to mention someone when creating a status.

Being mentioned in a status

Any WhatsApp user may mention you in a status, not just your contacts. For example, people in the same WhatsApp Group or Community could mention you to share a status update.

When someone mentions you in their status, you’ll receive a new message between you both in the Chats tab. If someone mentions a group you’re in, you’ll see the status mention in the existing group chat.

If you’re mentioned in someone else’s status:

  • If you’re mentioned individually, other people viewing the status can’t see you were mentioned—not even other people who were mentioned.
  • If you’re in a group which was mentioned, all the group members can see the status mention.
  • You may reshare the status content as your own. When you reshare a status, you’ll be able to edit the content of the status and choose your audience before sharing as usual.

Learn how to reshare a status.

Controlling who can send you mentions

To stop receiving status mentions from a specific person or group, you can block the person or exit and delete the group. If you don’t want to be notified when someone mentions you, archive your chat with them or mute notifications for that chat.

If you muted someone’s status, they can still send you a chat with a mention, but their updates will remain hidden from view in the Updates tab. You can still see the status you were mentioned in.

If you think the status you were mentioned in included problematic content or spam, you can report it.

You can view, like, reply, and react to statuses shared with you.

View statuses

  1. Tap Updates.
  2. Tap a profile picture.
    • New statuses have a green border around them. Viewed statuses have a gray border.

To see hidden statuses, tap Hidden updates or swipe left on statuses and tap Hidden. Learn how to hide and unhide statuses.

Note:

  • The Hidden section only appears when there’s a live status from people you’ve hidden.
  • Your statuses are now archived. Your status archive lets you keep your own statuses and details like views, likes, and reactions after the 24-hour viewing window ends. Learn how to access your archived statuses.
  • People can see if you view their status, unless you or they have disabled read receipts.
  • If you don’t want people to see that you’ve viewed their status, turn off read receipts.

Like statuses

  1. Tap Updates.

  2. Tap your contact’s profile picture.

  3. While the status is displayed, tap

    [Image: Heart (heart)]

    .

The person will see a green heart next to your profile picture when they check status views. Learn more about how to see status views and likes.

Reply to statuses

Replies are sent to your shared chat and labeled as Status. You can reply with text, photos, attachments, emojis, and voice recordings.

  1. Tap Updates.

  2. Tap a profile picture.

  3. While the status is displayed, swipe up or tap Reply.

  4. Type your reply, tap

    [Image: Camera (camera)]

    to reply with a photo, or tap

    • Tap

      to attach a file.

      [Image: Emoji (smiley face)]

      to include an emoji.

  5. Tap

    [Image: Send (paper airplane within circle)]

    .

React to statuses

Reactions are like quick replies that are shared as soon as you tap them. They are sent to your shared chat and labeled as Status. You can react with stickers, your avatar, GIFs, and emojis.

  1. Tap Updates.
  2. Tap a profile picture.
  3. While the status is displayed, swipe up or tap Reply.

    • Near the top of the screen, tap

      [Image: Emoji (smiley face)]

      and select an emoji to react with.

    • To react with a sticker, tap

      [Image: Stickers (square with folded corner)]

      and select a sticker.

    • To react with a GIF, tap

      [Image: Stickers (square with folded corner)]

      [Image: GIF (the letters G-I-F)]

      . Select a GIF and tap

      [Image: Send (paper airplane within circle)]

      .

    • To react with your avatar, tap the picture of your avatar, then select and tap a sticker.

  4. As soon as you tap a reaction, it’ll be sent to your chat with that person.

Note: You can only react with avatar stickers if you’ve created an avatar. Learn how to create avatars.

You can view, like, reply, and react to statuses shared with you. For now, status likes aren’t available on web.

View statuses

Statuses from muted contacts are hidden under Muted. Click Show to see the muted statuses or click Hide to hide them.

Note:

  • If you don’t want people to see that you’ve viewed their status, turn off read receipts.
  • Your statuses are now archived. Your status archive lets you keep your own statuses and details like views, likes, and reactions after the 24-hour viewing window ends. Learn how to access your archived statuses.

Reply to statuses

Replies are sent to your shared chat and labeled as Status. You can reply with text and emojis.

  1. Click

    to share.

React to statuses

Reactions are like quick replies that are shared as soon as you click them. They are sent to your shared chat and labeled as Status. You can react with stickers and emojis.

  1. Click

      to react with a sticker.

  4. As soon as you click a sticker or emoji, it’ll be sent to your your chat with that person.

About call history on WhatsApp

On iPhone

Copy link

Android

iOS

More

Android

iOS

WhatsApp calls will appear in your phone’s call history. You can’t stop this from happening, but you can delete WhatsApp calls from your call history.

Find your call history

You can find your call history in the Calls tab in WhatsApp.

The Calls tab will show your incoming, outgoing, and missed calls. You can get more information about a call by tapping the specific call.

Delete calls from call history

  1. Open the Calls tab.
  2. Tap Edit.
  3. Tap Delete

To clear your entire call history, open the Calls tab. Tap Edit, Clear, then Clear Call History.

Restoring call history

After call history is deleted, it can’t be restored unless you create a backup first.

Your call logs are stored in your chat database file. Read about restoring your chat history.

Note:

  • WhatsApp calling uses your phone’s internet connection to make calls, not your phone plan.
  • WhatsApp calls won’t show on your phone bill.
  • Data rates will apply through your mobile provider. Contact your mobile provider for more information.
  • You can’t email or export your call history.
  • The only way to restore call history is through a backup. We can’t restore or print your call history for you.

On iPhone

Copy link

There are steps you can take to fix issues with video calling on WhatsApp.

Examples of issues that can be resolved with the steps below include:

  • Calls that are stuck reconnecting, and won’t connect.
  • Calls that are immediately disconnected.
  • Not being able to call someone.

Steps you can try

It’s a good idea for both you, and the person you’re trying to call, to try them.

  • Turn off your phone. Wait for 30 seconds, and turn it back on.
  • Force quit WhatsApp and open it again.
  • Make sure you have a strong, stable Wi-Fi.
  • Turn your WhatsApp permissions on and off again.
  • Make sure your operating system and device is supported.
  • Update WhatsApp to the latest version available.
  • Test if the microphone, camera, and speakers are working on your computer. You can troubleshoot your microphone and speakers through your computer’s sound settings.
  • Make sure another app isn’t using your microphone, camera or audio device. Don’t use a virtual camera or audio device.
  • Turn off battery saver and bluetooth.
  • Check your router’s security settings and firewall configurations. Update firewall settings to allow WhatsApp calling on UDP and TCP ports 3478, 3480, and 3484. Contact your service provider or network administrator for help if needed.

Other video calling issues

If you have audio or visual problems during a call, you might need to take additional steps to resolve the issue.

  • Try ending and restarting the call.
  • Turn the camera off and on again.
  • Turn mute off and on again.

There are steps you can take to fix issues with video calling on WhatsApp.

Examples of issues are:

  • Calls that are stuck reconnecting, and won’t connect.
  • Calls that are immediately disconnected.
  • Not being able to call someone.

Steps you can try

  • Close and reopen the WhatsApp Web tab or refresh the page.
  • Upgrade your browser to a recent version.
  • Make sure you have a strong, stable Wi-Fi.
  • If you’re currently connected to Wi-Fi, try connecting to a different Wi-Fi network.
  • Make sure your browser gives web.whatsapp.com the necessary permissions for notifications, camera and microphone and your OS gives the browser the necessary permissions for notifications and screen sharing.
  • Test if the microphone, camera, and speakers are working on your computer. You can troubleshoot your microphone and speakers through your computer’s sound settings.
  • Make sure another app isn’t using your microphone, camera or audio device. Don’t use a virtual camera or audio device.
  • When possible connect your computer to your power source.
  • Check your router’s security settings and firewall configurations. Update firewall settings to allow WhatsApp calling on UDP and TCP ports 3478, 3480, and 3484. Contact your service provider or network administrator for help if needed.

Other video calling issues

If you have audio or visual problems during a call, you might need to take additional steps to resolve the issue.

  • Make sure you have a camera. You can’t make a video call on a device without a camera.
  • Use a headset for the best audio. Audio issues can be caused by using a separate, external microphone and speaker devices.
  • Try refreshing the web page.
  • Try ending and restarting the call.
  • Turn the camera off and on again.
  • Turn mute off and on again.

There are steps you can take to fix issues with voice calling on WhatsApp.

Examples of issues that can be resolved by the above are:

  • Calls that are stuck reconnecting, and won’t connect.
  • Calls that are immediately disconnected.
  • Not being able to call someone.

Steps you can try

It’s a good idea for both you, and the person you’re trying to call, to try them.

  • Turn off your phone. Wait for 30 seconds, and turn it back on.
  • Force quit WhatsApp and open it again.
  • Make sure you have a strong, stable Wi-Fi or data connection.
  • If you’re connected to Wi-Fi, try connecting to a different Wi-Fi network or turn Wi-Fi off and place a call using your mobile data connection.
  • If you’re currently connected to mobile data, try turning Wi-Fi on and placing a call.
  • Turn your WhatsApp permissions off and on again.
  • Make sure your operating system and device is supported.
  • Update WhatsApp to the latest version available.
  • Test if the microphone and speakers are working on your phone. You can troubleshoot your microphone and speakers through your phone’s sound settings.
  • Make sure another app isn’t using your microphone or audio device. Don’t use a virtual audio device.
  • Turn off battery saver and bluetooth.
  • Check your router’s security settings and firewall configurations. Update firewall settings to allow WhatsApp calling on UDP and TCP ports 3478, 3480, and 3484. Contact your service provider or network administrator for help if needed.

Other calling issues

Below are other calling issues that you might need to take additional steps to resolve.

Seeing ‘Unable to initiate/place call’

This issue can affect iOS devices. We’d recommend contacting your device manufacturer for more information if you’re seeing this message.

A contact is unavailable

You might see a “contact is unavailable” message when you try to call someone. Or, the call might ring once and hang up. This can happen if:

  • The contact has a device problem.
  • They blocked you.
  • They have Focus or Do Not Disturb turned on.
  • They don’t have an internet connection.

Here’s what your contact can try:

  • Any of the general steps at the start of this article.
  • Unblocking you, if they blocked you.
  • Checking that Focus allows calls.
  • Checking that Do Not Disturb is turned off.

How to create and share WhatsApp call links

On iPhone

Copy link

Android

iOS

Windows

Mac

More

Android

iOS

Windows

Mac

Create and share a WhatsApp call link so that anyone with a WhatsApp account can join your call by opening the link. You can send it to a person or group on WhatsApp, or copy the link and share it another way.

Every time you create a call link, the URL is different and secure, so no one can guess your call links. Personal calls from call link calls are end-to-end encrypted.

  1. Tap the Calls tab.

  2. Tap

    [Image: New Call Or Group Call (phone with plus sign)]

    .

  3. Tap New call link.

  4. Select your call type, Video or Voice.

  5. To enable a waiting room for people to join the call, toggle Require approval to join.

  6. Tap Copy link, Send link via WhatsApp to share in WhatsApp, or Share link to share it in another app.

  • To schedule this call for a later time and date tap Add to calendar and fill out the details.

Note:

  • Anyone with your call link can join your call, so only share it with people you trust.
  • Blocked users can’t use your call link.
  • Links expire if they’ve been unused for 30 days.
  • Links can be revoked by WhatsApp for privacy and security reasons.

Manage the call waiting room

If the call link creator turned on Require approval to join, anyone joining the call will enter a waiting room. Only the call link creator can see who is in the waiting room and admit or deny people onto the call.

To enable a waiting room during a call, the call link creator can tap Participant list > toggle Require approval to join.

During the call, the link creator will see {User name} has requested to join. They can:

  1. Tap X to deny entrance to call.

  2. Tap

    [Image: approve check mark (checkmark)]

    to allow the user to join the call.

Alternatively, the call link creator can allow multiple people or tap Approve all to let everyone in.

Note:

  • The waiting room can hold up to 128 people.
  • Only the call link creator will be notified of approval requests.
  • If someone is denied, they’ll get a message. They can rejoin the waiting room if they think it was a mistake.
  • When the call ends, anyone still in the waiting room will be removed.

Remove or block a person on a call

The creator of a call link can remove a person as well as remove and block people. To remove a person from a call:

  1. In an ongoing call, long press the person’s name or phone number.
  2. Tap Remove {call person’s name} or {phone number}.
  3. Select Remove or Remove & block.

Note: People who’ve been removed will see You have been removed from the call by {name or phone}. When a removed or blocked contact tries to rejoin the call, they’ll see Unable to connect and won’t be able to join the call.

How to fix issues with WhatsApp call links

Copy link

You can create and share a WhatsApp call link so that anyone with a WhatsApp account can join your call by opening the link. If you’re experiencing issues with call links, we’ve listed some ways you might be able to fix the issue below.

Firstly, make sure WhatsApp is updated to the latest version. Read how to manually update WhatsApp.

Try turning your device off and on again, and checking your connection.

If you can’t join a call link, check that you haven’t blocked the contact, and that they haven’t blocked you.

You can’t join a link if it has been unused for 30 days. You or your contact will need to resend the link in this case.

Another reason why you may not be able to join a call link is if the call is full. The maximum number of people that can join a call link is 256 people.

Video calling lets you video call your contacts using WhatsApp.

[Embedded video omitted]

Free WhatsApp Video calls

0:00 / 0:18

Make a video call

  1. Open the individual chat with the contact you want to video call.

  2. Tap

    [Image: Video Call (video camera)]

    .

Alternatively, open WhatsApp, then tap the Calls tab >

[Image: Group Call or New Call (phone with plus sign)]

. Find the contact you want to video call, then tap

[Image: Video Call (video camera)]

.

Record video note

If they don’t pick up, you can leave a video note:

  1. Tap Record video note to start recording.

  2. Tap

    [Image: Stop Recording (square within circle)]

    to stop recording.

  3. Tap

    [Image: delete editing status (trash can)]

    to delete it, or

    [Image: Send (paper airplane within circle)]

    to send it.

Once sent, you’ll see the video note in your chat with them and they’ll get a notification.

Receive a video call

If your phone is locked, you’ll receive an Incoming video call… notification from WhatsApp when someone video calls you. You can:

  • Slide the notification to answer the call.
  • Tap Remind Me, then select if you want to be reminded When I leave or In 1 hour.
  • Decline the call by pressing the power button on the side of the iPhone two times.

If your phone is unlocked you’ll receive an Incoming video call… notification from WhatsApp when someone video calls you. You can:

  • Pull the notification down, then tap Accept or tap the notification to accept the call.
  • Pull the notification down, then tap Decline or tap the notification to decline the call.
  • Pull the notification down, then tap Message to decline the call with a note.
  • Pull the notification down, tap Remind Me, then select if you want to be reminded When I leave or In 1 hour.

Adjust video settings

Switch between front and rear cameras

To switch between the front camera and rear camera on your device during a video call, tap

[Image: Camera Flip (camera with two curved arrows within two circles)]

.

Video calls begin with the front camera enabled by default.

Switch from a video call to a voice call

  • Tap

    [Image: Camera Off (video camera with slash)]

    to turn your video off during calls. Your contact can choose to also turn their video off or leave it on.

  • Tap

    [Image: Video Call (video camera)]

    to turn your video back on.

Self view

You can hide your own video tile for a less cluttered screen. This doesn’t turn off your video for others.

  • To hide your view, drag the floating self-view to the edge of the screen until it disappears.
  • To restore it, tap or drag the hidden self-view back into the screen.

If you switch to PiP mode, the self-view will be restored.

Raise hand

To raise your hand during a video call:

  1. Tap

    [Image: more (three horizontal dots)]

    .

  2. Tap Raise hand to raise your hand.

  3. Tap Lower hand to lower it.

Picture-in-picture

Picture-in-Picture (PiP) allows you to watch videos or continue messaging in a chat while on a video call.

To enable picture-in-picture for video calls:

  1. Go to your device settings.
  2. Search and tap Picture-in-Picture.
  3. Confirm WhatsApp is selected.

Note:

  • You can’t switch between voice and video for group calls.
  • You can’t turn off the speaker during a video call.
  • There is no auto-answer for video calls.
  • You can’t change the camera orientation during a video call.
  • You can’t turn on your device’s flashlight during a video call.
  • Make sure you and your contacts have strong internet connections when placing or receiving video calls.
  • To save data, make and answer calls when connected to Wi-Fi. You can also turn Use less data for calls on or off in WhatsApp Settings > Storage and data.
  • You can’t access emergency service numbers through WhatsApp, such as 911 in the United States.
  • If your call isn’t going through, it’s possible the other person is on an older operating system or WhatsApp version.
  • To use WhatsApp as your primary calling app, set it as the default calling app in your phone settings. For more information, contact your phone’s manufacturer.

Voice calling lets you call your contacts using WhatsApp for free, even if they’re in another country. Voice calling uses your phone’s internet connection rather than your mobile plan’s minutes. Data charges may apply.

[Embedded video omitted]

Free WhatsApp voice calls (Data charges may apply)

0:00 / 0:20

Make a voice call

  1. Open the individual chat with the contact you want to call.

  2. Tap

    [Image: Voice call (phone)]

    .

Alternatively, open WhatsApp, then tap the Calls tab >

[Image: Add chat (plus sign within circle)]

in the top right corner. Find the contact you want to voice call, then tap

[Image: Voice call (phone)]

.

Use the keypad to make a voice call

You can use the keypad to make a voice call to people or businesses not saved to your contacts.

  1. Go to Calls.

  2. Tap

    [Image: Add chat (plus sign within circle)]

    .

  3. Enter the number you want to call.

  4. Tap

    [Image: Call (phone within circle)]

    .

Note: If you’re calling a number that’s not currently registered on WhatsApp, select Call to the pop-up that explains calls will be through mobile carrier. You’ll have the option to invite the user to join WhatsApp. If the user isn’t on WhatsApp, carrier and data charges may apply.

Add a contact to call through a chat thread

If you’re currently on a call, tap

[Image: Add Participant (silhouette of person with plus sign within a circle)]

to add a contact to the call.

If you have the call minimized, you can go back to the call and tap

[Image: Voice Call (phone)]

or

[Image: camera (camera)]

, depending on the type of call you’re in > Add to current call.

Leave a voice message

If they don’t pick up, you can leave a voicemail by tapping Record voice message.

After recording, you can:

  1. Tap

    [Image: play (left arrowhead)]

    to listen to it.

  2. Tap

    [Image: delete editing status (trash can)]

    to delete it.

  3. Tap

    [Image: Send (paper airplane within circle)]

    to send it.

Once sent, you’ll see the voice note in your chat with them and they’ll get a notification.

Schedule a voice or video call

From your Calls tab:

  1. Tap

    [Image: Add chat (plus sign within circle)]

    Schedule call.

  2. Optionally edit the title, add an optional description, and select the time, date, and type of call.

  3. Tap Next > select your recipients.

  4. Tap Send to share it with your recipients.

Receive a voice call

If your phone is locked, you’ll see an incoming WhatsApp Audio… screen when someone calls you, where you can:

  • Slide to answer the call.
  • Tap Remind Me, then select if you want to be reminded When I leave or In 1 hour.
  • Tap Message to decline the call with a note.
  • Decline the call by pressing the power button on the side of the iPhone two times.

Note: You can change your settings to silence calls from unknown callers.

Turn video on or off

Tap

[Image: Video call (video camera)]

to switch from a voice to video call. The other participant will start viewing your video instantly. They can choose to keep their video off or turn it on.

If the person isn’t saved as a contact and you haven’t interacted with them, they must accept the request to start seeing your video.

Tap

[Image: Video off (video camera with slash)]

to turn your video off again.

Note:

  • Make sure you and your contacts have strong internet connections when placing or receiving group voice calls.
  • Voice calling is available on iPhones running iOS 12 or newer.
  • You can’t access emergency service numbers through WhatsApp such as 911 in the United States. To make emergency calls, you must make other communication arrangements.
  • To use WhatsApp as your primary calling app, set it as the default calling app in your phone settings. For more information, contact your phone’s manufacturer.

Voice calling lets you call your contacts using WhatsApp Web for free, even if they’re in another country. Voice calling uses your internet connection. Web calling is supported on Windows, Linux and MacOS.

To make or receive voice calls on WhatsApp Web:

  • You’ll need an active internet connection on your computer and phone.
  • You’ll need to have an audio output device and microphone connected to your computer for calls.

Note: Use a headset for the best audio. Using a separate external microphone and speaker devices might cause echo.

Make a voice call

  1. Open the individual chat with the contact you’d like to call.
  2. Click Call > Voice or Video.

During the call, you can mute or unmute your microphone by clicking the Microphone icon. To end a call, click End call.

Answer a voice call

When you receive an incoming call, you’ll see a notification on your screen.

You can click:

  • Accept to accept the call.

  • Decline to decline the call.

  • [Image: More (three vertical dots)]

    to open microphone and video settings.

When you answer an incoming call, you can:

  • Click the Camera icon to switch to a video call.

  • Click

    [Image: More (three vertical dots)]

    to open microphone and video settings.

  • Click End call to end the call.

Switch between voice and video call

While on a voice call with a contact, you can switch to a video call.

  1. Click the Camera icon.
  2. The voice call will switch to a video call.

To make a voice call:

  1. Say “Hey Meta, call [name] on WhatsApp”.
  2. Confirm that you’ve selected the correct person.
  3. Once you’ve confirmed, the call will start connecting.
  4. When you’ve finished with the call, double-tap the touchpad on your glasses or hang up from your phone.
  • Note: You can also answer or decline incoming calls by saying “Hey Meta, answer” or “Hey Meta, decline”.

You can protect your internet protocol (IP) address from others on WhatsApp calls by relaying all of your calls through WhatsApp’s servers. If you turn on Protect IP address in calls, your calls won’t be connected directly and will avoid revealing your IP address to the person you’re calling.

Edit Protect IP address

To access this setting:

  1. Tap Settings or your profile picture, then tap Privacy.
  2. Tap Advanced.
  3. Turn Protect IP address in calls on or off.

Note:

  • Group calls are always relayed through WhatsApp’s servers by default.
  • When using call relaying, you might find the call quality is reduced.
  • Calls relayed through WhatsApp servers are end-to-end encrypted, like all calls on WhatsApp.

Protecting our users from a video calling cyber attack

On iPhone

Copy link

In May 2019 we stopped a highly sophisticated cyber attack that exploited our video calling system in order to send malware to the mobile devices of a number of WhatsApp users. The nature of the attack did not require targeted users to answer the calls they received. We quickly added new protections to our systems and issued an update to WhatsApp to help keep people safe. We are now taking additional action, based on what we have learned to date.

We sent a special WhatsApp message to approximately 1,400 users that we have reason to believe were impacted by this attack to directly inform them about what happened. Cyber security experts at the Citizen Lab, an academic research group based at the University of Toronto’s Munk School, volunteered to help us to learn more about the impact of this attack on civil society, including journalists and human rights defenders. The Citizen Lab has published information related to this specific attack here and remains available to provide support to this community.

WhatsApp cares deeply about the privacy and security of our users. Some of your most personal moments are shared on WhatsApp, which is why we built end-to-end encryption into our app. This attack was developed to access messages after they were decrypted on an infected device, abusing in-app vulnerabilities and the operating systems that power our mobile phones.

We agree with UN Special Rapporteur for Freedom of Expression David Kaye’s call for a moratorium on these attacks. There must be strong legal oversight of cyber weapons like the one used in this attack to ensure they are not used to violate individual rights and freedoms people deserve wherever they are in the world. Human rights groups have documented a disturbing trend that such tools have been used to attack journalists and human rights defenders. Working with research experts at the Citizen Lab, we believe this attack targeted at least 100 members of civil society, which is an unmistakable pattern of abuse. This number may grow higher as more victims come forward. We are committed to doing all we can, working with industry partners, to protect our users and guard against these kinds of threats.

WhatsApp has also filed a complaint in U.S. court that attributes the attack to a spyware company called NSO Group and its parent company Q Cyber Technologies. The complaint alleges they violated both U.S. and California laws as well as the WhatsApp Terms of Service, which prohibits this type of abuse. This is the first time that an encrypted messaging provider is taking legal action against a private entity that has carried out this type of attack against its users. In our complaint we explain how NSO carried out this attack, including acknowledgement from an NSO employee that our steps to remediate the attack were effective. We are seeking a permanent injunction banning NSO from using our service.

You can read more about our views published here.

If you received a message from us and have additional questions about this incident, you can message the WhatsApp team directly and securely by opening WhatsApp Settings > Help > Contact Us.

For those who believe they may be targeted by sophisticated attacks, WhatsApp offers Strict account settings. This is an advanced, optional security feature that, when enabled, applies WhatsApp’s strictest privacy and security controls to help reduce your vulnerability to cyber attacks. This feature is built for users who may face elevated risk and should only be turned on if you believe you may be targeted.

About security codes that automatically fill on WhatsApp

Copy link

[Embedded video omitted]

0:00 / 0:48

Certain apps may require you to submit a one-time passcode (OTP) before signing in. An OTP is usually an alphanumeric code sent via message and is valid for one use only. You can opt to receive these codes on WhatsApp.

If you opt to receive an OTP on WhatsApp:

  • To help you sign in, certain apps may configure their settings to automatically submit the code sent through WhatsApp to be verified on your behalf.
  • WhatsApp will automatically and securely deliver the OTP directly to the app, making it easier for you to quickly and safely access the apps you need.

Your message content is always protected. No one outside of the chat, not even WhatsApp, can read it.

Apps should always ask for permission before sending you a code via your WhatsApp account or any other kinds of messages. If you do not want a business to send you a one-time passcode over WhatsApp, you can select another delivery method that the business offers in their app.

How to share your view on a call on Ray-Ban Meta smart glasses

Copy link

With Ray-Ban Meta smart glasses, you can share your view with those you’re calling so they see what you see.

To enable sharing your view for the first time:

  1. Put your Ray-Ban Meta smart glasses on and turn them on.
  2. Start a video call on WhatsApp on your phone.
  3. Tap the glasses icon on WhatsApp on your phone during the call and follow the instructions.

Doing this once enables you to share your view on future calls by double tapping the capture button on your Ray-Ban Meta smart glasses.

To share your view on future calls:

  1. Double tap the capture button on your glasses during a video or audio call to start sharing your view.
  • Note: This will turn an audio call into a video call.
  1. Double tap the capture button on your glasses to switch back to your phone’s camera.

Note: You don’t need to link WhatsApp to Ray-Ban Meta to share your view on a call.

How to silence unknown callers

On iPhone

Copy link

Android

iOS

More

Android

iOS

Anyone who has your phone number can call you on WhatsApp. An unknown caller might be someone you haven’t contacted before or saved as a contact. You can block a phone number or silence calls from unknown callers by changing your privacy settings.

Silencing calls from unknown callers means you can focus on conversations that matter to you, while preserving your privacy and preventing unwanted contact.

Silence unknown callers

  1. Tap Settings or your profile picture, then tap Privacy.
  2. Tap Calls.
  3. Turn on or off Silence unknown callers.

You can see silenced calls from unknown callers in the Calls tab and your notifications, but your phone won’t ring. You can call an unknown caller back from within the Calls tab. Alternatively, tap the Silenced unknown caller message within a chat.

Note: If you call or message the silenced caller, you won’t be able to silence their calls in future. You can stop receiving calls from other WhatsApp users by blocking them.

How to use call waiting

On iPhone

Copy link

Android

iOS

More

Android

iOS

If someone calls you on WhatsApp while you’re already on a WhatsApp voice or video call, you’ll receive a notification. You can choose to either answer or decline the call. This won’t interrupt your existing call.

You can also choose to silence calls from unknown callers in settings. You’ll still see silenced calls from unknown callers in the Calls tab and in Notifications, but your phone won’t ring.

If someone calls you on WhatsApp

You can either:

  • End & Accept: End the call you’re currently on and accept the incoming call, or
  • Decline: Decline the incoming call and remain on the current call.

If someone calls you from outside of WhatsApp

If someone calls outside of WhatsApp during your WhatsApp voice or video call, you can tap:

  • End & Accept: End the call you’re currently on and accept the incoming call.
  • Hold & Accept: Put the current call on hold while you accept the incoming call.
  • Send to voicemail: Send the incoming call to voicemail and remain on the current call.

Note:

  • Carrier charges may apply for calls made outside of WhatsApp.
  • Charges may also apply for WhatsApp voice and video calls while roaming, or if you exceed your data limit.
  • If you don’t want to receive calls from a specific contact, you can block them. You can also silence calls from unknown callers.

About WhatsApp Web calling

Copy link

This feature is rolling out gradually and may not be available to you yet. In the meantime, we recommend keeping WhatsApp updated on your device so you can get the feature as soon as it’s available.

WhatsApp Web lets you call your contacts for free, even if they’re in another country. WhatsApp Web calling uses your internet connection.

WhatsApp Web calling is supported on: Windows, Linux and MacOS. Calling works best on Chrome, Edge, Safari and Firefox. Certain browser versions may not be supported.

To make or receive calls with WhatsApp Web you’ll need: An active internet connection on your computer.

To learn more, go to web.whatsapp.com in your browser.

If you prefer a native experience you can use WhatsApp for Windows or WhatsApp for Mac.

.

Note: Use a headset for the best audio quality. Using a separate external microphone and speaker devices might cause an echo.
